specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g cooked white rice into the blender. Add 100 ml water. Blend 60 s on high, scraping once at 30 s. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard residue. Reweigh the sieved base and record the mass in g. For the IDDSI Level 3 liquidised target, dose the thickener from that weighed mass: calibration starting point 3.0 g thickener per 100 g of sieved base — operator records the actual grams used. Whisk into the sieved base, rest 2 min, re-whisk 5 s. Re-weigh the final specimen and record.
specimens.iddsi_test: - Fork drip: lift a loaded fork and hold it level over the bowl. Pass = liquid drips through the tine gaps in a thin continuous stream, not a solid lump falling. - Spoon tilt: load a spoon and tilt to 45°. Pass = cohesive but spreadable — the mass moves and spreads on the tilted spoon, leaving a slow-travelling trail; it must not sit as a fixed lump that will not move. - 10 ml / 10 s syringe flow test (deciding test at L3): fill to the 10 ml mark, release, time 10 s. Pass = 8–10 ml remaining in the syringe (i.e., 0–2 ml flowed out), with the flow continuous through the full 10 s. - Fork pressure: skip — not applicable at L3. Fork pressure is the L4/L6/L7 test; an L3 specimen is lump-free and flowing and must not be required to hold a pressure imprint.
specimens.visual_qc: On fork: smooth glossy coating, single colour, no whole grains or white flecks. On spoon: mound holds a peak briefly then levels; surface matte-sheen, no free liquid pooling. When the spoon tilts, the mass slides as one and leaves a slow-travelling trail.

specimens.fail_modes: - Too thin (runs off the spoon; less than 8 ml remaining in the syringe at t=10 s, i.e. more than 2 ml flowed out): add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g of current specimen mass, whisk 30 s, rest 2 min, re-test. - Too thick (mound stands and will not move on the tilted spoon; 10 ml still in the syringe at t=10 s with no measurable flow, or the slow drip stalls before 10 s): stir in 5–10 ml water, re-mix, re-test. - Visible grains or flecks after sieving: re-blend 30 s and re-sieve. Re-make if any test still fails after two corrections.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g cooked white rice into the blender jar. Add 100 ml water. Blend 60 s on high. Stop, scrape the jar wall with a spatula, blend a further 30 s. Sieve through the 4 mm sieve, pressing with the spatula so all puree passes; discard residue (residue must be under 10 g — more means under-blending). Return puree to the blender. Measure the puree volume in the jug to the nearest 50 ml (this batch yields ≈350 ml). Add 4 g thickener per 100 ml of puree — 14 g at 350 ml, weighed to the nearest gram (calibration starting point — record the actual grams used). Blend 20 s to incorporate, rest 60 s, blend 10 s. The food list note says "blend-hold": there is no cooking or steeping step that fits this specimen, so none is recorded.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: the tines leave a clear, full-depth imprint that holds when the fork is lifted; the mound does not rebound or drip. Spoon tilt: a level spoonful, tilted to 45°, holds its shape on the spoon with no flow over the edge. Fork drip: a forkful held over the plate sits as a mound above the tines; nothing drips in 5 s. The L3 10 ml/10 s syringe flow test is not the L4 criterion and is not used here.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform off-white colour, no visible rice grains. Smooth, glossy surface with no separated liquid pooling around the mound. Holds a clean peak when spooned.

Clips: steamed_white_rice_L4_take4.mp4 (8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt); steamed_white_rice_L4_take5.mp4 (IDDSI test film, fork drip + spoon tilt in sequence).
specimens.fail_modes: Mound spreads or slumps on the tilted spoon, or puree drips through the fork tines → the specimen is too thin: THICKEN it by blending in 2 g thickener per 100 ml of puree (5 g at 250 ml; weigh the actual addition) and re-test. A 5 g/100 ml jump overshoots the L4 window, so never add more than 2 g/100 ml per addition, maximum three additions; if the specimen is still too thin after three, discard the batch. Liquid pools around the mound after resting → blend a further 20 s and rest 90 s to re-hydrate and thicken before re-test. Grainy texture or rice specks visible after sieving → re-blend 30 s and re-sieve. Maximum two re-makes per take; if still failing, discard the batch and record the outcome.

specimens.prep: Bought form and allergens (docs/BASE_FOOD_LIST.md, BF01): cooked white rice, rice cooker or takeaway; allergen tag = none (operator still confirms the pack label at portioning). Per-level note for BF01 L5 is "chop to <= 4 mm, moisten with warm water" — both parts are performed here.  Weigh 150 g cooked white rice on the 0.1 g scale. Chop on the board with a small knife for 60 s, or pulse the blender 3 x 3 s (scrape and rest between pulses), until grains are broken to particles <= 4 mm but still visibly granular; stop before it turns into a sticky paste. Add 40 ml warm water and fold through with a fork until evenly moist; final specimen ≈ 190 g — record actual mass. SIEVE AS GAUGE ONLY: scoop one 15 g sub-sample and press it through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon. Pass = the sample passes with light-to-moderate pressure, confirming particles <= 4 mm; fold the passed sample back into the batch. If it will not pass, chop a further 30 s and re-gauge with a fresh 15 g sub-sample. Do NOT press the whole batch through the sieve and do NOT discard retained material — at L5 the <= 4 mm grains are the specimen. Thickener is not an L5 calibration step; if free moisture separates after folding, sprinkle in gum-based thickener at 0.5 g per 100 g of mash (0.95 g for 190 g), weighed to 0.1 g, stir, rest 60 s, re-test; cap 2.0 g per 100 g (3.8 g for 190 g). Record every addition in prep.thickener_g. Microwave 10 s before plating. Keep a 50 g reserve of cooked rice for a re-make.
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon tilt (primary, L5): load a heaped teaspoon, hold level, tilt to 45°. Pass = the moist grains hold a loose mound that slumps only when shaken, with no separate thin liquid pooling on the spoon or tray; any pooling = fail. Fork pressure (supporting check only, not the L5 discriminator): press the fork tines flat into the specimen until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass = the grains squash and do not recover shape when the fork is lifted. Fork drip: skip — L3/L4 test only; an L5 specimen is a cohesive moist mince with no flowing stream to measure, so no drip is recorded. Syringe flow: skip — the 10 ml / 10 s test is L3 only; do not run it and do not record it.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: moist grains, every particle <= 4 mm, visible granule texture, uniform damp sheen — matte-wet, never glossy with pooling liquid. On the plate: no shiny free liquid at the rim. The mound holds a fork-pressed indentation without crumbling or flowing. If the surface reads completely smooth with no granule you can see or feel, the batch has gone to L4 — correct per FAIL MODES before shooting.
specimens.shots: Capture 3 stills + 2 clips against the A4 kit, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, never cropped. - steamed_white_rice_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame, specimen mass visible on the scale. - steamed_white_rice_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, full specimen mound visible. - steamed_white_rice_L5_take3.jpg — spoon-tilt close-up, mid-tilt, mound holding. - steamed_white_rice_L5_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s spoon-tilt then fork-pressure, one continuous take. - steamed_white_rice_L5_take5.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full L5 protocol (spoon tilt + fork pressure) unbroken.
specimens.fail_modes: Too wet — thin liquid pools on the plate or runs off the spoon (reads L4/L3, i.e. too THIN): sprinkle in gum thickener at 0.5 g per 100 g of mash, rest 60 s, re-test; cap 2.0 g per 100 g. Thickening moves the specimen toward L5. Too dry — crumbs fall off the fork and no mound forms: fold in 5 ml warm water at a time, re-mash, re-test; cap 40 ml total added water. Moistening moves the specimen toward L5. Grains above 4 mm on the gauge (reads L6, too coarse): chop a further 30 s and re-gauge with a fresh 15 g sub-sample. Never sieve the batch to correct this — sieving removes exactly the grains that make the specimen L5. Over-processed to a smooth sticky paste (reads L4): discard and re-make from 150 g fresh rice with a shorter pulse, or fold through 50 g of freshly chopped coarse rice and re-gauge. Any specimen failing its level test is re-made once from the reserve aliquot or marked FAIL in the log (tests.pass = false, reason in prep.notes); its media is never renamed into another level.

specimens.prep: - Weigh 75 g dry long-grain white rice, rinse, then simmer in 135 ml water, covered, 12 min; rest 5 min off the heat. Target: grains tender with no chalky core, surface matte and not sticky — this yields ≈200 g cooked. If starting from already-cooked rice, weigh 200 g cooked and skip this step. - Turn the cooked rice onto a clean plate. Working in batches of ≤40 g, break the grains apart against the plate wall with the back of a fork (or a knife tip) until every piece measures 8–15 mm on the 100 mm ruler. Re-cut anything over 15 mm; discard anything under 8 mm (it reads L5, ~4 mm). - Do not blend — blending makes rice paste, incompatible with L6. - Do not sieve — a 4 mm sieve cannot enforce a 15 mm limit, and passing L6 material through one destroys the piece structure. - Do not add thickener, stock, or any liquid — L6 is achieved by cutting, not by thickening. - Weigh the finished specimen and record the mass, plus the grams discarded as fines.
specimens.iddsi_test: - ACTIVE — 5.1 fork pressure. Lay one 8–15 mm piece on a flat white plate. Press the fork tines flat onto it with thumb pressure until the nail blanches white; hold 3 s; lift. PASS: the piece squashes, does not spring back, does not return to its original shape, and does not smear into paste. Test 3 separate pieces; all 3 must pass. - SKIP — 5.2 spoon tilt. Applies at L3/L4/L5 only; an L6 specimen is discrete pieces that must sit on a tilted spoon rather than flow, so the test cannot separate L6 from L7 — the 8–15 mm size window does that. - SKIP — 5.3 fork drip. Applies at L3/L4 only; pressed rice carries no free liquid to drip through the tines, so the test always passes and carries no information. - SKIP — 5.4 syringe flow. Every L3 only; 8–15 mm pieces will not enter or leave a 10 ml syringe. - L6 verdict = 8–15 mm size window met AND 5.1 fork pressure passes.
specimens.visual_qc: - Grains are no longer intact; each piece holds its own shape, matte and yielding, not glossy or sticky. - Every piece measures 8–15 mm against the 100 mm ruler — nothing above 15 mm, nothing below 8 mm. - The pile on the fork sits in a heap with visible gaps between pieces, not a smear and not a single cohesive bolus. - No whole grains visible; no free liquid or starch film on the plate.
specimens.shots: - bf01_steamed_white_rice_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero of the specimen mound with the 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler in frame. - bf01_steamed_white_rice_L6_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only, ruler along one edge. - bf01_steamed_white_rice_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. - bf01_steamed_white_rice_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s continuous fork-pressure sequence to completion (the only active IDDSI test at L6). - bf01_steamed_white_rice_L6_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: one fork press per piece, three pieces in order.
specimens.fail_modes: - A piece measures >15 mm: re-cut with the knife tip to 8–15 mm and re-measure against the ruler. Do NOT press harder to break it down — extra pressure makes paste (L5/L4), not smaller L6 pieces. - A piece measures <8 mm: remove it from the specimen — it reads L5. Re-press the remaining grains more gently, in smaller batches. - A piece does not yield to the thumbnail, or whole grains remain: the rice is undercooked. Return it to the pot with 20 ml water, simmer 5 min, drain 60 s, then re-press. - A piece rebounds to its original shape after the press: undercooked or under-pressed; discard and remake from a batch cooked 5 min longer. - The batch has smeared into paste: over-pressed. Start again from freshly cooked rice and stop pressing as soon as pieces reach 8–15 mm. Do not try to firm a paste back up with thickener — L6 is reached by cutting, never by thickening.

specimens.prep: Cook a fresh batch of white rice (long-grain, non-glutinous) and let it stand 2 min so the surface is dry and no free water remains. Portion 50 g ± 2 g of cooked rice. With dry hands or the back of a spoon, press the 50 g into one compact cake in the centre of the plate — target 25 mm across × 20 mm high, so that the smallest dimension is ≥15 mm (check against the 15 mm checkerboard cell: the cake must be wider than one full cell). Press firmly so the grains bind and the cake holds its moulded shape. Whole grains only. Do not blend, do not sieve, do not add thickener, do not add liquid — forming is the only manipulation and it does not change the food. Record the actual served mass on the data sheet before capture.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test (the only test that applies at L7): press the tines into the cake with the flat of the fork until the thumbnail blanches white. The cake must compress under the tines and must not return to its original contour when the fork is removed. Pass criterion: full white blanch, dent holds. Spoon tilt, fork drip and syringe flow do NOT apply at L7 — do not run them and do not record them as pass/fail. The former spoon-tilt criterion ("no individual grains roll off") is withdrawn: loose cooked grains cannot meet it, and it is not an L7 test.
specimens.visual_qc: Grains distinct, glossy, non-glutinous surface. Cake holds the moulded shape with no spreading at the base and no cracking. Smallest dimension ≥15 mm (spans more than one full 15 mm checkerboard cell). No pooling liquid at the plate contact; no steam fogging the lens.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, ruler along the front edge, checkerboard under the front-left quadrant. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard centred, full cake visible. Still 3: fork-press close-up, tines mid-press, thumbnail blanch captured. Clip 1: 8-12 s fork-press in one continuous take (fork pressure only — no spoon tilt at L7). Clip 2: IDDSI test film, fork-pressure sequence filmed full-frame. Files: steamed_white_rice_L7_take1.jpg, steamed_white_rice_L7_take1.mp4, plus _take2, _take3 suffixes for reshoots.
specimens.fail_modes: Grains too wet, pooling liquid on the plate, or the cake will not hold its moulded shape — a loose-grain serving is ~6-8 mm per grain and cannot be certified L7. Re-make from a fresh, drier batch, re-form, re-shoot all frames; do not add thickener or liquid. Grains overcooked to a paste: the fork test smears instead of holding a dent — too soft, below L7. Re-make from a fresh batch cooked 2 min shorter, re-form, re-shoot all frames. Grains firm, dent does not hold, cake springs back — re-cook the same batch 2 min longer, re-form, re-test; if it still springs back, reject the specimen. Long-grain rice that will not bind into a ≥15 mm cake: this specimen cannot be brought to L7 by any bench method. Reject it and re-shoot from a batch that binds; record the substitution. Do not submit loose grains as L7.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g takeaway or chilled plain congee into the blender jar. Add 50 ml water. Blend 45 s on high, scraping the wall once at 20 s. Sieve through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon, discarding any coarse residue that will not pass. Return the sieved liquid to a clean jug and weigh it. Add thickener at 1.0 g per 100 ml of sieved liquid as the calibration starting point; whisk in with a fork for 30 s, rest 2 min, re-whisk 15 s. If flow is too fast, add thickener in 0.2 g per 100 ml increments up to a ceiling of 1.8 g per 100 ml. Record the final grams used. The PER-LEVEL NOTE is blend-thin, and that step is performed.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a fork from the specimen; the liquid drips slowly in continuous thin streams through the tines. Pass if drips fall steadily but not in a single sheet. Fork pressure: pressing the fork tines into 5 ml on a flat plate leaves a clear print that does not fill back in within 5 s. Pass if the print holds. Spoon tilt: a heaped spoon tilted to 45 degrees slides off in 2-4 s, not instantly and not in one lump. Pass at 2-4 s. Syringe flow: fill the IDDSI 10 ml syringe to 10 ml, release, wait 10 s; pass if 8-10 ml remains in the barrel.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: glossy, fully smooth, no grains or rice skins catching the tines. On the spoon: coats the bowl in an even layer with no bare streaks. In the jug: flows like warm honey when tipped; pours in a continuous ribbon that stacks briefly before settling.

Stills: plain_congee_L3_take1.jpg hero at 45 degrees with ruler and checkerboard; plain_congee_L3_take2.jpg top-down with checkerboard centred; plain_congee_L3_take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press. Clips: plain_congee_L3_take1.mp4 fork-press and spoon-tilt, 8-12 s; plain_congee_L3_take2.mp4 full IDDSI syringe flow test from fill to 10 s mark.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny, drips in a continuous sheet through fork or leaves under 8 ml in syringe: add thickener in 0.2 g per 100 ml steps to a maximum of 1.8 g per 100 ml, rest 2 min, retest. Too thick, holds shape on spoon tilt or leaves more than 10 ml: dilute with 10 ml water, re-blend 15 s, retest. Grainy with visible rice skins, fails the smooth visual: re-blend 30 s and re-sieve; if it still fails, discard and re-make with a finer sieve pass or start a fresh batch. Any specimen failing two consecutive tests is discarded.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g thick-style takeaway or chilled plain congee into the blender cup. Add 60 ml hot water to loosen the chilled starch matrix. Blend on high for 45 seconds, stopping once to scrape the wall. Press through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon; discard retained solids and lumps — the per-level note "blend-hold" confirms sieving is required. Return puree to the cup and rest 30 seconds so the starch relaxes. If the mound flattens on the spoon, stir in thickener at 1.0 g per 100 ml as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used and the resulting appearance.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: a single fork pressed into the surface leaves a clear, clean-edged indent that holds its shape when the fork is lifted. Spoon tilt: a loaded spoon held at 45 degrees keeps the full mound on the bowl with no slide or drip. Fork drip: lifting a fork dipped 2 cm deep and held vertically over the plate, the puree sits as a cohesive mound above the tines — none flows through, none drips in 5 seconds. No separate thin liquid pools around the specimen.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface reads matte and even, not glossy or watery. A spoonful mounds and peaks rather than spreading. No grains, skin flecks, or ginger shreds visible against the fork tines.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, labelled plain_congee_L4_take1.jpg. Still 2: top-down on checkerboard only. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines clearly indenting. Clip 1: 8–12 seconds fork-press then spoon-tilt, plain_congee_L4_take1.mp4. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film, same stem.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen flows through the tines or pools thin liquid — re-blend 15 seconds, rest, re-test. Specimen cracks or falls off the spoon in a chunk — add water 10 ml, blend 10 seconds, re-test. Lumps or skin remain after sieving — re-sieve; do not proceed.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of thick congee onto the digital scale. Do not blend — thick congee with soft grains must be read for particle size, not pulverised. Press the congee through a 4 mm sieve with the back of a fork; discard what stays on the mesh. Re-weigh the sieved portion. Add thickener at 0 g per 100 ml as the calibration starting point — record the actual grams used. Stir with the fork until streaks disappear. The per-level note requires soft grains ≤4 mm; sieving achieves this. No water added. Stop if the congee weeps thin liquid — that is a fail, remake from a drier pack.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: place a 15 mm mound on the plate, press the fork tines until the thumbnail blanches white. The mound must squash, the surface must not spring back, and the grains must stay ≤4 mm. Pass = squash with no recovery. Spoon tilt test: load 4 ml on the spoon, tilt to 90°. The congee must hold its shape and slide off slowly as a cohesive mass, not pour. Fork drip test: lift fork from the bowl — the congee should sit in the mound, not drip through the tines. The L3 10 ml/10 s syringe flow test does not apply at L5; do not run it.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: moist sheen, soft rice grains visible, no free liquid pooling in the tine gaps. On the spoon: holds a rounded mound, surface matte not glossy, grains ≤4 mm. No separate thin liquid on the plate.
specimens.shots: Shoot on the A4 kit with 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler. Still 1: 45° hero, specimen mound, ruler and checkerboard in frame. Still 2: top-down over checkerboard. Still 3: fork-press close-up, mid-press, thumbnail blanched. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. Clip 2: IDDSI test film, full protocol. Files: plain_congee_L5_take1.jpg / plain_congee_L5_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Grains >4 mm after sieving — re-sieve or reject the pack. Thin liquid weeps on the plate — remake from a thicker pack, no water. Specimen recovers shape after fork press — too stiff, loosen with 5 ml hot water and retest.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g hor fun, fresh pack, blanched. Chop into 2-3 cm pieces. Add 80 ml water. Blend on high 45 s; stop, scrape down, blend 30 s more. Press through the 4 mm sieve; discard residue. Stir in thickener at 1.5 g per 100 ml of sieved liquid — calibration starting point only, record the actual g used and final ml. Stir 30 s, rest 60 s, stir 10 s. Re-weigh and record total specimen mass.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift fork from specimen at 5 cm/s; liquid drips in a continuous slow stream through the tines, drops form but do not pour. Fork pressure: fork prongs leave a clear, persistent score on the surface under light thumb pressure; surface does not flow back. Spoon tilt: small mound on a tilted spoon barely shifts; thick, controlled slide. IDDSI flow test: fill 10 ml syringe, cut at 10 ml mark, release for 10 s; 8-10 ml remains. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: On spoon: smooth, glossy, no lumps, no noodle strands visible, thick coat that holds the spoon shape. On fork: a clean coat between tines, drips threadlike not watery. Color uniform off-white.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen in plain bowl. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard under transparent bowl. Still 3: fork-press close-up, mid-press showing scored surface. Clip 1: 8-12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. Clip 2: IDDSI flow test, full 10 s. Name: hor_fun_flat_rice_noodle_L3_take1.jpg / .mp4. Retake as take2 if needed.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: drips pour off fork, syringe reads under 8 ml — add 0.25 g thickener per 100 ml, rest, retest. Too thick: holds shape on tilted spoon, syringe reads over 10 ml — add 5 ml water, stir, retest. Lumpy or grainy: sieve left residue — re-blend 20 s and re-sieve, then re-thicken to spec.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched hor fun on the digital scale. Add 80 ml cool water. Blend in the consumer blender 45 s, stop, scrape down, blend another 30 s until smooth. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any residue retained on the mesh. Return puree to the blender, add thickener at the calibration starting point of 2.0 g per 100 ml, blend 20 s to incorporate. Rest 60 s, then re-blend 10 s. If the mixture still flows through the fork tines, add thickener in 0.3 g per 100 ml increments, blending 10 s and resting 60 s between additions, until the mound holds. Record the final g per 100 ml on the run sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a forkful 5 cm above the plate; specimen must sit as a mound above the tines with no drip. Fork pressure: press the fork tines into the mound; surface must hold the imprint with no separation of thin liquid. Spoon tilt: scoop, tilt spoon to 45 degrees; specimen must stay seated, not slide off. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform pale off-white paste, glossy sheen, no visible noodle fragments or grains. Holds a sharp spoon edge and a clean fork-print ridge. No thin liquid pooling on the plate surface beside the mound.

specimens.fail_modes: Specimen drips through fork tines — too thin, add thickener 0.3 g per 100 ml and retest. Visible noodle specks or grainy texture — re-blend 20 s and re-sieve through 4 mm. Thin liquid separates and pools on the plate — too wet, return to blender with extra thickener 0.3 g per 100 ml. Any single failure: discard, re-make from fresh 200 g batch, log the corrective addition.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched hor fun on the scale. Chop across the noodles with a fork or knife until no piece exceeds 4 mm; sweep through a 4 mm sieve and discard any overs. Return choppings to the bowl, moisten with 30 ml warm broth from the pack, and mash with a fork until the mass clumps and a fork pressed into it squashes without springing back. Add more broth 5 ml at a time only if the mass looks dry; record the final broth volume. No blender is used. No thickener is added; L5 calibration starts at zero grams per 100 ml and the operator notes the actual on the sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the specimen until the thumbnail blanches white for ~5 s; pass when the piece squashes, does not spring back, and stays flattened. Spoon tilt: scoop a teaspoon, tilt 45 degrees; pass when the mass slides off in one clump, leaving little residue, with no separate thin liquid pooling. Fork drip: lift fork with specimen; pass when nothing drips through or off within 10 s. L3 syringe test is not required.
specimens.visual_qc: Specimen sits in a soft mound that holds fork-tine imprints. Surface looks moist and glossy, never dry or chalky. No noodle strand longer than a rice grain visible.

specimens.fail_modes: Long strands reappear after mashing: re-chop and re-sieve. Specimen springs back under fork: add 5 ml broth and re-mash; if still elastic, restart with a finer chop. Thin broth pools on the plate: drain or fold back in; if it persists, re-make with less added liquid.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched hor fun sheets on the scale. Stack sheets, cut across the width into strips, then cross-cut into pieces no larger than 15 mm. Confirm each piece measures ≤15 mm against the 100 mm ruler. Do not blend; do not sieve; do not add thickener. No liquid is added. The L3 calibration thickener row does not apply to this L6 specimen — record "N/A" in that column. Pieces must remain visually separate, not mashed into a paste.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test — press the fork tines into a piece until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass: the piece squashes, does not spring back, and can be mashed with easy pressure between fork and bowl. Spoon-tilt test — place a heaped teaspoon on the plate and tilt to 90 degrees. Pass: the piece sits in a pile and slides/plops off with little or no flow; it does not pour. Fork-drip test — lift a piece on the fork and hold over a white plate for 10 seconds. Pass: minimal drip, no continuous flow, no tail. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces on the fork should appear as distinct flat soft strips, not clumped or sticky. Surface should look moist and pliable, not dry-cracked or gummy. On the spoon-tilt, the mound should hold shape briefly before sliding; it must not level out to a smooth liquid layer.

specimens.fail_modes: Pieces exceed 15 mm — re-cut smaller. Pieces feel rubbery or spring back under fork pressure — discard, source is too firm, re-blanch or remake. Pieces clump into a sticky mass with no separation — overworked, discard and re-cut fresh. Any single failure → full re-make.

specimens.prep: Use hor fun as packed; do not blend, do not sieve, do not add thickener or water. Weigh 150 g of blanched sheets straight from the pack onto the capture plate. Keep the noodle mass intact — tear only at natural seams if the bundle exceeds the ruler field. Respect the per-level note: whole sheets as served, reference specimen, no processing.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the noodle stack until the tines blanch white; the sheets must compress fully and recover their shape when the fork is lifted. Spoon tilt: a heaped teaspoon holds its shape on a level spoon — no flow, no slump. Fork drip: lift the fork clear of the plate; zero drip from the tines or sheet edges. The noodle must look and behave as a solid food that is easy to bite and manipulate, with no separation of liquid or sheet fragments.
specimens.visual_qc: Sheets lay flat, smooth, glossy, and continuous, with no frayed edges or broken fragments. The stack holds its geometry under the fork. Color is uniform pale off-white with no translucent or mushy patches.

specimens.fail_modes: Sheets fragmenting into short strips or releasing starch water means over-handling or over-blanched stock — reject, re-blanch a fresh pack. Sheets that bend but fail to flatten on the spoon indicate undercooked texture — reject, re-cook to pack instructions. Any drip from the fork indicates excess surface moisture — drain 30 s on the sieve and re-test; if drip persists, re-make.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g cooked thin wheat noodles on the digital scale. Blend with 180 ml room-temperature water on high for 45-60 s until fully smooth. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; press residue with the back of a spoon and discard what remains. For each 100 ml of sieved liquid, add 1.5 g thickener as the calibration starting point; the operator must record the actual grams used to hit target. Stir 30 s, rest 60 s, stir 10 s. Re-weigh and record final mass. Per-level note says blend-thin: confirm the blend is fully smooth before sieving; if strands remain, re-blend 20 s.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift fork from specimen; liquid drips slowly in a continuous thin stream through the tines, not in dollops. Fork press: tines leave a clear, shallow impression on the surface with no flow back into the groove. Spoon tilt: spoon holds its shape when tilted to 45 degrees, then slides off in one mass within 1-2 s, not as a free pour. Syringe flow test: fill the 10 ml syringe, release for 10 s; 8-10 ml must remain in the barrel. All four must pass before capture.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface looks glossy and homogenous with no noodle strands, lumps, or bubbles. Coats the spoon back in an even film about 1-2 mm thick. Holds a soft mound on the fork without running through the tines between lifts.
specimens.shots: thin_wheat_noodles_L3_take1.jpg: 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in lower frame. thin_wheat_noodles_L3_take2.jpg: top-down, checkerboard centred under the bowl. thin_wheat_noodles_L3_take3.jpg: fork-press close-up mid-press, groove visible. thin_wheat_noodles_L3_take1.mp4: 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. thin_wheat_noodles_L3_take2.mp4: 10 s IDDSI syringe flow test, start and end volume visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: drip is a free stream or syringe leaves under 6 ml; add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, rest, retest. Too thick: fork drag is heavy or spoon does not slide; blend in 10 ml water per 100 ml and retest. Visible strands on sieve or in QC: re-blend 20 s and re-sieve; if still present, discard and remake.

specimens.prep: Cook 80 g thin wheat noodles in boiling water until fully tender, drain, and cool to room temperature. Weigh 100 g cooked noodles into the blender, add 30 ml water, and blend 45–60 s, scraping the lid and jar once. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard any residue and weigh what passed. In a small bowl, stir thickener into the blended mass at 2 g per 100 ml (calibration starting point — record the actual grams used and final texture). Let rest 2 min, then stir. Reject if any separate thin liquid pools or the mass flows through fork tines. If it flows, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, stir, rest 2 min, retest. If it crumbles, add 5 ml water and re-blend 10 s.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-drip: lift a fork tines-down through the specimen; the mass must sit in a mound above the tines with no drip or flow for 10 s. Spoon-tilt: scoop, then tilt the spoon 45°; the specimen must hold its shape and not slide off. Fork-pressure: press the fork tines flat into the specimen; the surface should show a clear thumbprint imprint with no separate liquid squeezing out. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Specimen mounds cleanly on the spoon with a smooth, glossy surface and no visible noodle strands or lumps. No thin liquid pools around the base on the plate. Fork tines come out coated but the mass stays heaped above, not dripping.
specimens.shots: thin_wheat_noodles_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. thin_wheat_noodles_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. thin_wheat_noodles_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. thin_wheat_noodles_L4_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. thin_wheat_noodles_L4_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence, one continuous take.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: flows through tines or forms a puddle — add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 2 min, retest. Too stiff: cracks or crumbles on the spoon — add 5 ml water, re-blend 10 s, retest. Visible strands or grit: re-blend 30 s and re-sieve; if still present, re-make from a new cooked batch. Two failed re-makes: discard and start over with a fresh 80 g cook.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g cooked thin wheat noodles onto the plate. Chop across the bundle with a fork until strands measure ≤4 mm. Add 60 ml warm broth per the per-level note and mash with the fork until cohesive and moist; no separate thin liquid should pool. Do not blend — noodles become a paste and lose L5 texture. Do not add thickener. If strands stay longer than 4 mm after chopping, do not proceed; re-chop. Record final mass.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the specimen until the thumbnail blanches white. Specimen must squash, not spring back, and must not recover its shape when the fork lifts. Spoon tilt: scoop 4 ml onto a spoon and tilt 45°. Specimen must hold together and fall off in one mass, not drip, not slide. Fork drip: lift a forkful 5 cm above the plate; no thin liquid must run off continuously. Reject if drips form a steady stream.
specimens.visual_qc: Visible particles no larger than a 4 mm checkerboard square. Surface glistens but no free broth in the plate well. Fork tines leave a clean impression that stays.
specimens.shots: thin_wheat_noodles_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. thin_wheat_noodles_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard flat beside specimen. thin_wheat_noodles_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. thin_wheat_noodles_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one take. thin_wheat_noodles_L5_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence, no cuts.
specimens.fail_modes: Strands longer than 4 mm: re-chop, do not re-sieve. Dry, crumbly mass lacking cohesion: add 10 ml broth, re-mash, retest. Thin broth pooling on plate: drain briefly on the sieve, then retest fork-drip. Two failed re-makes: discard batch, note on capture sheet.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g thin wheat noodles. Boil in unsalted water until just tender, drain, and cool to ≈40 °C. Cut all pieces to ≤15 mm with kitchen shears on the cutting mat; discard any longer strands. Do not blend or sieve; the food list requires intact pieces. Do not add thickener; L6 needs no viscosity adjustment. Do not add water beyond residual surface moisture. Portion a 30 g specimen onto the capture plate.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork tines onto a piece until the thumbnail blanches white; on release the piece must squash flat and not recover its shape. Spoon tilt: a small mound on a spoon holds its form when the spoon is tilted to 45°—no flow, no drip. Fork drip: lift a loaded fork; nothing drips or runs through the tines before the fork-pressure test begins. Pass criterion for L6: piece squashes and does not recover its shape after fork pressure, plus mound holds on spoon tilt.
specimens.visual_qc: (a) All visible noodle pieces clearly shorter than the 15 mm reference line on the ruler; no long strands. (b) Pieces show slight surface gloss but no pooling liquid on the plate. (c) Pieces deform cleanly under fork tine; they bend, they do not spring back.
specimens.shots: Capture 3 stills and 2 clips: (1) thin_wheat_noodles_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; (2) thin_wheat_noodles_L6_take2.jpg — top-down on checkerboard; (3) thin_wheat_noodles_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. Clips: thin_wheat_noodles_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt; thin_wheat_noodles_L6_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: (1) Pieces >15 mm: re-cut to ≤15 mm, re-shoot. (2) Pieces spring back after fork pressure (under-cook): reboil 60–90 s, re-test; if still firm, re-make. (3) Free liquid pools on plate: drain and pat surface dry on paper towel, re-shoot; if persistent, re-make with shorter boil time.

specimens.prep: Boil 60 g dry thin wheat noodles (or 150 g fresh) in 1 L unsalted water until just tender to the bite. Drain, shake off surface moisture for 30 s, portion 30 g onto the fork and plate. Do not blend, do not sieve, do not add thickener. Target is whole noodles as normally served; no processing is permitted at L7.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines fully into the specimen; noodles compress/deform and change colour at the bite mark, and do not return to shape when fork is withdrawn. Pass = clear bite mark visible, noodle holds together, no recovery. Spoon tilt: spoon a small portion and tilt to 45 degrees; noodles slide off in a bolus and fall. Pass = full slide in 1-2 s. Fork drip: lift forkful clear of plate; no continuous drip from noodles between fork and plate. Pass = no drip.
specimens.visual_qc: - Noodles are distinct, firm strands, ~2 mm diameter, pale yellow, no clumping or mash. - Bite mark on fork shows dented, lighter-coloured core; strand does not spring back. - Loose strands lift cleanly off plate; no liquid pooling.

specimens.fail_modes: 1. Overcooked: noodles squash fully under fork with no spring, pass fork pressure by mashing — re-cook a fresh batch to 1 min less. 2. Sauce or oil film present: noodles slide off spoon without bite test, dripping observed — drain 60 s longer, blot, re-shoot. 3. Strands stuck together in a clump: cannot isolate a single forkful — re-portion with tongs, reject clump, re-shoot.  Re-make rule: any single fail = discard specimen, re-cook, re-shoot full set; do not patch a take.

specimens.prep: Bought form: retail packet of instant/quick rolled oats, dry, bought as packaged goods (check the label — most are not gluten-free). Allergens: wheat/gluten (oats plus shared milling lines); no milk, egg, nut or soy is added by this card. Thickener: xanthan- or starch-based IDDSI thickener, allergen-free on most labels — confirm on the pack and log it. Weigh 60 g dry oats on the digital scale and 180 ml water heated to 80-85 °C. Combine in the blender, seal, run 25-30 s on high until fully liquidised. Gauge once through the 4 mm sieve: the sieve is a lump-free GAUGE, not a sizing step — anything retained goes back into the blender for 10 s more and the pass is repeated until nothing is retained (target retained mass 0 g; record actual). Measure the specimen volume in the jug (expect ~240 ml). Add thickener at the calibration starting point of 2.0 g per 100 ml of that measured volume (~4.8 g for a 240 ml batch); record actual grams used. Blend 10 s to incorporate, rest 60 s to hydrate, re-blend 5 s. Bring to 50 °C ±5 °C before testing (re-warm; never add cold water to cool). If the syringe reads off-spec, step thickener in 0.2 g/100 ml increments (~0.5 g), blend 5 s, rest 30 s, re-test; record final g/100 ml. Blending is mandatory at L3, not optional.
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon tilt (5.2) — ACTIVE. Load 5 ml on a dessert spoon and tilt to 45° over a cup. Pass = the specimen slides off in a slow continuous ribbon that takes 3-5 s to clear the bowl of the spoon; it must not sit in a mound (that is L4) and must not pour like water (that is L2). Fork drip (5.3) — ACTIVE. Load the fork tines and hold 10 mm above the cup, then tilt. Pass = the specimen drips slowly in a continuous thin stream — not a pour, not a blob. Syringe flow (5.4) — ACTIVE. Fill the 10 ml IDDSI syringe to the 10 ml line, release, and time exactly 10 s with a timer. Pass = 8-10 ml remains in the barrel. Record residual to 0.5 ml: below 8 ml is too thin, above 10 ml is too thick. Fork pressure (5.1) — SKIP: applies at L4, L6 and L7 (supporting only at L5). Not performed at L3 — an L3 specimen is lump-free and flows freely, so a tine impression carries no level information. Do not film it.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: glossy, uniform beige, no lumps, no separated water pooling at the rim. On the fork tines after drip: a smooth coating with no runny tails and no dry grainy streaks. Nothing above 4 mm survives the gauge. Colour even, no scorched or dry oat flakes on the surface.

specimens.fail_modes: Too thin — pours fast off the spoon, drips in a stream from the fork, syringe residual <8 ml. Add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml of specimen (~0.5 g), blend 5 s, rest 30 s, re-test. This thickens the specimen toward the L3 window. Too thick — drops from the fork in blobs, syringe residual >10 ml, spoon holds a peak. Add 5 ml water per 100 ml (~12 ml), blend 5 s, re-test. This thins the specimen toward the L3 window. Grainy or weeping — material retained on the 4 mm gauge or water separating at the rim: return to the blender, add 20 ml water, blend 10 s, re-gauge. If it stays grainy after two passes, re-make from scratch; do not patch with thickener. Never thicken past the point where the syringe holds >10 ml, and never thin past 8 ml — both leave the L3 window.

specimens.prep: Weigh 100 g rolled oats into the blender. Add 200 ml hot water. Blend 45–60 s on high until visually smooth with no intact flakes; record the actual blend time. Sieve a 30 g portion through the 4 mm sieve — at L4 the specimen is lump-free, so the whole 30 g must pass the mesh. Do not press or force the portion through, and do not read pass-through as a defect: material passing through IS the pass. Pass = no more than 1 g (3 %) residue left on the mesh. If more than 1 g remains on the mesh, blend a further 30 s and re-sieve. L4 is a lump-free level, so the 4 mm sieve is the gauge here and it must run clean; a mound retained on the mesh is a fail, not a target. Thickener is not needed for the 1:2 base ratio; record 0 g/100 ml as the calibration starting point, and record the actual grams used if any is added at the FAIL MODES stage. No additional water or milk.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: lift a forkful and hold it above the bowl for 5 s — the specimen must sit as a mound above the tines and may shed at most a single dollop; a continuous stream through the tines is a fail. Pass = mound on the tines, at most one dollop in 5 s. Fork pressure test: press the fork tines into the specimen on a flat plate with thumb pressure — the surface must blanch white but the tines must not cut cleanly through; pass = blanch without full separation. Spoon tilt test: scoop the specimen, then tilt the spoon 45° — the mass must not slide, pour, or fall off; pass = holds shape with no flow. No separate thin liquid must pool at the rim of the specimen on the plate. No syringe flow test at L4.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is uniform cream/beige with no visible oat flecks or bubbles. Coats the spoon back evenly with no run-back. Holds a peaked mound on the fork tines with clean edges.

(c) Fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into the specimen, ruler visible. Clips: (d) 8–12 s fork-press plus spoon-tilt, continuous. specimens.fail_modes: Specimen runs continuously through the fork tines, slumps off the tilted spoon, or will not hold a mound → too thin; THICKEN. Do not re-blend and do not add water. Stir in 1.0 g thickener per 100 ml of specimen (3 g for the ≈300 g batch), rest 2 min, and re-run all three tests. Tines cut cleanly through, or the mass is stiff and will not level on the plate → too thick; thin by stirring in 10 ml hot water and re-testing. Residue on the 4 mm sieve exceeds 1 g after the second blend, or visible oat flecks remain → under-blended; blend a further 30 s and re-sieve. White liquid pools at the plate rim → syneresis; discard and re-make with a fresh batch using the same 100 g oats : 200 ml water ratio, and record the syneresis in the log.

specimens.prep: Measure 40 g rolled oats. Add 100 ml hot water (85–95 °C). Stir once, lid on, rest 3 min. Fork-mash 60 s: break the flakes down until every piece is ≤4 mm and no whole flake remains, then stop — further mashing makes paste. Do not blend. Do not sieve the batch: at L5 the flake pieces are the texture, and sieving removes them. Add no thickener at any point on this specimen: none is used and `prep.thickener_g` stays null for it (the schema carries a thickener mass only at L3). If the batch is too wet, correct it by absorbing or draining free water (see FAIL MODES) — thickener binds the free water into a gel and destroys the visibly distinct flakes that make the specimen L5, so the specimen would leave L5 and read as L4. The 4 mm sieve is a GAUGE here, not a step: press a 1 tbsp (15 g) aliquot through it and confirm the whole aliquot passes. Anything held back on the mesh is a flake piece larger than 4 mm and fails the gauge — mash longer and re-gauge on a fresh aliquot, then return the whole aliquot to the batch. Never read a partly-retained gauge as a pass and never discard the retained flakes as waste: L5 requires every piece <= 4 mm. Target yield ≈135 g, with no free water standing on a tilted plate.
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable at L5: spoon tilt (primary); fork pressure (supporting check only). No fork drip at L5 (5.3 is scoped to L3/L4); no syringe flow at L5 (5.4 is L3 only). Spoon tilt (5.2, primary): scoop 5 ml onto the spoon, tilt to 45°, hold 10 s. Pass = soft moist flakes hold a loose mound that slumps and slides only slowly, with at most a small amount of free liquid at the spoon edge, and the spoon is not swimming in separate liquid (5.2, L5). A continuous stream off the edge is L4 — fail. A puree that slides off as one cohesive mass with little residue and no visible flakes is L4, not L5 — fail; the fork-pressure check below is what separates the two. Fork pressure (supporting only): press the fork tines into the specimen on a flat plate until the thumbnail blanches. Pass = the specimen squashes completely with no spring-back, and visibly distinct soft flake pieces remain on the fork and in the plate. A smooth paste with no visible flake pieces fails.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a cohesive clump of visibly distinct soft flake pieces, none larger than 4 mm. On the spoon: no loose water in the well. On the plate: surface matte and damp, flakes evenly dispersed, no lump over 4 mm on the gauge, no pooling liquid at the edges. A surface with no visible flake pieces at all is a smooth paste — L4 — and fails L5; stop and correct per FAIL MODES before shooting.

Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines half-submerged, ruler visible. Clip 1: 8–12 s, spoon-tilt followed by fork-press, continuous take. specimens.fail_modes: Too wet / too thin: free water pools on the plate and the spoon-tilt specimen runs continuously off the edge. Correct by ABSORBING or DRAINING the free water — do NOT add thickener, which gels the free water and hides the flakes that define L5, leaving a smooth gel that reads as L4. Drain the free water off the plate, or fold 10 g dry rolled oats through the batch and rest 2 min. On a re-make, drop the water to 80 ml. Re-test spoon tilt. Too dry / crumbly: the specimen will not hold a mound on the spoon. Correct by thinning in small steps — 10 ml hot water at a time, maximum 120 ml total. No cold water. Over-mashed to a smooth paste with no visible flake pieces: fails L5. Discard and restart from oats with fork-mash only, no blender; mash only to ≤4 mm pieces. Flakes >4 mm remain: mash longer or break with the fork edge, then re-run the 4 mm gauge on a fresh 15 g aliquot and return the pass-through to the batch. Never discard the sieved flakes.

specimens.prep: Weigh 100 g crust-off white bread. Tear into ~2 cm pieces, add 120 ml room-temperature water, blend 45 s on high, stopping to scrape the bowl once. Press through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon; discard what will not pass and note the loss. Weigh the sieved puree. Add thickener at 1.5 g per 100 ml of puree (calibration starting point — record actual used). Whisk 30 s, rest 2 min, whisk 10 s. If the syringe shows outside 8-10 ml at 10 s, add 0.1 g thickener increments, rest, retest. Note the final gram value.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: hold fork horizontal 1 cm over bowl; liquid drips in slow, continuous dollops, not a stream. Fork pressure: 4 mm white groove holds clean shape after thumb press; no crumbs. Spoon tilt: pooled dollop slides slowly down the spoon when tilted, not runny. Syringe flow: fill 10 ml, release stopwatch; after 10 s the syringe retains 8-10 ml.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy, smooth, off-white puree with no visible lumps or bread crust flecks. Coats a spoon evenly with a thin even film. Holds a soft mound briefly before flattening under its own weight.
specimens.shots: 1. white_bread_L3_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, fork holding a drip in frame with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard on grey card. 2. white_bread_L3_take2.jpg — top-down of bowl plus checkerboard and ruler. 4. white_bread_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, groove visible. 5. white_bread_L3_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. 6. white_bread_L3_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI syringe flow test, timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin if puree drips in a steady stream or syringe reads under 8 ml at 10 s; add 0.1 g thickener, rest, retest. Too thick if fork cannot carve a groove or reads above 10 ml; add 5 ml water, reblend 10 s, rest, retest. Lumpy or streaky after sieving; reblend 15 s and re-sieve — do not proceed.

specimens.prep: Weigh 60 g white bread (crust off). Cut into 2 cm cubes. Add 90 ml water. Blend 30 s on high, scrape, blend 20 s more. Press 1/3 of the puree through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; remaining puree should pass without grit. Return sieved portion. Add thickener per the calibration starting point stated on the kit card (1.5 g/100 ml as starting reference) and stir 20 s; let stand 2 min. Re-weigh final specimen and record. Target: smooth, cohesive, no lumps over 4 mm.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the fork tines into the specimen until thumbnail blanches white; specimen should compress and hold together, not flow through the gaps. Fork drip test: lift fork with a heaped mound; specimen must sit in a clear mound above the tines, not drip or run off. Spoon tilt test: scoop and tilt spoon; specimen must hold its shape and slide as one lump or stay, not flow off. Pass criterion for all three: specimen remains cohesive, holds shape, shows zero separation of thin liquid.
specimens.visual_qc: Puree on spoon: matte, uniform off-white, no crust streaks or dry flecks. Fork tines after pressure: puree shears clean between tines, gaps stay open, no thin tail dripping from the underside. Surface of specimen in bowl: smooth, soft peaks that slump slowly when tapped.

specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: drips off spoon or through fork tines; re-blend with 0.5 g thickener per 50 ml and retest after 2 min stand. Lumps over 4 mm or visible crust: sieve again; if still gritty, re-blend 10 s with 10 ml extra water and re-thicken to calibration. Thin liquid separates on standing: under-thickened; add 0.5 g thickener, stir, rest 2 min, retest.

specimens.prep: Start with 30 g of crust-off white bread torn into 1 cm pieces. Place in consumer blender. Add 90 ml water (1:3 bread-to-water). Blend on high for 25 s. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using a fork to push soft pulp through; discard any coarse residue retained on mesh — if more than ~20 % of the blend stays on the sieve, the bread is too fibrous to reach L5 as a single specimen and the operator should note this and switch to a fork-mash method instead: place 30 g torn bread in a bowl, add 30 ml water, mash with fork for 60 s until a uniform coarse paste forms, then sieve to confirm ≤4 mm. L5 does not require thickener; calibration entry is "0 g/100 ml" and the operator records actual as 0.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into a heaped teaspoon of specimen on a flat plate until thumbnail blanches white. Specimen must squash completely and not spring back. Spoon tilt: tilt a spoonful 45°; specimen must hold its shape with no drip or run. Fork drip: lift fork loaded with specimen; nothing must drip through tines or off within 10 s. (Syringe flow test not required at L5.)
specimens.visual_qc: Surface looks matte and damp, never glossy or pooling. Particles on the fork are soft lumps, not crumbs, all clearly under 4 mm. A heaped teaspoon holds its mound for ≥5 s without slumping.
specimens.shots: Capture three stills: (a) 45° hero with ruler along left edge and checkerboard top-left, specimen on white plate; (b) top-down, checkerboard filling frame, specimen centred; (c) fork-press close-up mid-press, tines half-submerged. Capture two clips: (d) 8–12 s fork-press + spoon-tilt sequence; (e) IDDSI test film, fork-pressure and spoon-tilt continuous. specimens.fail_modes: Specimen is too wet: liquid pools on plate or drips from fork — return to Step 1, reduce water by 10 ml. Specimen is too dry: particles hold shape and spring back from fork pressure — add 5 ml water and re-mash. Visible lumps >4 mm after sieving: re-blend 10 s and re-sieve. Re-make from fresh bread after two failed attempts.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of white bread, crusts removed, crumb only. Cut the crumb into cubes no larger than 15 mm using the ruler as a guide. Discard any cube that exceeds 15 mm. Place cubes in a bowl and add 30 ml water per 100 g bread; stir and rest 2 minutes so the bread softens. Do not blend; do not sieve; no thickener is used at L6. Fork-mash lightly only if a cube still feels firm at the edges.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the thumb nail into a cube until the nail blanches white. The cube must squash and stay squashed — no recovery. Fork drip test is not required at L6 but record the cube holds its shape with no drip from the fork prongs. Spoon tilt is not required at L6. L3 syringe flow does not apply.
specimens.visual_qc: Cubes sit on the fork tines as distinct soft pieces, not a paste. Surface looks moist, slightly springy when touched, no dry crust visible. Size of every cube reads 15 mm or smaller against the ruler.

specimens.fail_modes: Cubes over 15 mm — re-cut and re-check against ruler. Crust left on — re-pick, crust off only. Cube springs back after thumbnail press — add 5 ml water per 100 g, rest 1 minute, retest; if still firm, discard and remake.

specimens.prep: Take the loaf as bought. Cut one slice straight from the sealed/just-opened loaf using the kitchen knife; do NOT toast, butter, soak, blend, sieve, or add thickener. Record the slice mass to 1 g on the digital scale; expect roughly 25–35 g for a standard sandwich slice. Place the slice flat on the capture board with the 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. No water, no blender, no sieve. The per-level note "slice as sold" is honoured: the reference specimen is the bread exactly as the bakery sells it.
specimens.iddsi_test: L7 is proven by appearance plus fork pressure. Fork pressure: press the fork tines firmly into the slice; the bread must NOT pass through the slots, NOT smear, and the slice must retain its original shape on lift. Spoon tilt: slide the slice onto a spoon and tilt to 90°; the slice must NOT drip, flow, or fall off. Fork drip: lift the fork with a pierced piece and hold it level for 5 s — no drips, no strands. No syringe flow test applies at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: Slice holds its full rectangular outline with intact crust edge. Crumb is matte, dry, and springy, not glossy or compressed. Fork tines leave a clean dent that rebounds partially; no paste, smear, or extrusion through the slots.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45° hero of the slice on the board, ruler + checkerboard visible. Still 2: top-down flat lay with checkerboard only. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press showing tines indenting the crumb. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt sequence. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film, both methods. Files: white_bread_L7_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-compression turning the crumb to a paste that extrudes through fork slots = fail, remake with a fresh slice and lighter press. Stale or very soft bread that slumps or drips from the tilted spoon = fail, remake from a fresh loaf. Adding any moisture or thickener = fail and remake from dry slice as sold.

specimens.prep: Weigh 120 g defrosted mantou (no crust if present). Cut into 2 cm cubes. Add to blender with 80 ml cool water. Blend 45-60 s, scraping once, until smooth. Pass through 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any residue that will not pass. Weigh the sieved purée into the capture bowl. Add thickener at the calibration starting point of 2.5 g per 100 ml of purée; whisk to a uniform lump-free consistency. Record the actual grams used. Adjust with small thickener pinches (±0.2 g) until the specimen drips slowly through fork tines.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: hold fork loaded with specimen; correct L3 drips slowly in a continuous thin stream, not a single drop and not a pour. Spoon tilt test: specimen holds its shape on a tilted spoon, mounds, then slowly sloughs; it must not run off. Fork pressure test: when fork presses on specimen surface, the tines leave a clear imprint that does not fill in quickly. IDDSI flow test (mandatory for L3): fill 10 ml syringe, cut nozzle; after 10 s the syringe must retain 8-10 ml. Pass band is 8-10 ml retained. Record retained ml.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface looks glossy and uniform, no white lumps or fibrous streaks. Holds a soft mound on the spoon without flattening or weeping. Drips from the fork tines are continuous, thin, and slow — one drip roughly every second, not a thread.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen pooled with a fork resting on the rim. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard centred, full bowl visible, ruler along one edge. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines clearly indenting the surface. Clip 1 (8-12 s): fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous shot. Clip 2: full IDDSI flow test, timer visible.
