specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: retained volume under 8 ml — add 0.2 g thickener, re-whisk, retest. Too thick: over 10 ml retained or no drip from fork — add 5 ml water, re-blend briefly, re-sieve, retest. Grainy or lumpy after sieving: re-blend 15 s and re-sieve; if residue still exceeds roughly 10% by volume, re-make from a fresh 120 g portion.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g steamed mantou, torn into ~2 cm pieces. Add 90 ml room-temperature water. Blend 60 s on high, scrape down, blend 60 s more. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard residue if any lump remains larger than a pea. Return puree to blender, add 2.0 g thickener per 100 ml of puree (calibration starting point — record actual grams used). Blend 20 s to incorporate. Rest 2 min, stir, retest. Hold warm is not required; test at ~20–25 °C.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: mound the puree on the fork tines and lift; it must sit in a mound above the tines and not drip continuously through. Fork pressure test: press the fork tines into the mound until the blanched nail shows white through the puree; the surface must not separate, no thin liquid must pool. Spoon tilt test: scoop a heaped teaspoon, tilt the spoon 45°; the specimen must hold its shape and slide off as a single mass, not flow. L4 does not use the 10 ml/10 s syringe flow test (L3 only).
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is matte and uniform, no visible lumps or bun-fibre specks. Color is even off-white, no dark streaks from crust. Holds a clean ridge when the fork is dragged across the top; does not level out.
specimens.shots: mantou_steamed_bun_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. mantou_steamed_bun_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred under specimen. mantou_steamed_bun_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, blanched nail visible. mantou_steamed_bun_L4_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous take. mantou_steamed_bun_L4_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence: fork drip, fork pressure, spoon tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen flows through fork tines or drips in a continuous thread → under-thickened, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml and re-blend. Thin liquid separates on the plate after pressure → too wet, return to blender with extra 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml. Lumps >4 mm remain after sieving, or puree cracks when the fork lifts → blend longer and sieve again before re-testing; do not proceed to media.

specimens.prep: Take 200 g thawed mantou. Cut into ~2 cm cubes. Place in blender; add 60 ml water. Blend 10 s. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard retained lumps. Weigh sieved mash. Add water 10 ml at a time until the mash holds its shape on a spoon but a light shake flows, staying within L5 — do not exceed 100 ml total added water. Stir in 1.0 g thickener per 100 ml of mash and rest 60 s. Re-mash with a fork until uniform.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test (L5 proof): press fork tines into the specimen on a plate until the thumbnail blanches white. Specimen must squash and not spring back. Pass = visible deformation, no recovery. Spoon tilt test: load 5 ml onto a spoon, tilt to full vertical. Specimen must stay on the spoon without sliding or dripping. Pass = zero drop in 10 s. Fork drip test (absence-of-thin-liquid proof): lift fork holding 5 ml above plate for 10 s. Pass = no drip falls. No syringe test required for L5.
specimens.visual_qc: Mash sits in a soft mound, not a puddle; gloss on the surface but no free liquid pooling around it; tiny pale flecks visible at the sieve grain, all clearly under 4 mm against the ruler.
specimens.shots: mantou_steamed_bun_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. mantou_steamed_bun_L5_take2.jpg — top-down on checkerboard. mantou_steamed_bun_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. mantou_steamed_bun_L5_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. mantou_steamed_bun_L5_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: Too dry: mash cracks on the spoon tilt; add 5 ml water and re-rest. Too wet: free liquid pools or drips from fork; fold in 0.5 g thickener and rest 60 s. Lumps >4 mm: re-sieve before filming.

specimens.prep: Start 200 g frozen steamed mantou, steamed per pack instructions until core reaches ambient feel. Cool 60 s. Cut a slice ~20 mm thick, then cube to ≤15 mm on the checkerboard. Sieve not used. Blender not used. No thickener added — L6 calibration point is plain. Work in batches of ~30 g cubes. If a cube exceeds 15 mm on the ruler, re-cut; do not compress it to fit.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into a cube with thumbnail pressure until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass = cube squashes, does not recover its shape when fork is removed, and does not spring back. Spoon tilt: no spoon-tilt test for L6. Fork drip: not applicable. Bite-sized check: confirm every cube ≤15 mm on the ruler; reject if any cube sits at or beyond the 15 mm line. Texture note: surface should be soft and slightly springy, not crusty, not gummy.
specimens.visual_qc: Cube holds its cut shape on the fork without slumping. Cut face shows uniform soft crumb with no hard core when pressed. Edge does not fray into strings when lifted; no liquid pools on the plate.
specimens.shots: mantou_steamed_bun_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 3–4 cubes on fork tip, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, white background. mantou_steamed_bun_L6_take2.jpg — top-down of cube array on checkerboard, ruler along one edge. mantou_steamed_bun_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail whitening visible. mantou_steamed_bun_L6_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence, audio of texture cue optional. mantou_steamed_bun_L6_take5.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full fork-pressure execution in one continuous take.
specimens.fail_modes: Cube exceeds 15 mm — re-cut, do not compress. Cube springs back fully under fork pressure (under-cooked or too dense) — re-steam 2 min, re-test. Cube crumbles to dry crumbs (over-steamed, dried out) — discard batch, start fresh pack.

specimens.prep: Remove one mantou bun from the pack. Weigh it on the digital scale; record start mass, target 60–90 g. Steam covered over briskly boiling water for 6 min — 8 min if the bun is 90 g or larger or straight from the fridge — until the core reaches 70–75 °C on a probe thermometer. Doneness is a temperature, not a softness: do NOT steam "until soft", because softness is the defect at L7, and a bun taken past a 70–75 °C core dents under the fork and fails. Rest uncovered 2 min so surface condensation flashes off. Do NOT blend. Do NOT sieve — an L7 specimen is never reduced below 15 mm. Do NOT add thickener, water, or liquid. Use the bun whole, as steamed. Record final specimen mass in grams on the capture sheet. Set aside on the plate of the capture kit and shoot within 10 min.
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable at L7: fork pressure only (§5.1). Spoon tilt (§5.2) and fork drip (§5.3) are L3–L5 tests and must not be run, filmed, or recorded as pass/fail at L7. No syringe flow test above L3 (§5.4).  Fork pressure test (primary for L7): press the tines of a standard fork into the dome of the bun with normal thumb pressure until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass = the specimen does not compress, squash, or change shape; it returns to its original shape and shows no fingernail-depth indentation and no spread under the fork, and the piece requires chewing. Fail = any dent that remains when the fork is lifted — that is an L6 texture, not L7.  Size check: with the 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, confirm every dimension of the bun is ≥15 mm (a whole bun reads ~60 mm across and ≥30 mm high); record diameter and height in mm on the capture sheet.
specimens.visual_qc: Piece holds its domed bun shape with no slumping. Surface looks evenly matte-porous, springy to the touch, no wet sheen, no liquid pooling on the plate around the specimen. The fork leaves no indentation.
specimens.shots: - mantou_steamed_bun_L7_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen untouched. - mantou_steamed_bun_L7_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard visible, full bun in frame. - mantou_steamed_bun_L7_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines fully inserted, thumbnail blanch visible. - mantou_steamed_bun_L7_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then release, spring-back visible (L7 has no spoon-tilt step). - mantou_steamed_bun_L7_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: fork pressure plus the 15 mm size check against the checkerboard, audio on, specimen label visible at start.
specimens.fail_modes: Bun dents under the fork, stays flattened, or splits instead of springing back — too tender for L7 (over-steamed, or taken past a 70–75 °C core). Correct by SHORTENING the steam: discard and re-make from a fresh bun steamed 4 min to the same 70–75 °C core, then re-test. Do NOT re-steam 2–3 min — steaming only softens the crumb further and moves the specimen away from L7; that inverted branch is closed. Bun core below 70 °C (under-steamed, doughy centre) — continue steaming in 1 min steps until the core reaches 70–75 °C, then re-test. Under-steaming is a temperature defect, not a texture defect: it never makes a bun dent. Bun surface wet from condensation or a split leaking steam: liquid pools on plate and would read as free liquid → pat surface dry with paper towel, rest 1 min, re-shoot; do not re-steam. Bun collapsed from being squeezed in pack: loses domed shape → fails visual QC. Use a fresh bun from the pack, do not reshape.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed sweet potato flesh into the blender jar. Add 120 ml cool water. Blend 45 s on high, scraping down once. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard any fibrous residue (say so in notes if sieve pass is poor — re-blend 15 s). Measure the sieved volume. Add thickener at 3.0 g per 100 ml of puree as the calibration starting point; whisk in, rest 2 min, stir, re-measure viscosity. Record the actual grams used. Target pours but drips slowly off the fork.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: a 4 mm blob on the fork blanches the thumb pad white on full press but does not spread sideways; passes. Spoon tilt: a 5 ml spoonful sits in a mounded heap and slides slowly off a tilted spoon; no run, no drip-stream. Fork drip: 5-7 slow drips in 10 s when fork is lifted from the cup. Syringe flow test: fill to 10 ml, release; 8-10 ml remain after 10 s. All four must pass; if any fail, re-adjust thickener by 0.25 g/100 ml and retest.
specimens.visual_qc: Sheen visible on the surface. No lumps, fibres, or orange flecks — colour is uniform deep orange. Coats the back of the spoon in an even, opaque film that does not run to the edge in under 2 s.
specimens.shots: steamed_sweet_potato_L3_take1.jpg hero 45° with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, both flat and unobstructed. steamed_sweet_potato_L3_take2.jpg top-down on checkerboard, specimen pooled, no shadows. steamed_sweet_potato_L3_take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press, pad visible. steamed_sweet_potato_L3_take1.mp4 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. steamed_sweet_potato_L3_take2.mp4 IDDSI syringe test, timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: drips in a stream or syringe drops below 8 ml — add thickener 0.25 g/100 ml, rest, retest. Too stiff: fork-pressure spreads sideways or syringe holds more than 10 ml — add 5 ml water, re-whisk, retest. Lumpy or fibrous: sieve fails to clear — re-blend 15 s, sieve again; if still failing, record and start over. One re-make permitted.

specimens.prep: Weigh 300 g steamed sweet potato flesh on the digital scale. Load into the consumer blender; blend 25-30 s, scrape down, blend another 15-20 s until glossy. Pass through the 4 mm sieve with a spatula, discarding residue; re-weigh puree. Add water back at roughly 1 ml per 5 g puree lost to fibre to restore mouthfeel — record exact ml. L4 requires no thickener; if the puree slumps below the spoon-tilt line, dust 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml puree, blend 5 s, re-test, and log the actual figure used. Re-weigh final specimen.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a fork-tine-full 5 cm above the surface — puree must mound and drop as a single piece, not drip continuously. Fork pressure: press tines into a 1.5 cm mound on a flat plate; puree should flatten and leave a clear dent, not split or run. Spoon tilt: scoop, tilt spoon 45° — puree holds in the bowl, slides as one clump, no separate liquid pools. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform deep orange, no fibre streaks or dark specks; matte-sheen surface, not glossy or weeping; clings to the spoon without tailing.
specimens.shots: steamed_sweet_potato_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. steamed_sweet_potato_L4_take1.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. steamed_sweet_potato_L4_take1.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press. steamed_sweet_potato_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. steamed_sweet_potato_L4_take1.mp4 — full IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: Weeping thin liquid onto the plate — under-blended or over-watered; re-blend 10 s, sieve again. Puree runs through the fork tines — too thin; add 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml, re-test. Lumpy with visible fibre — under-sieved; re-sieve or blend longer.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g steamed sweet potato flesh on the scale. Hand-mash with a fork to coarse crumb. Pulse in the consumer blender for 5-8 s only, to break down any lump larger than 4 mm. Do not blend to a smooth purée; the per-level note requires visible lumps up to 4 mm, and a smooth purée is L4. Sieving at L5 is a GAUGE, not a production step: take a 20 g sample of the mash and press it against the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon — the sample must pass through with light pressure, which confirms no lump exceeds 4 mm. Any material retained on the mesh is an oversized lump: lift it off, hand-mash it with the fork, and re-gauge. Never blend the batch to force it through the mesh, and never discard the whole mash to remove fibre. Weigh the sieved... [gauge only] mash; sprinkle thickener at 0.5 g per 100 g mash, folding in — this is a binder for free moisture only and must not be increased to fill gaps, which would smooth the specimen toward L4. Add 10-15 ml hot water per 100 g until the mash coheres when pressed but still looks moist. Hold for 60 s before testing. Record actual grams of thickener and water used on the data sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon-tilt test (the required test at L5): load a heaped teaspoon and tilt to 45°; the specimen must sit in a cohesive pile and not slide, drip, or fall off the spoon. Fork-pressure test (supporting check only at L5, not a required test): press the fork tines into the specimen on a flat plate; the sample should squash, the tines should leave a clear imprint, and the material should not spring back — a specimen that fails this while passing spoon-tilt is still L5 and must not be rejected on fork pressure alone. No fork-drip test at L5: fork-drip applies at L3 and L4 only. No syringe flow test at L5: syringe flow applies to L3 only.
specimens.visual_qc: Coarse crumbs up to 4 mm clearly visible in the mound, sized against the 4 mm sieve holes and the 15 mm checkerboard; surface glistens with moisture but no free liquid pools around the mound on the plate; the pile holds its shape when the fork is withdrawn, leaving distinct tine marks.
specimens.shots: still_1 hero 45°: plate centred, 100 mm ruler left edge, 15 mm checkerboard top-right, whole specimen in focus, label card reading "steamed sweet_potato L5" in frame. still_2 top-down: checkerboard fills frame, specimen mound centred, coarse crumbs resolvable. still_3 fork-press macro (supporting check): tines mid-press into the specimen, ruler tip visible for scale. clip_1 10 s: fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous take. clip_2 10-15 s: full IDDSI test sequence for L5 — spoon-tilt, with fork-press as the supporting check — no cuts. Files: steamed_sweet_potato_L5_take1.jpg and .mp4 for each.
specimens.fail_modes: (a) Over-blended to a smooth purée — fails spoon-tilt by spreading and sliding off the tilted spoon, i.e. it reads L4; remake with a fresh 250 g portion, hand-mash to coarse crumb and pulse 5-8 s only, then gauge with the 4 mm sieve. (b) Too dry, crumbs do not cohere, fall off the tilted spoon — add 5 ml water per 100 g and rest 60 s before re-testing. (c) Excess liquid pools on the plate, indicating the specimen is too thin (L4 or lower) — fold in 0.2 g thickener per 100 g, rest 60 s, re-test.

specimens.prep: Take 200 g peeled steamed sweet potato. Cut into cubes that fit a 15 mm checkerboard square — none may exceed 15 mm on any side. Do not blend; do not sieve; do not add thickener or liquid. L6 requires discrete bite-sized pieces, so any pureeing step would destroy the specimen. Keep pieces covered so they do not form a dry skin before capture.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines firmly against one cube until thumbnail blanches white. The piece must squash, not spring back, and stay squashed. Spoon tilt is not required for L6. Fork drip test: lift a piece on the fork; no liquid should run through or drip from the tines. No syringe flow test applies at L6.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork the cube should hold a clean cube shape with rounded, slightly fibrous edges and an even orange color. No surface gloss from added liquid, no crumbs, no pieces larger than the 15 mm checkerboard square.
specimens.shots: 1. steamed_sweet_potato_L6_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame beside the pile. 2. steamed_sweet_potato_L6_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only, full bed of cubes visible. 3. steamed_sweet_potato_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press on one cube, nail blanch visible. 4. steamed_sweet_potato_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt clip. 5. steamed_sweet_potato_L6_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, fork press then fork drip.
specimens.fail_modes: Piece exceeds 15 mm: re-cut and re-shoot. Cube springs back under fork pressure and thumbnail does not blanch: sweet potato is under-steamed; re-steam 3–5 min and retest. Surface wet or liquid pools under the pile: too much condensate; pat dry with paper, re-shoot.

specimens.prep: Take 200 g steamed sweet potato wedge as it comes from the steamer — no peeling, no cutting smaller than the served wedge, no blending, no sieving, no water, no thickener. Place the wedge intact on the plate. Record the actual mass on the scale and the actual piece dimensions against the 100 mm ruler. The per-level note requires "wedge as steamed"; do not mash, chop, or process. If a single wedge is smaller than 30 mm at its widest, flag it and substitute a larger wedge from the same batch.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork tines fully into the wedge until the tines bend or the wedge breaks cleanly under thumb pressure. Pass = wedge breaks, splinters, or deforms with effort; the fork does NOT sink freely.  Fork drip: lift the wedge on the fork and hold over the plate for 5 seconds. Pass = no continuous drip, no slumping, no strands falling.  Spoon tilt: not applicable as a primary L7 test for a rigid wedge; if any soft interior squeezes out, it must hold on the spoon without flowing.  No flow test, no drip test beyond the above — L7 is established by hardness, not by flow.
specimens.visual_qc: Wedge holds its original steamed shape with intact edges; skin-on or skin-off surface intact, not collapsed. Surface is matte-moist, not wet or glossy with free liquid. Fork tines leave a clear indent, not a clean cut-through.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame, wedge untouched. steamed_sweet_potato_L7_take1.jpg Still 2: top-down on checkerboard, ruler alongside. steamed_sweet_potato_L7_take2.jpg Still 3: fork-press close-up, tines mid-indent into the wedge. steamed_sweet_potato_L7_take3.jpg Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press action, audible snap or splinter if present. steamed_sweet_potato_L7_take1.mp4 Clip 2: IDDSI test film — fork press, lift, hold, full pass sequence. steamed_sweet_potato_L7_take2.mp4
specimens.fail_modes: Wedge is over-steamed and the fork sinks through with light pressure → re-make from a less-steamed batch, record new steam time. Wedge has free surface moisture pooling on the plate → pat surface dry with paper, re-shoot. Wedge arrives pre-mashed or broken → reject piece, select an intact wedge of similar mass.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g steamed taro into the blender jar. Add 80 ml water. Blend on high for 45 s, stopping to scrape the walls once. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve, pressing with the back of a ladle; discard residue. Measure the volume of sieved purée in a jug and record it (target ~300 ml). Stir in thickener at 1.5 g per 100 ml of measured purée (grams = 1.5 × measured ml / 100) as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Stir for 30 s, rest 60 s, stir 10 s. Calibrate against the pass window, not against appearance: if the purée pours freely in a fast stream or <8 ml remains in the syringe, add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml and re-stir; if it drops off the fork as a lump or holds a mound on the 30° spoon, whisk in 5 ml water per 100 ml. Record the final figure. Sieving is mandatory; coarser taro fibres will collapse the syringe reading.
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable tests at L3 (CAPTURE_PROTOCOL §5.2, §5.3, §5.4): spoon tilt, fork drip, 10 ml syringe flow. All three must pass. Fork pressure is not an L3 test — do not run it, do not film it, and do not use its "no flow-back within 5 s" criterion to decide anything. Fork drip: hold fork vertically 50 mm above an empty spoon; correct specimen flows in slow drips — a fine thread or separate drops — not a stream and not a lump drop. Spoon tilt: tilt a heaped teaspoon 30°; specimen slides off slowly in a single ribbon, leaves a thin film. Pass when it flows slowly; a ribbon or slow trail IS the L3 pass. Fail if it pours freely and fast (too thin) or sits in a mound that does not move (too thick). Flow test: fill the 10 ml syringe, release for 10 s; pass when 8-10 ml remains in the barrel.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is glossy and smooth, no visible fibre or specks. Drips slowly through the fork tines in a fine thread with no lump drop — it must not hang as a curtain. Coats the back of the spoon evenly, masking the metal, and slides off in a slow ribbon.
specimens.shots: steamed_taro_L3_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, spoon half-tilted. steamed_taro_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, ruler along one edge. steamed_taro_L3_take3.jpg — fork-drip close-up, fork held 50 mm above the spoon, thread and drops in frame. steamed_taro_L3_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-drip then spoon-tilt, audio-free. steamed_taro_L3_take5.mp4 — IDDSI syringe flow test, full 10 s timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny (too thin): drip streams off the fork in a fast pour, or <8 ml remains in the syringe — add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 60 s, retest. Too thick: drops as a lump, holds a mound on the 30° spoon, or >10 ml remains in the syringe — whisk in 5 ml water per 100 ml, rest, retest. Lumpy after blending: sieve failed — re-blend 15 s and re-sieve; do not photograph. If the specimen still will not sit inside the 8-10 ml window after two thickener steps (total ≤2.0 g per 100 ml added), remake from a fresh batch rather than chasing the syringe window with more thickener — that is how an L3 becomes an L4.

specimens.prep: Peel and steam 300 g fresh taro until fork-tender (~20 min). Cube into ~2 cm pieces, add 60 ml warm water. Blend in the consumer blender on high for 45-60 s until smooth. Stop and scrape the wall at 30 s if needed. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard fibrous residue retained on the sieve. Weigh the dry sieve before first use and record its tare mass on the capture sheet, so retained residue can be weighed rather than estimated by eye. The target consistency is a soft mound, not a pourable puree. Do NOT add thickener at this stage — L4 taro holds shape from its own starch. If the mound slumps after sieving, measure the puree volume in a jug to the nearest 10 ml first, then work in 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml of that measured volume, blend 10 s, and re-test.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: mound on the fork sits in a clear pile above the tines, does not drip or run through gaps — pass. Fork pressure: pressing the fork tines into the specimen leaves a clear indentation that does not bounce back fully; the surface cracks slightly — pass. Spoon tilt: a heaped spoonful holds its shape when the spoon is tilted 45 degrees and does not slide off in under 10 s — pass. Fork drip (tine-gap form): no puree flows through the 4 mm tine gaps when the loaded fork is lifted and held 5 s — pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Matte surface, no wet sheen. Uniform pale lavender-grey colour with no purple flecks. A peak stays where the spoon drops it.
specimens.shots: Stills — steamed_taro_L4_take1.jpg: 45-degree hero, fork holding mound, ruler and checkerboard in lower third; steamed_taro_L4_take2.jpg: top-down on white plate, checkerboard centred under specimen; steamed_taro_L4_take3.jpg: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines 5 mm into puree. Clips — steamed_taro_L4_take1.mp4: 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence; steamed_taro_L4_take2.mp4: full IDDSI test film, all three tests in one continuous take.
specimens.fail_modes: Too wet: puree flows through fork gaps or drips — re-blend 10 s; if still wet, measure the puree volume and add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml of measured volume, then re-test. Too stiff: fork cracks the mound cleanly with no give — add 10 ml water per 200 g of puree (15 ml for a ~300 g batch), blend 10 s, re-test. If it is still too stiff after 30 ml total added water, re-prep rather than keep thinning. Lumpy: purple fibre strands visible — re-blend 20 s and re-sieve through the 4 mm sieve. Weigh sieve plus residue and subtract the recorded tare: retained residue must be ≤15 g (5% of the 300 g starting weight). If it is still above 15 g after that second pass, the batch fails — re-prep with a 25 min steam and a longer blend.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g steamed taro on the digital scale. Place in bowl and mash with a fork to a coarse, moist mash that still shows discernible 2-4 mm lumps throughout — do NOT mash it "until uniform": a uniform mash is the L4 puree, and at L5 the 2-4 mm lumps ARE the specimen. Pick out individually the woody core strands that will not mash — this is inedible-core removal, not a particle-size step. Re-weigh the mashable material, target 200 g. SIEVE AS GAUGE ONLY, AND IT IS A TWO-SIDED GAUGE: scoop one 15 g sample and press it through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon. (a) The sample must pass under light-to-moderate pressure, so no particle is over 4 mm. (b) Visible 2-4 mm lumps must be left on the mesh: a sample that passes clean with nothing retained means the mash has gone smooth and the specimen is L4, not L5 — stop and correct per FAIL MODES before shooting. Do NOT press the whole batch through the sieve and do NOT discard the retained material — at L5 the 2-4 mm lumps are the specimen. Add 20 ml warm water and thickener at 2.0 g per 100 g of mash (4.0 g for a 200 g batch), sprinkling it in while stirring; record actual water (ml) and thickener (g) used. Rest 60 s, stir again. If any piece fails the fork-pressure check, re-mash 30 s and re-gauge.
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon tilt (primary, L5, 5.2): load a teaspoon, tilt to 45 degrees. Pass = soft moist particles hold a loose mound that slumps rather than pours, and the spoon is not swimming in separate liquid (5.2, L5). A continuous stream off the spoon is L4 — fail. A puree that holds a peaked shape and slides off as one cohesive mass with little residue is L4, not L5 — fail. Fork pressure (5.1 — the supporting check for L5, and here the L5/L4 discriminator): press the fork bowl into the specimen on a flat plate with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white, then lift. Pass = the specimen squashes with no spring-back and visibly distinct 2-4 mm lumps remain on the fork and on the plate. A smear with no visible lumps is an L4 puree — fail. Fork drip and syringe flow are not applicable at L5; do not record them.
specimens.visual_qc: On fork tines: uniformly tan-purple paste with discernible 2-4 mm lumps throughout and no lump above 4 mm, slight surface sheen from added moisture. On spoon: a loose mound of soft moist particles that slumps when the spoon tilts, not a peaked puree that holds its shape. No free liquid pooling at the rim of the plate. If the surface reads completely smooth with no lump you can see or feel, the batch has gone to L4 — stop, and correct per FAIL MODES before shooting.
specimens.shots: Capture three stills and two clips onto A4 kit with 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler visible. - steamed_taro_L5_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler+checkerboard in frame. - steamed_taro_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard flat. - steamed_taro_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. - steamed_taro_L5_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s spoon-tilt then fork-press sequence. - steamed_taro_L5_take5.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full protocol continuous.
specimens.fail_modes: Batch has gone lump-free and smooth (reads as L4): it was over-worked or over-sieved. Weigh out a further 50 g steamed taro, mash it coarsely with the back of a fork, fold it through the batch, and re-gauge. Never sieve to correct this — sieving removes exactly the lumps that make the specimen L5. Woody core strands left intact: pick them out individually. Spot-picking inedible core is correct here; do not re-sieve the whole batch, which would also strip the L5 lumps. Gauge sample will not pass the 4 mm sieve (side (a) fails): mash a further 30 s only and re-gauge once. If it still will not pass, the batch is too coarse for L5 — discard and record. Do NOT keep mashing to force the gauge: two or more long mashes destroy the 2-4 mm lumps and hand back the L4 puree this batch must not become. Too dry, specimen cracks under fork instead of squashing: add 5 ml water at a time, re-test, cap at 40 ml total. Too wet, free liquid pools at the plate rim: sprinkle thickener at 0.5 g per 100 g of mash (1.0 g for a 200 g batch), rest 60 s, re-test, cap total thickener at 3.0 g per 100 g. Never exceed the cap to clear pooling liquid: over-thickened taro stops reading as moist particles and reads as a cohesive paste — L4 — which fails VISUAL QC. Any fail after two remakes, discard batch and record.

specimens.prep: Start with 250 g steamed taro. Cut into 15 mm cubes with a knife and ruler check; reject any cube above 15 mm. Do not blend. Do not sieve. Do not add thickener or liquid — L6 pieces must hold shape under fork pressure, and liquid would mask the failure mode we are capturing. Do not mash, rice, or pulse. Keep cubes whole. Portion 8–10 cubes (≈60–80 g) onto the fork for the press test; keep remainder on plate for hero and top-down stills. If any cube exceeds 15 mm after cutting, re-trim before capture.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the tines into a cube with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass: cube squashes, breaks apart, does not return to original shape. Cube must break under thumbnail pressure, not just dent. Size check: all cubes measure ≤15 mm on the ruler — any cube above is a fail. Spoon tilt is not the gate test for L6 but perform it on a single cube to confirm the piece does not flow; it should sit and slide, not pour. Fork drip is not applicable — pieces do not drip.
specimens.visual_qc: Cube edges are soft, slightly rounded, no crisp raw-looking corners. Surface looks moist but not wet or pooled with liquid. Colour is even pale lavender-grey with no dark firm core visible at the cut face. Cube compresses visibly under fork with no spring-back.
specimens.shots: Three stills: steamed_taro_L6_take1.jpg hero at 45° with ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; steamed_taro_L6_take2.jpg top-down with checkerboard; steamed_taro_L6_take3.jpg fork-press close-up at mid-press. Two clips: steamed_taro_L6_take1.mp4 fork-press 8–12 s showing squash and non-recovery; steamed_taro_L6_take2.mp4 full IDDSI test 8–12 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Cube exceeds 15 mm — re-trim and reshoot. Cube springs back under thumbnail — pieces under-steamed, re-steam 5 min and reshoot. Cube crumbles to paste before pressure — over-steamed, cut from a fresh batch at 12 min steam.

specimens.prep: Do not blend, sieve, or add liquid. Take a wedge of steamed taro as it comes from the steamer, approximately 50 g. Record the exact starting weight on the capture sheet. Cut or break one wedge into a piece roughly 30 mm × 30 mm × 20 mm for the fork-press test; keep a second wedge whole for the reference specimen. Confirm the taro is tender enough to cut cleanly with a fork — no further processing. No thickener. No sieve.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: place the taro piece on a flat plate, press the fork tines flat onto it until the tines blanch fully white. The taro must squash, change shape, and not return to its original form — it does not need to pass through the gaps. Fork drip: lift the fork; nothing drips or runs off. Spoon tilt: tilt a spoon holding a small portion 45 degrees; the piece sits on the spoon without flowing or dripping. L7 = soft, moldable, holds shape; not pourable, not sticky-pasty. No syringe test applies.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface looks matte and slightly moist, not wet or glossy. Edges of the cut wedge are clean, no stringy fibers or pooling liquid around the piece. When squashed under the fork, the taro shows a smooth, even mash with no hard lumps or skin fragments.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, whole wedge on plate, ruler and checkerboard in frame. Still 2: top-down of the same wedge, checkerboard only. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines blanched, taro deforming. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt sequence. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film. Files: steamed_taro_L7_take1.jpg, steamed_taro_L7_take1.mp4, plus takes 2–3.
specimens.fail_modes: Under-steamed taro resists fork pressure and stays springy — re-steam 3–5 min, do not blend. Over-wet wedge pools liquid on the plate — pat dry with paper, not pressed out; if taro is waterlogged, reject and re-steam a fresh wedge. Taro breaks into dry crumbs instead of squashing smoothly — record as borderline; re-make one batch before tagging L7.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed pumpkin flesh, no skin or seeds. Add 60 ml water. Blend 30 s on high. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard residue. Measure the sieved volume. Add thickener at 2 g per 100 ml of puree as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Stir 15 s, rest 60 s. If the slurry is too runny, add thickener 0.2 g at a time; if too stiff, add water 5 ml at a time. The puree must pour in a slow ribbon and drip through the fork tines in 1-2 s drops.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: the slurry drops in 1-2 second drips through the tine gaps, not a continuous stream. Spoon tilt: a 5 ml spoonful slides off a tilted spoon within 2-4 s, leaving a thin coating. Fork pressure: light thumb press on the spoon-blade leaves a clear dent that does not refill quickly; no crumb break. Syringe flow test: fill to 10 ml, release 10 s; 8-10 ml remains in the barrel. Pass only if all four match.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork tines, the slurry hangs as a glossy, uniform orange ribbon with no fibre streaks or lumps. On the spoon, it levels flat with no peaks and no free liquid pooling at the edges. Colour stays steady pumpkin orange; no pale water rings.
specimens.shots: Still 1, steamed_pumpkin_L3_take1.jpg: 45-degree hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame alongside the specimen cup. Still 2, steamed_pumpkin_L3_take1.jpg: top-down with checkerboard centred under the cup. Still 3, steamed_pumpkin_L3_take1.jpg: fork-press close-up at mid-press on the spoon. Clip 1, steamed_pumpkin_L3_take1.mp4: 8-12 s fork-press plus spoon-tilt. Clip 2, steamed_pumpkin_L3_take1.mp4: the full IDDSI syringe flow test, timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin, runs through tines in a stream or leaves under 8 ml in the syringe: whisk in thickener 0.2 g per 100 ml and retest. Too thick, sits in a blob on the spoon or leaves over 10 ml: whisk in 5 ml water per 100 ml and retest. Grainy or fibrous after sieving: re-blend 10 s and re-sieve.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed pumpkin flesh. Blend 45 s on high until smooth. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard residue. Weigh the sieved purée; add 5 g thickener per 100 ml of purée (record the actual grams used). Stir 30 s, rest 60 s, stir 10 s. No water added.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the tines into the mound on the spoon. Pass criterion — the purée keeps a clear thumb-nail print but does not split or run. Spoon tilt test: tilt the spoon. Pass criterion — the mound sits, no drip, no slide. Fork drip test: lift the fork loaded with purée. Pass criterion — purée mounds above the tines and falls as one piece or sits; nothing drips through the gaps. L4 requires all three.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: matte surface, no liquid pooling at the rim, no skin or fibre flecks. On the fork after lift: a single soft clump sitting above the tines, tines still visible underneath.
specimens.shots: steamed_pumpkin_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. steamed_pumpkin_L4_take2.jpg — top-down on checkerboard. steamed_pumpkin_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. steamed_pumpkin_L4_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt. steamed_pumpkin_L4_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: Runny — purée flows through fork gaps or drips from a tilted spoon: re-blend 10 s with +2 g thickener per 100 ml, retest. Rubbery — fork leaves no mark: discard, re-blend fresh batch, halve thickener to 2.5 g per 100 ml. Stringy with orange flecks — sieve was skipped or rushed: discard, re-sieve the same batch, retest.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g steamed pumpkin flesh onto the plate. Mash thoroughly with a fork until uniform; press and drag to break every lump. Sieve one fork-load at a time through the 4 mm sieve, discarding or re-mashing any residue that sits on top of the mesh — repeat until the whole portion passes. Do not add water, milk, or thickener; the per-level note states the food is moist as-is. The blender is not used. Target specimen: ~250 g of moist mash with all particles ≤ 4 mm and no free liquid pooling on the plate.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines into the specimen until the tines blanch white, hold 1 s, then lift. Pass: the squash mark remains, the food does not spring back or recover its shape, and the tines do not slide through loose liquid. Spoon-tilt test: load a heaped teaspoon, invert it over the plate until the spoon is near-vertical. Pass: the specimen sits in a cohesive clump, holds together for several seconds, may slide slowly, and does not pour or drip. Fork-drip test: lift a fork-load 10 cm above the plate. Pass: very little to no drip falls; any that does is drops, not a stream.
specimens.visual_qc: Mash sits on the spoon as a soft, damp mound with no sheen of free liquid around the base. Colour is uniform orange with no pale chunks. Fork-tine marks are visible on the surface, confirming softness.
specimens.shots: steam_pumpkin_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard visible. steam_pumpkin_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. steam_pumpkin_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press, squash mark visible. steam_pumpkin_L5_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, no cuts. steam_pumpkin_L5_take5.mp4 — continuous IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: Lumps ≥ 4 mm sitting on the sieve — re-mash, re-sieve, retest. Pooling of thin liquid on the plate — drain briefly; do not add thickener, re-mash and retest. Springy recovery after fork press — specimen too firm or fibrous, re-mash finer. If any fail persists after one re-make, record the failure and stop.

specimens.prep: Cube steamed pumpkin flesh into 15 mm squares on the checkerboard grid; reject any cube that exceeds 15 mm in any axis. Weigh 150 g of in-spec cubes on the scale. No blender, no sieve, no thickener, no added water. Fork-pressure-check three random cubes against the thumbnail blanch criterion before shooting; if any cube does not blanch, re-steam the batch for 60 s and recube.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork tines onto a cube with thumbnail-grade force; the cube must squash and not recover, and the thumbnail must blanch white. Spoon tilt: a single cube on a spoon must not flow, slide, or drip when the spoon is tilted to 45 degrees. Fork drip: lift the fork with a cube on it; no liquid must drip through the tines within 10 s. All three are required to pass. (No syringe test; L6 does not use it.)
specimens.visual_qc: Cube holds a clean 15 mm edge with no crumble halo on the plate. Surface looks moist but not wet; no free liquid pools next to the cube. Pressing the fork leaves a visible mash without splatter.
specimens.shots: still_hero_45deg.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. still_topdown.jpg — top-down on checkerboard, cubes spaced. still_forkpress.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. clip_forkpress_spoontilt.mp4 — 8-12 s, fork press plus spoon tilt on one cube. clip_iddsi_test.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, all three checks. Rename takes as steamed_pumpkin_L6_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Cube exceeds 15 mm after cutting → recube, do not shoot. Cube rebounds after fork press (under-steamed) → re-steam 60 s, recube, recheck. Cube smears to liquid (over-steamed to puree) → discard batch, start over with a firmer pumpkin.

specimens.prep: Open capture kit. Confirm 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard are clean and within frame guides. Zero the digital scale with the empty specimen plate. Steam one pumpkin wedge 12–15 min, until a fork tip enters the flesh with light resistance and the wedge still holds a clean edge; drain 2 min on the tray. Weigh out a representative wedge of steamed pumpkin, 80–120 g, as normally served; do not blend, do not sieve, do not add water or thickener. The per-level note directs a wedge as steamed, so preserve skin and flesh geometry intact. Cut the wedge so that its smallest dimension is at least 15 mm, and read it against the 100 mm ruler before it goes on the plate — a wedge thinner than 15 mm is an L6 specimen, not L7. Place the wedge on the white plate, set the ruler along the lower edge and the checkerboard in the upper corner. Calibration starting point: none — this is an unprocessed reference specimen, so the only recorded value is the starting mass of the wedge before any handling.
specimens.iddsi_test: Run the fork-pressure test only (protocol 5.1). The spoon-tilt, fork-drip and syringe-flow tests do not apply at L7 — do not film them as evidence for this specimen. Fork pressure: place the wedge on the plate, press the bowl of the fork down onto it with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white, then lift. Pass when the wedge squashes readily under that pressure and does not recover its shape. In the same take, hold the wedge against the 100 mm ruler and read it on camera: every dimension must measure >= 15 mm. The fork-pressure result alone cannot separate L6 from L7 — the ruler read does, and both must hold. A wedge that mashes to a puree with no piece structure left, or one that measures under 15 mm, is not an L7 result.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: intact wedge geometry, matte orange flesh, defined skin edge, no pool of free liquid at the plate. On the ruler: the wedge reads >= 15 mm in every dimension against the 100 mm scale. Color uniform steamed-orange, no grey or raw patches.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame, full wedge centered. Still 2 — top-down, checkerboard visible, ruler along one edge. Still 3 — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail blanching visible. Clip 1 — 8–12 s fork press with the ruler sizing read in the same take. Clip 2 — IDDSI test film, the fork-pressure test unbroken, with voiceover noting pass/fail. Files: steamed_pumpkin_L7_take1.jpg / .mp4 for each; increment take number on re-makes.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-steamed wedge collapses to mash under the fork — fails L7; re-make with a shorter steam (10 min) and re-shoot. Wedge does not squash and springs back under thumbnail pressure — fails; re-steam 60 s and re-shoot, do not blend. Wedge reads under 15 mm in any axis — that is an L6 specimen; cut a larger wedge from the same batch or mark the cell FAIL, and never submit it as L7. Free liquid weeps onto the plate — pat the surface dry with paper towel and re-shoot, recording the observation; if the wedge itself is exuding liquid, re-make with a shorter steam. Fork splits the wedge cleanly into crumbs — re-make from a fresh wedge at the pinned 12–15 min steam; a crumbly wedge is a dry or stale pumpkin, not an under-steamed one. If the wedge mashes to puree even at the shortest edible steam, this batch has no honest L7 form — mark FAIL and skip the cell rather than submit an L6 wedge. Each fail requires a new take number.

specimens.prep: Bought form: 200 g fresh (or fully thawed frozen) skinless, boneless white-fish fillet — cod, sea bass or similar firm white fish — as sold, unbreaded and unmarinated. Allergen: FISH; the specimen itself is the allergen, so do not substitute a non-fish protein. Lay the fillet in a shallow heatproof dish and steam over a rolling boil, covered, for 10 min; the flesh must flake and show no translucency. Cool 2 min. Tip the fish and any released liquid into the blender, add 80 ml cold water, and blend 45 s on high, scraping the wall once at 20 s. Pass through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon and discard the retained fibres and skin so the purée is lump-free. Weigh the sieved purée (expect 220–250 g). Add thickener (modified maize starch or equivalent) at 2.0 g per 100 g of purée as the calibration start; stir 20 s, rest 60 s, stir 10 s, then run the syringe test. If less than 8 ml remains, add a further 0.3 g per 100 g, stir 20 s, rest 60 s and retest, up to a ceiling of 3.0 g per 100 g. Record the actual grams used.
specimens.iddsi_test: - 5.4 Syringe flow — ACTIVE, the deciding L3 test. Fill the IDDSI 10 ml syringe to the 10 ml mark, release, and time 10 s. Pass = 8–10 ml remains in the barrel. - 5.2 Spoon tilt — ACTIVE. Place a level 5 ml scoop on a spoon and tilt to 45°. Pass = the purée slides off slowly in one mass over about 2–4 s and coats the spoon; it must not pour instantly and must not sit unmoved. - 5.3 Fork drip — ACTIVE. Lift a fork from the purée. Pass = the purée drips slowly in thin streams or single drops through the tines — not a continuous sheet, and not a mound that will not drip at all. - 5.1 Fork pressure — skip: fork pressure is a Level 4/6/7 test (supporting check at L5 only) and has no pass criterion for a Level 3 liquid; do not use it to accept or reject this specimen. All three active tests must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform pale ivory, glossy and completely smooth — no flakes, no dark specks, nothing catching the spoon. Coats the back of a spoon in an even layer with no bare streaks. A line drawn through the surface with the back of a spoon levels out within 3–5 s. No standing liquid separates from the mound on the plate.

Still 2: bf11_steamed_fish_fillet_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, bowl centred, checkerboard full frame. specimens.fail_modes: Too thin — syringe empties below 8 ml at 10 s, or the purée pours off the spoon in under 2 s: add 0.3 g thickener per 100 g, stir 20 s, rest 60 s, retest (ceiling 3.0 g per 100 g). Too thick — the syringe has not moved at 10 s, or the purée sits as a mound that will not slide off the spoon: add 5 ml water per 100 g, blend 10 s, retest. Grainy or flaky, or dark specks visible after sieving: re-blend 20 s and sieve once more; if still not smooth, discard and re-make from a fresh 200 g fillet. Any specimen failing two consecutive tests is discarded and the batch remade.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g steamed fish fillet on the digital scale. Add to consumer blender with 60 ml warm water. Blend 45 s, scrape down, blend 30 s more. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any residue remaining in the sieve. Return puree to blender, add thickener at the calibration starting point of 3 g per 100 ml, blend 20 s to incorporate. Rest 60 s, then stir. Record the actual thickener mass used. Final specimen should weigh approximately 210 g. Per-level note is respected: blend then hold on spoon.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press fork tines into the specimen on a flat plate with firm thumb pressure; surface must retain a clear dent, no full recovery, and must not push through the gaps. Pass = visible dent, holds shape.  Fork drip test: lift fork with a loaded mound; specimen must sit in a mound above the tines for 5 s with zero drip. Pass = zero drip.  Spoon tilt test: scoop a heaped teaspoon and tilt to full vertical; specimen must stay on the spoon with no sliding or run-off. Pass = no flow.
specimens.visual_qc: Mound sits cleanly above fork tines with sharp edges, glossy but matte (no pooled shine), and a single uniform cream-white color with no flakes, fibers, or separated liquid around the base.
specimens.shots: still_1: 45-degree hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame. steamed_fish_fillet_L4_take1.jpg still_2: top-down with checkerboard centered under specimen. steamed_fish_fillet_L4_take2.jpg still_3: fork-press close-up mid-press, dent visible. steamed_fish_fillet_L4_take3.jpg clip_1: 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. steamed_fish_fillet_L4_take1.mp4 clip_2: full IDDSI test film, fork drip + spoon tilt + pressure, continuous. steamed_fish_fillet_L4_take2.mp4
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: drips through fork tines or runs off spoon tilt. Re-make: add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, blend, retest.  Grainy or lumpy: visible fibers, flakes, or sieve residue in puree. Re-make: re-sieve or blend an extra 20 s with 10 ml extra water, then re-thicken.  Separate thin liquid pooling around specimen: insufficient hydration or thickener. Re-make: blend 10 s, rest 2 min, stir, retest.

specimens.prep: Weigh 180 g steamed fish fillet. Break into chunks on a board. Pulse in the consumer blender 6 s, scrape, pulse 4 s more. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using a spoon; discard what stays behind; record retained mass. Weigh the sieved mince. Whisk 1.5 g thickener into 30 ml warm fish broth (calibration starting point; record actual grams per 100 ml on the data sheet). Stir the thickened broth into the mince until it binds and looks glossy-wet, not soupy. Re-weigh final specimen. If it slumps to a puddle, add 0.3 g thickener per 100 g and re-mix.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the specimen until thumbnail blanches; on release the slot holds, no recovery. Pass = visible slot, fish does not spring back. Fork drip: hold fork with 1 cm of specimen above a plate for 5 s. Pass = at most a trace drop, no continuous drip. Spoon tilt: scoop, tilt spoon 30 degrees. Pass = specimen sits as a cohesive mound, slides only as a whole. Fork-drip and spoon-tilt together confirm no separate thin liquid.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a soft mound of pale flecks, every piece smaller than a peppercorn. Glossy surface, no pooling broth on the plate beside it. Holds the fork-print shape for at least 5 s.
specimens.shots: steamed_fish_fillet_L5_take1.jpg hero 45-degree, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; take2.jpg top-down, checkerboard only; take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press. steamed_fish_fillet_L5_take1.mp4 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt; take2.mp4 IDDSI test film, single continuous take, specimen ID visible at start.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen too wet, broth pools within 5 s: add 0.3 g thickener per 100 g, re-test. Visible pieces above 4 mm after sieving: re-blend 4 s and re-sieve. Spring-back on fork test, indicates L6 texture: add 5 ml broth per 100 g and re-test once; if it still springs back, re-cut smaller and re-sieve.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed fish fillet. Flake against the grain into pieces no larger than 15 mm using fork and knife; do not blend — blending turns fish to paste and is incompatible with L6. Inspect every flake for bones; discard any piece containing bone. Hold pieces on a plate, do not sieve, do not add thickener, do not add water. Record starting mass on the scale log. Forks and spoon must be dry.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure: press fork tines onto a piece on a flat plate until thumbnail blanches white. Pass when the piece squashes, does not spring back, and breaks apart rather than recovering shape. Spoon-tilt: lift a heaped spoonful and tilt until vertical; pass when pieces sit in a pile on the spoon and slide off together, not as a single cohesive bolus that pours continuously. Fork-drip: no liquid should drip through the tines; pass is zero drip. Skip the syringe flow test — that is L3 only. L6 requires size plus fork-pressure evidence only.
specimens.visual_qc: Flake surface shows clear muscle layers, not a uniform paste. Pieces each measure under 15 mm against the 100 mm ruler. Pile holds shape on the spoon with visible gaps between pieces; no pooling liquid on the plate.
specimens.shots: Stills: steamed_fish_fillet_L6_take1.jpg at 45° hero with ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; steamed_fish_fillet_L6_take2.jpg top-down with checkerboard; steamed_fish_fillet_L6_take3.jpg fork-press close-up at mid-press. Clips: steamed_fish_fillet_L6_take4.mp4 (8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence); steamed_fish_fillet_L6_take5.mp4 IDDSI test film, full fork-pressure narration.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces exceed 15 mm — re-flake and re-measure. Fillet is over-steamed to a wet mash, so fork leaves liquid on plate — re-make with a shorter steam and pat pieces dry. A bone is found during QC — discard that piece and any from same fillet section; re-flake remaining muscle.

specimens.prep: Take one steamed fish fillet as it comes out of the steamer. Record starting mass on the digital scale (typical 120-180 g). Do not blend. Do not sieve. Do not add thickener, water, or any liquid. Do not mash, flake, or press the flesh. Place the whole fillet onto the white capture plate. This is the reference specimen for L7 — what the diner actually sees and cuts with a fork. Handle once, on the plate, before tests.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the tines of a standard metal fork fully into the thickest part of the fillet. The fillet must resist the press; the fork should NOT cut all the way through cleanly with light thumb pressure. White flakes separating from the muscle along natural layers are acceptable; the piece should hold its shape and not smear between thumb and fork.  Spoon tilt test: lift a forkful and tip it over a white plate. The piece must slide off in one mass or sit firmly on the spoon — no continuous drip, no flow, no sauce-like pour.  Fork drip test: hold a loaded fork over the plate for 5 seconds. Zero drip. A single droplet of surface moisture is acceptable; steady dripping is not.
specimens.visual_qc: Fillet holds an intact, recognisable shape on the plate. Visible natural flake lines along the muscle, no pooling liquid around it. Fork lifts a defined portion, not a smear.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — steamed_fish_fillet_L7_take1.jpg: 45-degree hero, fillet centred, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame.  Still 2 — steamed_fish_fillet_L7_take2.jpg: top-down, checkerboard under plate for scale and white-balance reference.  Still 3 — steamed_fish_fillet_L7_take3.jpg: fork-press close-up, fork tines half-buried mid-press.  Clip 1 — steamed_fish_fillet_L7_take1.mp4: 8-12 s, fork-press followed by spoon-tilt in one continuous take.  Clip 2 — steamed_fish_fillet_L7_take2.mp4: IDDSI test film, both tests shown back-to-back.
specimens.fail_modes: Fillet is over-steamed and collapses under fork pressure — that is L6, not L7; re-steam a shorter time.  Fillet releases free liquid that drips continuously from the fork — L6 or L5; drain on paper, retest, if still dripping re-make with a drier fillet.  Fillet has been blended, flaked, or sauced — wrong specimen; re-make from a fresh steamed fillet with no processing.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed minced pork patty on the digital scale. Tip into consumer blender. Blend 45 s, scraping down at 25 s if needed, until a smooth paste with no visible fibre. Sieve through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any residue that will not pass. Weigh paste, note volume in ml. Add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml of paste as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Stir with the fork 30 s, rest 60 s. If paste sits too stiff for a slow drip, add water 5 ml at a time up to 15 ml total and re-stir. Target: pours in a continuous thick ribbon, drips slowly through fork tines, IDDSI syringe shows 8–10 ml remaining at 10 s.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: hold fork horizontal 50 mm above plate; paste should drip in slow, отдельный drips, not a stream. Fork pressure: tines leave a clear, holding imprint when pressed; paste does not recover. Spoon tilt: a teaspoonful sits in a cohesive mound, slides off slowly when tilted 30 degrees, not runny. Syringe flow: fill 10 ml, release; 8–10 ml remains at 10 s. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: On fork: glossy, uniform, no meat fibre or fat specks, clings in a thick ribbon. On spoon: holds shape, slow slide, no separation of liquid. Surface matte-smooth, single colour, no air pockets.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame, paste mounded on white plate. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard visible, specimen spread to show texture. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines embedded. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. Clip 2: full IDDSI syringe test with timer visible. Files: steamed_minced_pork_patt_L3_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Drips too fast: under-thickened, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 60 s, retest. Holds shape on spoon but will not drip from fork: over-thickened, add 5 ml water, re-stir, retest. Lumps or fibre visible after blending: re-blend 15 s, re-sieve, retest. Re-make from scratch if paste splits or fat pools after 2 min rest.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g steamed minced pork patty into blender. Add 40 ml warm water. Blend 25 s, stop, scrape, blend 20 s more. Pass through 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard coarse residue. Return puree to blender, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml of puree (≈0.95 g for the ≈190 ml recovered from 150 g patty + 40 ml water; confirm against the recorded final weight), blend 10 s to incorporate. Let rest 60 s. Record final weight and actual thickener mass on the data sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press fork tines into the specimen on a flat plate. The tines must leave a clear, defined groove; the puree must not spring back, must not flow to refill the gap, and must not drip continuously through the slots. Fork drip test: lift fork with a standard mounded load. Specimen must sit in a mound above the tines; nothing must drip or flow through within 10 s. Spoon tilt test: a level teaspoonful must hold its shape when the spoon is tilted to 45 degrees; no flow, no drip. No separate thin liquid may be visible pooling on the plate under the specimen.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is smooth and matte, with no visible meat fibre, no crust fragments, no liquid sheen. Colour is uniform pale grey-brown from edge to centre. Specimen mounds cleanly on the spoon and peaks on the fork without slumping.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero shot, fork and spoon staged beside the specimen, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard both in frame. Still 2: top-down, full checkerboard filling the frame, specimen centred, ruler along one edge. Still 3: fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines partially indented, ruler for scale. Clip 1: 8-12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous take. Clip 2: IDDSI test film, full fork-drip and spoon-tilt sequence. Naming: steamed_minced_pork_patt_L4_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen weeps thin liquid onto the plate: under-blended or over-thinned — remake, holding step 1 to 40 ml warm water (never more) and adding the full base dose of 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml of puree at the post-sieve step (not the 0.25 g half dose, and not step 1, which contains no thickener); blend 10 s and rest 60 s before retesting. Specimen flows through fork tines or slumps off the spoon: insufficient thickener — remake at 1.0 g thickener per 100 ml of puree (base 0.5 g plus an extra 0.5 g). Specimen shows fibres or grain after sieving: blend longer before sieving, do not push residue through.

specimens.prep: Bought form: 150 g fresh minced/ground pork shoulder as sold, about 20% fat, minced once, unseasoned. Seasoning for the whole 150 g: 2 g salt, 0.5 g white pepper, 10 ml cold water, plus 5 g cornflour/cornstarch if a firmer set is wanted. Allergens: none of the major declared allergens as seasoned here (pork, salt, white pepper, water, cornstarch). Do not add soy sauce or oyster sauce — both introduce soy and wheat/gluten. Mix the mince with the salt, pepper, water and cornstarch and stir 60 s in one direction until sticky. Form into a patty 100 mm across and 15 mm thick on a heatproof plate. Steam over a rolling boil, covered, for 12 min — cooked when a broken piece shows no pink. Cool 2 min. Tip the patty and all released juices into a bowl, then mash and chop with the back of a fork against the bowl wall for 30–40 s, scraping the bowl, until no particle visibly exceeds 4 mm. Gauge check — the 4 mm sieve is a gauge here, never a production step: take a 20 g sample of the mashed mass and press it against a 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon. If the sample passes, particles are ≤4 mm and the batch is gauged. If material is retained on the mesh, mash the whole batch a further 20 s and re-gauge. Never press the whole batch through the sieve and never discard what stays on the mesh. If the mass looks dry to the eye, fold in 5 ml of the reserved steaming liquid, fold 20 s, and reassess; up to 10 ml in total. No thickener in the base prep (corrective use only, see FAIL MODES, ceiling 1.0 g per 100 g). Plate the whole batch — expect 130–140 g after steaming — and record the plated mass.
specimens.iddsi_test: - 5.2 Spoon tilt — ACTIVE, the deciding L5 test. Take a heaped 5 ml teaspoonful and tilt the spoon to 45°. Pass = the mass holds its shape as a cohesive mound and does not slide off, run or drip. - 5.1 Fork pressure — SUPPORTING CHECK only at L5; per section 5.1 it is a pass/fail test at L4/L6/L7, not at L5. Press the tines flat into the specimen and record whether the mass squashes under thumb pressure and stays squashed with no rebound. Log the result as supporting evidence; it does not decide the level on its own. - 5.3 Fork drip — skip: applies at L3 and L4 only; a moist L5 mince is scored by spoon tilt, and fork drip has no pass criterion at L5. - 5.4 Syringe flow — skip: applies at L3 only; an L5 specimen cannot be drawn into a 10 ml syringe.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a cohesive lump sitting as one mass with no crumbs falling away, glinting with moisture, and no individual particle visibly larger than 4 mm against the 15 mm checkerboard. On the spoon: the mound holds its peak at 45°, surface slightly glossy from the meat juices. On the plate: no separate liquid pooling around the mass — a light moist film at most. Colour is uniform pale grey-brown throughout with no pink showing, confirming every particle reached temperature.
specimens.shots: Still 1: bf12_steamed_minced_pork_patt_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, specimen mound centred, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in the lower frame. Still 2: bf12_steamed_minced_pork_patt_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, full specimen footprint on the checkerboard. Still 3: bf12_steamed_minced_pork_patt_L5_take3.jpg — spoon-tilt close-up at 45° showing the mound holding. Clip 1: bf12_steamed_minced_pork_patt_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s, spoon tilt to 45° then release. Clip 2: bf12_steamed_minced_pork_patt_L5_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence: spoon tilt, then the supporting fork-pressure check, one continuous take.
specimens.fail_modes: Any particle over 4 mm at the gauge check: mash that portion against the bowl wall for a further 20 s and re-gauge with the 4 mm sieve (gauge only — do not sieve the batch as a production step and do not discard retained material). Too dry — the mass is crumbly, falls apart on the fork and will not hold a mound on the spoon: fold in 5 ml reserved steaming liquid, mash 20 s, retest; up to 10 ml in total. Too wet — the mass slides off the spoon at 45° and liquid pools on the plate: spoon off and discard the free liquid, then re-mash; if it is still loose, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g specimen, fold 30 s, rest 60 s, retest (ceiling 1.0 g per 100 g). Mass feels firm or rebounds under the supporting fork-pressure check: re-steam — the intact patty for 3 min if caught before mashing, or the mashed mass in a covered dish for 3 min if caught after — then re-mash and retest. Very lean mince that stays crumbly even with the full 10 ml of liquid: this batch cannot reach L5 by this method — remake with mince of ≥20% fat and note the deviation on the data sheet.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g seasoned minced pork; form into a patty and steam 12–15 min until just cooked through (no pink core). Cool until firm enough for a clean knife cut (≈10–15 min). Do NOT fork-crumble. Cut the cooled patty into 8–15 mm cubes with a sharp knife, measuring each against the 15 mm checkerboard: every piece must be ≥8 mm AND ≤15 mm. Re-cut any piece over 15 mm; set aside any crumb that falls under 8 mm. Do NOT blend. Do NOT sieve. Do NOT add thickener. Do NOT add water.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure (the only L6 test): place 5 representative pieces (each 8–15 mm) in a row on a flat plate. Press the fork tines flat onto one piece until the thumbnail blanches white. The piece must squash and not spring back; lift and repeat on each piece. Pass = all five pieces squash and stay squashed. Spoon tilt: not applicable for L6. Fork drip: not applicable for L6. Syringe flow: not applicable for L6. L6 is confirmed by fork-pressure alone plus the 8–15 mm size window on the checkerboard — a piece must be neither over 15 mm nor under 8 mm.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces are irregular soft cubes; no strand longer than one checkerboard square and no crumb under 8 mm. Surface looks moist, not dry or crusty. Color is uniform cooked pork brown with no pink core.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45-degree hero, patty cubes mounded on plate, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2 — top-down, cubes spread on checkerboard showing the 8–15 mm size. Still 3 — fork-press close-up, fork tines mid-press on a single 8–15 mm piece. Clip 1 — 8–12 s, slow fork-press sequence on 3 pieces. Clip 2 — 8–12 s, the full IDDSI fork-pressure test on the flat plate. Name all files steamed_minced_pork_patt_L6_take1.jpg or .mp4 with _2, _3 suffixes as needed.
specimens.fail_modes: Any piece over 15 mm: re-cut smaller, re-measure, re-shoot. Any crumb under 8 mm: the batch is too fine — re-cut from a firmer patty; do not certify sub-8 mm crumbs as L6. Pieces spring back under fork pressure (under-cooked, too-dense mince): steam a fresh patty 2 min longer, cool until firm, re-dice — a too-firm piece needs more softening so it will squash. Pieces crumble to powder (over-steamed): reform a new patty with 200 g mince, steam 10 min only — a firmer piece so the 8–15 mm cubes hold. Reliability: steamed mince has a narrow softness window (springy if under-cooked, powdery if over-cooked). If a batch will not hold 8–15 mm cubes that squash without springing back, mince cannot be certified L6 reliably by this bench method — re-form with a firmer/coarser grind; do not shoot fines or springy pieces as L6.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g steamed chicken thigh (skin and visible fat removed). Add 100 ml cool water. Blend on high for 45 s; stop, scrape down, blend 30 s more. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve; discard residue. Whisk in 2.0 g thickener per 100 ml of liquidised puree as the calibration starting point; record the actual mass used. Stir 30 s, rest 60 s. Stir again; if the puree runs off the spoon, add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml and rest 30 s. Repeat up to twice. The per-level note instructs blend-thinning; coarse mince or chop is not appropriate for L3.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: a fork pressed fully into the surface leaves a clear pattern that does not rebound; the slot between tines is filled, no chunks remain. Spoon tilt: a level spoon held tilted to 45 degrees flows in a steady, slow ribbon, not a pour and not a pile. Fork drip: when lifted, 3-5 slow drips fall in 10 s, none dropping as a stream. Syringe flow test: after 10 s the syringe retains 8-10 ml; 7-11 ml is acceptable, record the actual.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform pale beige puree with no visible fibres or fat specks; smooth sheen on the spoon; surface settles flat within 2 s when spooned; clings to the fork tines as a thin, even coating.
specimens.shots: Steamed_chicken_thigh_L3_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Steamed_chicken_thigh_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. Steamed_chicken_thigh_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. Steamed_chicken_thigh_L3_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. Steamed_chicken_thigh_L3_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI syringe flow test, stopwatch visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Syringe reads below 7 ml after 10 s (too thick): whisk in 5 ml water, rest 30 s, retest. Visible fibres or fat specks in the puree: re-sieve; if still present, re-blend 20 s and re-sieve. Syringe reads above 11 ml after 10 s (too thin): add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 30 s, retest. After any re-make, re-run all four IDDSI checks and re-shoot the affected media.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g steamed chicken thigh (skin removed, boneless, cooled to ≤40 °C). Add to consumer blender with 60 ml water at ≤40 °C — do not use hot water; if the blend is slow to break down, blend longer rather than hotter, because the specimen must be ≤40 °C when it is tested. Blend on high for 90 s, scrape jar walls, blend 60 s more. Pass purée through a 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any fibrous residue that does not pass — note retained mass. Weigh sieved purée. L4 is lump-free, so this sieve is mandatory: no un-sieved specimen is tested. Add thickener at 1.0 g per 100 g sieved purée as the calibration starting point (3.0 g for a 300 g yield); whisk in, rest 2 min, re-stir 10 s. If the fork-drip test shows flow below the tines, add 0.2 g per 100 g per increment (0.6 g for a 300 g yield) up to a maximum of 1.8 g per 100 g (5.4 g for a 300 g yield), re-testing after each increment. Record final thickener rate (g per 100 g) and final specimen mass (g).
specimens.iddsi_test: Test at 20–40 °C. Fork pressure: press fork tines into the specimen on a flat plate with normal thumb force for 5 s. Pass — tines leave a clear, persistent impression and the surface does not rebound fully; sample does not squeeze between tines. Spoon tilt: load a dessert spoon, tilt to 90°. Pass — specimen sits in a cohesive mound, does not slide, pour, or drip. Fork drip: lift a forkful 10 cm above the plate, hold 5 s. Pass — sample mounds above the tines, zero drip.
specimens.visual_qc: Matte, uniform pale beige surface; no pink fibres, no separated broth pooling at plate edge; spoon mound holds a defined peak without slumping.
specimens.shots: Stills: steamed_chicken_thigh_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in lower frame; take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred; take3.jpg — fork-press close-up at mid-press. specimens.fail_modes: Too thin — slides off spoon or drips through tines: add 0.2 g thickener per 100 g, rest 2 min, re-test (maximum 1.8 g per 100 g). Too stiff — cracks on the plate or surface fractures under fork: thin with 10 ml water at ≤40 °C, re-blend 30 s, re-test. Visible fibres or pooled liquid: re-sieve and discard residue before judging.

specimens.prep: Steam 180 g fresh chicken thigh over boiling water until just cooked through (no pink, core 74 °C). Strip and discard skin, bone, and visible fat. Place 120 g cooked meat in the blender; add 40 ml warm broth from the steaming pot. Pulse 6–8 s, scrape down, pulse 4 s more. Stop and check: the meat must be a coarse, moist mince of distinct granules about 2–4 mm across — not a purée.  The 4 mm sieve is a **GAUGE** here, not a size reducer. Do not rub the batch through it and do not discard the retained fraction. Gauge check: place one heaped teaspoon of mince on the 4 mm sieve and press once with the back of a spoon — the mince must break into granules of about 2–4 mm and pass under light pressure, no single lump may sit on the sieve larger than 4 mm, and no stringy fibre may bridge a hole. Return the gauged sample to the bowl and pick out only any long fibres caught in the sieve. If any lump is larger than 4 mm, pulse the whole batch 2–3 s and re-gauge.  Transfer to a bowl, fold through 2 ml more warm broth with the fork to bring to moist, cohesive mince (not wet, not dry). No thickener required. Record final mass; final portion served for test: 80 g.
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon tilt (mandatory at L5): scoop a heaped teaspoon of mince, tilt the spoon to ~45° and then to near-vertical. PASS — the mince sits in a mound on the spoon; it does not slide off, flow, or pour, and no separate thin liquid runs off the spoon. FAIL — it slides or runs (too wet / over-processed), or it falls away in dry crumbs (too dry).  Fork pressure (supporting check only at L5 — it does not by itself pass the specimen): press fork tines into the specimen until the tines blanch, hold 5 s. SUPPORTING — the mince squashes, does not spring back, and the thumb leaves a clear print, while the squashed mass still shows distinct granules of about 2–4 mm. If it squashes to a smooth paste with no visible granules, the specimen has been over-processed toward L4.  Fork drip and syringe flow are not applicable at L5 and are not run.
specimens.visual_qc: Mince on the fork shows distinct granules, all visibly 2–4 mm and none larger than 4 mm — not a paste. No long stringy fibres visible when the mound is pulled apart with the fork. Surface glistens but no free broth pools on the spoon or the plate. A light thumb-print stays indented.
specimens.shots: steamed_chicken_thigh_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. steamed_chicken_thigh_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. steamed_chicken_thigh_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines blanching mid-press. steamed_chicken_thigh_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press (supporting) then spoon-tilt. steamed_chicken_thigh_L5_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence in one take: spoon tilt, then fork pressure.
specimens.fail_modes: Mince still strings or shreds at the gauge check (fibres bridging the sieve, shreds longer than 4 mm) — re-pulse 2–3 s and re-gauge; if still fibrous, re-cook longer before mincing, or discard the batch. A specimen with visible fibres is not L5. Mince has become a smooth paste with no visible granules — it is now lump-free and holds a soft shape, i.e. L4, not L5. Discard and restart from a fresh 180 g portion, pulsing in 2 s bursts only. Specimen weeps free liquid into the cup or pools on the spoon or plate — too wet: drain on the sieve 30 s, re-fold with less broth, and re-run the spoon-tilt test. Specimen balls up dry on the fork or crumbles off the spoon — too dry: fold in 2–3 ml warm broth and retest. Any re-make requires a fresh take number.

specimens.prep: - Steam one fresh chilled chicken thigh (220–260 g raw) in a steamer basket over 1 L briskly boiling water for 18–22 min, until the core reaches 75 °C on the probe and the juices run clear with no pink. Rest 2 min. - Strip off and discard the skin, the bone, and every piece of gristle and visible fat. Weigh the cooked trimmed meat: target 150 g (record actual). - Dice **by hand** with a knife on the board into cubes whose longest dimension measures **8–15 mm** — no piece under 8 mm, none over 15 mm. Check every cube against the **100 mm ruler** (mm minor ticks, cm majors): the longest dimension must read between the 8 mm and 15 mm marks. Do **not** size against the checkerboard. The printed 15 mm fiducial card is 15 mm across its outer black frame and its checkerboard cells are **3.75 mm** (`tools/capture_kit.py`: 15 mm card, 4x4 grid), so "one full cell" is 3.75 mm, not 15 mm, and "half a cell" is 1.9 mm, not 8 mm. An operator who sizes by cells cuts 2–4 mm pieces — L5 material — and labels them L6. - Pick out by hand any fragment below 8 mm; that is L5 material and must not enter an L6 specimen. - **No blender. No sieve** — a sieve cannot enforce a 15 mm limit and must never be used to size an L6 specimen. **No thickener, no added liquid, no oil.** - Plate **80 g** of diced meat in a single layer on the tray (record actual mass). Test at **20–40 °C**.
specimens.iddsi_test: - Fork pressure (5.1 — the only test that applies at L6): place **three** cubes on the tray — one from the top, one from the middle and one from the bottom of the plated portion. Press the flat of the fork bowl down onto each in turn with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white, then lift. **Pass** = **every** cube tested compresses/crushes under that pressure and does not recover its shape when the fork is lifted; each stays one piece that the fork lifts whole. One cube in three that springs back fails the specimen — a single filmed cube can pass on the softest piece in a mixed batch. - Sizing check, in the same unbroken take: hold two or three cubes against the 100 mm ruler. Every piece must measure **8–15 mm** on its longest dimension. One piece over 15 mm fails the specimen. - Spoon tilt: **skip** — 5.2 covers L3/L4/L5. L6 is cut pieces, not a spoonable mass, so this test is not run and is not recorded as pass/fail. - Fork drip: **skip** — 5.3 covers L3/L4. L6 pieces have no flow through the tines to observe, so this test is not run and is not recorded as pass/fail. - Syringe flow: **skip** — 5.4 is required on every L3 only; an L6 solid is not a 10 ml flow sample.
specimens.visual_qc: - Cubes are matte pale-beige with clean cut faces — no glistening skin, no jelly sheen, no yellow fat. - Every cube measures **8–15 mm on its longest dimension against the 100 mm ruler**; no fragment under 8 mm anywhere in the plated portion. The 15 mm fiducial card is the photo scale reference only — its checkerboard cells are 3.75 mm and must never be used as the L6 sizing gauge. - Cubes sit separately, not clumped or stuck, and hold their cut geometry on the tray. - No free liquid pools on the tray or runs from a cube when it is lifted. - The fork leaves a compression mark that stays.
