specimens.fail_modes: - A cube will not crush under blanching pressure and springs back (**too firm — above L6**): re-steam the whole batch **2 min** over briskly boiling water and re-test; if it still will not crush, reject the specimen. Never blend or sieve to "soften" it — blending makes paste (L4/L5) and a sieve cannot size a 15 mm limit. - Cubes mash to paste under light finger pressure (**too soft — below L6, L5 material**): discard and re-make from a fresh thigh steamed to a 75 °C core, dicing by hand only. Do not add thickener or liquid to recover the level; neither moves a specimen toward L6. - Any piece over 15 mm: re-dice against the **100 mm ruler** and re-check the whole plated portion before filming. A batch diced "to the checkerboard" (3.75 mm cells) is L5 material, not L6 — discard it and start again from a fresh thigh, sizing against the ruler. - Any fragment under 8 mm: pick it out by hand or re-dice it. A batch with more than about 1 piece in 10 under 8 mm is too fine for L6 — start again from a fresh thigh and dice coarser. - Gristle, skin or fat found in QC: discard those pieces and re-trim the remainder before plating. - Free liquid pooling on the tray: the thigh is over-steamed. Wipe the tray edge, re-shoot within 60 s; if liquid keeps coming out of the meat, re-make with the 18 min minimum steam. - One re-make from a reserve aliquot is allowed; a second failure on the same criterion is logged as a FAIL row (`tests.pass = false`), never relabelled.

specimens.prep: Place the fresh chilled thigh on a plate, steam until the core reaches 75 °C and the juices run clear, then rest 2 minutes. Target specimen weight is one whole cooked thigh (record actual mass in g on the capture sheet). Do NOT blend, sieve, or add liquid — the per-level note requires the whole thigh as steamed. No thickener. Weigh the specimen on the digital scale before plating for the hero shot.
specimens.iddsi_test: 1) Fork pressure test: press the tines of a standard fork fully into the meat. The specimen must NOT separate, mash, or ooze through the tine gaps; the fork must lift the piece cleanly with no liquid pooling beneath. 2) Spoon tilt test: place the thigh piece on a spoon and tilt to 45°; it must NOT slide, drip, or flow off. 3) Fork drip test: lift the specimen on the fork to ~15 cm above the plate for 5 seconds; no drip should fall. All three must pass. No syringe test applies at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: Firm, opaque white-meat surface with intact skin and visible muscle fibre direction. Holds its anatomical shape when lifted — no slumping. No juice puddle forming on the plate within 30 seconds of plating.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45° hero, ruler (100 mm) and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, whole thigh centred: steamed_chicken_thigh_L7_take1.jpg Still 2 — top-down with checkerboard only, thigh flat on plate: steamed_chicken_thigh_L7_take2.jpg Still 3 — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into meat: steamed_chicken_thigh_L7_take3.jpg Clip 1 — 8–12 s continuous fork-press then spoon-tilt, no cuts: steamed_chicken_thigh_L7_take1.mp4 Clip 2 — full IDDSI test sequence (pressure, tilt, drip) narrated, 15–30 s: steamed_chicken_thigh_L7_take2.mp4
specimens.fail_modes: (a) Thigh is under-steamed — flesh tears and oozes pink juice on the fork; re-cook that piece, do not proceed. (b) Thigh is over-steamed and stringy — fibres separate through fork tines; reject, steam a new thigh to 75 °C only. (c) Pooled liquid on plate from resting too long — pat surface dry with paper towel, re-shoot within 60 s; if persistent, rest a freshly steamed thigh for exactly 2 minutes.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g set steamed egg custard (eggs + water, steamed to set). Break into chunks. Add 120 ml cool water. Blend in consumer blender 30 s, scrape down, 15 s more. Sieve through 4 mm sieve into a bowl; press soft residue through with the back of a spoon, discard coarse that won't pass. Measure the sieved liquid and record the volume V (expect about 250 ml). Add thickener at the calibration starting point for the thickener type in use, taken from docs/BASE_FOOD_LIST.md: gum-based (xanthan/gum blend) 1-2 g per 100 ml of measured sieved liquid, starch-based (grain-derived) 4-8 g per 100 ml. The figure fixed by calibration on BF01-BF05 overrides this and is recorded per specimen; weigh to 0.1 g and record the actual grams used on the data card. Whisk 20 s, rest 2 min, stir again. Titrate to the syringe window in 0.5 g (gum) or 1 g (starch) per 100 ml steps, each weighed to 0.1 g — never pinched. If the window cannot be reached inside the food-list range for the thickener in use, after the FAIL MODES corrections have been tried, the water ratio is wrong and the remedy depends on which way the reading misses: if the syringe still holds more than 10 ml at the top of the range the base is too stiff — discard and re-make with 160 ml water instead of 120 ml; if the residual has already fallen below 8 ml the base is over-thinned — discard and re-make with 90 ml water instead of 120 ml. Never thin a too-thin base with water and never thicken a too-thick one with thickener: on this test a larger residual means a thicker specimen, so each of those moves the reading away from the 8-10 ml window. The BF14 per-level note is blend-thin, and the water plus blend above IS that step; the 4 mm sieve is the lump-free gauge, not the texture step. Log this specimen only under the full level-suffixed ID bf14_steamed_egg_custard_L3 — the bare base-food ID carries L3, L4, L5 and L6 in the food list and must never be used as a ground-truth key.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a loaded fork clear of the bowl; the specimen drips slowly through the tines in a continuous flow (about 1-2 drips per second, never a free stream) and leaves a coating on the fork. Pass = steady slow drip; a stream is too thin, a mound sitting on top of the tines is too thick. Spoon tilt: a full spoon tilted to 45° pours off in a slow continuous stream over 2-4 s — not instantly, not as one lump — with no separate thin liquid pooling on the spoon or tray. Syringe flow test (L3, mandatory): fill the 10 ml syringe to the 10 ml mark, release with the nozzle open, start the 10 s timer; pass = 8.0-10.0 ml remaining at t = 10 s with a measurable discharge during the 10 s, and both the t=0 fill level and the t=10 reading legible on film. All three must pass. Fork pressure is not an L3 test and is not performed on this specimen.
specimens.visual_qc: Smooth, glossy pale-yellow film across the spoon with no lumps and no white curds. Pours off the tilted spoon as one continuous slow ribbon that stacks briefly before settling; surface self-levels in under 2 s after a shake. Drips from fork fall as fat droplets that merge into a continuous slow ribbon. No visible bubbles, streaks, or separate liquid running ahead of the body.

specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: residual <8.0 ml, or drips stream from the fork — whisk in 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml (weighed to 0.1 g), rest 60 s, re-test. Too thick: 10.0 ml remains with no measurable discharge at 10 s, or the specimen sits as a mound on the fork with no drip through the tines — thin with 5 ml water, re-blend 10 s, re-test. Never correct a too-thick specimen with thickener: on this test a larger residual means a thicker specimen, so extra thickener moves the reading the wrong way. Lumpy/grainy from curds: sieve failed — re-blend 20 s and re-sieve before thickening; if the re-sieved puree is still grainy, discard the batch and re-make, do not simply re-test the original. Any specimen failing two consecutive tests is discarded and marked FAIL.

specimens.prep: Crack 3 large eggs (~150 g) into a measuring jug. Add 150 ml room-temperature water and whisk until fully combined with no visible streaks. Pour through the 4 mm sieve into a heatproof bowl to remove chalazae and unbroken yolk membrane (this is a lump-free level, so sieving the raw mix is correct). Steam covered for 12–15 min until just set — the surface no longer wobbles as liquid and the centre reads 80–85 °C; cool to room temperature (~30 min). Weigh 200 g of the set custard into the blender and blend on high for 45–60 s until completely smooth with no grain. Do NOT add thickener — at 1 egg : 50 ml water the custard sets firmly enough to blend straight to L4. Record final specimen mass on the data sheet (target 200 g ± 5 g).
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure (primary at L4): press the fork tines into the specimen on a flat white plate with normal thumb pressure. The tines must blanch white, the specimen must take a clean dent and not spring back, and no thin liquid may run between the prongs. Fork drip (applies at L3/L4): lift the fork with a loaded mound. The specimen must sit as a cohesive mound above the tines for the full 8 s hold; at most a single slow tail may form — no continuous flow through the tines. Spoon tilt (applies at L3/L4/L5): scoop a heaped teaspoon, invert the spoon 90° over the plate. The specimen must hold a soft mound and must NOT pour off as a stream, and must NOT slide off as one mass; slow slump and flow down the spoon over the 8–10 s hold is the expected, passing L4 result. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is glossy and uniform pale yellow with zero white streaks or grain. The mound on the fork has clean, defined edges that soften slowly rather than slumping flat. On the spoon at 90°: the scoop holds a soft mound and flows slowly, leaving a thin, even film behind — it does not drop off as one mass. No separation of clear liquid.

specimens.fail_modes: Too runny — flows continuously through the fork tines, or pours off the spoon as a stream at 90°: the egg:water ratio was low or the steam was short. Re-make with 4 eggs (200 g) per 150 ml water and steam to the same endpoint. Do not try to thicken an already-blended batch with starch. Too thick — holds a stiff shape with no flow at 90° inversion, fork tines do not blanch: thin it. Re-make with 2 eggs (100 g) per 150 ml water, or blend in 10 ml water at a time (5 s each) and re-run the fork-pressure and spoon-tilt gates. Grainy or streaky texture: blender under-cycled or sieve skipped — re-blend 30 s and re-sieve. Clear liquid pools on the plate after spoon tilt: syneresis from over-steaming — discard the batch and re-make with 4 eggs (200 g) per 150 ml water, steaming no longer than 12–15 min.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed set custard onto the plate. Press firmly with the back of a fork until the curd collapses; mash through the curd, not through the sieve, working the liquor back in as you go. Re-mash until no lump exceeds 4 mm when checked against the ruler. Sieve the mash through the 4 mm sieve only as a verification pass — anything retained goes back through the fork. Target retained mass: at least 180 g. The per-level note ("spoon-mash to curds <= 4 mm with its liquor") is followed; do not blend. Do not add water. Do not add thickener at L5 — start here, thicken only if the spoon-tilt fails and a re-make is logged.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines flat into the specimen until the blanch shows; the custard must squash and not recover when the fork is lifted. Fork-drip test: lift fork from the specimen — no thin liquid drips continuously off the tines. Spoon-tilt test: scoop a teaspoonful, tilt spoon to about 45°; the mass slides off in one soft bolus, it does not run and does not hold shape on the spoon. No syringe test at L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a soft, glossy yellow curd with no dry crumbs and no pooling liquid around the mound. On the spoon: a single coherent quenelle that wobbles, not a pourable sauce. Particle size visibly under 4 mm against the ruler.

specimens.fail_modes: Wet, soupy mash that pools thin liquid on the plate — under-mashed or over-steamed original; re-mash and rest 30 s, re-shoot. Visible lumps above 4 mm; sieve again and re-mash, re-shoot. Custard holds shape on the tilted spoon like a gelatin set; discard, re-cook a softer custard and start prep again.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of steamed egg custard on the scale. Cut the set custard into cubes ≤ 15 mm with the fork or a knife against the 15 mm checkerboard. Do NOT blend — pureeing destroys the piece identity required for L6. Do NOT sieve. Do NOT add thickener. Do NOT add water; the custard already holds its moisture. Record the starting mass.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: place one cube under the fork tines. Press with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white, holding 1 second. Pass criterion: the cube squashes, deforms, and does not spring back to shape. Spoon tilt: scoop one cube onto the spoon and tilt 45 degrees over the capture mat. Pass criterion: the piece sits full on the spoon, does not slide off, does not drip liquid. Fork drip: lift a cube on the fork and hold 5 seconds above the mat. Pass criterion: the piece holds on the fork with no drip and no fall.
specimens.visual_qc: Cube edges are clean and ≤ 15 mm against the checkerboard. Surface is pale yellow, smooth, and glossy with no pooled water on the mat. When pressed, the cube visibly flattens under the thumbnail and stays flattened.

specimens.fail_modes: Cubes exceed 15 mm: re-cut smaller and re-shoot before any other test. Cube springs back after fork press, holding shape like a sponge: the egg set is too firm or under-steamed; re-make with a wetter ratio (more water per egg) and re-test. Liquid pools on the mat from a cube: custard is under-set and weeping; re-make and drain before capture.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g hard-boiled egg (white + yolk, no shell). Add 100 ml cool water. Blend in consumer blender 45-60 s on high until fully smooth. Press through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon; discard any residue retained on mesh (L3 is lump-free — a clean sieve pass is required). Transfer sieved purée to a cup on the digital scale. Add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml of sieved purée (≈250 ml, i.e. ≈5.0 g) as the calibration starting point; whisk briskly 30 s, rest 2 min, re-whisk 10 s. Record actual grams used, final weight (g), and total volume (ml, by graduated cylinder). Target: specimen pours in a continuous slow ribbon and drips slowly through the fork tines; 8-10 ml remains in the syringe at t=10 s.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift fork; sample flows through the tines as a slow, continuous drip, not as separate drops and not as a stream. Spoon tilt: tilt spoon 45°; specimen flows off in a steady ribbon in 3-5 s. Syringe flow (mandatory at L3): fill 10 ml syringe, release; after 10 s, 8-10 ml remains in the barrel.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy, uniform pale-yellow liquid with no yolk granules, white flecks, or specks visible against white cup. Coats spoon back as an even thin film; leaves the spoon in one continuous ribbon, not in clumps. No free water separation at the cup wall.

specimens.fail_modes: Too thin (drips through fork as a stream, <8 ml left in syringe): whisk in extra thickener 0.3 g/100 ml increments, re-test. Too thick (spoon tilt holds a mound and gives no ribbon; syringe still holds 10 ml at t=10 s with no flow): stir in 5-10 ml water, re-whisk, rest 2 min, re-test. Do not add thickener on this branch. Gritty or speckled (visible yolk lumps, sieve residue): re-blend 20 s and re-sieve; if still gritty, re-make — specimen must pass sieve cleanly.

specimens.prep: Weigh 100 g hard-boiled egg (yolk + white, no shell) into the blender. Add 60 ml water. Blend 45 s, scrape, blend 30 s. Push through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard residue. Weigh the sieved puree. Add thickener at 0 g per 100 g sieved puree as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Stir in, rest 2 min, stir again. If the spoon-tilt test below is failed, add thickener in 0.5 g increments per 100 g sieved puree, rest 2 min between each, and re-test. Note: a hard-boiled egg cannot reach L4 by blending alone because the yolk is lipid-rich and the white is protein-firm; thickener is required to suppress thin-liquid separation.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the fork tines fully into the puree; the tines must leave a clear, clean impression that does not fill back in, and the puree must not flow through the slots between the tines. Pass = visible tine marks retained and no extrusion through the gaps. Spoon tilt test: load a heaped spoon; tilt until vertical. Pass = the mound sits on the spoon and falls off as a single lump, not a slow pour, and leaves little residue on the spoon. Fork drip test: lift the fork with a loaded mound. Pass = the mound sits above the tines for 5 s and does not drip continuously through the gaps.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a soft, glossy mound that sits clearly on top of the tines with pale-yellow uniform colour and no white flecks, yolk streaks, or wet sheen around the base. On the spoon: holds its rounded shape after the tilt, smooth surface without granules, and no thin yellow liquid pooling on the plate.
specimens.shots: hardboiled_egg_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, spoon loaded. hardboiled_egg_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard visible at one corner, full specimen. hardboiled_egg_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines buried, ruler edge in shot. hardboiled_egg_L4_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s clip: fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous motion. hardboiled_egg_L4_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full fork pressure, fork drip, spoon tilt sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Thin yellow liquid pools on the plate within 30 s: yolk has broken — keep the batch, do not discard it. Drain the pooled liquid off the plate, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g sieved puree, rest 2 min, and re-test with spoon tilt and fork drip. Puree is grainy or shows white specks: blend inadequate or sieve skimped — keep the batch, do not discard it. Blend the same puree another 30 s, then re-sieve fully through the 4 mm sieve, and re-test. Mound slumps off the spoon before vertical tilt: under-thickened; add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g sieved puree, rest 2 min, re-test. Never thin the specimen with water at this stage.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g shelled hard-boiled egg on the scale; cut into rough chunks. Pulse in the consumer blender 6–8 s. Press through the 4 mm sieve using the fork back; discard overs. Return the sieved mince to the bowl. Add 20 ml water per 100 g mince and stir until evenly moist; the mince must look wet, not dry. Fork-mash to break any lumps remaining after sieving. If the mix reads too dry to hold shape on the spoon, add water 2 ml at a time. No thickener is needed for L5; record the actual water ml used.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines flat against the mince for 5 s. Pass when the mince squashes and does not spring back, and the tine slots are not blocked. Spoon-tilt test: rest 10 ml of mince on the spoon, tilt to near-vertical. Pass when the sample slides off in one moist clump, not a flow. Fork-drip test: lift 3 fork-loads one after the other; no thin liquid drips from the slots between lifts.
specimens.visual_qc: Mince sits as soft, wet lumps on the spoon — no whole chunks, no glossy water pooling underneath. Fork tines leave clear, non-rebounding dents. Colour is pale yellow, uniform, no dry streaks.
specimens.shots: hardboiled_egg_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, spoon heaped with mince. hardboiled_egg_L5_take2.jpg — top-down on A4 capture kit, checkerboard centred. hardboiled_egg_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines half-sunk. hardboiled_egg_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press followed by spoon-tilt. hardboiled_egg_L5_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, fork-pressure, spoon-tilt, fork-drip in sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Lumps over 4 mm left after sieving: re-press through the sieve, do not mash harder. Dry, crumbly texture that does not hold on the spoon: add water 2 ml per 100 g and re-test. Free thin liquid pooling on the plate: drain on paper, then re-test; if it returns, reduce water by 2 ml per 100 g next batch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g peeled hard-boiled egg (white and yolk). Before chopping, mark an 8 mm line and a 15 mm line on the board using the ruler and a marker. Chop on the board with a knife into pieces whose longest dimension measures 8–15 mm — no piece under 8 mm and none over 15 mm. Check the longest edge of every piece against the two marked lines. Do not blend — the level note says chop, not puree. Do not sieve. Do not add water or thickener. Record the actual mass of the chopped specimen in g.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure (primary): press the fork tines onto a piece until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass — the piece squashes and does not return to shape; it breaks apart, not springs back. Spoon tilt: skip — L6 is not spoonable, so tilt is not the deciding test. Fork drip: skip — L6 pieces do not drip. Run fork-pressure as the primary test.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces are irregular, soft-looking, yellow-cream, with visible yolk and white mixed. Hold a piece on the fork — it visibly deforms under its own weight and when pressed. No liquid weeps from the piece. Check every piece against the 100 mm ruler: each must measure 8–15 mm on its longest edge. A batch containing pieces under 8 mm is not L6 material — see FAIL MODES.
specimens.shots: hardboiled_egg_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero: chopped pile on plate, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. hardboiled_egg_L6_take2.jpg — top-down: checkerboard under plate only. hardboiled_egg_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, fork tines mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. hardboiled_egg_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press clip showing squash and non-recovery. hardboiled_egg_L6_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full fork-pressure sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces over 15 mm — re-chop. Pieces under 8 mm — the batch is too fine for L6 (sub-8 mm pieces are L5 material and must not be captured and labelled L6): discard the undersize pieces and re-chop the remainder to size; if more than about 1 piece in 10 is under 8 mm, start again with a fresh egg and chop coarser. Egg rubbery and springs back under fork — egg overcooked, start again with a freshly boiled egg. Pieces crumble to powder rather than squash — egg undercooked, re-boil.

specimens.prep: Start with one whole hard-boiled egg as purchased, weighed on the digital scale; record starting mass in grams (typical 50–60 g). Do NOT blend. Do NOT sieve. Do NOT add thickener, water, or liquid. Per the per-level note, present the egg whole or halved as boiled, cooled to room temperature (≈20–25 °C, ~5 min rest). This is the reference specimen. No processing step applies.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the tines of a fork into the egg white until the thumbnail blanches white. The egg must squash completely, change shape, and not return to its original form when the fork is removed. Pass = full deformation, no recovery. Spoon tilt test: place a spoonful of egg (white and yolk) on a spoon and tilt until the spoon is nearly vertical. The specimen must slide/fall off easily with little or no residue left on the spoon. Pass = slides off readily. Fork drip test: lift the specimen on the fork; no drip applies (solid). N/A — record as not applicable. No syringe test required at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: matte, opaque white and yellow yolk surface; clean tine marks visible after press; no pooled liquid, no glossy sheen, no liquid weeping from the yolk. On the spoon: dense, cohesive mound that drops cleanly when tilted.
specimens.shots: hardboiled_egg_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. hardboiled_egg_L7_take1.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred under the egg. hardboiled_egg_L7_take1.jpg — fork-press close-up, fork mid-press into white. hardboiled_egg_L7_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press + spoon-tilt clip. hardboiled_egg_L7_take1.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full protocol in one continuous take.
specimens.fail_modes: Undercooking → soft or jammy yolk that spreads on tilt; discard, rebatch. Cracked or rubbery overcooked white that springs back under fork pressure → discard, rebatch. Wet condensation or yolk film pooling on the plate → pat dry, retake; if persistent, rebatch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g silken tofu. Add 90 ml water. Blend 25 s on high until pourable. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve; press solids through with the back of a spoon, discard coarse residue retained on the mesh. Weigh blended yield, then thicken to the L3 calibration starting point of 1.5 g thickener per 100 ml blended liquid. Whisk in the powder with a fork, rest 90 s, stir 10 s. Re-weigh and record the actual thickener grams per 100 ml used on the capture sheet before filming.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: tilt a fork from a loaded spoon; liquid must drip in slow, continuous drops through the tines, not run in a stream. Spoon tilt: a teaspoon tilts and the specimen flows off in a steady ribbon, not a pour, not a slide. Fork pressure: the fork prong leaves a clear, clean imprint on the surface under light thumb pressure with no surface rupture or separation. Syringe flow test: fill the IDDSI 10 ml syringe to the 10 ml mark, release, wait 10 s; 8-10 ml must remain in the barrel. Any value below 8 ml means re-thicken; above 10 ml means it is too thin.
specimens.visual_qc: Specimen on the spoon is glossy, uniform off-white, with no visible curds, lumps, or whey pooling. On the fork it clings as a smooth continuous film that releases as one slow drip when tilted. No grain, no streaks, no free liquid running off ahead of the body.
specimens.shots: still_1 silken_tofu_L3_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. still_2 silken_tofu_L3_take1.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. still_3 silken_tofu_L3_take1.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press. clip_1 silken_tofu_L3_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press plus spoon-tilt. clip_2 silken_tofu_L3_take1.mp4 — IDDSI syringe flow test, full 10 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: passes the fork as a stream or leaves under 8 ml in the syringe; add 0.1 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 60 s, retest. Too thick: clings to the spoon without dripping or blocks the syringe above 10 ml; blend in 5 ml water, retest. Grainy or curdled: sieve step skipped or over-blended; discard and remake.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g silken tofu directly into the blender jar. Add 30 ml water. Blend 10 s on high; stop, scrape the walls with a fork, blend a further 10 s. Hold the lid for the full cycle. Sieve the blend once through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a fork — discard any retained solids or note them. The per-level note says "brief blend, blend-hold", so do not over-process: target is smooth but cohesive, not aerated or glossy-runny. No thickener is specified by the food list for L4; this is the calibration starting point. Record the actual gram weight on the capture sheet. Do not add ice, salt, oil, or acid. Keep the specimen covered until shot 1 to prevent surface skin.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a loaded fork (tines loaded across the full width) 5 cm above the plate. Specimen must sit as a mound above the tines and fall off in a single clump within 10 s — no thin tail, no drip through gaps. Fork pressure: press the fork tines flat into the mound; the specimen must yield to clear thumb pressure (1-2 mm) and not return to shape, and must not run between tines. Spoon tilt: a level 5 ml spoon heaped and tilted 45° must hold its shape with no flow, no drip from the spoon lip, no separate thin liquid pooling on the plate.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is matte-smooth, no visible tofu curds, no weeping liquid ring on the plate after the spoon tilt. Mound on the fork retains defined edges and a flat top. One uniform off-white colour throughout.
specimens.shots: Stills: silken_tofu_L4_take1.jpg hero at 45° with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; silken_tofu_L4_take2.jpg top-down, checkerboard only; silken_tofu_L4_take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press, tines partly submerged. Clips: silken_tofu_L4_take4.mp4 (8-12 s) fork-press plus spoon tilt in one continuous move; silken_tofu_L4_take5.mp4 IDDSI test film covering fork drip, fork pressure, spoon tilt in that order. Lock focus and exposure before each capture.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-blended: glossy, aerated, flows through fork tines — discard, re-make with 5 s less total blend. Under-blended: visible curds caught on the 4 mm sieve — discard, re-make with 10 s more total blend after scraping. Added water too high: thin tail on fork drip or liquid pools on plate — discard, re-make with 10 ml less water. Any fail = full re-make, do not patch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g silken tofu onto the scale. Tip onto a clean plate; mash thoroughly with a fork until uniform — no whole curds remain. Press the mash through the 4 mm sieve using the back of the fork or a spatula, discarding anything that will not pass; re-mash any retained lumps and sieve again. The target is soft particles ≤ 4 mm with surface moisture, no pooling liquid. No blender is required and none should be used — the food list notes spoon-break to curds ≤ 4 mm, which the fork-and-sieve sequence delivers. No thickener is added; no water is added.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines flat into the specimen for one second. The specimen must squash, and the tine marks must remain — no elastic recovery. Fork-drip test: lift a forkful 5 cm above the plate; nothing should drip or run through the slots. Spoon-tilt test: tilt a spoonful slowly past vertical; the full portion must slide off together, not pour, drip, or fall as separate liquid. All three must pass to confirm L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork, the specimen should hold its shape as a coherent lump with a glossy, moist sheen — not wet, not dry, not crumbly. On the spoon, it should mound as one piece that slides off together. No free liquid should pool on the plate.
specimens.shots: silken_tofu_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. silken_tofu_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. silken_tofu_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press, marks visible. silken_tofu_L5_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s clip of fork-press and spoon-tilt, audible commentary optional. silken_tofu_L5_take5.mp4 — IDDSI test film: fork pressure, fork drip, spoon tilt, full sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Particles exceed 4 mm after sieving — re-mash and re-sieve. Free thin liquid pools on the plate — drain briefly on absorbent paper, do not add thickener. Specimen recovers shape after fork press — specimen is too firm, discard and remake from a fresh block using gentler mashing.

specimens.prep: Drain liquid from the chilled box. Place 400 g silken tofu on a board and cut with a knife and ruler into cubes measuring 8–15 mm in every dimension (nominal 12 mm). Do NOT blend; the per-level note requires intact pieces. Do NOT sieve — a 4 mm sieve cannot size an L6 piece and would reduce the batch to L5 or finer. Do NOT add thickener; L6 is unthickened. Do NOT add water. Check every piece against the 100 mm ruler: no dimension below 8 mm, none above 15 mm.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test (the only IDDSI test that applies at L6): press the flat of a fork down on one cube until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass if the cube squashes, does not spring back, and breaks apart easily. Piece-size check: with the 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, verify every piece in the batch measures 8–15 mm in all three dimensions. A piece under 8 mm is an L5 lump and must be re-cut, not served as L6. Spoon tilt and fork drip are L3–L5 and L3–L4 tests respectively and do not apply at L6 — do not run them and do not record them as pass/fail. Skip the syringe flow test; it is L3 only.
specimens.visual_qc: Cubes hold a clean, sharp cut edge with rounded corners. Surface is glossy and wet, not torn or smeared. Pieces separate when lifted with a fork; no paste or smear between them.
specimens.shots: silken_tofu_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, pieces on a spoon. silken_tofu_L6_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only, a 3×3 cube grid. silken_tofu_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail visible. silken_tofu_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press in one continuous shot. silken_tofu_L6_take2.mp4 — the IDDSI test film: fork pressure showing blanched thumbnail and squash, then the piece-size check against ruler and checkerboard.
specimens.fail_modes: Cubes cut above 15 mm: re-trim and reshoot. Cubes cut below 8 mm: the batch is L5, not L6 — re-cut from a fresh block to 8–15 mm. Pieces collapse into a paste or smear rather than deforming as a discrete cube under the fork: the block is too fragile for L6 — pat cubes dry with paper towel and reshoot; if they still paste, replace with a firmer block from a fresh box. Pieces spring back when pressed: tofu too firm — set aside and replace with a softer block from a fresh box.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g steamed firm tofu. Crumble into blender jar, add 100 ml cool water, blend 45-60 s until smooth. Press through the 4 mm sieve; discard any residue that does not pass. Weigh the sieved puree. Add thickener at 1.5 g per 100 ml of puree as the calibration starting point; whisk in, rest 90 s, stir, re-weigh. Record actual grams used. Target consistency: pours slowly, drips through fork tines in a thick continuous ribbon. Adjust with extra thickener (0.25 g increments) or water (5 ml) and re-test.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift fork from a 50 mm depth; puree drips through tines in slow, continuous drops, not a steady stream. Spoon tilt: 10 ml on a spoon holds shape, slides slowly when tilted to ~45 degrees. Fork pressure: a visible dent forms under fork tines with light pressure, puree does not recover, no lumps. Syringe flow test (L3 requirement): fill 10 ml syringe, cut to 10 ml mark, release; 8-10 ml remains in syringe after 10 s. Pass = drip through fork tines, no flow from spoon, dent under fork, 8-10 ml retained in syringe.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface on spoon is glossy, smooth, no grain or curds. Ribbon falling from fork holds its line for ~2 cm before merging. Color is uniform off-white, no translucent tofu fragments.
specimens.shots: Shoot on A4 kit, ruler + checkerboard visible. 1. firm_tofu_L3_take1.jpg - 45-degree hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. 2. firm_tofu_L3_take1_topdown.jpg - top-down, checkerboard flat. 3. firm_tofu_L3_take1_forkpress.jpg - fork-press close-up mid-press. 4. firm_tofu_L3_take1.mp4 - 8-12 s clip of fork-press and spoon-tilt. 5. firm_tofu_L3_take1_flow.mp4 - IDDSI 10 ml syringe flow test, full 10 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: flows from spoon, <8 ml retained in syringe - whisk in thickener 0.25 g, rest 90 s, re-test. Too thick: leaves >10 ml in syringe, blocks fork drip - whisk in 5 ml water, re-test. Lumpy/grainy: did not pass sieve - re-blend 30 s and re-sieve before adjusting thickener. Re-make from base if puree separates after standing.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g chilled firm tofu, steamed. Cube ~1.5 cm. Add to consumer blender with 60 ml water. Blend 45 s on high, stop, scrape, blend 30 s more until glossy. Pass through 4 mm sieve using a spoon; discard residue. Target ~210 ml puree. Add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml as the calibration starting point; stir in, rest 2 min, re-stir. If fork-drip test (Section 2) fails, step up in 0.25 g/100 ml increments and record the actual grams used.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: a soft white mound stays when the fork presses; thumb blanching is acceptable. Spoon tilt: the specimen sits on the spoon, does not flow off when tilted to 45 degrees, and slides off in one piece when tilted to 90 degrees. Fork drip: when the fork is lifted, the puree mounds on top of the tines and drops slowly, not in a steady stream. No separate thin liquid in the bowl.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy, smooth, uniform off-white surface; no lumps, grains, or tofu flecks. Holds its shape on the spoon without slumping. Coats the fork tines without running through them.
specimens.shots: firm_tofu_L4_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame, specimen mounded on a spoon. firm_tofu_L4_take1.jpg — top-down, checkerboard visible, spoon and fork resting beside the specimen. firm_tofu_L4_take1.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. firm_tofu_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s clip: fork-press then spoon-tilt. firm_tofu_L4_take1.mp4 — IDDSI test film: full fork drip, spoon tilt, fork pressure sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: puree flows through fork tines or off the spoon — add 0.25 g/100 ml thickener, rest, re-test. Too stiff: cracks or tears when pressed — blend in 5-10 ml water and re-test. Grainy or streaky: sieve was skipped or under-blended — re-sieve and re-test; do not photograph until pass.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed firm tofu. Add 60 ml warm broth. Pulse in the blender 6 s; scrape; pulse 4 s. Press through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard what stays behind. Return the sieved crumb to the bowl. Mash with a fork until cohesive. Moisten with extra broth, 5 ml at a time, up to 20 ml, until the mass holds together but no free liquid pools. Do not add thickener for L5; L5 is calibrated at this crumb texture. Record any deviation.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the fork tines into a 1.5 cm mound on a plate until the thumbnail blanches white. The specimen must squash, not spring back, and the crumbs must not squeeze liquid out. Spoon tilt test: load a 5 mm layer onto a spoon and tilt to 45 degrees; the specimen must hold its shape and not slide, drip, or run. Fork drip test: lift a forkful 5 cm above the plate; no thin liquid must drip through or off the tines. Pass when all three are met. Syringe flow test does not apply at L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a moist, cohesive crumb of clearly visible pieces no larger than a green pea, all sitting within a 4 mm grain. On the spoon: the layer stays mounded at tilt, surface glistens but no liquid sheen pools on the plate beside it.
specimens.shots: Shoot on the A4 kit with the 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler. - firm_tofu_L5_take1.jpg: 45-degree hero, specimen mound in frame with ruler and checkerboard edges visible. - firm_tofu_L5_take1_top.jpg: top-down, checkerboard fills background, ruler alongside. - firm_tofu_L5_take1_press.jpg: fork-press close-up at mid-press, tines buried. - firm_tofu_L5_take1.mp4: 8-12 s clip, fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. - firm_tofu_L5_take1_test.mp4: IDDSI test film, fork pressure then spoon tilt, no cuts.
specimens.fail_modes: Crumb too coarse, individual pieces above 4 mm. Re-blend 3 s and re-sieve. Specimen too wet, broth pools on tilt or drips from the fork. Drain on the sieve 30 s, re-mash, retest. Specimen too dry, cracks or crumbles apart under the fork instead of squashing. Moisten with 5 ml broth, re-mash, retest. If still failing after two re-makes, change operator and reset to step 1.

specimens.prep: - Weigh 150 g of drained, patted-dry tofu on the digital scale; record the mass. - Cut on the board with a sharp knife: trim the block to a 12 mm-thick slab against the 100 mm ruler, cut the slab into 12 mm strips, then cross-cut into 12 mm cubes. - Gauge every cube on the 15 mm checkerboard: each cube must sit inside a 15 mm square. Discard any cube measuring 15 mm or more (that is L7 territory) and any fragment under 8 mm (that is L5). - Do not blend, do not sieve, do not add thickener, do not add water. A 4 mm sieve is a gauge, not a production step, and it cannot enforce a 15 mm limit. - Lay the cubes in a single layer on a white plate, cover with an upturned plate, rest 2 min at room temperature. Blot surface water once with a dry paper towel. - Record: 150 g start, 12 mm cubes, no liquid added, no thickener, sieve not used, blender not used.
specimens.iddsi_test: - 5.1 Fork-pressure — ACTIVE, and the deciding test at L6. Lay one cube flat on the plate, press the fork tines down with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white, hold 1 s, release. Pass = the cube squashes to about half its height, the tines sink in, and the dent remains after the fork is lifted — no spring back, no cracking into dry crumbs. - 5.2 Spoon-tilt — skip: the mapping applies it to L3, L4 and L5 only. An L6 specimen is discrete cut pieces, not a spoonable mass, so a tilt result cannot grade it. - 5.3 Fork-drip — skip: the mapping applies it to L3 and L4 only. There is no pourable phase at L6 and nothing can drip through the tines. - 5.4 Syringe flow — skip: L3 only (8–10 ml remaining at t = 10 s). A 12 mm cube cannot be drawn into a syringe. - Size gate, run before the press test: every cube measures 8–15 mm on the checkerboard.
specimens.visual_qc: - Cubes are clean-cut, matte pale-white, with square corners; no ragged torn faces, no pooled water on the plate. - Cubes hold their shape on the plate without slumping or spreading. - Under fork press the cube compresses visibly and the dent stays after release. - No free liquid film under the cubes after the 2 min rest.
specimens.shots: - firm_tofu_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, three cubes with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. - firm_tofu_L6_take2.jpg — top-down, cube array laid on the checkerboard. - firm_tofu_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, thumbnail blanched. - firm_tofu_L6_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press on one cube, continuous take. - firm_tofu_L6_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: size gate on the checkerboard, then fork pressure.
specimens.fail_modes: - Any cube measures 15 mm or more — re-cut the batch to 12 mm and re-measure on the checkerboard. Never re-sieve and never blend: L6 is cut, not pureed. - Cube springs back to full height after the press (block too firm for L6) — re-make from a softer block (medium-firm tofu that still cuts a clean 12 mm cube) and re-test. Do not add water to soften. - Cube smears to paste or weeps water onto the plate (too soft, drifting toward L5) — re-make from a firmer block, chill 10 min, re-cut to 12 mm and re-test. - Fragments under 8 mm after trimming — re-cut larger to 12 mm; do not mash the trimmings back in. - Batch held over 30 min at room temperature — discard and re-cut fresh.

specimens.prep: 1. Remove tofu from pack, drain packing liquid, pat block dry with paper towel. 2. Starting amount: 200 g whole block, kept intact. Do NOT blend, do NOT sieve, do NOT add thickener or water. Reference specimen for L7 must be the food as normally served. 3. Per the per-level note ("block/slice as served"), cut a single 30 mm × 30 mm × 15 mm slice on the capture board with the 100 mm ruler for scale. Record actual cut dimensions on the data sheet. 4. Keep remaining block chilled for re-takes if needed.
specimens.iddsi_test: - Fork pressure: press the square tines of a standard fork fully into the slice until the tines bend. The slice must NOT break apart, mash, crumble, or pass through the tine gaps. Pass = specimen remains as one cohesive piece under full thumb pressure. - Spoon tilt: tilt a standard spoon 45°. The slice must NOT slide, drip liquid, or fall off. Pass = specimen stays on the spoon. - Fork drip: lift fork with slice clear of the plate for 10 s. Pass = no drips, no liquid runs. - Syringe flow test: NOT applicable (L7 only). State "N/A" on sheet.
specimens.visual_qc: - Slice holds a clean, sharp rectangular edge with no crumbling at corners. - Surface shows smooth, intact skin with no split layers or weeping liquid pooling on the plate. - Block retains original pale ivory colour; no translucent mushy zones at cut faces.

specimens.fail_modes: - Slice smears, splits, or crumbs under fork thumb pressure → under-cooked/soft batch; re-make with a firmer chilled pack and re-record actual supplier code. - Visible liquid pools on plate from cut faces → excess syneresis; drain longer, pat drier, re-cut slice. - Slice bends without breaking and tines sink in fully → L6 not L7; re-make from a denser block, document on sheet.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g braised pork belly including a 1:1 ratio of its cooking sauce and any soft fat. Add 80–100 ml warm water in 20 ml splashes until the pack loosens. Blend on high for 45–60 s, scraping the jar wall at 30 s, until a coarse slurry forms. Push through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any skin or sinew that refuses to pass. Weigh the sieved purée, then stir in thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml as the calibration starting point. Whisk for 20 s, rest 60 s, stir again. If it does not drip slowly through the fork tines, add 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml and re-test; record the actual grams used. The 4 mm sieve step is the floor; finer is fine, coarser is a fail.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: continuous slow drip, no continuous stream, drops ≈1 cm long. Fork pressure with the flat of a tine: the surface blanches but no liquid pools around the prong. Spoon tilt: 5–10 mm slump in 3 s, holds a soft mound. Syringe flow: draw 10 ml, release, 8–10 ml remains at 10 s. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy even brown, no visible meat fibre, skin flecks, or fat beads. Coats the spoon back without running. Holds a shallow pour line on the plate for several seconds.
specimens.shots: braised_pork_belly_L3_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard visible. braised_pork_belly_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. braised_pork_belly_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. braised_pork_belly_L3_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. braised_pork_belly_L3_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI syringe flow, 10 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Thickener under-dosing gives a runny stream through the fork tines and <6 ml syringe residue. Over-dosing gives a stiff mound, no drip, and ≥10 ml residue. Visible meat fibre or skin after sieving. Re-make once with adjusted thickener or by re-blending; second fail, swap the pack.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g braised pork belly with its cooking liquor. Load into the consumer blender. Blend 45 s; stop, scrape the wall, blend 15 s more. Press the pulp through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon; discard any skin or fat that will not pass. Return the sieved puree to the blender, add 40 ml of the reserved liquor, blend 10 s. Spoon a 1 g mound of thickener over the surface, fold in, rest 60 s. If the mound slumps under its own weight, add another 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml and re-fold. Record the final grams-per-100 ml used.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: the four tines leave a clear dent that holds its shape; no puree squeezes up between the tines. Spoon tilt: a heaped teaspoon stays on the spoon when tilted to 45 degrees; it does not slide off in under 10 s. Fork drip: lift the fork; the puree sits as a mound above the tines, nothing drips through the gaps within 10 s. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is glossy and uniform, no visible meat fibre or fat fleck. Colour is even brown from edge to centre. Mound on the spoon holds a soft peak; on the fork it clings as one lump with clean tine marks.
specimens.shots: Shoot in order on the A4 capture kit with the 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. braised_pork_belly_L4_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler+checkerboard visible, spoon in foreground. braised_pork_belly_L4_take2.jpg — top-down on the checkerboard, fork loaded. braised_pork_belly_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press. braised_pork_belly_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. braised_pork_belly_L4_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, fork drip then spoon tilt, 8-12 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Puree flows through the fork gaps → blend another 15 s, sieve again, rest 10 min before retesting. Mound slumps on the spoon tilt → whisk in 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml and re-fold. Grainy texture with visible fibre → re-sieve, do not add water. Any fail: discard, remake from 200 g, record the corrective step.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of braised pork belly including braising liquor. Pick out any leaf-wrapped aromatics or whole spices and discard; keep soft connective tissue and fat. Pulse in the consumer blender for 6-8 s to a coarse mince. Press through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a fork; if more than ~10% stays behind, pulse the retained 10 g portion for 3 s and re-sieve. The soft braising liquor already present supplies moisture; do not add water. Add thickener at 0 g per 100 ml as the calibration starting point — record the actual grams on the card. Mash the sieved mince with the back of the fork until visually uniform.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork tines into a 15 mm mound on a flat plate; the mound must squash, the tines leave a clear imprint, and it must not recover its shape when the fork is removed. Spoon tilt: a heaped 5 ml spoonful must hold its shape on a spoon tilted to 45 degrees and must slide off slowly in one cohesive lump, not run. Fork drip: tilt a fork-load 30 degrees; nothing should drip through the tines.
specimens.visual_qc: The mince on the fork looks wet and glossy, not dry or crumbly. Pieces are visibly separate grains no larger than a match head, sitting in a thin clinging sauce with no free puddle. No intact slabs of fat or skin are visible.
specimens.shots: Stills: 45-degree hero on the capture mat, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard both in frame; top-down of the specimen with checkerboard under the plate; fork-press close-up at the moment tines indent the mound. Clips: 8-12 s of fork-press and spoon-tilt; the full IDDSI test film. Files: braised_pork_belly_L5_take1.jpg, braised_pork_belly_L5_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Fat or skin pieces left above 4 mm: re-sieve, not re-blend first, to avoid paste. Free thin liquid pools on the plate: drain briefly or thicken the retained liquor before re-mixing. Mound springs back after fork press: sieve finer and mash again; do not add water, which will worsen flow.

specimens.prep: Start with 400 g braised pork belly, both lean and fat present. Dice to ≤15 mm pieces on the cutting board using the 100 mm ruler to gauge. Mix lean and fat evenly into each piece. Do not blend — the L6 spec requires intact soft pieces, not a puree. Do not sieve. Do not add water or thickener; L6 is the as-eaten texture. If the pack arrives in large slabs, dice before portioning the 400 g. Weigh the diced 400 g on the digital scale into the capture dish.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test is the primary L6 check. Press the fork tines flat onto a single piece sitting on a plate. The piece must squash, the thumbnail pressed under the fork must blanch white, and the piece must not return to its original shape when the fork is lifted. Repeat on three pieces, mixing lean and fat samples. Spoon tilt: a piece lifted on the spoon and tilted should hold its shape and not drip or fall. Fork drip: lifting a piece on the fork should show no continuous drip through the tines. Pass only if all three pieces squash and do not recover.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces are glossy brown with visible alternating lean and fat layers, edges clearly diced not torn. Each piece sits as a distinct cube on the fork tines, not mashed. Surface sheen from the braise is intact, no separate liquid pooling at the bottom of the dish.
specimens.shots: braised_pork_belly_L6_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, dish centred. braised_pork_belly_L6_take2.jpg — top-down over the dish, checkerboard filling frame. braised_pork_belly_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, thumbnail visible mid-press. braised_pork_belly_L6_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s clip of fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. braised_pork_belly_L6_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, three pieces tested.
specimens.fail_modes: Piece exceeds 15 mm when checked against the checkerboard — re-dice finer. Piece springs back after fork pressure — pieces are too firm, re-dice from a more tender cut or extend braise time on a fresh 400 g batch. Fat layer runs liquid when pressed — pat pieces briefly on absorbent paper, do not reheat.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of braised pork belly straight from the pack at room temperature per the per-level note. Keep slices as braised — do NOT blend, do NOT sieve, do NOT add water or thickener. This is the reference specimen: the food as normally served. If the pack is in one large piece, cut a representative slice about 30 mm × 40 mm × 20 mm thick; measure the thickness with the ruler (18–22 mm acceptable). Before use, confirm the slice holds its cuboidal shape under its own weight for 60 s at room temperature — a slice that slumps within that minute is not an L7 slice. Record starting mass and the cut dimensions on the sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure (the only IDDSI test that applies at L7): press a standard metal fork down on the slice with the thumb until the nail blanches white, then lift. Pass = the slice does not mash flat and does not break apart under that pressure: the tines score the surface, the score mark persists and does not fill back in, but the tines do not pass through the thickness; the piece keeps its cuboidal shape and must be cut with a knife or chewed to break down; no liquid runs off it. A slice that squashes flat, breaks into soft crumbs, or slumps off the fork is L6, not L7. Spoon tilt (L3–L5), fork drip (L3–L4) and the syringe flow test (L3 only) do not apply at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: Slice holds its cuboidal braised shape — 30 mm × 40 mm × 20 mm, every dimension ≥15 mm — with visible skin, fat, and lean layers; glossy dark sauce coats but does not pool excessively on the fork. A second look should show no soft collapse when the fork lifts the piece — if it slumps or mashes, it is failing toward L6.
specimens.shots: 3 stills, naming braised_pork_belly_L7_take1.jpg, _take2.jpg, _take3.jpg: 45-degree hero shot, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, sauce glistening visible; top-down with full checkerboard; tight fork-press close-up mid-press with blanched thumbnail and the tine score mark in the slice. 2 clips, naming braised_pork_belly_L7_take1.mp4 and _take2.mp4: 8-12 s fork-press to completion (press, lift, inspect the mark); continuous IDDSI test film covering the fork-pressure test in one take.
specimens.fail_modes: Slice spreads, slumps under its own weight, or mashes flat under fork pressure → too tender for L7, failing toward L6; re-cut at the full 20 mm thickness from the firmer centre of the pack and re-shoot. If a 20 mm centre slice still slumps or mashes, that pack cannot produce L7 by bench manipulation — record the specimen as L6 and re-shoot from a firmer pack; do not relabel an L6 slice as L7. Sauce runs or pools on the piece → dab with a paper towel before shooting; the slice must not sit in free sauce. Tines fail to score the surface and the slice springs back with no mark → the slice is tougher than the braised L7 reference (under-braised, or cut from a dry part); a thicker cut cannot fix toughness — re-braise longer until the tines score, or take the slice from the middle of the pack.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g steamed peeled shrimp on the scale. Add to blender with 80 ml cool water. Blend on high for 45 seconds. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any retained solids. Weigh the sieved puree and add thickener at 3.0 g per 100 ml as the calibration starting point (record the actual grams used; per-level note requires blend-thin, so adjust downward by 0.2 g increments if the mixture is too stiff). Stir 30 seconds, rest 2 minutes, stir again. Re-weigh final specimen and note total volume in ml.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: pressing the fork against a white plate leaves a clear pattern; the groove does not close. Spoon tilt: the specimen slides slowly off a tilted spoon, not a runny pour. Fork drip: drips slowly in continuous blobs through the tines, not a steady stream. Syringe flow test: fill to 10 ml, release; after 10 seconds, 8-10 ml remains in the syringe. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is smooth, glossy, and uniform pink-white with no visible shrimp chunks or fiber specks. Coats the spoon back in an even layer without dripping off the edge. Holds a soft mound on a flat plate for 2-3 seconds before slowly spreading.
specimens.shots: Still 1, 45-degree hero: bowl on A4 kit, ruler and checkerboard in frame. Still 2, top-down: checkerboard centered under bowl. Still 3, fork-press close-up: mid-press, grooves visible. Clip 1, 8-12 seconds: fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous take. Clip 2: full 10-second syringe flow test, timer visible. Files: steamed_shrimp_peeled_L3_take1.jpg and steamed_shrimp_peeled_L3_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thick: syringe retains more than 10 ml; remake with 0.2 g less thickener. Grainy texture from incomplete blending: re-blend 15 seconds and re-sieve. Syneresis or weeping on standing: discard and remake with a slightly higher thickener dose.

specimens.prep: Weigh 120 g steamed peeled shrimp on the scale. Add 60 ml hot water (just off boil). Blend on high for 45-60 s until completely smooth, scraping the bowl once at 30 s. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve, pressing with the back of a spoon; discard retained solids. Add 1.5 g thickener per 100 ml of puree as the calibration starting point; stir in, rest 2 min, re-stir. Record the actual grams used. Target mass ~170-180 g.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: mound holds shape; pressing with fork base leaves a clean indent that does not close, no separation of liquid. Pass = indent clearly visible, puree stays mounded. Spoon tilt: a standard spoon tilted 45 degrees holds the puree on the bowl without sliding. Pass = zero flow off the spoon. Fork drip: lift fork vertically through the puree; puree sits in a mound above the tines and does not drip or run between prongs. Pass = mound intact, tines not visible through liquid.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform pale pink-cream color with no visible shrimp flecks or shell specks. Matte, glossy surface with no free liquid pooling on the plate. Smooth, spreadable but holds peaks when scooped.
specimens.shots: Still 1: steamed_shrimp_peeled_L4_take1.jpg - 45-degree hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame, full bowl. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard flat beside bowl. Still 3: fork-press close-up, fork at mid-press. Clip 1: steamed_shrimp_peeled_L4_take1.mp4, 8-12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt. Clip 2: IDDSI test film, full fork-drip + spoon-tilt sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Grainy texture with shrimp specks after sieving = re-blend 15 s and re-sieve. Puree flows through fork tines or runs off spoon = add 0.3-0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 2 min, retest. Separate liquid pooling on plate = blend longer or drain excess water before thickening.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed peeled shrimp onto the plate. Mash with the fork until no piece exceeds 4 mm; pick out and measure the largest particle against the 100 mm ruler or push the mash through the 4 mm sieve, discarding anything retained. Do not blend — blending releases thin liquid and collapses the L5 particle structure, and the per-level note requires minced ≤ 4 mm, not puréed. Moisten with 30 ml warm water per 100 g mash and stir until the mash holds together but no free liquid pools on the plate. Add 0 g thickener at this level; thickener is the L3 calibration starting point only — record the actual grams used (0 g for L5). Target final specimen ≈ 230 g.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines into the specimen until the thumbnail blanches; the mash must squash and not spring back, and the slots between tines must hold material without it running through. Spoon-tilt test: a heaped spoon tilted to 45° must hold its shape — no slide, no drip. Fork-drip test: lifting the fork, nothing must drip continuously through the tines. All three must pass to confirm L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a soft, cohesive mound sitting in the tine gaps with a glossy moist sheen, never wet or weeping. On the spoon: a soft peak that slumps only when tilted past 45°. No orange pooling liquid around the mash on the plate.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen mounded on plate. Still 2 — top-down, checkerboard under the plate, full specimen footprint visible. Still 3 — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines loaded. Clip 1 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous take. Clip 2 — IDDSI test film: fork-pressure, spoon-tilt, fork-drip. Files: steamed_shrimp_peeled_L5_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-blending produces a smooth purée that flows through fork slots — fail, re-mash a new batch from intact shrimp. Insufficient mashing leaves particles > 4 mm; sieve and remove oversize or re-mash. Excess water creates a separate thin layer on the plate — drain briefly and re-test; if persistent, re-make with 20 ml water per 100 g.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed peeled shrimp on the scale. Confirm each piece is already ≤15 mm; trim any oversized pieces with a knife. Do not blend — shrimp is naturally soft at this cook, and blending creates a puree. Do not sieve — no skin or fibrous material to remove. Do not add thickener — L6 is not a thickened level. Do not add water. Plate directly from the steamer onto the capture surface.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test (L6): press the fork tines fully into a shrimp piece until the thumbnail blanches white, then release. Pass: the piece squashes and does not recover its shape. Fork-drip test (applies only if any liquid pools): tilt the fork. Pass: very little drip runs through the tines, none falls off in a steady stream. Spoon-tilt test: if the piece sits in liquid on the spoon, tilt. Pass: cohesive, does not flow off freely. No syringe flow test — that is for L3 only.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork, a correct piece is opaque pink-white, moist but not weeping, and holds a soft rounded shape. On the plate, pieces look intact, none reduced to paste, no free liquid pooling beyond a thin sheen.
specimens.shots: still_1 steamed_shrimp_peeled_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. still_2 steamed_shrimp_peeled_L6_take1.jpg — top-down on checkerboard, multiple pieces spread. still_3 steamed_shrimp_peeled_L6_take1.jpg — fork-press close-up, thumbnail blanching mid-press. clip_1 steamed_shrimp_peeled_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork-press plus spoon-tilt in one continuous take. clip_2 steamed_shrimp_peeled_L6_take1.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, audio off, hands and specimen centred.
specimens.fail_modes: Firm or rubbery texture after steaming: re-steam 1–2 minutes and re-test; if still firm, note as failed and re-make. Piece exceeds 15 mm: trim or cut and re-test that piece. Piece collapses to paste under fork pressure: record failure, do not re-make as L6 — would belong to L4/L5 with thickener.

specimens.prep: Bought form (BASE_FOOD_LIST BF19): fresh or frozen peeled shrimp, steamed. Allergen: **crustacean** — confirm against the pack label; wash down tray, fork and scale before the next food. Weigh 200 g of raw peeled shrimp on the 0.1 g digital scale and record the actual mass. Steam in a basket over boiling water for 5–7 min (start at 6 min), stopping when the flesh is opaque pink-white and just firm; do not overcook. Drain 30 s on paper towel, cool 2 min on the plate. Plate 3 whole shrimp beside the capture kit and record the plated mass. Do NOT blend. Do NOT sieve — no 4 mm sieve is used at L7 (it is the L5 particle gauge and cannot size a ≥15 mm piece). Do NOT add thickener, water or any liquid. Per-level note "whole as steamed" applies: the specimen is the intact cooked shrimp exactly as served.
specimens.iddsi_test: ACTIVE at L7 — **5.1 fork pressure**: place a whole shrimp on the tray and press the bowl of the standard metal fork down with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass = the shrimp squashes/compresses under that pressure, changes shape, and does not recover its shape when the fork is lifted (clear deformation, no spring-back). Camera must show food, utensil action and result in one unbroken take. Ruler sizing check in the same take (a size check, not an IDDSI flow test): hold one shrimp against the 100 mm ruler — each specimen piece is a single whole shrimp ≥15 mm. NOT APPLICABLE AT L7 — named only so the test set is unambiguous: - Spoon tilt (5.2): **skip** — 5.2 applies at L3, L4, L5 only; log `tests.spoon_tilt = null`. Not performed, no pass/fail recorded. - Fork drip (5.3): **skip** — 5.3 applies at L3, L4 only; log `tests.fork_drip = null`. Not performed, no pass/fail recorded. - Syringe flow (5.4): **skip** — 5.4 is required for every L3 only (8–10 ml remaining at t=10 s); log `tests.flow_ml_remaining = null`. Not performed at L7. L7 is decided on fork pressure plus the ≥15 mm whole-piece check; flow behaviour is not an L7 criterion.
specimens.visual_qc: Whole peeled shrimp, intact C-shape, no breakage at the bend. Surface opaque pink-white, matte-dry, light surface moisture only, no pooled liquid on the plate. Each shrimp sits across the fork tines without falling through and measures ≥15 mm against the 100 mm ruler. 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler fully in frame, specimen beside them, never covering them.
specimens.shots: Capture kit (15 mm checkerboard + 100 mm ruler) flat on the tray, left edge in frame, never cropped. steamed_shrimp_peeled_L7_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 2–3 whole shrimp fanned, ruler + checkerboard visible. steamed_shrimp_peeled_L7_take2.jpg — top-down over the checkerboard, one whole shrimp centred. steamed_shrimp_peeled_L7_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines visibly deforming the shrimp, thumbnail blanched. steamed_shrimp_peeled_L7_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-pressure action clip, one unbroken take. steamed_shrimp_peeled_L7_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: the fork-pressure sequence with voiceover of the pass criteria.
specimens.fail_modes: (a) Shrimp springs back fully under fork pressure (rubbery) — under-steamed, too firm for L7; steam a fresh 200 g batch 2–3 min longer and re-test (softer → toward L7). (b) Shrimp turns mushy and pasty and no longer holds as a whole ≥15 mm piece — over-steamed, reads toward L6/L5; discard and steam a fresh 200 g batch for 5–7 min only, stopping at just opaque (firmer → toward L7). (c) Shrimp measures under 15 mm — reads L6, not L7; re-portion using a larger shrimp size (e.g. 26/30 count) so every piece is ≥15 mm. Never chop, mash or blend smaller to "fix" it — that moves toward L6/L5. (d) Liquid pools on the plate — pat the shrimp dry with paper towel before shooting; do not re-cook and do not add liquid.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed spare ribs (meat only, bones removed). Add 120 ml warm water to the blender jar first, then ribs. Blend 45 s on high. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard solids retained. Measure the sieved volume. Add thickener at the calibration starting point of 4.0 g per 100 ml of liquid; whisk in, rest 90 s, re-whisk. If the sample pours when the cup tilts, it is too thin; if it mounds and does not drip from the fork, it is too thick. Record the actual thickener mass and final volume on the capture sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: hold fork horizontal 1 cm above the cup; liquid drips in slow, continuous drops within 10 s — pass. Spoon tilt: spoon tilted 45 degrees lets the sample flow off in a slow ribbon, not a pour and not a stack — pass. Fork pressure: tines pressed into 1 cm of sample leave a clear impression that does not refill — pass. Syringe flow: fill to 10 ml, release; 8-10 ml remain after 10 s — pass. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface looks matte and smooth, no lumps, no meat fibres. Holds a soft peak on the fork that slowly slumps. No free liquid pools around the specimen on the plate.
specimens.shots: Still 1: steamed_spare_ribs_black_L3_take1.jpg, 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2: steamed_spare_ribs_black_L3_take1.jpg, top-down on A4, checkerboard visible. Still 3: steamed_spare_ribs_black_L3_take1.jpg, fork tines pressed mid-action into specimen. Clip 1: steamed_spare_ribs_black_L3_take1.mp4, 8-12 s fork press plus spoon tilt. Clip 2: steamed_spare_ribs_black_L3_take1.mp4, 10 ml syringe flow test, 10 s real time.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: drips in a stream from fork, syringe leaves under 8 ml — add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, rest, retest. Too stiff: mounds on spoon, no drip, syringe leaves over 10 ml — thin with 5-10 ml water, retest. Fibrous: strands catch on sieve or fork tines — re-blend 20 s and re-sieve; if still fibrous, the food is unsuitable at L3.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g cooked ribs with 80 ml pan juices. Blend on high for 45 s, scrape, blend 30 s more. Press through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; L4 is lump-free, so the purée must pass and the mesh must run clean. Discard any fibre that will not pass and weigh it: residue must not exceed 5 g (2.5 % of the 200 g input). Record the residue mass in the log — this is a hard limit, not a note that the step is incomplete. If residue exceeds 5 g, blend a further 20 s and re-sieve once; if it still exceeds 5 g, do not proceed — discard the batch and re-make. Weigh the sieved purée (target 270–275 g). Add thickener at 1.5 g per 100 g of purée as the calibration starting point; whisk in, rest 2 min, re-weigh and record the actual grams used. Target final mass ≈ 275–285 g, smooth, glossy, no visible meat fibre.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: a full fork pressed into the surface for 5 s leaves a clear, persistent dent without the purée spreading or breaking; surface does not flow to refill the gap. Spoon tilt: a heaped teaspoon held over a plate does not drip, slide, or pour when tilted 45°, then 90°; the mound holds shape. Fork drip: lifting a loaded fork, no thin liquid drips through the tines; purée sits as a mound on top of the tines. No flow-test syringe required at L4.
specimens.visual_qc: Mound sits proud of the fork tines, no thin-liquid drip. Spoon tilt holds a clean profile with no slumping or pooling on the plate. Surface is uniform, glossy, mid-brown, no meat fibre or black-bean skins visible.

specimens.fail_modes: Mound slumps on spoon tilt or thin liquid drips through the fork → too thin, add thickener 0.5 g per 100 g of purée (≈1.4 g for this batch), rest 2 min, and retest. Visible fibre or bean skins in the finished purée, or sieve residue above 5 g → re-blend 20 s and re-sieve; do not proceed until the mesh runs clean. Puree cracks or splits under fork pressure → too thick, whisk in 10 ml pan juices and retest.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g steamed ribs on the scale. Strip meat from bone; discard bones and excess fat. Place meat in blender; pulse 6 s, scrape, pulse 4 s — coarse mince only, target lumps 3–4 mm with no particle larger than 4 mm. Sieve 4 mm as a GAUGE: press the mince through with the back of a spoon and reject the overs; the mince must still read as mince — if most of it drops through as a smooth purée the specimen is L4, not L5, so re-make from a fresh 250 g batch with shorter pulses. You should have 180–200 g sieved mince; below 170 g means the sieve took too much, re-mince rather than continue. Reserve 60 ml of the cooking juices separately. Fold 30 ml juices through the mince to moisten; if it clumps dry, add 5 ml juice at a time up to 50 ml total — final specimen 230–250 g including juice. No thickener at L5. Per-level note "mince meat <= 4 mm with juices" is satisfied; do not over-blend to a paste.
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable tests at L5: 4 mm sieve as gauge (PREP), spoon tilt, fork pressure as a supporting check only. Spoon tilt (primary): load 5 ml on a spoon and tilt to 45°; the heap must slide off in one mass with no run-off of thin liquid. Pass. Fork pressure (supporting check only — record it, do not use it as the pass criterion): press fork tines into a 15 mm heap (~10 g) on the plate until the thumbnail blanches; the heap must squash and not spring back. Fork drip: NOT APPLICABLE at L5 — §5.3 scopes fork-drip to L3/L4, so do not run it. No syringe flow test at L5.
specimens.visual_qc: Minced particles clearly visible but none larger than a checkerboard square (4 mm); the pile reads as coarse 3–4 mm lumps, not paste. Surface glistens wet; no pooling liquid on the plate. Fork lifts a cohesive mound, not a smear.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. Still 2 — top-down, checkerboard only. Still 3 — fork-press close-up mid-press, particles visible. Clip 1 — 8–12 s spoon-tilt then supporting fork-press, continuous. Clip 2 — full IDDSI test film: load, tilt, press. Files: steamed_spare_ribs_black_L5_take1.jpg / .mp4, increment take on reshoot.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-blended to paste — loses L5 texture; re-make, pulse only. Mince passes the sieve as purée with no visible lumps — reads as L4; re-make from raw, knife-chopped 3–4 mm lumps, sieve as gauge only. Particles exceed 4 mm — rejected by sieve; re-mince the overs. Fat pools free on the plate — separates thin liquid; drain surface and fold in dry mince to absorb. Re-make rule: any fail means discard and start a fresh 250 g batch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed ribs. Strip meat off bone; discard bone and gristle per per-level note. Hand-dice meat on board to cubes ≤15 mm; target 8-12 mm pieces. Do not blend and do not sieve — dicing is required at L6. No thickener and no added liquid: this specimen is calibrated dry on the meat; operator records actual final weight (g) and piece count from a 10 g scoop. If a piece measures >15 mm on the ruler, re-dice; if bone fragment is found, re-pick.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test only: press fork tines onto a piece on the plate until thumbnail blanches white. Pass when the piece squashes, does not spring back, and splits rather than rebounds. Repeat on the largest piece in the sample; if the largest passes, the batch passes. Spoon tilt is not the deciding test here but confirm a scoop sits as a moist pile, not a dry crumble or a runny pool. Fork drip is not applicable at L6 — record "N/A, L6".
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces should be glossy dark-brown, wet but not pooling sauce, with visible fibrous flake at the cut face. They should hold shape on the fork without sliding off, and a pressed piece should leave a clear wet thumb-mark on the plate. No dry crumb edges, no bone shards, no whole-peppercorn-sized lumps >15 mm.
specimens.shots: Steamed_spare_ribs_black_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. Take 2: top-down on checkerboard. Take 3: fork-press close-up mid-press. Steamed_spare_ribs_black_L6_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt clip. Take 2 .mp4 — full IDDSI test film, audio of "press, hold, release".
specimens.fail_modes: Piece >15 mm on ruler → re-dice and re-shoot. Bone or gristle fleck spotted → re-pick entire batch, discard, re-shoot. Piece springs back under fork → meat undercooked or over-diced to mince; re-steam a fresh portion and re-dice.

specimens.prep: Use one steamed rib portion exactly as received, meat on bone. Record starting mass on the digital scale; aim for 120–160 g including bone. Do not blend. Do not sieve — an L7 specimen is never reduced below 15 mm. Do not add water, liquid, or thickener. The per-level note requires meat on bone, so processing is not performed: the operator photographs the whole piece as served and keeps the bone-in piece intact for the tests. If the portion arrives cold, steam covered 4–5 min until the meat core reaches 70–75 °C on a probe and no longer — longer steaming tenderises the meat toward L6. Size check: measure the thickest meat cross-section with the 100 mm ruler; every meat dimension must be ≥15 mm, and the meat must be firm, fibrous, and require chewing. Record the measured dimensions in mm on the capture sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable at L7: fork pressure only (§5.1). Spoon tilt (§5.2) and fork drip (§5.3) are L3–L5 tests and must not be run, filmed, or recorded at L7. No syringe flow test above L3 (§5.4).  Fork pressure test: press the meatiest non-bone section with the fork tines, normal thumb pressure, until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass = the meat does NOT compress, squash, or change shape; any indentation springs back and the meat does not hold the fork mark, and it does not flake apart under the tines. Fail = the meat squashes and holds a deep indentation, or breaks into flakes — that is an L6 texture, not L7. L7 is passed when fork pressure passes and the ≥15 mm size check in PREP is recorded.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork the meat shows visible fibre separation with a moist, glossy black-bean coating, no pooled liquid at the fork base or on the plate. On the plate the rib keeps its served shape, bone exposed, sauce clinging, not runny. No lasting fork indentation.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, bone visible. Still 2: top-down on checkerboard, whole rib centred. Still 3: fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into meat, ruler edge in shot. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press then release, slow, rebound visible. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film — the fork-pressure test plus the 15 mm size check in one continuous take. Files: steamed_spare_ribs_black_L7_take1.jpg, _take2.jpg, _take3.jpg, _take4.mp4, _take5.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Sauce runs off and pools on the plate — blot the excess sauce with paper towel and re-shoot; if the sauce is still runny, remake with a fresh portion. Meat falls cleanly off the bone before pressure, or squashes flat and holds the indentation, or splits into puree-like mash under the fork — too tender for L7. Do NOT re-steam or reheat further, which tenderises it more: pick a firmer piece from the pack or remake with a fresh portion, then re-test. Meat cross-section under 15 mm — fails the L7 size check; select a larger piece and re-shoot. Meat dry, tough, and stringy with no fibre separation — not a regular L7 texture; discard and remake with a fresh portion.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched choy sum stems and leaves. Blend with 120 ml water for 45 s, scrape, blend 30 s more. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard fibre that will not pass (the per-level note requires blend-thin, so a coarse sieve pass is not optional). Weigh the sieved puree. Add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml of puree — this is the calibration starting point only; record the actual grams used so the ratio is reproducible. Stir with the fork 30 s, rest 2 min, stir again. The spec must pour in a slow ribbon, drip through the fork tines in a continuous thin stream, and read 8-10 ml in the IDDSI syringe at 10 s. If any check fails, add thickener in 0.5 g per 100 ml increments, rest 2 min, retest.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: the tines leave a clear, persistent line in the surface and the puree does not regain shape when the fork is lifted — pass. Spoon tilt: the puree flows off the tilted spoon in a slow, continuous ribbon within 4 s — pass. Fork drip: a thin, continuous drip falls through the tine gaps; no sitting blob — pass. Syringe flow test (Level 3 specific): fill the 10 ml syringe, release, wait 10 s; 8-10 ml remain in the barrel — pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface holds a fork-tine imprint for at least 3 s. Tilting the spoon produces a smooth ribbon that breaks at about 3-4 cm, not a splat. Colour is uniform pale green with no visible fibre flecks after sieving.
