Still 2 — top-down, checkerboard under the bowl: blanched_choy_sum_L3_take2.jpg. Still 3 — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines half-submerged: blanched_choy_sum_L3_take3.jpg. Clip 1 — 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one take: blanched_choy_sum_L3_take1.mp4. Clip 2 — full IDDSI syringe flow test, timer visible: blanched_choy_sum_L3_take2.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Runny — too thin for Level 3, drips through syringe leaving under 8 ml: remake, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, retest. Sticky / gummy — holds shape on the spoon or blocks the syringe above 10 ml: thin by whisking in 5 ml water per 100 ml puree, retest. Stringy — visible fibre strands after sieving: re-blend 20 s and re-sieve; if strands persist, the specimen fails and must be remade from fresh.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched choy sum stems and leaves on the digital scale. Cut into 2 cm pieces. Add to consumer blender with 60 ml cool water; blend 45 s on high. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using a spoon; discard fibrous residue retained on mesh — at L4 the sieve is a production step, not a gauge, because L4 must be lump-free. Return sieved puree to blender; blend 30 s more. Transfer to a bowl and weigh the sieved puree in grams. Mix in thickener at 2.0 g per 100 g of sieved puree (calibration starting point — record the actual mass used on the run sheet). Stir with fork 20 s, rest 60 s, stir 10 s. The mixture must hold its shape on a spoon without spreading. Note: sieving is mandatory; choy sum fibres cannot be softened to L4 by blending alone — if fibres remain stringy after the sieve pass, the batch fails and must be re-made from a fresh 200 g portion blanched 60 s longer to soften the fibre; it must not be rescued by re-blending the failed batch.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press fork tines into the mound until the tines blanch; surface must hold the impression with no surrounding liquid pooling. Pass: clean imprint, no flow. Spoon tilt test: load a spoon, tilt 45 degrees over a plate; specimen must sit, not slide or drip. Pass: stays on spoon or drops as one piece. Fork drip test: lift forkful 5 cm above plate; puree must sit in a mound on the tines, not drip through. Pass: no continuous drip within 10 s. L4 requires no separate thin liquid; a small bead on the spoon is acceptable, a puddle is not. No syringe flow test at L4: syringe flow applies to L3 only.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: matte, even green, no visible fibre strands, no water weeping. On the spoon: rounded mound, edges hold sharp, slight gloss only at the very peak.

Still 2: blanched_choy_sum_L4_take1_02.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, spoon and fork laid parallel. specimens.fail_modes: 1. Stringy fibres visible after the sieve — the fibre cannot be blended away; re-make with a fresh 200 g portion blanched 60 s longer to soften it, blend 45 s, and sieve once through the 4 mm mesh. Do not simply re-blend and re-sieve the failed batch, and do not pass a specimen with visible strands. 2. Specimen flows through fork tines — too wet; whisk in 0.5 g thickener per 100 g, rest 60 s, retest. 3. Specimen cracks or crumbles on spoon tilt — too thick; whisk in 5 ml water per 100 g and retest.

specimens.prep: Start with 300 g blanched choy sum, drained, patted dry on a clean cloth. Chop the stems and leaves together with a knife until the largest pieces are no more than 4 mm; discard any stalk core that resists chopping. Do not force the whole mass through the 4 mm sieve — L5 is a lumpy level (lumps ~4 mm) and sieving it makes it lump-free L4. Use the 4 mm sieve as a gauge only: hold a pinch of chopped mash against it, and any piece larger than a 4 mm hole goes back on the board to be re-chopped. Weigh the chopped mash and record the grams. Press and smear with a fork in a circular motion for 60-90 seconds until it holds together as a coarse mash with visible flecks but no whole leaves. Sprinkle 3 g thickener per 100 g of mash, fold in with the fork, rest 60 seconds, then re-mash briefly. The thickener must bind moisture only — the ~4 mm lumps and flecks must stay visible and distinct after it is folded in. Add 10-15 ml warm water only if the mash is crumbly; the final mix must feel moist but not wet, and must show no separate thin liquid. Record actual thickener grams and water ml on the card.
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable at L5 (CAPTURE_PROTOCOL §5.2, with §5.1 as a supporting check only): spoon tilt is the deciding test; fork pressure is a supporting check. Fork drip and syringe flow are L3/L4 tests and must not be run at L5. Spoon tilt: a teaspoon-sized portion must hold its shape on the spoon when tilted to 45 degrees without sliding off or dripping; slight slumping is acceptable, collapse is not. Fork pressure (supporting check only): press the tines flat onto the mash for 5 seconds; the mash must squash, the surface must blanch pale, and it must not spring back when the fork is lifted. All applicable tests must pass; if any fails, re-mash or re-thicken, do not film.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: cohesive clump, no loose bits falling, surface shows green flecks and lumps up to ~4 mm with no whole leaf blades and no smooth glossy paste (a smooth, paste-glossy surface means the specimen is L4, not L5). On the spoon: holds a rounded mound, slight sheen from moisture, no pooling liquid at the rim.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, mash mounded on the white plate, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2: top-down on the same plate with checkerboard visible. Still 3: fork-press close-up, tines mid-press, squash visible. Clip 1: 8-12 s showing fork-press then spoon-tilt in one take. Clip 2: full IDDSI test sequence, 15-20 s, slow enough to see recovery or non-recovery. Name the files blanched_choy_sum_L5_take1 through take5 with .jpg or .mp4 — one filename per shot.
specimens.fail_modes: Mash too wet: a watery halo forms on the plate; add 1 g thickener per 100 g, rest, re-mash, re-film. Pieces too coarse: stalks remain larger than the 4 mm holes of the gauge sieve; re-chop and re-check, do not patch with extra water. Mash too dry and crumbly: fork-pressure leaves clean tine marks without squashing; add 5 ml water and 0.5 g thickener, re-mash, re-test. Mash has gone smooth and glossy with no visible lumps: the specimen is now L4, not L5 — reduce the thickener by 0.5 g per 100 g and re-mash; if the flecks and lumps cannot be brought back, restart the batch with fresh blanched greens.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched choy sum stems only. Stack leaves; discard or reserve off-spec. Cut stems across the grain into 15 mm pieces — do not exceed 15 mm in any dimension. Blanch 90 s in rolling water, drain, pat dry on a clean cloth. No blender, no sieve, no thickener, no added liquid for this level. Confirm each piece sits flat under a ruler; any oversize piece is trimmed.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press fork tines against one piece until thumbnail blanches white. The piece must squash, hold the pressed shape, and not spring back. Pass = full squash with zero recovery across 3 pieces tested. Fork-drip test: lift 4 pieces on fork tines; no liquid must drip through the tines within 10 s. Spoon-tilt test is not the gate for L6 but confirm any soft residue on the spoon stays cohesive and does not flow.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces sit cleanly on the fork tines without sagging through gaps. Cut faces show compact, uniform green-white flesh with no fibrous strings. Pressed piece retains a clean thumbprint edge and stays as one mass.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45° hero: 15–20 pieces fanned on matte plate, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, scale reading visible. Still 2 — top-down: checkerboard fills frame, pieces arranged in a single layer. Still 3 — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines clearly indenting the piece. Clip 1 — 8–12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt. Clip 2 — IDDSI test film, full fork-pressure sequence on three pieces. Files: blanched_choy_sum_L6_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Any piece over 15 mm — re-trim, re-shoot. Fibrous strands that resist fork-pressure squash — re-cut thinner, re-blanch 30 s. Piece springs back after press — downgrade to L7 or re-cut against grain. Re-make before re-shooting; never edit around a fail.

specimens.prep: Use whole blanched choy sum stalks as served, no cutting, no blending, no sieving, no thickener, no added liquid. Working mass 80–120 g per specimen; record actual mass on the scale. Keep stems intact so the fork-press lands on the natural stalk cross-section. Do not reprocess — L7 requires the food as normally served, and the per-level note explicitly keeps stalks as blanched.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press a standard fork flat onto a stalk with thumb pressure equal to pressing your thumbnail to blanch white. Pass when the stalk flattens, splits, or breaks; it must not return to its original shape. Spoon tilt: scoop a stalk and tilt the spoon 45 degrees; pass if the piece sits on the spoon without flowing or dripping. Fork drip: lift a stalk from the liquid and hold over a fork; pass when no liquid runs through the fork prongs in drips. No syringe test at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: Stalk sits flat on the fork tines without sagging. Cut end shows distinct fibrous rings under bright light. Surface holds a slight natural sheen from blanching, not a pooled sauce film.
specimens.shots: Stills: blanched_choy_sum_L7_take1.jpg hero at 45 degrees with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard both in frame; take2.jpg top-down with checkerboard under the plate; take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press, tines visible. Clips: take1.mp4 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one cut; take2.mp4 IDDSI test film, fork-pressure pass followed by fork-drip check.
specimens.fail_modes: Stalk bends but springs back — under-blanched, too elastic, re-blanch 20 s and retest. Stalk crushes to mush — over-blanched, discard and use a fresher bundle. Liquid pools and drips continuously through the fork — reassess as L6 or below, re-classify, do not label L7.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g blanched bok choy (drained). Add 60 ml water. Blend 45 s on high; stop, scrape down, blend 30 s more. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; press with the back of a spoon to extract purée, discard coarse fibre. Measure 200 ml purée. Add thickener at the calibration starting point of 2.0 g per 100 ml (record actual mass used). Stir 30 s, rest 60 s, stir 15 s. Re-weigh total specimen and record.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift fork tines 5 cm; purée drips slowly in a thick continuous ribbon, falls in ≤3 drops over 10 s. Pass = ribbon + ≤3 drops. Fork pressure: press fork tines fully into specimen; tines leave a clear impression and purée does not flow back to level. Pass = clear imprint retained. Spoon tilt: spoon a heaped teaspoon, tilt to 45°; specimen slides slowly off in one cohesive mound, not a pour. Pass = slides as a mound. IDDSI flow test: fill 10 ml syringe, cap tip, invert, release after 10 s. Pass = 8-10 ml remaining (i.e. only 1-2 ml flowed out).
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform pale-green purée, no visible leaf fragments or fibre. Coats the back of a spoon in an even, opaque layer with no run-through. Hangs from fork tines as a continuous ribbon before falling. No free liquid pooling at the rim of the container.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45° hero: specimen in shallow dish, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2 — top-down: dish flat, checkerboard only. Still 3 — fork-press close-up, tines half-pressed into specimen. Clip 1 — 8-12 s: fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous take. Clip 2 — IDDSI syringe flow test, 10 s timed. Name files blanched_bok_choy_L3_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: re-add thickener in 0.2 g/100 ml increments, retest. Too thick / does not drip from fork: thin with water in 5 ml steps, retest. Visible fibre after sieving: re-blend 20 s and re-sieve; if fibre persists, L3 is not achievable for this batch — re-make with a finer sieve or switch food.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched bok choy (drained). Add 60 ml warm water. Blend 45 s on high; scrape down; blend 30 s more. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard fibrous residue. Return purée to blender with 2.0 g thickener per 100 ml as the calibration starting point; record the actual mass used. Blend 20 s, rest 60 s, blend 10 s. Adjust: +0.5 g thickener per 100 ml if it flows through fork tines; -0.3 g per 100 ml if it cracks on the spoon. Re-blend 15 s after any adjustment.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: a 4 mm-wide mound holds its shape when the fork presses to 1 cm above the plate without squashing flat. Pass criterion: clean edges, no liquid bleed. Spoon tilt: a 4 ml scoop on a 1 cm spoon sits and slowly slides only 1-2 cm before stopping. Pass criterion: mounded, not liquid, not stiff. Fork drip: mound rests above tines with no drip in 10 s. Pass criterion: no drop falls; gloss only on tine surface.
specimens.visual_qc: Matte sheen, uniform pale-green, no leaf flecks or fibres. Mound holds sharp ridges from fork tines. No puddle forming around the base on the white plate.
specimens.shots: Still 1 - 45° hero: mound on white spoon, ruler (mm side up) and 15 mm checkerboard in lower frame. Still 2 - top-down: mound centred, checkerboard filling one quadrant, ruler along right edge. Still 3 - fork-press close-up mid-press: tines entering mound to 1 cm depth. Clip 1 - 8-12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous move. Clip 2 - IDDSI test film: full fork-drip sequence, 10 s timer visible. Name all files blanched_bok_choy_L4_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Visible green fibres or seed specks → re-sieve and re-blend. Mound slumps below tine tops within 5 s → add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, re-blend, re-test. Liquid ring forms at base → too wet, re-blend with extra 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml. Re-make from raw if any two tests still fail after two adjustments.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched bok choy on the scale. Pat dry briefly with paper towel, then chop finely with a chef's knife on a board, aiming for pieces under 4 mm in every dimension. The per-level note permits water moistening; add 20 ml warm water and mash with a fork until the mass is cohesive, no separate thin liquid pools on the board, and no piece exceeds 4 mm when checked against the 4 mm sieve. Sieve a small scoop to confirm; if any fragment sits on top of the mesh, rec chop that portion and re-mash. Do not blend — the per-level note calls for fork-mash, not puree, and a consumer blender would over-process this leaf into a pourable fluid. No thickener; L5 does not calibrate thickener, so do not add any.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the flat of the fork into a heaped teaspoon of specimen with firm thumb pressure until the thumbnail blanches white. The specimen must squash, the fork tines leave a clear imprint, and the food must NOT spring back when the fork is lifted. Spoon-tilt test: tilt a teaspoon 45 degrees; the specimen should hold together as one mass and slide off slowly in a single clump, not flow, drip, or run. Fork-drip test: lift a loaded fork; no thin liquid should drip through the tines within 10 seconds.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a coarse, granular mash with visible green flecks, glistening with moisture but not glossy or soupy. On the spoon: holds a peaked mound without slumping; no standing liquid in the spoon bowl. Color stays bok-choy green-white, not pale yellow-green from over-blanching.
specimens.shots: blanched_bok_choy_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame. blanched_bok_choy_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. blanched_bok_choy_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. blanched_bok_choy_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press + spoon-tilt. blanched_bok_choy_L5_film.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen recovers shape after fork press → too dry or chopped too coarse; re-mash with 5 ml water per 100 g and re-check against the 4 mm sieve. Thin liquid pools on the board or drips off the fork → over-moistened; drain on paper towel and re-mash. Pieces exceed 4 mm → rec chop those fragments, do not blend.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g trimmed raw bok choy on the scale. Blanch in 1 L rapidly boiling unsalted water for 60 s, drain, pat dry between paper towels. Record actual cooked weight on the capture sheet. Slice stems lengthwise into halves, then cross-cut every 10-12 mm. Leaves: stack, roll to a log no thicker than 15 mm, and cut the log into 8-15 mm lengths. Target final size: 8-15 mm in EVERY dimension — no piece under 8 mm, none over 15 mm. Sizing check: lay the cut pieces on the 15 mm checkerboard; every piece must be shorter than one 15 mm square and longer than half of one. Pieces over 15 mm: re-trim. Pieces under 8 mm: set aside and re-cut from a thicker stem section. Do NOT blend; the fork-pressure criterion requires intact soft pieces, and blending destroys the test geometry. Do NOT sieve; sieving is for purées and a sieve can never enforce an 8-15 mm window. Do NOT add thickener; L6 pieces carry their own structure. Record final piece size range (mm, min-max) on the capture sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test (the only test at L6): press thumbnail into a stem piece until nail blanches white. Pass = piece squashes, does not spring back, and the nail blanches white. Sizing is part of the pass: measured on the 100 mm ruler, every piece is 8-15 mm in its longest dimension and ≥8 mm in its narrowest. No spoon-tilt test, no fork-drip test, no syringe flow test at L6.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: pieces hold together as discrete chunks, not mash; visible moisture sheen but no pooling liquid. On the spoon: pieces sit as a small mound, not a slurry — presentation only, spoon tilt is not an L6 test. Colour should read pale to mid-green, glossy, not dull or fibrous-looking.
specimens.shots: Shoot three stills and two clips, handheld or tripod, 45 cm distance, smartphone, natural desk light + lamp. 1) 45° hero: pile of pieces on white plate with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. 2) Top-down with checkerboard centred under the pile. 3) Fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail blanching white. Clip A: 8-12 s fork-press, then a continuous sizing pan across the pile against the ruler. Clip B: IDDSI test film, full sequence. Files: blanched_bok_choy_L6_take1.jpg; blanched_bok_choy_L6_take2.jpg; blanched_bok_choy_L6_take3.jpg; blanched_bok_choy_L6_take4.mp4 (Clip A); blanched_bok_choy_L6_take5.mp4 (Clip B).
specimens.fail_modes: (1) Pieces >15 mm → re-cut, reshoot. (2) Pieces <8 mm → too small for L6, discard them and re-cut from thicker stem sections; if most of the batch is under 8 mm it is an L4 specimen and must be reshoot on the L4 card, not this one. (3) Pieces too firm, nail does not blanch white → re-blanch 30 s longer in boiling water, re-test, reshoot. (4) Pieces collapse to purée under the thumbnail, or turn slippery and translucent → over-blanched; start again with a 40 s blanch. (5) Excess water pooling → drain, pat dry, reshoot.

specimens.prep: Take 200 g of whole blanched bok choy heads as bought. Do not blend, chop, or sieve. The per-level note specifies heads as blanched, so keep the leaves and stems intact on each head. Place each whole head directly onto the plate for capture. No liquid, no thickener. Record starting mass on the scale before plating.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the tines of a fork firmly into a stem section. The food must visibly compress, flatten, or break under pressure without returning to original shape — confirm it does not spring back.  Fork drip test: lift a head with the fork. No liquid must drip or run through the tines.  Spoon tilt test: rest a leaf section on a spoon and tilt to 90 degrees. The food must stay in place or slide slowly; it must not flow or pour.  All three passing confirms L7 Regular.
specimens.visual_qc: Whole intact leaves with visible white stems and green leafy tops, no puree, no mash, no sauce pooling on the plate, no liquid sheen when tilted under the smartphone light.
specimens.shots: - blanched_bok_choy_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame. - blanched_bok_choy_L7_take1.jpg — top-down, checkerboard beneath the specimen. - blanched_bok_choy_L7_take1.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press on a stem. - blanched_bok_choy_L7_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. - blanched_bok_choy_L7_take1.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full fork drip, fork pressure, spoon tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-blanching turns stems to mush, failing fork pressure as food disintegrates rather than compresses cleanly — re-blanch a fresh head for shorter time. Pooled water from the blanch bath produces drip test failure — drain and pat heads dry before plating. Cut or separated leaves read as processed rather than whole — re-make with whole intact heads.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched water spinach (drained). Blend on high 45-60 s until smooth. Add 60 ml water; blend 15 s. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard fibrous residue. Weigh the sieved purée; for every 100 ml, add 2.0 g thickener (this is the L3 calibration starting point — record the actual grams used). Stir 30 s, rest 2 min, stir 10 s. If still too runny, add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml and re-mix; if too stiff, add 5 ml water per 100 ml. Record final thickener g/100 ml and total volume.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift fork from cup; purée flows in a continuous slow ribbon and drips through the tines within 5-10 s — passes if it drips, fails if it pours in a stream or sits. Fork pressure: press fork tines into 1 cm of purée; tines leave a clear imprint that does not level out; surface holds the mark. Spoon tilt: tilt a heaped spoon to about 30°; purée slides off slowly in one dollop, not a pour, not a stack. Syringe flow (L3 confirmation): fill the 10 ml IDDSI syringe, release for 10 s; pass = 8-10 ml remains in the barrel.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: glossy green, even colour, no leaf flecks or fibres, smooth ribbon between tines. On the spoon: one cohesive mound that slides as a single lump. No watery halo around the specimen.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45° hero, ruler (mm side up) and checkerboard in frame, specimen in a cup beside. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard filling the frame, cup centred. Still 3: fork-press close-up, tines half-pressed, mid-action. Clip 1 (8-12 s): fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous take. Clip 2: full IDDSI syringe test, start to 10 s mark. Files: blanched_water_spinach_L3_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin — drips in a steady stream or <8 ml remains in syringe: add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, rest, re-test. Too thick — sits on fork or ≥10 ml stays in syringe with no movement: whisk in 5 ml water per 100 ml, re-test. Visible fibres or specks on the sieve residue: re-blend 20 s and re-sieve; if fibres persist, L3 is not achievable for this batch — record and stop.

specimens.prep: - Blanch: bring **1 L** water to a brisk boil, add **200 g** fresh water spinach (leaves with tender stems), push under, blanch **60 s**, lift out and drain **30 s** in the sieve. Keep **100 ml** of the blanching water. - Trim: cut off and discard the tough bottom **40 mm** of every stalk, and any stalk that will not bend without cracking. Weigh the drained, trimmed greens: target **180 g** (record actual). - Blend: greens in the blender with **40 ml** of the reserved blanching water (≤40 °C). Blend on high **45 s**, scrape the walls down once, blend **20 s** more (**65 s** total). Start on low and vent the lid if the greens are still warm. - Sieve: press the blend through the **4 mm sieve** with the back of a spoon and discard what stays on the mesh. At L4 the sieve is the fibre remover (equipment list item 3), and this food's per-level note is "blend, sieve out stem fibres, blend-hold" — **no un-sieved specimen is tested**. Weigh and record the retained fibre mass. - Weigh the sieved purée: target **200–220 g** (record actual). - Thicken — required, not optional: the blanched-green purée will not hold a shape on its own. Whisk in thickener at the calibration starting point of **1.5 g gum-based per 100 ml** of purée (if only a starch-based thickener is stocked, start at **6.0 g per 100 ml**). Whisk **20 s**, rest **60 s**, stir **10 s**. Record the actual grams used in `prep.thickener_g`. - Titrate against section 2 in **0.5 g (gum) or 1.0 g (starch) per 100 ml** steps, up to a ceiling of **4.0 g gum / 12.0 g starch per 100 ml**. Test the specimen at **20–40 °C**.
specimens.iddsi_test: - Fork pressure (5.1): press the fork tines flat into the purée on the tray until the thumbnail blanches white, hold **5 s**, lift. **Pass** = a clear impression remains, the surface does not rebound, and the purée does not squeeze through the tine gaps. - Spoon tilt (5.2, L4 criterion): scoop a full spoon, hold it level, then tilt to **90°**. **Pass** = the purée holds its shape on the spoon and slides off as one cohesive mass with little residue left behind, and no separate thin liquid separates out. - Fork drip (5.3, L4 criterion): scoop with the fork and hold it over the tray. **Pass** = the sample sits in a mound above the tines and does **not** flow through them. - Separation check (QC rule 4): watch the whole clip — no thin green liquid may pool on the spoon or the tray at any point before it ends. Any pooling fails the specimen at L4. - Syringe flow: **skip** — 5.4 is required on every L3 only. Running the 10 ml / 10 s flow test here would invite thickening toward the L3 window and drop the specimen below L4, so it is not run and is not recorded.
specimens.visual_qc: - Uniform dark-green smooth purée with no stem fibres, no leaf flecks and no grit; the sieve residue has already been discarded. - Holds a clean peaked mound on the spoon; surface slightly glossy but not wet; nothing runs down the spoon handle. - A fork press leaves a clean dent with no green liquid weeping around the tines. - No separate liquid layer at the rim of the spoon or the edge of the tray.
specimens.shots: - `bf23-waterspinach_l4_take1_45.jpg` — 45° hero, purée mounded on the tray, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame (`media.photo_45`). - `bf23-waterspinach_l4_take1_top.jpg` — top-down, checkerboard centred under the mound (`media.photo_top`). - `bf23-waterspinach_l4_take1_fork.jpg` — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press, dent visible (`media.photo_fork`). - `bf23-waterspinach_l4_take1_press.mp4` — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon tilt in one continuous take (`media.clip_file`). - `bf23-waterspinach_l4_take1_testfilm.mp4` — full IDDSI test film: fork pressure, spoon tilt, fork drip in sequence, one unbroken take (`tests.test_film_file`).
specimens.fail_modes: - Purée pours off the tilted spoon, runs through the fork tines, or a thin green liquid separates and pools (**too thin**): whisk in **0.5 g gum (or 1.0 g starch) per 100 ml** of purée, rest 60 s, re-stir 10 s, re-test. This moves the specimen toward L4. - Purée cracks or tears under the fork and will not spread (**too stiff** for a level that must hold a soft shape): thin with **10 ml** reserved blanching water per 100 ml of purée, re-blend **20 s**, re-test. - Visible fibres or flecks after sieving: re-blend **20 s** and re-sieve through the 4 mm sieve; record the retained mass. If fibres still pass through, this bunch cannot be made lump-free on the bench — log the attempt, mark the row FAIL, and re-make from a younger, more tender bunch. - Purée too loose because the greens released too much water: drain the blend in the sieve **60 s** before thickening, then thicken from the drained mass. Never add dry starch or flour straight in — every addition is weighed to 0.1 g and logged. - Achievability, stated plainly: water spinach reaches L4 only by blending the trimmed greens and then sieving out the stem fibres, with the thickener titrated to the L4 window. Chopping finer or mashing longer will not produce a lump-free purée — do not try it.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched water spinach leaves and tender stems; discard thick stems. Chop finely with a chef's knife on a board until pieces are visually ≤4 mm. Do not blend — pureeing would drop the level below L5. Pass the chopped mass through the 4 mm sieve; tap and discard oversize pieces that do not pass; record retained mass if any. Lightly rinse-mass with 5–10 ml water to keep the surface moist, then drain on the sieve for 30 s so no separate thin liquid pools. Fork-mash against the bowl side for 20 s to a cohesive, wet mince. No thickener — L5 does not use it. Record the sieve oversize mass on the data card.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the tines flat against a 15 mm heap for 10 s; pass when the heap squashes to a thin smear and does not rebound or recover shape. Spoon-tilt test: load 4–5 ml onto a spoon and tilt to 90°; pass when the full portion slides off together in one motion with no separate drip. Fork-drip test: lift a forkful and hold level for 5 s; pass when nothing drips through or off before the fork enters the mouth zone. No syringe test at L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: uniformly fine green mince, no stem shards above 4 mm, glossy surface sheen, no free liquid at the bowl edge. On the fork: clumps hold together between tines yet separate cleanly when mashed.
specimens.shots: Capture at 0°, 45°, and 90° lighting; white card background. - blanched_water_spinach_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame. - blanched_water_spinach_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. - blanched_water_spinach_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press with daylight. - blanched_water_spinach_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork-press followed by spoon-tilt. - blanched_water_spinach_L5_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence, t ≤ 60 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Oversize particles: sieve rejects too much — chop finer and re-sieve; if oversize > 20 %, re-make. Dry heap that does not squash flat on the fork-press — rinse-mass with another 5 ml water and re-mash. Free liquid pools at the bowl base — drain 30 s more on the sieve before retesting.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g blanched water spinach (tender stems and leaves only — discard fibrous stem cores; the per-level note restricts L6 to tender parts ≤15 mm). Pat dry on a clean cloth. On the cutting board, align leaves, slice across the grain into strips ≤15 mm wide, then cross-cut into pieces ≤15 mm in the longest dimension. Do not blend; do not sieve. Do not add thickener or water — L6 is a soft-solid specimen, not a liquid, so no calibration gram count applies. Confirm the cut size against the 15 mm checkerboard squares before proceeding.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: place a piece on a flat plate, press the flat of a standard fork down until your thumbnail blanches white. The piece must squash, smear, and not return to its original shape. Pass = squash with no recovery. Fork drip test is not applicable (no liquid). Spoon tilt test is not applicable (solid specimen, not a puree).
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: pieces are uniformly dark green, glossy, and visibly wet but not dripping. On the plate: pieces hold their cut geometry yet yield visibly under fork pressure without springing back. No fibrous white cores should be visible on any cut face.
specimens.shots: 1. blanched_water_spinach_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. 2. blanched_water_spinach_L6_take1.jpg — top-down, checkerboard beneath specimen. 3. blanched_water_spinach_L6_take1.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. 4. blanched_water_spinach_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press / spoon-tilt clip. 5. blanched_water_spinach_L6_take1.mp4 — full IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: Fibrous stem cores included (does not squash cleanly under fork). Pieces exceed 15 mm after cutting (re-trim before plating). Pieces spring back after pressure (re-blanch 60 s, re-cut). Re-make rule: discard batch, return to PREP, re-cut from tender leaves only.

specimens.prep: Weigh 60 g blanched water spinach stalks + leaves as served. Do NOT blend, sieve, or add thickener — L7 reference specimen is whole food. If any processing step is suggested, refuse it; the per-level note states stalks are taken as blanched.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines fully into a stalk bundle; the food must flatten, squish, and not return to shape when fork is removed. Spoon tilt: place stalks on a spoon and tilt to ~45°; food must slide/fall off easily with negligible residue. Fork drip: lift stalks on fork; pieces may fall but no continuous liquid stream. All three must pass to confirm L7 Regular.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: stalk pieces hold shape, appear moist but not glossy-wet, matte green surface, no pooled liquid in spoon well. On the spoon: pile sits up, leaves drape naturally, no sheen indicating free sauce or oil pooling.
specimens.shots: Stills: blanched_water_spinach_L7_take1.jpg hero 45° with 100 mm ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame; take2 top-down on checkerboard; take3 fork-press close-up mid-press. Clips: take1 fork-press and spoon-tilt 8–12 s; take2 full IDDSI test sequence. Verify ruler mm and checkerboard 15 mm squares in focus before capture.
specimens.fail_modes: Pooling liquid in spoon — stalks are waterlogged from blanching; pat dry on paper towel, re-plate, re-test. Stalks snap rather than squish — over-blanched or too thin; re-blanch fresh batch 30 s only. Fork drip shows continuous stream — residual cooking water; drain 60 s and pat dry before re-shoot.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g braised winter melon onto the scale. Add 60 ml water. Blend on high for 45 s until fully broken down. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard residue. Return puree to the blender cup. Add thickener at 1.5 g per 100 ml of puree as the calibration starting point; blend 10 s to incorporate. Pour into the capture bowl. Record the actual thickener mass used per 100 ml before adding. Reject the batch if total added thickener drifts outside 1.2-1.8 g per 100 ml without re-sieving.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: hold fork vertically; liquid should not flow in a continuous stream, drop slowly in 2-4 s drips. Pass: drips every 2 s or slower, no steady stream. Fork pressure: press fork tines flat into surface; if tines leave a clear imprint and surface does not return to level, reject as too thick for L3; accept only if surface barely retains a faint mark. Spoon tilt: spoon should pour readily off the tilted edge but not run; pass if it slides in a thick ribbon, not a thin stream. Syringe flow: fill 10 ml IDDSI syringe, release for 10 s. Pass: 8-10 ml remaining in barrel. Outside that range, re-adjust and re-record.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface sheen even, no visible fibres or melon skin flecks. Coats back of spoon with thin film. Fork tines show pale, translucent coating when lifted.
specimens.shots: Still 1 braised_winter_melon_L3_take1.jpg: 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2 braised_winter_melon_L3_take1.jpg: top-down, checkerboard centred under bowl. Still 3 braised_winter_melon_L3_take1.jpg: fork-press close-up, tines half-submerged mid-press. Clip 1 braised_winter_melon_L3_take1.mp4: 8-12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt continuous. Clip 2 braised_winter_melon_L3_take1.mp4: full 10 s syringe flow test, start to stop.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: drips in a steady stream, syringe drops below 8 ml. Re-make by sieving again and adding 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, re-test. Too thick: spoon piles, fork holds shape. Re-make by diluting with 10 ml water and re-sieving, never add more thickener without re-sieving. Fibrous: visible strings on fork lift or sieve residue. Reject; re-blend 30 s and re-sieve before adjusting thickness.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g braised winter melon including its cooking liquid. Tip into the blender; blend 45-60 s until fully smooth. Sieve through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard fibrous residue. Return puree to the blender, add 2 g thickener per 100 ml of puree (record actual grams used on the data sheet). Blend 20 s, rest 60 s, blend 10 s more so the thickener is fully hydrated. Do not add water. The starting mass and final mass are recorded for yield.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the fork tines flat into the surface; the prongs leave a clear, clean imprint and the puree holds the dent without running back together. Fork drip test: lift the fork; the puree sits as a mound sitting on top of the tines, not flowing through or dripping in a thin stream. Spoon tilt test: scoop a heaped spoonful and tilt to a steep angle; the mound must sit on the spoon without sliding off, no separate thin liquid pools on the plate. Level 4 confirmation: all three must pass; the fork-drip mound above the tines is the deciding cue.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is glossy, uniform, off-white to pale jade with no fibre specks. A spoon drawn through it leaves a slow-filling groove that holds its outline for several seconds. A fork lifted from the surface carries a soft peak that sits proud of the tines.
specimens.shots: braised_winter_melon_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. braised_winter_melon_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard filling background. braised_winter_melon_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines half-submerged. braised_winter_melon_L4_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. braised_winter_melon_L4_take5.mp4 — 8-12 s IDDSI test film, fork drip + spoon tilt continuous.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: puree flows through fork tines or liquid pools on tilt — add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, reblend, rest 60 s, retest. Too thick / gummy: puree cracks or balls under fork pressure — thin with 5-10 ml of the original braising liquid, reblend, retest. Lumpy or fibrous: residue visible after sieving — re-sieve the full batch, do not patch; if fibre persists, re-blend an extra 30 s and sieve again. Re-make from the recorded base recipe; do not adjust blind.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of braised winter melon, drained of braising liquid. Reserve the liquid in a small cup; you will use a few ml only if needed. Press the melon through a 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon, working in small batches; discard any fibrous bits that will not pass. Mash the sieved pulp with a fork until uniform. Check particle size: spread a teaspoon on the checkerboard A4 sheet and confirm no piece exceeds one small square (~4 mm). If the mash looks dry, fold in 5–10 ml of the reserved braising liquid a teaspoon at a time; do not add so much that free liquid pools. Do not blend — blending destroys the L5 particle structure. Do not add thickener; L5 does not require it, and any added gum will hide the real texture. The blender is unused for this specimen.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork tines into a heaped teaspoon of specimen on a flat plate until the blanching shows white under the nail, then lift. Pass: the mash squashes flat, does not spring back, the tines leave a clean print. Fork drip: lift a forkful 10 cm above the plate and hold 5 s. Pass: only soft dollops may drop; no free liquid runs through the tines. Spoon tilt: tilt a heaped teaspoon 45°. Pass: the specimen holds its shape and slides as a cohesive mass; it does not pour. Skip the syringe flow test — that is for L3 only.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a moist, lumpy mash with visible flecks no bigger than a grain of coarse pepper; clings to the tines without dripping. On the spoon: a soft mound that holds its peak for several seconds, surface slightly glossy from the braising liquid, no puddle forming at the base.
specimens.shots: braised_winter_melon_L5_take1.jpg — hero, 45°, fork resting on the mound, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. braised_winter_melon_L5_take1.jpg — top-down, checkerboard filling frame, specimen centred. braised_winter_melon_L5_take1.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into the specimen. braised_winter_melon_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork-press followed by spoon-tilt. braised_winter_melon_L5_take1.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full protocol: fork pressure, fork drip, spoon tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Particles larger than 4 mm because the sieve was skipped or pressed too lightly — re-sieve the batch. Specimen too wet, with thin liquid pooling on the plate — drain longer, then fold in pulp only, no extra liquid; if still failing, re-make from a drier portion of the braise. Specimen too stiff and crumbly because too much fibrous flesh was retained — discard stringy bits during sieving and fold in a teaspoon of reserved liquid at a time until the fork-pressure test passes.

specimens.prep: Dice braised winter melon into cubes ≤15 mm per side. Do not blend. Do not sieve. Do not add thickener; this is L6, not L3, so no liquid calibration is required. Weigh 200 g of diced pieces on the digital scale as the working specimen. Confirm no skin, fibrous core, or seed clusters remain — winter melon flesh must be uniformly soft through to the centre of each cube.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the tines of a fork against a single cube until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass criterion: the cube squashes fully and does not return to its original shape; it breaks apart easily. Spoon-tilt test: place a cube on a spoon and tilt to 45°. Pass criterion: the piece slides/rolls off readily — it must not sit as a solid lump. Fork-drip test: lift a fork-load of cubes; pass criterion: pieces sit proud on the tines, nothing pours through the gaps as liquid.
specimens.visual_qc: Cubes on the fork appear translucent-ivory with a slight gloss, no opaque white core. Edges look soft-rounded rather than sharp-cut. Surface yields visibly under the fork tines before pressure is even applied.
specimens.shots: Capture: braised_winter_melon_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. braised_winter_melon_L6_take2.jpg — top-down on checkerboard only. braised_winter_melon_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. braised_winter_melon_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. braised_winter_melon_L6_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: Cubes exceed 15 mm — re-dice smaller. Centre of cube is firm or opaque — winter melon was under-braised; re-braise until fully soft. Pieces hold shape on spoon-tilt with no squash on fork-press — texture is closer to L7; re-cook at lower temperature longer.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of braised winter melon with skin and seeds removed, cut as served. Do not blend. Do not sieve. Do not add thickener or water. Spoon the chunks onto a plate, keeping the braising glaze that clings to the pieces. Target specimen is whole food as normally served. If chunks arrived mashed or pureed, stop and re-prep from fresh braised melon.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press a fork onto a chunk until the thumbnail blanches white, then release. The chunk must not fully flatten, smear, or push between the tines; it must return toward its original shape or hold a clear dent. Spoon tilt test: lift a chunk on a spoon and tilt to a steep angle. It must not slide or drip off under its own weight. Fork drip test is not applicable at L7; the chunk must not drip through the tines. If any chunk squashes flat like puree, the specimen fails L7.
specimens.visual_qc: Chunks keep their cube or wedge outline, not smeared or fibrous. Surface is glossy from the braising glaze, not watery or soupy. A fork lifts a discrete piece, not a slumping mass.
specimens.shots: braised_winter_melon_L7_take1.jpg: 45-degree hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. braised_winter_melon_L7_take2.jpg: top-down, checkerboard under the plate. braised_winter_melon_L7_take3.jpg: fork-press close-up, fork mid-press on one chunk. braised_winter_melon_L7_take1.mp4: 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. braised_winter_melon_L7_take2.mp4: full IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: Chunk mashes to puree under fork pressure — re-prep from fresh, less-cooked braised melon and keep larger pieces. Excess thin braising liquid pools on the plate and drips from the spoon — drain the chunks briefly on the capture plate and re-shoot. Pieces so soft they split between the tines — re-cook shorter next time so chunks hold shape.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g stewed hairy gourd (including liquor) on the digital scale. Blend 30-45 s until fully smooth. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve, pressing with the back of a spoon; discard retained fibre. Add the calibration starting point of 3.0 g thickener per 100 ml of sieved puree, stirring to fully disperse. The per-level note permits blend-thinning, so add 50 ml water to bring the puree to pouring consistency, then re-stir. Record the actual thickener mass used. The specimen must pour in a steady stream from the cup.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: tilt the fork; the puree drips slowly in a continuous, thick ribbon, not a thin stream. Fork pressure test: pressing the fork against the cup leaves a clear pattern that does not recover; the puree does not flow back into the grooves. Spoon tilt test: a spoonful holds shape when the spoon is tilted, then drops off as one cohesive lump. IDDSI syringe flow test: fill the 10 ml syringe, release for 10 s; 8-10 ml must remain in the syringe. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Even pale-green puree with no visible fibre. Smooth, glossy surface, no liquid separating around the edges. Coats the back of the spoon in a thin, even layer.
specimens.shots: Still 1, 45-degree hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame. Still 2, top-down, checkerboard centred. Still 3, fork-press close-up, mid-press. Clip 1, 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. Clip 2, full IDDSI 10 ml syringe flow test, timer visible. Name all files stewed_hairy_gourd_L3_take1.jpg or .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Thin and runny like a drink: sieve was skipped or thickener under-dosed; re-make and add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml. Lumpy with visible fibre: blend time too short; re-blend 20 s and re-sieve. Liquid pools around puree on the spoon: water added before thickener, or under-gelled; re-make from scratch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 300 g stewed hairy gourd (skin and seeds removed, cooked soft), drained 2 min in the sieve so that the water below is the only added liquid. Add 60 ml hot water. Blend 60 s on high, stopping once at 30 s to scrape the sides down, until fully smooth. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon, pressing until only fibre remains; discard the fibrous residue. The 4 mm sieve is the gauge for lump-free: puree that will not pass is re-blended, never pushed through as lumps. No thickener goes into the base prep — stewed hairy gourd puree holds at L4 on its own mucilage, and the fork-drip test in section 2 is the gate. If that test fails, correct it in this order: (a) re-make the batch with the hot water cut to 40 ml, then to 20 ml; (b) only if it still runs, add thickener weighed to 0.1 g in 0.5 g per 100 g of puree increments, log every addition in prep.thickener_g, rest 60 s, re-stir and re-test. Plate a 120 g aliquot for capture.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the bowl of the fork down onto the puree on a flat plate with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white; the puree squashes and does not recover — passes L4. Fork drip: scoop puree and turn the fork tines down over a plate; the puree sits in a mound above the tines and does not flow or drip through within 10 s — passes L4. Spoon tilt: tilt a heaped spoon to 90°; the puree holds its shape and slides off as one cohesive mass with little residue — passes L4. No separate thin liquid may pool on the spoon or the plate at any point before the clip ends. (The 10 ml / 10 s syringe flow test is the L3 criterion and is not used here.)
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform pale green-beige color with no visible fiber strands or skin flecks, and no particle larger than 4 mm on the cut surface of the mound. Surface matte and slightly glossy, not wet or shiny. Holds a clean ridge when drawn with the fork tines.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, specimen mound on white plate with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame — stewed_hairy_gourd_L4_take1.jpg. Still 2: top-down, plate centred on checkerboard only — stewed_hairy_gourd_L4_take2.jpg. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines depressing the mound — stewed_hairy_gourd_L4_take3.jpg. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt — stewed_hairy_gourd_L4_take1.mp4. Clip 2: continuous IDDSI test film (fork pressure, fork drip, spoon tilt) — stewed_hairy_gourd_L4_take2.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny — puree flows through the fork tines or separate liquid pools on the plate; the specimen is too thin, so correct by thickening: re-make the batch with the hot water cut to 40 ml, then to 20 ml, and if it still runs add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g of puree, weighed to 0.1 g and logged, rest 60 s and re-test. Too stiff — puree cracks or crumbles on the spoon instead of holding soft ridges; the specimen is too thick, so correct by thinning: add 5 ml water (measured, not splashed), re-blend 10 s, and re-run the fork-drip test, treating any run-through as the runny branch above. Visible fiber or skin specks caught in the sieve residue — re-blend 20 s and re-sieve, or discard the batch; do not submit a coarse specimen as L4. Separate thin liquid pooling after the puree rests — fails L4; skim and re-blend 15 s, or discard, and do not photograph a separated specimen. If the puree will not hold a mound even at 20 ml added water plus logged thickener, mark the cell FAIL rather than submit a runny specimen as L4.

specimens.prep: Weigh 300 g stewed hairy gourd (skin and seeds removed). Place in blender; blend 8-10 s until coarse. Transfer to tray and mash firmly with fork until no lumps exceed 4 mm. Press all material through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard residue that will not pass. Return sieved mash to bowl and fold gently to redistribute moisture; if the mash sits in a loose pool, add thickener at 1.0 g per 100 ml of mash and stir to combine. Record final grams and any thickener added on the capture sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the specimen on a flat spoon until the thumbnail blanches white; the mash must squash, hold the depressed shape, and not spring back. Spoon tilt: tilt a heaped spoonful 45 degrees; specimen stays as a cohesive mass with no run-off or drip. Fork drip: lift fork clear of the bowl and hold 5 s; nothing drips through or falls from the tines. Particle check: lift a 5 g scoop and confirm no piece exceeds 4 mm against the ruler.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface looks uniformly wet and glossy with fine specks only. No skin threads, no free liquid pooling at the bowl edge. Particles are rice-sized or smaller, evenly distributed.
specimens.shots: stewed_hairy_gourd_L5_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, fork resting beside specimen. stewed_hairy_gourd_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, specimen spread in a 60 mm circle. stewed_hairy_gourd_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. stewed_hairy_gourd_L5_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence, ruler visible. stewed_hairy_gourd_L5_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: fork pressure, spoon tilt, fork drip, particle check.
specimens.fail_modes: Stringy fibres or skin remain and refuse to pass the sieve; re-blend 3 s and re-mash. Mash weeps thin liquid on standing; add thickener 0.5 g per 100 ml and rest 60 s before re-testing. Mash holds shape on tilt but springs back under fork; it is L4 or L6, not L5 — thin with 5-10 ml warm water and re-sieve to <=4 mm, restart.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g stewed hairy gourd (skin + flesh, cooked soft). No blender, no sieve, no thickener. Dice on a clean board with a chef's knife into cubes no larger than 15 mm in any axis. Discard any piece that crumbles to a mash when cut — that is overcooked and fails L6 bite-sized. Reserve any firm central core pieces and re-dice smaller or set aside. Target final specimen mass 200–220 g of intact soft cubes. If pieces are wet, drain 30 s on a sieve; do not press.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines firmly onto one cube against a white plate until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass: the cube squashes and does not rebound to its original shape when the fork is lifted. Spoon-tilt test: place 5–6 cubes on a standard spoon and tilt to 45°. Pass: cubes sit in a pile; a small amount of thin liquid is acceptable, but no cubes slide off. Fork-drip test: lift a forkful of cubes 10 cm above the plate. Pass: cubes stay on the fork; minor drip of free liquid is acceptable. No syringe flow test — not applicable to L6.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: cubes hold their diced edges, surface slightly glossy, no liquid pooling between tines. On the spoon: pile holds shape when tilted, cubes visibly distinct, not a puree. Against the white plate: pieces are uniform green-cream, no translucent mush, no hard pale core flecks.
specimens.shots: stewed_hairy_gourd_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. stewed_hairy_gourd_L6_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. stewed_hairy_gourd_L6_take1_press.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail blanched. stewed_hairy_gourd_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt. stewed_hairy_gourd_L6_take1_iddsi.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, fork drip, tilt, pressure.
specimens.fail_modes: (1) Cube larger than 15 mm on any edge — re-dice that piece. (2) Piece springs back under fork pressure — undercooked core, discard and re-cook the batch until fork passes, then re-dice. (3) Cube collapses to puree on contact — overcooked, re-cook a fresh batch to fork-tender, do not blend.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of stewed hairy gourd as lifted from the pot; do not blend, do not sieve, do not add water, do not add thickener. Transfer the whole chunks straight to a white plate. Keep pieces in the size they were cooked to per the food-list note "chunks as stewed" — no cutting down, no mashing. The reference specimen is the food as served.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press a standard dinner fork onto a chunk until the tines visibly blanch the nail of your thumb held beside the piece. Pass if the chunk does not fully squish flat between fork and plate. Spoon tilt: tilt a dessert spoon 45 degrees; pass if the chunk sits on the spoon without flowing or dripping off. Fork drip: lift forkful 15 cm above plate; pass if no liquid runs off between fork tines. Syringe flow test is not required at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: Chunk holds its cooked shape on the fork with clear edges. Surface shows soft, moist stewed texture, not a smooth puree. Gentle press with fork leaves a visible indentation but the piece stays intact on the plate.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero of the plated chunks, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2: top-down of the plate with checkerboard visible. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, thumb reference in shot. Clip 1: 8-12 s fork-press plus spoon-tilt sequence. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film with all three checks. Files: stewed_hairy_gourd_L7_take1.jpg and stewed_hairy_gourd_L7_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Chunk collapses to puree under fork pressure — re-make and check cooking time was not excessive. Free liquid pools on the plate — drain briefly on the spoon before capture, re-shoot. Pieces cut smaller than "chunks as stewed" — re-make from fresh batch, do not re-cut.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed carrot, soft enough to crush with a fork. Add 120 ml cool water. Blend 45-60 s until completely smooth, no visible flecks. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard anything that will not push through and note the loss. Measure the sieved volume in ml. Stir in thickener at the calibration starting point of 1.5 g per 100 ml of puree, then rest 2 min and stir again. The operator records the actual grams used and the final ml. The flow should be a thick pour that drops in a continuous ribbon from the spoon. Adjust with small extra thickener (0.1-0.2 g) or water (5 ml) only if the IDDSI test fails, and re-record.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: lift the fork; the puree drips slowly in a thick continuous ribbon, not in separate drops. Spoon tilt: the specimen holds its shape on a tilted spoon, then slides off as one lump when the spoon is nearly vertical. Fork pressure: pressing the tines leaves a clear imprint but no liquid pools around it. Syringe flow: fill to the 10 ml mark, start the timer for 10 s; pass if 8-10 ml remains in the syringe.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface looks glossy and even, no orange specks, no bubbles. Coats the back of the spoon in a uniform layer about 2-3 mm thick. Holds a soft peak that slowly flattens.
specimens.shots: Stills: steamed_carrot_L3_take1.jpg hero at 45 degrees with ruler and checkerboard in frame; steamed_carrot_L3_take2.jpg top-down with checkerboard only; steamed_carrot_L3_take3.jpg fork-press close-up at mid-press. Clips: steamed_carrot_L3_take4.mp4 fork press and spoon tilt, 8-12 s; steamed_carrot_L3_take5.mp4 full IDDSI syringe flow test with timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Runny like a drink: too little thickener, add 0.2 g per 100 ml and re-test. Holds shape too firmly on spoon tilt and blocks the syringe: over-thickened, whisk in 5 ml water and re-test. Visible fibre or specks catching on the sieve: blend a further 20 s and re-sieve. Any fail means remix from the recorded quantities; do not patch the existing specimen.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed carrot. Add 60 ml hot water, blend 45 s on high until smooth. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard fibrous residue. Return puree to blender, add 1.5 g thickener per 100 ml puree, blend 15 s. Rest 60 s, stir, retest. If too soft to mound on the spoon, add 0.5 g/100 ml increments, re-blend 10 s, rest 30 s, until the specimen sits above fork tines. Record actual final thickener mass g/100 ml on the data card.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: turn fork tines-down; puree must sit as a cohesive mound above the tines, not drip through or fall. Fork pressure: press fork tines into the puree on a plate; puree should yield to pressure, flatten and smear under the fork, not return to original shape, and not flow through the gaps. Spoon tilt: scoop puree and tilt spoon; specimen must hold shape, slide off as a single mass, not run. L4 does not require the syringe flow test.
specimens.visual_qc: Smooth, uniform orange surface with no fibre specks, no separate liquid pooling at the edges of the mound. The mound keeps clean edges where the fork or spoon lifted it.
specimens.shots: 3 stills: steamed_carrot_L4_take1.jpg hero at 45° with ruler and checkerboard in frame; steamed_carrot_L4_take2.jpg top-down with checkerboard only; steamed_carrot_L4_take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press. 2 clips (8-12 s, 1080p, 30 fps): steamed_carrot_L4_take1.mp4 fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence; steamed_carrot_L4_take2.mp4 full IDDSI test (drip, pressure, tilt).
specimens.fail_modes: (a) Puree drips through fork tines or runs on spoon tilt — puree is too thin, too much water or not enough thickener, or insufficient rest time; remake and re-thicken in 0.5 g/100 ml steps. (b) Puree cracks or splits when pressed with fork — too thick, over-thickened or sieved too dry, re-blend with 5-10 ml hot water and retest. (c) Visible fibre specks or pale streaks — sieve pass incomplete, re-sieve and discard residue before thickener step.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed carrot. Mash with a fork on a plate until no lumps >4 mm remain. Do NOT press the mash through the 4 mm sieve — pressing with the back of a spoon grinds the mash finer than 4 mm and drifts the specimen toward L4. Use the 4 mm sieve as a GAUGE only: tip 20 g of the dry mash onto the sieve and tilt it 3 times without pressing or rubbing; return the material that falls through to the plate, and re-mash by hand anything retained on the mesh until the 20 g aliquot passes. Discard only woody core fibre that will not break down. Weigh mash. Stir in 10 ml water per 100 g mash to moisten; do not add so much that liquid pools. Do not blend — a blender reduces carrot to a smooth puree and loses the L5 particle character. No thickener required for this level; if the mash looks dry and crumbly, dust in up to 0.5 g thickener per 100 g and re-test.
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon tilt (pass/fail): tilt a spoonful 45°; the mass must sit in a pile, cohesive, sliding slowly as a single lump rather than flowing off. Fork pressure (supporting check only — record it, do not gate on it): press fork tines into the specimen on a plate until the tines blanch; the mash must squash, leave a clear dent, and NOT spring back. Spoon tilt must pass. Fork drip and the syringe flow test are NOT in the L5 set — do not apply them.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: discrete, soft orange flecks, none longer than a tine-width (~4 mm), surface glistens but no shine of free liquid. On the spoon: holds the scoop shape, mound stays together when plate is tapped.
specimens.shots: Place 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler in frame. Still 1: 45° hero shot of the plated specimen, fork resting beside it. Still 2: top-down with checkerboard centred under the specimen. Still 3: fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines blanched, dent visible. Clip 1 (8–12 s): fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous action. Clip 2 (8–12 s): the IDDSI test film — spoon tilt, with fork pressure recorded as the supporting check. Files: steamed_carrot_L5_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Free liquid pools on the plate within 60 s → too much water added; drain on the 4 mm sieve for 30 s without pressing, or re-make with 5 ml less water per 100 g. Mash is dry and crumbly and will not hold a pile → too dry; add 5 ml water per 100 g, or dust in 0.5 g thickener per 100 g, and re-test. Mash is smooth/pureed with no visible flecks → over-blended or pressed through the sieve; re-mash a fresh portion by hand and stop at 4 mm — do not blend, do not press the mash through the sieve. Particles retained on the 4 mm gauge exceed 4 mm, or the mass springs back under the fork → insufficient mashing; re-mash by hand and re-gauge. Do not re-pass the whole mash through the sieve to correct this.

specimens.prep: Dice steamed carrot into 15 mm cubes (measure with 100 mm ruler; reject any cube that exceeds 15 mm on any edge). Transfer 200 g of diced carrot to the blender. Add 40 ml water. Pulse 6 seconds total in 2-second bursts; stop and inspect between bursts. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; press firmly so soft material passes. Weigh the sieved mash. Record starting weight, blended weight, and any material retained on the sieve. Do NOT add thickener; L6 requires visible pieces, not a flow-controlled bolus. Dice retention is acceptable only if pieces meet the fork-pressure test below.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into a representative piece on a flat plate until thumbnail blanches white. Pass: piece squashes and does not return to original shape. Size check: 10 of 10 random pieces must measure ≤15 mm with the ruler. Spoon tilt: sample must sit in a stable mound on the spoon; minor spread acceptable, no liquid pool. Fork drip: lift fork; nothing should drip through tines. Reject if any piece remains firm or springs back, or if purée is sticky enough to require a 10 ml/10 s syringe flow test.
specimens.visual_qc: Soft 15 mm dice visible, not puréed. Pieces hold shape on fork tines without sliding off. Light orange, moist surface, no separated liquid pooling on the plate.
specimens.shots: steamed_carrot_L6_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, pieces scattered to show size. steamed_carrot_L6_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, full specimen visible. steamed_carrot_L6_take1_fork.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, thumbnail blanch captured. steamed_carrot_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press plus spoon-tilt in one continuous take. steamed_carrot_L6_take1_IDDSI.mp4 — IDDSI test film, ruler visible, audio note stating pass/fail for each criterion.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces exceed 15 mm after dicing: re-dice and re-weigh. Pieces spring back under fork pressure: re-steam 3 minutes, re-test. Excess water pools on plate: drain 30 seconds on paper, re-shoot, do not blot pieces.

specimens.prep: Use 250 g fresh peeled carrot, steamed soft in a steamer basket 18–20 min until a fork pierces it with no resistance. Cut into batons ≈50 mm long × 15 mm cross-section, matching how the food is normally served. Do not blend, do not sieve, do not add thickener, do not add water. This is the L7 reference specimen. Plate three batons for the test, one baton for each still, one baton for each clip.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the baton until the blanched nail whitens. The carrot must compress, mash, and break apart under the fork — it must not return to its original shape. Spoon tilt: lift a broken piece on a standard teaspoon and tilt; the piece stays on the spoon, it does not flow or drip. Fork drip: lift a baton on fork tines and hold over the plate; no liquid runs through or drips off. All three must pass to confirm L7.
specimens.visual_qc: Muted orange surface, slight sheen from steaming, no pooled liquid on the plate. Edges of batons are rounded from cooking, not sharp. Surface breaks into coarse granules, not paste, under fork press.
specimens.shots: steamed_carrot_L7_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame. steamed_carrot_L7_take2.jpg — top-down on checkerboard. steamed_carrot_L7_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. steamed_carrot_L7_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. steamed_carrot_L7_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: Baton still firm or springs back under fork — under-cooked, re-steam 4 min and re-shoot. Water pools on plate — drain batons on paper towel 30 s before plating. Carrot collapses to puree on fork — over-cooked, discard batch and start with a fresh carrot and 2 min less steam.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g braised lotus root. Add to blender with 100 ml cool water; blend 45 s until smooth. Pass through the 4 mm sieve once to remove fibrous strands; discard residue. Measure 200 ml of sieved puree. Add 3 g thickener per 100 ml (6 g total) — this is the L3 calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Stir in with a fork for 30 s, rest 2 min, stir again. If the puree runs off a spoon, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml increments up to a max of 5 g/100 ml; if it sits in a mound that holds shape, dilute with 5 ml water and retest. Per-level note: blend-thin is feasible — sieve the fibres out, then thin with thickener and water to a pourable consistency.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: spoon a small mound onto the fork tines; the specimen should drip slowly through the gaps in 1-2 drips, not pour and not sit as a solid lump. Fork pressure test: press fork tines into the specimen on a plate; the tines leave a clear, persistent impression but the specimen does not recover shape. Pass. Spoon tilt test: tilt a heaped spoon; the specimen flows off in a slow ribbon that leaves a thin coating on the spoon. Pass. Syringe flow test: fill the 10 ml IDDSI syringe to the 10 ml mark, release for 10 s; pass when 8-10 ml remains in the syringe (i.e., 0-2 ml flows out).
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: smooth pale beige coating that drips in a slow continuous thread, no visible fibrous strands. On the spoon at rest: a glossy pool that slowly levels but does not run flat instantly, no lumps, no separation of liquid ring around the edge.
specimens.shots: Capture three stills: (a) 45-degree hero of the specimen in a shallow bowl with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; (b) top-down with checkerboard underneath the bowl; (c) fork-press close-up mid-press, tines sunk halfway into the specimen. Capture two clips: (d) 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt sequence; (e) full IDDSI syringe flow test, start to 10 s mark. Save as braised_lotus_root_L3_take1.jpg and braised_lotus_root_L3_take1.mp4. Repeat takes if focus is soft or motion blur hides the drip.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: pours cleanly through fork tines, syringe empties below 8 ml. Re-make: add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml and retest. Too thick: mounds on fork without dripping, syringe retains more than 10 ml. Re-make: add 5 ml water, stir, retest. Fibrous strands blocking drip: visible threads between fork tines. Re-make: re-sieve through 4 mm and increase initial water to 120 ml, then re-thicken.

specimens.prep: Take 150 g braised lotus root. Cut into 2 cm pieces, add 40 ml hot water. Blend 45 s, rest 15 s, blend 30 s until a coarse slurry forms. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any fibrous residue that will not pass. Return sieved pulp to the blender, blend 20 s to a uniform smooth paste. Calibrate from L3 starting point: 1.5 g thickener per 100 ml paste, stirred in with a fork and rested 60 s. If the fork-drip mound collapses below the tines, add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml and re-test. Record the final grams per 100 ml on the data sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: a 5–7 mm mound sits cleanly on the tines and does not flow through or drip continuously. Fork pressure: tines pressed into the mound leave a clear indentation; the mound does not split into separate liquid and solid, and pieces do not fall below. Spoon tilt: a spoon holding the specimen tilted 45° holds the full mound with no slide or run-off. No separate thin liquid pools on the plate surface.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is glossy-smooth with no visible fibre or speckle. Colour is uniform deep beige-pink across the mound. Mound edges hold a rounded dome with no weeping liquid ring at the base.
specimens.shots: braised_lotus_root_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard both visible. braised_lotus_root_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. braised_lotus_root_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up at mid-press. braised_lotus_root_L4_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. braised_lotus_root_L4_take5.mp4 — IDDSI test film, fork-drip and pressure in one continuous clip.
specimens.fail_modes: Mound flows through fork tines → re-sieve and add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml. Visible fibres or speckle remain → re-blend 20 s and re-sieve. Liquid pools around the mound on the plate → discard, re-blend with 10 ml less water and recalibrate thickener.

specimens.prep: Start with 200 g braised lotus root. Press each slice flat with the back of a fork against the chopping board, then chop across into strips no wider than 4 mm, then cross-chop into pieces ≤4 mm. Do not blend; blending turns the soft, fibrous flesh into a uniform puree that masks the L5 minced texture. Transfer chopped material to a bowl and moisten with 30-40 ml of reserved braising liquor so no separate thin liquid pools on the surface. Hold back 1-2 slices intact for the fork-pressure test. No sieve, no thickener, no calibration row needed.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift 4-5 pieces on the fork tines; they cluster together, almost no liquid drips off. Fork pressure: press fork tines into a single piece until the thumbnail blanches white; the piece squashes and does not spring back. Spoon tilt: tilt a spoonful 30 degrees; the full sample slides off as one cohesive mass, not as separate drips. The intact-slice fork test should give a clean squash with no recovery. All three pass = L5 confirmed.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: individual minced pieces are just visible, no smeared puree. On the spoon: surface looks moist and glossy, not dry or weeping. Pieces hold together when tilted, not falling apart into crumbs.
specimens.shots: braised_lotus_root_L5_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. braised_lotus_root_L5_take2.jpg — top-down on A4 board, checkerboard centred. braised_lotus_root_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail white. braised_lotus_root_L5_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt sequence. braised_lotus_root_L5_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film showing all three tests.
specimens.fail_modes: Too dry: pieces look pale and pull apart when tilted; re-moisten with 5-10 ml braising liquor and re-shoot. Too wet: thin liquor pools on the surface; drain off excess and re-test drip. Pieces too large: any piece over 4 mm; re-chop finer and re-shoot. Re-make from fresh 200 g if all three fail.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g braised lotus root. Confirm soft pieces already dice ≤15 mm; do not blend — blending breaks fibres and shifts the specimen out of L6. Skip sieve (not applicable, already bite-sized). No thickener (L6, not L3). Reserve 30 ml of the braising liquid in case a 2-second re-steam is needed to soften any firmer core. Keep liquid separate until after tests.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press fork tines into a piece until thumbnail blanches white. PASS if the piece squashes, does not spring back, and flattens cleanly. Spoon-tilt test: lift a piece on a spoon; PASS if the piece holds shape on the spoon and slides off only when tilted or shaken, never pouring. Fork-drip test: pass through a 4 mm sieve. PASS if nothing flows through, only soft residue smears under the tines. Record fork-pressure video as the IDDSI test film.
specimens.visual_qc: Check on the fork: (1) piece collapses fully under thumb without splitting into hard shards, (2) cut face looks moist, fibrous, uniformly translucent-pink with no white firm core, (3) surface glistens but no free liquid pools on the spoon. In seconds: a quick thumb-press should leave a permanent flat dent.
specimens.shots: braised_lotus_root_L6_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. braised_lotus_root_L6_take2.jpg — top-down on checkerboard, three pieces spread. braised_lotus_root_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, thumbnail white. braised_lotus_root_L6_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press plus spoon-tilt. braised_lotus_root_L6_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film (fork-pressure + drip).
specimens.fail_modes: (1) Piece springs back or core stays white → not soft; re-steam 60 s and retest. (2) Fragmenting into small shards on press → too fibrous; not L6, discard and remake from softer batch. (3) Free liquid runs through sieve → too wet; dab, then retest. Any fail: remake, do not patch.

specimens.prep: Use the braised lotus root as purchased. Do not blend, sieve, or thin. Per the food list, handle as slices as braised. Select one intact slice ~15 mm thick, ~40-50 g, as the reference specimen. Place on the A4 capture mat. Record actual specimen mass on the data sheet. No thickener, no water, no processing of any kind.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press fork tines into the slice until thumbnail blanches white. The slice must compress, deform, or break apart under this pressure — it must not return to its original shape. Spoon tilt test: lift a portion on a spoon and tilt to 90 degrees; the piece must fall off easily with no flowing liquid and no sticky residue pulling back toward the spoon. Fork drip test: hold a loaded fork over a plate; no continuous drip should run through the tines. Pass criterion for L7: food can be cut, mashed, or broken apart with pressure from a standard fork or spoon, and holds its shape on the plate while sitting in its own sauce.
specimens.visual_qc: Slice keeps its round, holed lotus-root cross-section with visible cavities. Color is deep mahogany-brown, surface glossy from braise. A light pool of sauce sits around the slice but does not flood the plate. Edges of any break show fibrous, cooked-through texture — no pale raw core.
specimens.shots: braised_lotus_root_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, slice in frame, ruler along left edge, checkerboard lower-right. braised_lotus_root_L7_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard filling frame, slice centered, ruler at bottom. braised_lotus_root_L7_take1_press.jpg — fork-press close-up, fork mid-press on slice. braised_lotus_root_L7_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. braised_lotus_root_L7_take1_iddsi.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Slice too firm to deform under fork pressure: re-pick a thinner slice from the same batch. Slice collapses into puree under pressure: re-pick and confirm the sample is sliced, not mashed. Excess thin sauce runs through fork tines: drain briefly on paper, re-plate, re-shoot.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g steamed bitter melon on the scale. Add 100 ml cool water. Blend on high for 60 s until fully liquefied. Press through the 4 mm sieve; discard coarse residue. Weigh the sieved liquid and record the grams. Add thickener at 4 g per 100 ml of sieved liquid — this is the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Stir 30 s, rest 60 s, stir again 15 s. Re-weigh the final specimen. The thickener amount is the only knob; do not add more water.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: lift fork from the specimen, let it fall from the fork tines in 3-4 slow drips over 5-7 s — pass. Fork pressure: the tines leave a clear, full imprint when pressed lightly; no spring-back — pass. Spoon tilt: spoon at 30°, specimen slides off slowly in one mass, not in a stream — pass. Syringe flow test: fill the 10 ml syringe, start the timer; after 10 s the syringe holds 8-10 ml — pass. All four must pass. If any fails, remake (see FAIL MODES).
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: an even, glossy film that does not run; slow drips that round into teardrops. On the spoon: surface flattens and levels within 1 s, no pooling at the rim. Colour: uniform dull green, no white fibres or yellow seed specks.
specimens.shots: 1. steamed_bitter_melon_L3_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, ruler flush along the front edge of the capture base. 2. steamed_bitter_melon_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred under the specimen. 3. steamed_bitter_melon_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, fork mid-press, tines fully buried. 4. steamed_bitter_melon_L3_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. 5. steamed_bitter_melon_L3_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test: fork drip, spoon tilt, syringe 10 s countdown reading.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: drips run like water, syringe reads under 8 ml — add thickener in 0.5 g steps, rest 60 s, retest. Too thick: no drips, syringe holds above 10 ml — thin by adding water in 5 ml steps, record volume, retest. Fibre lumps, white strands, or visible seed particles — re-blend 30 s and re-sieve; if still visible, reject the batch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed bitter melon, chop into 2 cm pieces, add to blender with 80 ml water. Blend 45 s on high. Pass through 4 mm sieve; discard coarse residue. Return puree to blender, add 2 g thickener per 100 ml puree as the calibration starting point; blend 15 s. Re-weigh, record actual grams of thickener added. If puree flows through fork tines, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml and re-blend 10 s, then re-test. If puree will not drop from an inverted spoon, add 5 ml water and re-blend.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines fully into the specimen on a flat plate; the tines leave a clear dent and the puree does not flow through the gaps. Pass = visible tine marks, no extrusion between tines. Spoon tilt: load a heaped teaspoon, tilt to 90 degrees over a plate; specimen sits in a mound, does not slide or drip.
