Pass = mound holds, zero drip in 5 s. Fork drip: lift fork with a heaped load; specimen sits as a mound above the tines, no drips fall within 10 s. Pass = mound stable, no drops. Syringe flow test is not required for L4.
specimens.visual_qc: Mound on spoon holds a soft peak without slumping. Color is uniform pale green with no dark seed flecks. Surface is smooth, matte, no separate liquid pooling at the plate edge.
specimens.shots: 1. steamed_bitter_melon_L4_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. 2. steamed_bitter_melon_L4_take2.jpg — top-down with checkerboard. 3. steamed_bitter_melon_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. 4. steamed_bitter_melon_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. 5. steamed_bitter_melon_L4_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence, fork drip then spoon tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen flows through fork tines: too thin, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml and re-blend. Separate liquid pools on plate: seeds or water not fully incorporated, re-blend 20 s and re-sieve. Specimen cracks on spoon tilt: over-thickened, add 5 ml water per 100 ml and re-blend. Re-make from scratch after two failed corrections; log actual thickener mass and water volume used.

specimens.prep: Trim 200 g steamed bitter melon, discard seeds. Chop on board, then pulse in blender 5 s to break down. Pass through 4 mm sieve; discard coarse residue. Mash retained fraction with fork until uniformly minced. Add 15 ml water per 100 g minced portion to moisten; stir. Target particle size ≤ 4 mm throughout. L3 thickener calibration: not applicable at L5.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into specimen on plate; flesh must squash and not recover shape when fork is removed. Spoon tilt: tilt spoon 45 degrees; specimen must hold together without sliding or dripping. Fork drip: lift fork with specimen; no thin liquid should run through tines separately. L3 10 ml/10 s syringe flow test: not applicable.
specimens.visual_qc: On fork: discrete moist particles all clearly ≤ 4 mm, no visible fiber strands longer than 4 mm. On spoon: cohesive mound that holds its shape when spoon is tilted, surface glistening but no pooled liquid at edges. Color uniform green-cream, no translucent liquid separating in the plate well.
specimens.shots: Steamed_bitter_melon_L5_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero shot, specimen on white plate with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Steamed_bitter_melon_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard under transparent plate, ruler alongside. Steamed_bitter_melon_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, fork mid-press into specimen. Steamed_bitter_melon_L5_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s clip, fork-press then spoon-tilt sequence, continuous. Steamed_bitter_melon_L5_take5.mp4 — IDDSI test film, fork-pressure full protocol with spoon-tilt insert.
specimens.fail_modes: Particles exceed 4 mm after sieving: re-blend 2 s, re-sieve. Specimen appears dry or crumbly on spoon tilt: add 5 ml water per 100 g, stir, retest. Thin liquid pools on plate beside mound: drain on sieve 30 s, retest fork drip. Re-make from fresh portion if any failure persists after two corrections.

specimens.prep: Start with 200 g bitter melon flesh, seeds and pith removed. Steam 20 min, then check every 2 min to a hard cap of 25 min total. The batch is ready only when a piece pressed with the fork tines until the thumbnail blanches white squashes and does not recover its shape — the section 5.1 criterion, not a thumbnail mark: a piece can leave a clean, persistent white mark under the thumbnail and still spring back, which is the L7 direction and must not be read as "done". Cool 60 s. Slice into pieces 8–15 mm in every dimension, measuring each against the 100 mm ruler: no piece may be under 8 mm or over 15 mm. Re-cut any piece over 15 mm. Fines under 8 mm are set aside and never plated, never photographed and never certified as L6 — a sub-8 mm fine in frame is L5 material carrying an L6 label, and the photograph is the training input. Re-weigh the plated portion and confirm every piece on the plate reads 8–15 mm before any shot is taken. Do not blend and do not sieve. No thickener, no added water or liquid. The pieces must hold their own shape when lifted on the fork, and must squash without recovery when pressed.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test (the only L6 test): press the fork tines onto one 8–15 mm piece on a flat plate, chosen without selecting it for softness, until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass criterion: the piece squashes under the tines, does not recover its shape when the fork is lifted, AND remains a single coherent piece that can be lifted clear on the tines. A piece that breaks apart, smears into purée or releases free water FAILS — that is the L5 direction, and "it squashed and did not recover" is not on its own an L6 pass. Repeat on three further pieces from different parts of the batch; all three must pass and a failing piece is not swapped for an easier one. Confirm with the ruler that each tested piece measures 8–15 mm (not under 8 mm, not over 15 mm). Spoon tilt: not applicable for L6. Fork drip: not applicable for L6. Syringe flow: not applicable for L6. L6 is confirmed by fork-pressure alone plus the 8–15 mm ruler check.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces on fork should look moist but not wet, with visible ridges from the melon interior intact. Edges are soft and rounded, not torn or fibrous. Colour is translucent olive-green; no free liquid pools on the plate. A fork press with the thumbnail blanching white leaves the piece visibly squashed, with no spring-back and no purée smear at the tines.
specimens.shots: Steamed_bitter_melon_L6_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame, 3-5 pieces fanned on a white plate. Steamed_bitter_melon_L6_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only, full portion spread. Steamed_bitter_melon_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press on one piece. Steamed_bitter_melon_L6_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press on three pieces plus ruler size-check, continuous. Steamed_bitter_melon_L6_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, fork-pressure on three pieces with size confirmation.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces larger than 15 mm: re-cut smaller, do not re-steam. Pieces under 8 mm: re-cut from a larger piece; do not certify sub-8 mm fines as L6 and do not leave them on the plate — a plate carrying fines is a mixed-size plate and the hero shot is a mislabelled L6 image. Pieces rubbery or springing back under the fork (too firm, L7-like): re-steam in 2 min steps and re-test after each, but never past the 25 min total cap in the PREP. If the flesh is still rubbery and springs back at 25 min, it cannot reach L6 softness by this bench method: the specimen behaves as L7 (firm, needs chewing) and must NOT be certified L6. Re-make once from the reserve aliquot or mark the event FAIL with tests.pass = false and the reason in prep.notes — the media is never renamed into L7 (protocol section 7, QC rule 1); the L7 label belongs to the L7 aliquot, which is whole steamed rings served as-is. Pieces breaking to puree, smearing, or releasing free water under the fork (too soft, L5 direction): this fails the fork-pressure pass criterion above, not just the look of the plate. Discard the batch and reduce steam time on the next batch. Do not try to rescue it by re-cutting smaller, which only moves the specimen further toward L5. Reliability: bitter melon flesh steamed on its own tends to stay rubbery/fibrous and most often lands at L7 rather than L6. L6 is reached only if the flesh softens enough to squash under the fork while holding 8–15 mm pieces; if it will not, choose a softer food or record the event as unresolved — do not certify it as L6 and do not re-label this media as L7.

specimens.prep: Weigh 120 g steamed bitter melon rings straight from the steamer; do not blend, do not sieve, do not add thickener or water. Keep rings intact as served. Portion the whole-food reference specimen onto the capture plate in a single layer with one ring standing on its edge for the side view.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press a dinner fork onto a ring with normal thumb pressure; the ring must flatten, break apart, or fully lose its shape under the fork tines — it must not return to its original shape when the fork is lifted. Spoon tilt: tilt a spoon holding a ring; the ring must slide off or fall off easily with minimal coaxing, not stay stuck to the spoon. Fork drip: lift a pierced ring on the fork; no continuous drip or flow through the tines. All three must pass to confirm L7.
specimens.visual_qc: Ring holds its hollow cross-section and pale-green outer skin. Edges look tender and moist, not mushy or collapsed. Wall thickness reads roughly even around the ring with no translucent breakdown zones.
specimens.shots: steamed_bitter_melon_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. steamed_bitter_melon_L7_take2.jpg — top-down over checkerboard. steamed_bitter_melon_L7_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. steamed_bitter_melon_L7_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. steamed_bitter_melon_L7_take5.mp4 — IDDSI test film, all three checks in sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-steamed ring collapses to a paste and passes L6 only — re-make with shorter steam. Under-cooked ring resists the fork and reads L5 or above — re-steam and re-test. Wet surface that drips through the fork tines fails the drip test — drain briefly on paper and re-shoot.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed eggplant. Add 80 ml water. Blend 60 s on high. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard retained skins/seeds — re-blend is impossible if residue exceeds ~10% of mass, re-steam a fresh piece. Weigh puree, then add thickener at 1.5 g per 100 ml of puree as the calibration starting point; the actual grams used are recorded. Stir 30 s, rest 90 s, stir 10 s. Pour — must flow but drip slowly through fork tines.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: when fork is lifted, puree drips continuously through tines in ≤10 s, not a single sheet. Fork pressure: a thumbnail-sized portion spread on a flat spoon blanches the spoon fully white when pressed with the fork base. Spoon tilt: a 5 ml scoop on a spoon tilts 30° and slides off without holding shape. Syringe flow: fill the IDDSI 10 ml syringe, cap, hold 10 s; 8–10 ml must remain. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy, smooth, uniform mauve-grey film coating the spoon; no flecks, fibres, or seed specks. Coats the back of the spoon evenly without running. Falls from the fork in a slow, continuous, ribbon-like drip, not drops and not a sheet.
specimens.shots: 1) steamed_eggplant_L3_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard visible at frame edge. 2) steamed_eggplant_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only, spoon at centre. 3) steamed_eggplant_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, fork mid-press with puree blancing spoon white. 4) steamed_eggplant_L3_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous take. 5) steamed_eggplant_L3_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI flow test, timer visible, start and end volumes recorded.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: runs through tines in a sheet, <8 ml retained. Too thick: piles under fork, holds shape on tilt, >10 ml retained. Grainy: visible fibre or seed specks post-sieve. Re-make: re-blend 15 s and re-sieve; if texture off, add thickener in 0.25 g per 100 ml increments and re-test. Do not re-record until all four IDDSI tests pass.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g steamed eggplant (skin removed, all visible seeds removed). Place in consumer blender with 40 ml water. Blend on high for 40 s, scrape the jar walls, blend 20 s more until uniform. Press through 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard residue. Weigh sieved purée. The per-level note is blend-then-sieve-hold: L4 is lump-free, so the sieve is mandatory and no specimen is judged before it has been pressed through — the blend step never replaces it. Add thickener at the calibration starting point of 3 g per 100 g sieved purée (7.0 g for a 235 g yield); record the actual grams used. Stir 20 s, rest 60 s. If the fork-drip test fails, add 0.5 g per 100 g per increment, re-rest 60 s and re-test, up to a maximum of 5 g per 100 g.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the specimen until the tines blanch; puree leaves a clear imprint, no spring-back. Pass = clean impression, holds shape. Fork drip: lift fork with a loaded mound; puree sits in a mound above the tines for 10 s with zero drip. Pass = zero drip in 10 s. Spoon tilt: scoop, level the edge, tilt spoon to 45 degrees; specimen must not slide, pour, or drip. Pass = sticks to spoon, no flow. Syringe test is NOT required at L4.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is matte and even, no free liquid pooling around the mound. Color is uniform grey-violet, no dark skin flecks or seed specks. Mound on the fork keeps its peaked shape; the spoon-tilted sample stays put.
specimens.shots: steamed_eggplant_L4_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen on fork. steamed_eggplant_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only, specimen mound filling center. steamed_eggplant_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines fully inserted. steamed_eggplant_L4_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s clip, fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. steamed_eggplant_L4_take5.mp4 — 8-12 s IDDSI test film: scoop, fork drip 10 s, spoon tilt 10 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: drips through fork tines or runs off spoon — add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g, rest 60 s, retest (maximum 5 g per 100 g). Too thick / crumbly: cracks or breaks on fork press, loses sheen — add 5 ml water per 100 g, stir, retest. Visible skin or seed specks after sieving: re-blend 15 s and re-sieve; the sieve is never skipped at L4.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g freshly steamed eggplant (skin on, tender; peel away any tough or papery outer strips, as retained skin must be tender enough to mash to about 4 mm). If any piece is larger than 4 mm, mash it with a fork on a plate; if the mash remains uneven, pulse in the blender 5–10 s only — do not purée.  The 4 mm sieve is a **GAUGE** at L5, not a size reducer. Do not press the batch through it and do not discard the retained fraction. Gauge check: put one heaped teaspoon of mash on the 4 mm sieve and press once with the back of a spoon — the mash must break into lumps of about 2–4 mm with no single lump larger than 4 mm; return the gauged sample to the plate. If a lump is larger than 4 mm, re-mash or pulse 2–3 s and re-gauge.  Target yield: about 200 g of soft, moist mash with visible lumps of 2–4 mm, none larger than 4 mm, and no separate liquid pooling on the plate. Add no water, no oil, no thin liquid, no thickener (thickener is not used at L5; this is the L3 calibration field only — leave blank).
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon tilt (mandatory at L5): place a heaped teaspoon on the spoon and tilt it to ~45°, then to almost vertical. PASS — the specimen sits in a pile, does not slide off, and does not run; no separate thin liquid runs off the spoon.  Fork pressure (supporting check only at L5 — it does not by itself pass the specimen): press the tines of a fork into a heaped teaspoon of specimen on a flat white plate with firm thumb pressure until the thumbnail blanches; the mash must squash completely and stay squashed — no spring-back, no original shape recovered — while still showing visible lumps of 2–4 mm in the squashed mass.  Fork drip does not apply at L5 and is not run.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: damp, soft clumps the size of coarse minced meat (2–4 mm), no shiny wet film, no droplets falling between tines. On the spoon: holds a heaped mound when tilted; surface looks matte-moist, not glossy. On the white plate under the specimen: no free liquid ring spreading around the mash.
specimens.shots: Capture three stills and two clips, named steamed_eggplant_L5_take1.jpg / .mp4, take2, take3, take4, take5. Stills: (1) 45° hero shot with the 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, fork resting beside the heap; (2) top-down frame-filling shot of the specimen on the plate with checkerboard beside it; (3) fork-press close-up, mid-press, thumbnail blanched, ruler tip visible. Clips: (4) 8–12 s continuous fork-press (supporting) plus spoon-tilt on the same heap; (5) the IDDSI test film combining spoon tilt and fork pressure in one unbroken sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: (a) Any lump larger than 4 mm at the gauge check: re-mash the retained fraction or pulse 2–3 s and re-gauge; if lumps still exceed 4 mm the batch is too fibrous — discard and start with a softer eggplant. (b) Free thin liquid pools on the plate: the eggplant was over-steamed or watered; drain on a paper towel for 2 min, then re-run the spoon-tilt test. (c) Specimen springs back under fork pressure: it is under-processed — mash by fork or pulse-blend 2–3 s, re-gauge, then re-test; if it has gone smooth and pasty with no visible lumps it has been over-processed to L4, so discard and restart from a fresh 250 g portion, steaming only until just tender. (d) Spoon tilt fails because the mash runs off the tilted spoon: it has collapsed to L3/L4, not L5 — start from a firmer eggplant, steam only until just tender (not collapsing), and mash by hand rather than blending.

specimens.prep: Steam 250 g whole eggplant (pierced twice) at 100 °C for 12–15 min, until a fork pressed into the flesh with the thumbnail blanching white sinks in and the flesh does not push back against the tines — the section 5.1 criterion. A knife sliding in is a kitchen doneness cue, not a level test: "no resistance" to a knife over-softens the flesh toward L5 and drives weep water up, so do not use it to decide readiness. Longer steaming increases weep water. Halve, cool 5 min, and scoop the flesh away from the peel; discard the peel. Remove seeds and pull out strings by hand. Weigh the usable flesh — expect 200–240 g — and use all of it; record the actual starting weight. If usable flesh falls below 180 g, do not top the pack up from a second eggplant: two fruits steamed in the same load can differ in firmness, and one specimen of two textures cannot be certified at one level — record the smaller mass and shoot it, or reject the pack. Cut on a clean board with a spoon or blunt knife into 8–15 mm pieces: every piece must measure 8–15 mm along its longest edge on the 100 mm ruler and must not be smaller than 8 mm. The 100 mm ruler is the L6 sizing instrument (protocol 5.1 and docs/SHOT_LIST.md: "the 100 mm ruler is the sizing reference for L6 pieces"); the 15 mm checkerboard in frame is the scale reference for the photograph and is not a substitute for the ruler read-out. Weigh the cut pieces and record the actual yield; the loss at this step is fines and crumbs from cutting, because seed and string were already removed before the weigh — record it, do not top it up, and do not plate or photograph any of it: sub-8 mm fines in frame are L5 material carrying an L6 label, and the photograph is the training input. Re-weigh the plated portion and confirm every piece on the plate reads 8–15 mm before any shot is taken. No thickener, no added liquid. Do not use a blender and do not pass the specimen through the 4 mm sieve: a 4 mm sieve cannot enforce a 15 mm limit, it would reduce the batch to ≤4 mm (L5), and it is not a gauge for an 8–15 mm specimen. If free water collects, drain in a colander 30 s — do not squeeze the pieces. Hold at ≥60 °C for no more than 20 min; capture within 10 min of draining.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test (5.1) — the only mapped test that applies at L6: press the fork tines into one piece until your thumbnail blanches white. PASS = the piece squashes, does not return to its shape, expresses no free water, AND stays in one piece that can be lifted clear on the tines. "It squashed and did not recover" is not on its own an L6 pass: a piece that breaks apart or smears into purée has failed in the L5 direction, and a piece that keeps a clean 8–15 mm edge and only dents under full thumbnail pressure has failed in the L7 direction. Size criterion (level definition, not a 5.x flow test): every piece 8–15 mm along its longest edge, read on the 100 mm ruler. No fork-drip (5.3 is L3/L4) and no spoon-tilt (5.2 is L3/L4/L5) at L6. No syringe test at L6.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces hold a soft, moist but matte surface — no free liquid pooling on the plate or spoon and no water squeezing out under the fork. Colour stays uniform purple-grey flesh with no stringy fibres pulling away and no seed-coat fragments. Every piece reads 8–15 mm along its longest edge on the 100 mm ruler, and no piece is collapsed or smeared at the cut faces.
specimens.shots: Sizing reference is the 100 mm ruler (protocol 5.1; docs/SHOT_LIST.md names it the sizing reference for L6 pieces); the 15 mm checkerboard in frame is the scale reference for the photograph, not the sizing gauge. Still 1: 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, full portion visible. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard centered, pieces spread so individual sizes are readable. Still 3: fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into one piece, thumbnail blanch visible. Clip 1: 8–12 s continuous fork-press on one piece, tines visibly deforming the flesh. Clip 2: IDDSI test film, fork-pressure on three pieces in sequence plus the ruler size read-out, 20–30 s. Name files steamed_eggplant_L6_take1.jpg / .mp4, increment take on re-shoot.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-blended or over-worked to a purée or paste: a purée cannot be brought back to 8–15 mm pieces by any bench adjustment — discard the batch and re-make by hand-cutting only; the blender is not to be used on this specimen. Pieces left larger than 15 mm after cutting: re-cut, do not re-blend. Pieces under 8 mm, or a batch that collapses to 4 mm or less under its own weight: the flesh is too soft to hold an L6 piece, and this pack cannot be brought to L6 by any reliable bench method — the closest achievable level for this pack is L5 (lumps ~4 mm, moist, fork-mashable). Re-make once from a firmer pack, or mark the event FAIL with tests.pass = false and the reason in prep.notes. Do NOT relabel the specimen L5: protocol section 7 QC rule 1 forbids renaming a specimen's media into another level, and an L6 image re-labelled L5 is a corrupted ground-truth row in both directions. Free water pooling on the plate: drain in a colander 30 s, do not squeeze, and capture within 10 min; if water re-accumulates within 2 min of draining, the pack is too wet to hold L6 as served — re-make with a 12 min steam and record. If the 12 min remake still weeps within 2 min, this pack cannot hold L6 as served: mark the event FAIL rather than thinning the specimen or labelling it L5.

specimens.prep: Weigh out 200 g steamed eggplant as served (no cooking added). Do not blend, do not sieve, do not add thickener, do not add water. Cut into strips roughly 5 cm long × 1.5 cm wide as steamed per spec. Use these strips as the reference specimen.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press a strip flat with the fork tines; the strip flattens easily and does not recover its shape when the fork is lifted — pass. Spoon tilt test: the strip sits on the spoon without sliding off when tilted; minimal spread, no flowing — pass. Fork drip test: no liquid drips through the tines between fork lifts — pass. Adult-sized bite ≈ 1.5 cm cube is chewed normally without effort — pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Strip holds its cut shape on the fork, surface looks tender-firm not mushy, no pooled liquid pools around the strip. Colour uniform cooked-eggplant purple-tan, no raw patches.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero shot of three strips on a white plate, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, file: steamed_eggplant_L7_take1.jpg. Still 2: top-down of same arrangement, checkerboard visible, file: steamed_eggplant_L7_take2.jpg. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press on one strip, file: steamed_eggplant_L7_take3.jpg. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt on a strip, file: steamed_eggplant_L7_take1.mp4. Clip 2: IDDSI test film — fork pressure, spoon tilt, fork drip on three separate strips, file: steamed_eggplant_L7_take2.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Strip smears or collapses fully under the fork → too soft, remake with a firmer batch. Liquid pools on the plate or drips from fork → not drained properly, pat strips dry and retest. Strip recovers shape after fork lift → under-steamed, steam a fresh batch 2–3 min longer.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g sweetcorn kernels (drained canned or thawed frozen, heated). Add 100 ml hot water. Blend 60 s. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; press to express liquid; discard fibrous residue. Measure the sieved liquid and top up with hot water to 200 ml total. Add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml (4.0 g for the 200 ml batch), weighed to 0.1 g, as the calibration starting point; record the actual mass. Stir 30 s, rest 2 min, stir 15 s. Titrate to the syringe window in 0.5 g per 100 ml steps, each weighed. The BF30 per-level note "blend-thin" applies: thin the specimen to pour. Do not chase a chewable, shape-holding or imprint-leaving texture — those are higher levels, and an L3 specimen that holds an imprint is an L4 specimen.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: fork lifted 2 cm clear of the surface; the specimen drips slowly through the tines in a continuous flow and leaves a coating on the fork. Pass = steady slow drip within 10 s; a free stream is too thin, a mound sitting above the tines is too thick. Spoon tilt: a full spoon tilted to 45° pours off in a slow continuous stream over 2-4 s, not instantly and not as one lump. Pass = slow pour, with no separate thin liquid pooling on the spoon or tray. Syringe flow test (L3, mandatory): fill the 10 ml syringe to the 10 ml mark, release with the nozzle open, start the 10 s timer; pass = 8.0-10.0 ml remaining at t = 10 s with a measurable discharge. Any value outside 8.0-10.0 ml is corrected and re-tested; it is never logged as a pass. Fork pressure is not an L3 test and is not performed on this specimen.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a smooth, glossy coat clings between the tines with no kernels, skins or yellow flecks visible. On the spoon: the surface is flat and level while held and pours as one slow ribbon when tilted; no pooling of free liquid. Colour uniform pale yellow, no graininess or streaks.
specimens.shots: Capture, then verify each file exists. sweetcorn_kernels_L3_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. sweetcorn_kernels_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard fills background. sweetcorn_kernels_L3_take3.jpg — fork-drip close-up mid-drip, ruler and checkerboard in frame. sweetcorn_kernels_L3_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-drip then spoon-tilt. sweetcorn_kernels_L3_take2.mp4 — IDDSI 10 ml syringe flow test, full 10 s, fill and final reading both legible.
specimens.fail_modes: (1) Visible specks, skins or yellow flecks after sieving: re-blend 15 s and re-sieve; if flecks persist, discard and remake. (2) Too thin — residual <8.0 ml, or a stream off the fork: add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml (weighed to 0.1 g), stir, rest 2 min, retest. (3) Too thick — 10.0 ml remains with no discharge, or the specimen holds a mound on the spoon: thin with 10 ml hot water, re-blend 10 s, retest; if it still holds a mound, discard and remake at 1.5 g thickener per 100 ml. The two directions are not interchangeable: too thin is corrected by thickening, too thick by thinning, and no imprint criterion is ever used to judge this specimen.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g canned or frozen sweetcorn kernels, drained. Add to consumer blender with 60 ml water. Blend 45 s on high, then pass through the 4 mm sieve to remove skins and fibrous hulls per the per-level note; discard the sieve residue. Return the sieved puree to the blender and blend a further 30 s until smooth. Transfer puree to a small bowl. Add thickener at the L3 calibration starting point of 2.0 g per 100 ml, stir vigorously 15 s, rest 60 s, stir 5 s. If flow fails, add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml increments, stir, rest, re-test; if too stiff, add 1 ml water. Record the actual grams of thickener per 100 ml and total water used on the run sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press fork tines into the specimen on a flat white plate. Specimen must compress and leave a clear full tine-pattern indentation with no surface recovery for several seconds. Pass = clean impression holds. Spoon tilt test: scoop 5 ml onto a teaspoon, tilt to 90 degrees. Specimen must sit in a mound on the spoon, not pour or drip. Pass = holds mound without sliding. Fork drip test: lift fork from the bowl; specimen sits in a mound above the tines and does not flow or drip through the gaps. Pass = mound stays, tines visible underneath.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform yellow colour, no visible yellow flecks, skins, or fibrous threads. Smooth glossy surface that mounds on the fork rather than coating it thinly. Holds its own shape on the spoon without pooling liquid at the edges.
specimens.shots: sweetcorn_kernels_L4_take1.jpg — hero, 45-degree angle, ruler and checkerboard in frame alongside the spooned specimen. sweetcorn_kernels_L4_take2.jpg — checkerboard top-down, specimen mounded on the plate. sweetcorn_kernels_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines pressed to mid-depth, full impression visible. sweetcorn_kernels_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s clip of fork-press then spoon-tilt sequence. sweetcorn_kernels_L4_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, 8-12 s, fork drip then spoon tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin, flows through fork tines or drips off spoon: add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 60 s, re-test; re-shoot if remake. Visible skins or fibrous strands after sieving: re-blend and re-sieve; one pass only, do not push residue through. Grainy texture with visible yellow flecks: blend a further 15-20 s and re-test; if still grainy, remake.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g canned or frozen sweetcorn, drained and blotted dry (record the drained weight). Pulse in the consumer blender in 1 s bursts for 5–8 s total — do not purée; target pieces of 2–4 mm. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; the sieve is a GAUGE — every piece must pass a 4 mm opening without applied pressure. Discard overs; if more than ~15 g is retained, weigh in an equal mass of extra drained kernels so the batch stays at 150 g. Do not force material through and do not blend below ~2 mm, which gives L4. Return the fines to a bowl, add 22 ml water (15 ml per 100 g drained solids), and mash firmly with a fork for 30 s until cohesive and visibly moist with no pooled liquid. If it sits wet, stir in thickener at 1 g per 100 g of drained kernels — weigh the solids, this specimen has no 100 ml — as the calibration starting point, then record the actual grams used. The fork pressure supporting check must pass before filming.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure (supporting check only at L5 — not a primary L5 test): press the tines into the mound on a flat white plate with normal thumb pressure. The specimen must be mashable with the side of the fork, the mound must hold its shape after release, and the tines must NOT blanch white. Blanching tines means the specimen has been taken past L5 toward L4 — re-make. Spoon tilt (applies at L3/L4/L5): a loaded spoon holds a rounded heap at rest without slumping; tilted to 90° the specimen slides off as one mass rather than slumping into a paste, pouring, or crumbling. No fork drip test applies (L5, not L3/L4). Free liquid: the specimen must be moist, but no thin liquid may pool in a ring wider than 10 mm around the mound after it sits on a plate for 1 min.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: granular but cohesive mass, no whole kernel slipping off, surface sheen from added water. On the spoon: holds a rounded heap without slumping at rest, and slides off as one mass when tilted. On the plate: leaves a thin wet film or trail, no pool of free liquid around the mound — a ring wider than 10 mm fails.
specimens.shots: Stills: sweetcorn_kernels_L5_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard visible at frame edge. sweetcorn_kernels_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, 100 mm ruler along one edge. sweetcorn_kernels_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press, no blanch. Clips: sweetcorn_kernels_L5_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous shot. sweetcorn_kernels_L5_take5.mp4 — 8-12 s IDDSI test film, mound mashable and not recovering.
specimens.fail_modes: Whole kernels survive above 4 mm — re-pulse 2–3 s and re-sieve, then top up with extra drained kernels to restore 150 g. Slumps into a paste or pours off the spoon when tilted (too wet / over-mashed) — drain and blot the surface 10 s with paper towel, or stir in 25 g additional drained kernels, and re-mash 15 s. If it still will not cohere, bind with 1 g thickener per 100 g drained solids and re-mash 30 s; re-shoot from step 2. Crumbles and will not hold a heap (too dry) — add 5 ml water per 100 g of drained kernels, re-mash 15 s, re-test. Free liquid pools in a ring wider than 10 mm after 1 min (too wet) — drain, blot 10 s, stir in 25 g drained kernels and re-mash 15 s; thickener only as a last resort at 0.5 g per 100 g of drained solids, never per 100 ml.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g sweetcorn kernels on the digital scale. Drain canned kernels; if frozen, thaw and pat dry with paper towel. L6 is a bite-sized-piece level: every kernel must measure 8–15 mm along its longest axis against the 100 mm ruler. Halve any kernel exceeding 15 mm and re-measure the halves; discard any piece under 8 mm and top the batch back up to 200 g with 8–15 mm kernels from the same batch. No sieve is used at any mesh size — a sieve cannot enforce a 15 mm upper limit and would cut the specimen below L6. No blender. No thickener. No water added.  Firmness gate — this is the step that decides whether the batch can be L6 at all. Press one kernel from the batch with the thumbnail until the thumbnail blanches white: it must squash flat and not rebound. Canned kernels normally pass as-is. If the kernel stays firm or rebounds the batch is not yet L6: simmer at a bare simmer 5 min, drain, pat dry, cool 2 min, re-test. Add a further 3 min only if still firm, to a 10 min total maximum — past that the kernels pulp and the batch has fallen to L5. If a kernel still rebounds after the full 10 min, sweetcorn from this batch cannot be brought to L6 by a reliable bench method; reject it and do not shoot.  Re-weigh 200 g onto the A4 capture kit surface. The per-level note states "serve as-is, kernels ≤ 15 mm" — do not blend; the simmer above only softens the kernel, it adds nothing and changes no level.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test (mandatory at L6): press the fork tines firmly onto a single kernel with the thumbnail until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass: the kernel squashes flat and does not return to its original shape. Repeat on 3 kernels from different areas of the plate; all 3 must pass. Spoon-tilt and fork-drip are not L6 tests in this protocol and are not run.
specimens.visual_qc: Kernels appear intact, glossy yellow, individual and countable on the fork. No slurry, no puree, no pooling liquid on the plate (visual check only — free liquid is not a scored test at L6). Each kernel measures 8–15 mm against the 100 mm ruler in the frame.
specimens.shots: sweetcorn_kernels_L6_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. sweetcorn_kernels_L6_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred under specimen. sweetcorn_kernels_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, thumbnail mid-press blanching white. sweetcorn_kernels_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press sequence on 3 kernels. sweetcorn_kernels_L6_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full fork-pressure procedure with thumbnail cue.
specimens.fail_modes: Kernel > 15 mm (fails L6 size rule): halve oversized pieces, re-measure the halves, keep only pieces still 8–15 mm, re-shoot. Kernel < 8 mm (too small for L6): discard the small pieces and top the batch up to 200 g with 8–15 mm kernels; do not shoot a mixed-size plate. Kernel remains firm and rebounds under the thumbnail (fails fork-pressure — too firm, not yet L6): the batch is under-softened or the wrong variety. Simmer 3–5 min longer (10 min total maximum), drain, pat dry, cool 2 min, re-test. If it still rebounds after the full 10 min, sweetcorn from this batch cannot reach L6 by a reliable bench method — reject the batch and source softer kernels; do not shoot and do not substitute a finer level. Kernels pulp, split or lose countability (over-simmered — the batch has dropped to L5): discard, fresh batch, shorten the simmer to 5 min and re-test. Free liquid pools on the plate: drain longer or pat dry, re-shoot.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g sweetcorn kernels straight from the tin or heated from frozen; drain off packing liquid, blot 10 s on paper towel. Do not blend. Do not sieve. Do not add water or thickener. Each kernel must remain whole, separate, and not crushed during handling. No bench softening step of any kind is applied to this specimen — no simmer, no halving, no re-cutting: L7 is "food as bought and normally served" (protocol section 2), and the simmer step that bf30_sweetcorn_kernels_L6 requires to pass its firmness gate would make this specimen an L6 specimen. Specimen is calibration starting point; operator records actual mass weighed.  L6/L7 separation gate — read before shooting. For this food the L7 specimen and the L6 specimen are the same physical object: a kernel straight from the tin is already <= 15 mm and already flattens under the fork, which is exactly what the L6 card asks for, so the two hero photographs are identical. The only difference the protocol allows is that L7 carries no preparation step at all. Therefore: log the L6 event for this same batch first, and record on the capture sheet, in words, "BF30 L7 is not photographically separable from BF30 L6 — no bench step applied". If the L7 shot would be the same photograph as the L6 shot, the L7 label is not independently supportable for this food and the event is recorded as such rather than shot as a fresh L7 specimen.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test (5.1) — the only test that applies at L7: press fork tines fully into the pile of kernels with thumb pressure until the thumbnail blanches white. Specimen passes L7 only if every pressed kernel flattens, splits, or smashes apart — no pressed kernel remains hard, rounded, or bounces back. Press at least five kernels taken from different parts of the plate; all five must pass, and a kernel that stays hard is not replaced by a softer one. Spoon tilt: not applicable at L7 (5.2 covers L3/L4/L5 only) and is not run. Fork drip: not applicable at L7 (5.3 covers L3/L4 only) and is not run. Syringe flow: not applicable at L7 (5.4 is every L3 specimen only) and is not run. L7 is confirmed by fork-pressure alone. No spoon-tilt criterion is scored, filmed or recorded for this specimen.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: kernels show flat, crushed, split faces with maize starch exposed; no whole round kernel survives. On the plate: loose, dry, individual pieces; no clumping, no slick glaze, no sauce film binding them, no pooled packing liquid. Kernels sit as separate fragments, not a paste, and no kernel has been halved or re-cut.
specimens.shots: sweetcorn_kernels_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, pile centred on A4 kit, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, mass noted on card. sweetcorn_kernels_L7_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard filling frame, kernels spread single layer so individual size is readable against 15 mm squares. sweetcorn_kernels_L7_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines depressing kernels, thumbnail blanch visible. sweetcorn_kernels_L7_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press on five kernels taken from different parts of the plate, continuous take, thumbnail blanch visible in each press. sweetcorn_kernels_L7_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: fork-pressure on five kernels in sequence, ruler and checkerboard in frame at the start of the take.
specimens.fail_modes: Any kernel stays whole and hard after full fork pressure: re-make with fresh kernels; reheat to steaming, re-drain, re-blot. Kernels clump or sit in a sticky mass on the plate because residual syrup is binding them: re-drain, rinse briefly under cold water, re-blot fully before reshooting. Pile looks mashed or creamy rather than discrete fragments: operator over-pressed during prep; re-make, do not crush with fork before the test shot. Any kernel found halved, re-cut or simmered: the specimen has been given the L6 bench step and is an L6 specimen, not an L7 one — discard it and re-make from the unopened tin or frozen pack with no bench step. A specimen that has been simmered to softness is never certified L7: L7 is the as-bought reference, and softness bought by simmering is the L6 card's route, not this one.

specimens.prep: Peel ripe banana; weigh 120 g. Add 60 ml water. Blend 25-30 s on high until fully smooth (L3 is lump-free: blend to a smooth purée before thickening). Sieve through the 4 mm sieve into a bowl; press with the back of a spoon; discard fibre. Weigh the sieved purée and the bowl to get volume by difference (1 g ≈ 1 ml). Add thickener at the calibration starting point of 3.0 g per 100 ml of sieved purée. Stir with a fork for 30 s, rest 2 min, stir 15 s. Operator records the actual grams used and the final weight (g) on the data sheet. If it will not pour off the spoon, add 5 ml water and re-stir; if it drips freely through the fork, add 0.2 g thickener and re-stir. Total target: about 180 g finished specimen.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: tilt a fork loaded with specimen; liquid drips in a slow, continuous stream, not a steady pour and not a single dollop. Pass = slow continuous drip. Spoon tilt test: a spoon held at 45° releases most of its load in a slow ribbon; a thin coating remains. Pass = slow ribbon, thin residual. Syringe flow test (mandatory at L3): fill the syringe to 10 ml; after 10 s, 8-10 ml remains. Pass = 8-10 ml retained.
specimens.visual_qc: Specimen on the fork: glossy, smooth, no visible fibre lumps; drips off the lower tines before the upper ones clear. On the spoon: fluid surface levels flat when the spoon stops moving, with no peaks or splits. Colour uniform pale cream, no brown specks.
specimens.shots: banana_L3_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard both in frame, specimen pooled on a white plate. banana_L3_take1_td.jpg — top-down, checkerboard fills frame, specimen pooled centrally. banana_L3_take1_fd.jpg — fork-drip close-up, tines loaded mid-drip. banana_L3_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s clip of fork drip then spoon tilt in one continuous take. banana_L3_take1_flow.mp4 — IDDSI syringe test, start to the 10 s mark.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: drip test runs as a steady pour, syringe leaves under 8 ml; add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, stir, rest 2 min, re-test. Too thick: fork drips as a single dollop or not at all, and the syringe still holds 10 ml at t=10 s with no appreciable flow; whisk in 5 ml water, re-test. Visible fibre on the fork after drip: sieve was skipped or rushed; re-sieve and re-thicken, do not patch the existing batch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g peeled ripe banana on the scale. Cut into 2 cm coins. Add to blender with 60 ml water. Blend 25 s on high, stop, scrape down, blend 20 s more. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard fibrous residue. Weigh the sieved puree and record the actual mass — target 190–210 g; do not work to a guessed volume. Return puree to blender, add thickener at 1.5 g per 100 g sieved puree (about 3 g for a 200 g batch) as the L4 calibration starting point, blend 10 s to homogenize, rest 2 min, stir, and re-test. 0 g is not a valid L4 starting point for banana: ripe banana puree is thin and separates on standing and will not hold L4 without thickener. The operator records the actual thickener mass used on the capture sheet. The 60 ml of water above is the only water this specimen ever gets: adding water to a runny L4 is the route to L3, which pours off the spoon and drips slowly through the fork tines, and the FAIL MODES below forbid it outright.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the fork tines fully into the specimen. The specimen must hold a clean indentation with no surface recovery for several seconds and must not flow through the slots between the tines. Spoon tilt test (protocol 5.2, the L4 wording): scoop a full spoon, hold it level, then tilt it sideways. Pass = the specimen holds its shape on the level spoon and then slides off as one cohesive mass with little residue left behind, with no separate thin liquid pooling on the spoon. A specimen that pours off in a slow continuous stream or drips in threads is too thin — that is the L3 criterion, not L4. A specimen that will not slide off at all and has to be scraped away is over-thickened and is past L4. "Zero flow off the spoon" is NOT the L4 pass: an L4 puree does slide off, and chasing a zero-flow endpoint over-thickens the specimen out of L4. Fork drip test: lift a forkful 5 cm above the surface. The mass must sit in a mound above the tines with no drip or thread. No separate thin liquid may pool on the surface of the specimen at any time.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface shows a soft satin sheen, not glossy or wet. Color is uniform pale cream, no brown flecks, no seed specks, no fiber strings. The mound on the spoon holds clean edges with no slumping shoulders.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45-degree hero: specimen in a small white bowl, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard placed in frame, label visible. File: banana_L4_take1.jpg. Still 2 — top-down: bowl centered, full checkerboard alongside. File: banana_L4_take2.jpg. Still 3 — fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines partially buried. File: banana_L4_take3.jpg. Clip 1 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous take. File: banana_L4_take1.mp4. Clip 2 — full IDDSI test film: pressure, drip, tilt. File: banana_L4_take2.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Runny: puree flows through the fork tines or drips in threads — add thickener in 0.5 g per 100 g of puree (1.0 g on a 200 g batch), re-blend 5 s to disperse, rest 2 min after each addition, until fork drip holds a mound above the tines and spoon tilt slides off as one cohesive mass with little residue. Never thin a runny batch with water: water is the L3 route, and a watered batch that passes fork-drip by holding a mound is a different level from the one on the label. Over-thickened: the specimen will not slide off the tilted spoon and has to be scraped away, or holds a sharp cut edge and cracks — the titration has overshot L4. Do not add water to rescue it; re-make from the reserve aliquot at the last dose that passed and re-test. If no dose between 1.5 and 4.0 g per 100 g gives a puree that both holds a mound above the fork tines and slides off the spoon as one mass, banana L4 is not reachable for this pack — record the event as unresolved and do not label it L4. Lumpy: visible fiber or seed specks remain after sieving — re-pass through the 4 mm sieve, do not push through with force. L4 is lump-free, so a lumpy specimen is too coarse; it is never corrected by leaving it. If a second pass does not clear it, the specimen is coarser than L4 (the L5 direction): mark the event FAIL with tests.pass = false, do not shoot it as L4, and do not re-label the media L5 — protocol section 7 QC rule 1 forbids renaming a specimen's media into another level. Thin liquid pooling on top after standing 30 s — the puree is separating and is under-thickened. Do NOT drain it off and re-blend, which mixes the free liquid straight back in; add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g puree, rest 2 min, re-test. If pooling recurs at the ceiling dose of 4.0 g per 100 g puree, the banana was over-ripe (soft and watery) — swap for a just-ripe batch and restart. Ceiling: banana L4 is reachable only with thickener. If the specimen still fails the spoon-tilt criterion above — either still pouring in a stream at 4.0 g thickener per 100 g puree, or refusing to slide off the spoon at all — record the event as unresolved and do not label it L4.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g peeled ripe banana on the digital scale and record the mass. Mash thoroughly with a fork against the bowl wall for 60-90 seconds until uniform; do not use the blender — blending collapses the loose L5 particle structure into the smooth puree that L4 requires. Gauge the mash with the 4 mm sieve: rub one fork-load at a time over the mesh, re-mash anything held back, and repeat until the whole portion passes, so that no particle exceeds 4 mm. The sieve is a particle gauge, not a finishing step — the finished specimen must still read as loose soft moist particles and never as a smooth satin puree. Fold briefly to redistribute moisture, then confirm and record the final mass on the scale. Add no thickener: 0 g at this level. Thickener is the L4 calibration starting point (banana needs roughly 1.5 g per 100 g of puree before it will hold a shape), so a specimen that only behaves once thickener goes in is L4 and must be filed against the L4 card. Add no liquid to begin with — ripe banana is moist as-is. Only a mash that is dry and crumbly and will not hold a mound is moistened, with water in 1 ml steps per 100 g, re-testing after every step.
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable tests at L5, per docs/CAPTURE_PROTOCOL.md section 5: the 4 mm sieve gauge, the spoon-tilt test, and the fork-pressure test as a supporting check. The fork-drip test and the 10 ml / 10 s syringe flow test are L3/L4 tests: they do not apply at L5 and must not be run, filmed or recorded as L5 evidence.  4 mm sieve gauge: rub one fork-load of mash over the mesh; re-mash and re-pass anything retained until the whole portion passes. Pass = nothing is retained above 4 mm.  Spoon tilt test: scoop a level teaspoon, hold it level, then tilt it sideways to 90 degrees over the bowl. Pass at L5 = the soft moist particles hold a loose mound that slumps and spreads as it comes off the spoon; the spoon is not swimming in separate liquid; the specimen does not pour off in a stream. Record on camera that no separate thin liquid pools on the spoon or the tray — any pooling means the specimen fails its level.  Fork pressure test (supporting check only): press the tines of the fork into a heaped spoonful until the thumbnail blanches white, then withdraw. Pass = the mash squashes readily and does not recover its shape when the fork is lifted.  Boundary against L4: a specimen that holds its shape on the spoon and slides off as one cohesive mass with little residue left behind, that sits in a mound above the fork tines with no drip at all, or that takes a clean indentation is behaving as L4 puree, not L5. It has not passed L5, whatever the sieve gauge says — re-label it and shoot the L4 test set (fork pressure, spoon tilt, fork drip) instead.
specimens.visual_qc: Loose soft moist particles, not a puree: the mound on the spoon has an open, grainy surface with shoulders that slump when the spoon is tilted, and it carries a slight natural sheen rather than the satin gloss of a blended puree. No particle above 4 mm against the ruler or the checkerboard. Colour uniform pale yellow with no white fibrous threads. No separate thin liquid pooling on the spoon, the bowl or the tray. No held shape, no clean-cut edges and no gel-like gloss — those are L4 and L6 features and disqualify the specimen at L5.
specimens.shots: Still 1, banana_L5_take1.jpg: 45-degree hero, specimen heaped on a spoon with the mound and its grainy surface visible, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2, banana_L5_take2.jpg: top-down of the bowl and the 4 mm sieve with the checkerboard centred. Still 3, banana_L5_take3.jpg: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines embedded in the mound, thumbnail blanching visible. Clip 1, banana_L5_take1.mp4: 8-12 s spoon-tilt in one unbroken take — level spoon, tilt to 90 degrees, the slump and spread, and the clean or pooling spoon. Clip 2, banana_L5_take2.mp4: full L5 test film — 4 mm sieve gauge, spoon tilt, then fork pressure as the supporting check, ruler in frame. No fork-drip and no syringe footage: neither is an L5 test.
specimens.fail_modes: (1) Particles or fibrous strands above 4 mm — re-mash and re-pass through the 4 mm sieve until the whole portion passes. (2) The specimen reads as a smooth puree, holds a clean shape, or slides off the spoon as one cohesive mass — that is L4 behaviour; add no thickener to force a pass. Re-label and shoot the L4 test set (fork pressure, spoon tilt, fork drip). (3) Thin liquid pools or separates — the specimen fails its level. Do NOT drain it on a paper towel: draining strips out the moisture that makes this L5 and leaves a denser, puree-like mass that then passes an L4-style fork-drip check. Re-make from a reserve aliquot with a just-ripe banana; if it pools again, record the event as FAIL with tests.pass = false. (4) The mash is dry and crumbly and will not hold a mound, or it recovers its shape after the fork press — moisten with water in 1 ml steps per 100 g, re-testing after each step; if it then pours off the spoon in a stream it has gone too far and is L3, so re-make. (5) The banana is underripe and the mash stays firm and grainy — use a riper fruit. Record any remake in the log.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g ripe banana flesh on the scale and record the mass. Peel, then cut the flesh by hand into slices and pieces measuring 8-15 mm on the longest edge, checked against the 100 mm ruler; aim for 12 mm plus or minus 2 mm. No mashing, no sieving and no blender: banana at L6 is cut fruit, and any step that takes the flesh below 8 mm — mashing it, pressing it through a 4 mm mesh, or re-forming sieved puree into cubes — produces L5 or L4 particles wearing an L6 label. Do not add thickener; L6 is solid pieces, not a thickened liquid. Do not add water or any other liquid. Hold the pieces cut-face up on a plate under an inverted bowl or a dry paper towel to slow browning — nothing damp, nothing that wets the cut faces — until capture. Target specimen 200 g, filmed within 10 min of cutting.
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable tests at L6, per docs/CAPTURE_PROTOCOL.md section 5: the fork-pressure test only. The spoon-tilt, fork-drip and 10 ml / 10 s syringe flow tests do not apply at L6 and must not be run, filmed or recorded as L6 evidence.  Fork-pressure test with the L6 sizing check in the same take: hold two or three pieces against the 100 mm ruler so the measurement is legible on camera, then place one of those measured 8-15 mm pieces under the fork tines and press with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass = the piece squashes and deforms under that pressure and does not recover its shape when the fork is lifted, and every piece in frame measures 8-15 mm on its longest edge. A piece that springs back is too firm for L6 and fails. A piece that smears or slumps before the fork touches it is too soft and fails.  The piece pressed must be one of the cut pieces measured in the same take, with its own cut faces visible — never a cube re-formed from mashed or sieved flesh, which measures 15 mm on the outside and is L5 inside.
specimens.visual_qc: Discrete cut slices with clean-cut faces and intact, not ragged, edges, every piece 8-15 mm on the longest edge against the 100 mm ruler; no piece below 8 mm. The cut face shows the fruit's own soft structure — not a smooth puree, and not a pressed-together or re-formed surface. Colour uniform pale yellow with no browned flecks and no white fibrous threads. The pieces hold their shape when lifted on a fork and no weeping juice pools on the plate or the fork. A pile that reads as mash, slumps when lifted, or shows no cut faces is L5 or L4 and fails L6.
specimens.shots: Still 1, banana_L6_take1.jpg: 45-degree hero, several pieces with their cut faces toward the camera, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2, banana_L6_take2.jpg: top-down on the checkerboard with several pieces against the 100 mm ruler. Still 3, banana_L6_take3.jpg: fork-press close-up mid-press on one measured piece, thumbnail blanching visible. Clip 1, banana_L6_take1.mp4: 8-12 s fork-press on one measured piece, showing the squash and the non-recovery. Clip 2, banana_L6_take2.mp4: full L6 test film — ruler sizing of two or three pieces, then the fork press on one of those same pieces. No spoon-tilt and no fork-drip footage: neither is an L6 test.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces above 15 mm — re-cut smaller and re-measure on the ruler. Pieces below 8 mm — the batch has fragmented; re-cut from a firmer section, do not capture. A piece springs back under the fork — too firm for L6; re-test a riper section, and if no section of the fruit passes, re-make with a riper banana rather than re-labelling a piece that will not squash. Never rescue a firm piece by mashing it, sieving it or re-cutting it into a cube: that converts the specimen to L5 or L4, so a card passed that way is a false label. Pieces weep juice on the plate — too ripe; lift the juice off and re-check. If it re-accumulates within 2 min the fruit is overripe for L6: re-make the batch as L5 (fork-mash to 4 mm with the sieve as gauge; the L5 test set is the 4 mm sieve gauge, spoon tilt, and fork pressure as a supporting check) and file it against the L5 card — never file it as L6. Record any remake in the log.

specimens.prep: Peel one firm ripe banana — fully yellow, no brown spotting, no oxidised patches; the cut face must feel firm to thumb pressure. Per-level requirement, stated on this card: L7 = pieces 15 mm or more, regular, requiring real chewing. Cut the peeled banana crosswise into halves with a single knife stroke. Keep one half as the reserve for a re-shoot; place the other half cut face up on the plate. Weigh the plated half on the digital scale: it must be 90–110 g and at least 15 mm in every dimension (a half is, by construction); record the actual mass to 1 g on the capture sheet — that recorded mass is the reference value for the set. Do not blend, do not sieve, do not add thickener, do not add water. This specimen is a whole food as normally served, so there is no calibration to perform and no grams-per-100 ml to record.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure (the deciding test at L7): hold the half steady on the plate and press the fork tines fully into the flesh with the same thumbnail-blanching pressure used at L6. Pass: the piece holds its shape — it may dent, split along the fibres, or cleave into two pieces, but it must NOT squash flat to a paste, smear, or collapse to something that needs no chewing. Pass = clear shape retained and real chewing required. A piece that flattens with little effort is L5/L6, not L7 — fail the specimen, do not record it as L7. Spoon tilt: not required at L7; skip. Fork drip: not required at L7; skip. Syringe flow: not required at L7; skip.
specimens.visual_qc: Whole peeled banana half on plate, pale cream to pale yellow flesh, no brown oxidation streaks. Skin-on is wrong; blended paste is wrong; sliced coins are wrong; a half that has squashed flat is wrong.
specimens.shots: banana_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, full half visible. banana_L7_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard under the half. banana_L7_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into the flesh. banana_L7_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press clip. banana_L7_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full fork-pressure sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Served unpeeled with skin on. Cut into coins or mashed beyond the L7 piece. Left out long enough to brown — cut fresh faces or re-make. Flesh over-ripe and squashing flat to a paste under the fork with little effort — reads as L5/L6, not L7 — re-make from a firm just-ripe banana. Resisting the fork is the required L7 behaviour and is NOT a failure. Any failure: re-make from a fresh banana, re-shoot the full set, do not patch a single frame.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g peeled ripe mango flesh. Add 60 ml water. Blend 45 s on high until smooth. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard fibrous residue; you should obtain roughly 280 ml of purée. Transfer to a cup on the digital scale and tare. Add thickener at 3 g per 100 ml of purée (≈8.4 g for 280 ml) as the calibration starting point. Whisk 20 s, rest 2 min, re-whisk 10 s. If the flow test shows less than 8 ml retained, add thickener in 0.5 g increments and retest. The per-level note "blend-thin" applies: sieve first, then thicken; do not skip the sieve.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: spoon 5 ml, tip a fork; the drop falls in a continuous thin stream over 4-6 s, not a single drop. Fork pressure: press fork tines flat into the surface for 5 s; the surface blanches but the fork does not sink through, and the specimen does not run between tines. Spoon tilt: tilt a heaped spoon 45°; the specimen slides slowly and pools rather than pouring. Syringe flow test (the L3 gate): draw 10 ml into the IDDSI syringe, start the timer, release; after 10 s, 8-10 ml remains in the syringe barrel. Record actual grams used and actual retained volume on the data sheet.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy, uniform yellow with no visible fibre or seed flecks. Coats a spoon in a thin even layer that holds its shape briefly then settles. Holds a fork-drip pattern for a second before merging back into the bulk.
specimens.shots: Capture against the A4 kit, checkerboard and 100 mm ruler visible. Stills: ripe_mango_L3_take1.jpg (45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame), ripe_mango_L3_take2.jpg (top-down, checkerboard centred), ripe_mango_L3_take3.jpg (fork-press close-up mid-press, tines buried, surface blanching). Clips: ripe_mango_L4_take1.mp4 (8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one take), ripe_mango_L4_take2.mp4 (full 10 s IDDSI syringe flow test, timer visible).
specimens.fail_modes: Runny: retained volume below 8 ml; add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 2 min, retest. Too thick: retained above 10 ml or fork holds its print without blanching; whisk in 5 ml water and retest. Lumpy / flecked: sieve was skipped or blender under-run; discard and re-blend 60 s then sieve. Any fail triggers a full remake; partial fixes are not logged.

specimens.prep: Peel ripe mango, remove pit. Weigh 250 g flesh, add 40 ml water. Blend 45 s on high until smooth. Pass through 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard fiber. Return puree to blender, blend 10 s to re-homogenize after sieving. Add thickener at 0 g per 100 ml starting point (calibration baseline); record actual grams added to reach L4 hold. No further dilution.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press fork tines into the specimen; puree must mound and not drip between tines under gravity; a clear tine outline should hold. Spoon tilt test: load a heaped spoon; surface stays mounded at a 20–30 degree tilt; no thin tail runs off. Fork drip test: lift fork; specimen sits in a mound above the tines and does not flow through gaps; no separate thin liquid pools on the plate. (Syringe flow test is for L3; not required here.)
specimens.visual_qc: Specimen on fork: uniform bright yellow, no visible fiber or seed flecks, matte sheen, clean tine outline visible beneath the mound. Specimen on spoon: smooth, glossy, mounded surface that holds its peak. No free liquid ring around the mound.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45-degree hero, puree mounded on spoon, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, scale showing 0.00 g: ripe_mango_L4_take1.jpg. Still 2 — top-down of sieve over bowl with checkerboard beneath, showing smooth passing residue: ripe_mango_L4_take2.jpg. Still 3 — fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines partly submerged, mound holding: ripe_mango_L4_take3.jpg. Clip 1 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt demonstrating mounded hold: ripe_mango_L4_take1.mp4. Clip 2 — IDDSI test film: full fork drip sequence from neutral to lift to 5 s hold: ripe_mango_L4_take2.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen drips through fork tines or flows on tilt — too thin; re-make adding thickener in 0.5 g per 100 ml increments and re-test. Visible fiber streaks or seed specks after sieving — sieve was rushed; re-pass and re-blend. White starch haze or gummy mouthfeel — over-thickened; re-make from baseline and step up in 0.25 g per 100 ml increments. If any re-make is required, re-shoot all five media items before logging the specimen as L4.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g ripe mango flesh on the digital scale; reserve natural juice. Pulse in the consumer blender 6-8 s only — do not purée to smooth. Transfer to bowl, mash firmly with fork 30 s to break fibres; keep dice <=4 mm. Pass mash through the 4 mm sieve using the fork back; discard any coarse strands that will not pass. Weigh back; record retained mass. Re-incorporate the reserved juice; stir to uniform moistness. No thickener added; no water added. Target final 180-200 g. This step is impossible if the sieve yields <120 g — then the mango is too fibrous for L5 and must be reported as off-spec.
specimens.iddsi_test: S — Fork pressure: place fork tines down on 1.5 cm mound; press thumb on bowl until thumbnail blanches; the specimen must squash, leave clear tine marks, and not spring back. Spoon tilt: load 5 ml onto spoon; tilt 45°; specimen must sit in a cohesive pile, not slide or run. Fork drip: lift fork with sample; no thin liquid must drip through tines within 10 s. No separate thin liquid visible pooling on plate. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: On fork: moist bright orange-yellow particles clearly visible, all <=4 mm, tines print into the sample without resistance. On spoon: holds a peaked mound at tilt, glossy surface, no free juice pooling at the rim.
specimens.shots: ripe_mango_L5_take1.jpg: 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. ripe_mango_L5_take2.jpg: top-down, checkerboard centred, full specimen spread. ripe_mango_L5_take3.jpg: fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines embedded. ripe_mango_L5_take1.mp4: 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. ripe_mango_L5_take2.mp4: full IDDSI test sequence, audio-free, single take.
specimens.fail_modes: (a) Blender run too long creates a smooth purée — fails fork pressure (springs back) and shows thin liquid; re-make by re-dicing fresh flesh, do not re-blend. (b) Sieve step skipped leaves >4 mm strands — fails particle size and pressure test; re-mash and re-sieve. (c) Juice drained off leaves dry crumb — fails spoon tilt (slides off); re-incorporate reserved juice or discard batch and start over.

specimens.prep: Dice 200 g ripe mango flesh on a clean board into 8–12 mm cubes. Confirm no piece exceeds 15 mm by visual check against the 100 mm ruler; reject any oversized cube. Do not blend, sieve, or thicken. Ripe mango at L6 needs no liquid, no gum, and no mechanical breakdown. State in notes: per-level note caps pieces at 15 mm — dicing only.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure: press the tines flat onto a piece with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass if the piece squashes, does not spring back, and the thumbnail clearly whitens. Fork drip: lift a loaded fork; pieces must not drip through or fall. Spoon tilt: tilt a spoon holding 4–5 pieces; pieces stay without sliding off.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: cubes hold shape but glisten with fibrous moisture; surface looks soft, not rubbery. On the spoon: pieces sit in a shallow pool of their own juice, edges rounded, no intact skin strips. Color is uniform mango yellow-orange with no green.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45-degree hero, ripe_mango_L6_take1.jpg, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard visible at frame edge. Still 2 — top-down with checkerboard centered, pieces spread in a single layer. Still 3 — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumb blanch captured. Clip 1 — ripe_mango_L6_take1.mp4, 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. Clip 2 — IDDSI test film, full protocol.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces over 15 mm: re-dice smaller. Under-ripe fruit springs back under thumb: re-make with riper mango or discard. Excess juice pools and drips through fork tines: drain 30 s on the sieve, re-shoot.

specimens.prep: Bought form: one whole fresh ripe mango (250–350 g, Ataulfo/Alphonso type or similar) as sold — skin on, unpeeled, uncooked. Allergens: none of the major declared allergens (no milk, egg, fish, crustacean, mollusc, peanut, tree nut, soy, wheat/gluten, sesame, celery, mustard, lupin, sulphites). Wash and dry the fruit. Cut one cheek from each side of the flat pit with a chef's knife. Peel each cheek with a vegetable peeler and discard the skin. Cut each cheek into wedges 15–20 mm thick and 20–25 mm wide; lay every piece against the 15 mm checkerboard and set aside any piece under 15 mm in any direction. Weigh 150 g of accepted wedges onto the capture plate. Do not blend, sieve, chop fine, cook, or add thickener, water or any liquid. The specimen is the fruit exactly as served at the table.
specimens.iddsi_test: - 5.1 Fork pressure — ACTIVE, and the only applicable test at L7. Place one wedge on the plate and press the fork tines flat onto it with thumb pressure until the thumbnail blanches. Pass = the wedge squashes, splits or crumbles and does not return to its original shape when the fork is lifted. Test three wedges; all three must pass. - 5.2 Spoon tilt — skip: applies at L3, L4 and L5 only; it scores flow and hold of smooth and minced textures and has no criterion for a whole piece at L7. - 5.3 Fork drip — skip: applies at L3 and L4 only; a solid wedge neither drips nor flows, so the test cannot discriminate at L7. - 5.4 Syringe flow — skip: applies at L3 only; a solid wedge cannot be loaded into the 10 ml syringe.
specimens.visual_qc: Each wedge keeps its own outline on the plate, separated from its neighbours by ≥10 mm; pieces do not mound or stick together. Cut faces show visible fruit fibre with a light juice sheen, and no free juice pools anywhere on the plate. Colour is uniform ripe yellow-orange with no grey or brown bruising and no black oxidised spots on the test wedge. Every piece measures ≥15 mm in all directions against the 15 mm checkerboard.
specimens.shots: Still 1: bf32_ripe_mango_L7_take1.jpg — 45° hero, wedges fanned, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2: bf32_ripe_mango_L7_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard filling the frame. Still 3: bf32_ripe_mango_L7_take3.jpg — fork-pressure close-up, tines mid-press on one wedge. Clip 1: bf32_ripe_mango_L7_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork pressure applied to three wedges in one take. Clip 2: bf32_ripe_mango_L7_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence (fork pressure only), one continuous take.
specimens.fail_modes: Wedge resists fork pressure and springs back (under-ripe) — too firm for L7: replace with a riper mango, re-cut and retest. Do not steam, blend or sieve to soften it; those steps move the specimen toward L4/L3, away from L7. Wedge collapses to purée or runs as juice under light pressure (over-ripe) — behaves as L3/L4: reject and use a firmer ripe specimen; do not add thickener, which cannot return mashed fruit to whole pieces. Any piece measures under 15 mm — re-cut a larger wedge; if the fruit is too small to yield ≥15 mm wedges, use a larger mango (≥300 g). Wedges stick together in a mound with juice pooling — separate onto the plate with a ≥10 mm gap and shoot within 10 min of cutting; do not add liquid.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g ripe papaya flesh. Blend in consumer blender 30 s on high until smooth; do not sieve — sieving a blend-thin fruit strips the fibres that carry the L3 body. The specimen must pour, so thin with water: add 40 ml water and blend 5 s more. Pour into a cup and weigh total. Calculate thickener at 1.0 g per 100 ml of specimen as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Sprinkle the thickener on the surface, rest 30 s for hydration, then stir 20 s with the fork until homogenous. Wait 2 min before testing. If the mix runs off the spoon like juice, add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, stir, rest 1 min, retest. Up to three additions; beyond that, re-make.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork tines into 10 ml of specimen; surface must yield to light pressure with the tines leaving a clear, persistent imprint. Spoon tilt: a 5 ml spoonful on the spoon must hold its shape when the spoon is tilted to 45 degrees; it should slide off slowly as a single cohesive blob, not run. Fork drip: lift the fork; the specimen drips continuously but slowly in a thick ribbon through the tines — it must not pour in a stream nor sit solid on the fork. Syringe flow: fill the 10 ml IDDSI syringe, release, start timer. After 10 s, 8–10 ml must remain in the barrel. Above 10 ml = too thick, below 8 ml = too thin.
specimens.visual_qc: 1. Glossy uniform orange surface with no free liquid pooling around the cup edge. 2. On the fork, it mounds then settles slowly into a soft peak that holds shape. 3. No fruit fibre strands, lumps, or unblended pulp visible.
specimens.shots: Still 1, hero: specimen in a white cup on A4 mat, 100 mm ruler vertical, 15 mm checkerboard front-left, camera at 45 degrees. Still 2, top-down: same mat, checkerboard centred, specimen cup centred. Still 3, fork-press close-up: frame the tines mid-press, ruler edge in shot for scale. Clip 1, 8–12 s: fork press followed by spoon tilt, continuous. Clip 2, 8–12 s: IDDSI syringe fill, 10 s hold, final meniscus read. Name every file papaya_L3_take1.jpg or .mp4, incrementing the take number on reshoot.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: drips through fork in a thin stream and syringe reads under 8 ml — add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 1 min, retest once. Too stiff: holds shape on tilted spoon and syringe reads over 10 ml — whisk in 5 ml water per 100 ml, rest 1 min, retest once. Grainy or fibrous: blender time was too short — re-blend the batch 15 s on high before any thickener adjustment. If still grainy after one re-blend, discard and re-make from fresh fruit.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g ripe papaya flesh, peel and dice. Add to consumer blender with 60 ml water; blend 45 s. Pass through 4 mm sieve; discard coarse residue. Return puree to blender, add 2.0 g thickener per 100 ml as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Blend 20 s, rest 60 s, blend 10 s. Target final mass approximately 300 g.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift fork; puree must sit in a mound above the tines, not drip through. Pass = no drip in 10 s. Fork pressure: press fork tines into specimen on a flat plate; puree must flatten and hold, not run back through gaps. Pass = clean tine spacing, no flow. Spoon tilt: scoop, tilt spoon 45°. Pass = specimen stays on spoon, no sliding off.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface glossy and uniform, no pulp specks or liquid ring on the plate. Color even orange-pink, no streaks. Holds a soft peak when mounded with the fork.
specimens.shots: papaya_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame, specimen mounded on plate. papaya_L4_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only, full specimen. papaya_L4_take1_fork.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. papaya_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. papaya_L4_take1_iddsi.mp4 — IDDSI test film: fork drip, fork pressure, spoon tilt, each 5-10 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: puree flows through fork tines or drips in 10 s; re-blend and add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, retest. Too thick: specimen cracks or holds tine imprint without spreading; re-blend with 10-15 ml water, retest. Visible liquid pooling around mound: under-thickened or over-blended; sieve again and add thickener in 0.5 g per 100 ml steps.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g ripe papaya flesh. Dice to ≤4 mm on the board using the 100 mm ruler as a guide. Do NOT blend: per-level note requires dice ≤4 mm with its juice, and blending would make the texture pasty rather than minced & moist. Press lightly with the fork to release juice; discard loose drippings so no separate thin liquid pools on the plate. If pieces fall outside 4 mm, re-dice. If juice runs freely, drain and re-mix with the pieces. No thickener. No water.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines flat against the specimen; particles squash, do not spring back, and remain cohesive on the fork head. Pass = full squash, no recovery, particles separate easily under fork pressure. Spoon-tilt test: tilt a heaped spoonful; specimen holds shape, slides off in one soft clump, not running, not stacked. Pass = cohesive slide, no liquid drips. Fork-drip test: lift forkful above plate for 5 s; no drops fall. Pass = zero drip. No syringe test for L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: visible fine dice ≤4 mm, glossy and wet but not runny, pieces mat together as one mass. On the spoon: soft mound that flattens slightly under its own weight, juice sheens the surface, no free liquid in the plate well. Colour uniform bright orange.
specimens.shots: papaya_L5_take1.jpg ×3: hero 45° with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard visible alongside specimen; top-down framed on checkerboard showing spread of dice; fork-press close-up mid-press showing squash. papaya_L5_take1.mp4 ×2: 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt clip; IDDSI test film covering all three tests in sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces >4 mm visible against ruler: re-dice. Free thin juice pools on plate: drain and re-combine. Specimen bounces back under fork pressure (too firm) or liquefies (over-pressed): discard and remake from fresh dice.

specimens.prep: Select a firm-ripe papaya — flesh that yields to firm thumb pressure but still cuts into cubes that hold their shape and do not exude free juice. Peel, halve, and scoop out seeds. Dice the flesh on a clean board into 8–15 mm cubes, target 12 mm ± 2 mm, measuring each cut batch against the 100 mm ruler. Gauge for oversize only: pass the dice over a 15 mm sieve — or, if no 15 mm sieve is in the kit, measure every piece against the 100 mm ruler, which is the required sizing reference and is stricter, since a sieve lets a long thin piece through diagonally — and re-dice anything over 15 mm until nothing is held back. Do NOT pass the papaya through a 4 mm sieve at any point — a 4 mm mesh cannot enforce a 15 mm limit, and nothing in the 8–15 mm L6 range can pass it, so a 4 mm sieve would shred the batch to L5. You need 200 g of diced pieces for the specimen plate. Spread the dice on the board for 5 min and lift off any free juice that collects, so no separate liquid is carried to the plate. Do not blend — pureeing destroys the L6 bite-sized texture. Do not add thickener; L6 is solid pieces, not a thickened liquid. Do not add water.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test — the only IDDSI test that applies at L6: press the flat of a fork onto one piece, applying pressure through your thumbnail until the thumbnail blanches white, hold 10 s, then lift. Pass = the piece squashes, changes shape, and does not recover. Size confirmation on the 100 mm ruler: every piece must measure 8–15 mm on its longest edge. Spoon-tilt, fork-drip, and syringe-flow tests are not used at L6 and must not be run or recorded as level evidence.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces should look moist and glossy with clean-cut faces and intact, not ragged, edges, measured 8–15 mm against the 100 mm ruler; no piece below 8 mm. Pieces hold their shape when lifted on a fork — no weeping juice pooling on the plate or spoon. Colour uniform pale orange, no collapsed or mushy cut faces.
specimens.shots: Stills: papaya_L6_take1.jpg hero at 45 degrees with ruler and checkerboard in frame; papaya_L6_take2.jpg top-down on checkerboard with several pieces against the 100 mm ruler; papaya_L6_take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail blanching visible.
