Clips: papaya_L6_take1.mp4 8–12 s fork-press then size check against the 100 mm ruler; papaya_L6_take2.mp4 full IDDSI test sequence — ruler sizing of two or three pieces, then fork press hold 10 s, recover check.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces recover after fork press — too firm; re-test a riper section. If no section of the fruit passes, this fruit cannot be produced at L6 by bench method: the closest achievable is L5 (fork-mashable, ~4 mm), so re-cut the whole batch to 4 mm, re-test, and file it as L5 — do not file an L6 card against fruit that springs back. Pieces smear or crush to paste — overripe or blended; restart with a firmer fruit, and if the whole fruit is uniformly overripe, record L5 as above. Pieces larger than 15 mm — re-dice and re-gauge on the 15 mm sieve (or against the 100 mm ruler) before capture. Pieces below 8 mm — the batch has fragmented; re-cut from a firmer cube, do not capture. Free juice pools on the plate — too ripe or insufficiently drained; lift off the juice and re-check; if it re-accumulates within 2 min, the fruit is overripe for L6 and the batch goes to L5.

specimens.prep: Start with 200 g fresh ripe papaya, peeled and seeded. Per the per-level note, cut into slices as normally served — no blending, no sieving, no thickener. No water or liquid added. The fruit's natural moisture is expected at L7; the operator records actual juice release onto the capture surface. Specimen must be at room temperature (20–24 °C) for testing.
specimens.iddsi_test: L7 is proven by behaviour, not flow. Fork pressure: the prongs must be able to pierce the slice and lift it cleanly with the fruit holding its shape — no squashing through the tines. Spoon tilt: a slice rests on an inverted spoon without sliding off under gravity. Fork drip: no liquid pours through the tines or drips continuously; a small amount of natural juice on the fork is acceptable, but no flow. No syringe test applies at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: Slice holds a clean cut edge, not collapsed or fibrous-strewn. Colour is uniform ripe orange-red with no bruising. On the fork the slice sits flat across the tines without sagging between them.
specimens.shots: papaya_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, slice centred. papaya_L7_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard under the slice. papaya_L7_take1_press.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, showing the slice under the tines. Clip 1: papaya_L7_take1.mp4, 8–12 s, fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. Clip 2: papaya_L7_take1_test.mp4, the full IDDSI L7 test pass.
specimens.fail_modes: Slices too thin to support their own weight on the fork — re-cut to 15–20 mm thickness. Over-ripe fruit pools excessive juice (visible drip >1 s) — re-make with firmer ripe papaya and blot surface. Under-ripe fruit resists fork pierce and fractures rather than cuts — re-make with fully ripe fruit only.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g ripe dragon fruit flesh (no skin). Add 80 ml water. Blend 25 s on high until smooth. Sieve through 4 mm once; discard fibrous residue. Add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml of sieved volume as the calibration starting point; record actual grams used. Stir 20 s, rest 2 min, stir 5 s. If the mix runs off the spoon, add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml and re-stir; record final value.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: hold fork over bowl for 10 s; drips slowly and continuously through tines — passes if it does not pour in a single stream and does not sit as a lump. Fork pressure: press fork tines into specimen on a plate for 5 s; surface m dents clearly, no full separation, specimen does not spring back. Spoon tilt: tilt a loaded spoon; specimen slides off slowly in one cohesive dollop, leaves a thin even coating. Syringe flow: fill 10 ml IDDSI syringe, release, wait 10 s; leaves 8-10 ml in the syringe. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Even magenta-pink, no skin flecks or fibre. Smooth glossy surface that mounds then slowly levels on the spoon. Coats the spoon back without running off the rim.
specimens.shots: dragon_fruit_L3_take1_hero.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen loaded on spoon. dragon_fruit_L3_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. dragon_fruit_L3_take1_forkpress.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. dragon_fruit_L3_take1_forkpress.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. dragon_fruit_L3_take1_iddsitest.mp4 — full IDDSI flow test, timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: drips in a steady stream off fork, syringe reads under 8 ml — add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 2 min, re-test. Too thick: piles and holds shape, leaves over 10 ml — whisk in 5 ml water per 100 ml, re-test. Fibre lumps: visible specks, sieve catches residue — re-blend 10 s and re-sieve. Max one re-make; second fail = discard and note cause.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g fresh ripe dragon fruit flesh on the digital scale. Cube into 2 cm pieces. Add to the consumer blender with 50 ml water. Blend 45 s on high, stop, scrape down, blend 30 s more. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard fibrous residue and seeds that do not pass. Weigh the sieved puree. Per 100 ml puree, add 1.0 g thickener as the calibration starting point — record the actual grams used. Stir with a fork for 30 s, rest 2 min, stir 10 s. If the mound collapses, add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 2 min, and re-test. Do not exceed 2.0 g per 100 ml; if L4 is not reached, re-make with longer sieve work and re-blend rather than over-thickening.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the fork tines into the mound on a flat plate; the surface must hold a clear indentation without the mound splitting or liquid bleeding — pass if the print stays. Spoon tilt test: load 5 ml onto a spoon and tilt to 45 degrees; the specimen must sit in a mound and not flow or drip off — pass if it stays piled. Fork drip test: lift the fork; the specimen must sit in a mound above the tines, not drip continuously through them — pass if zero drips in 10 s. No separate thin liquid must pool on the plate.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a soft, glossy magenta mound with no visible seed flecks or white pulp chunks and a clean indentation under the tines. On the spoon: a rounded dome that holds its peak when tilted. On the plate: matte surface, no watery halo around the base of the mound.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero shot, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, mound centered. Still 2: top-down with checkerboard filling the frame. Still 3: fork-press close-up, tines mid-press, ruler edge visible. Clip 1: 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous take. Clip 2: the full IDDSI test film — fork pressure, fork drip, spoon tilt, in that order. Files: dragon_fruit_L4_take1.jpg, dragon_fruit_L4_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Fail 1: watery pink liquid pools on the plate within 30 s of plating — puree was under-thickened or not rested; re-make and add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml. Fail 2: mound slumps flat on spoon tilt — too much water or insufficient rest; re-make with 30 ml water instead of 50 ml. Fail 3: visible seed specks or fibrous strands on the surface — sieve was skipped or rushed; re-blend and re-sieve, do not over-thicken to hide it. Maximum two re-makes per take; on the third failure, swap fruit batch and restart.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g peeled dragon fruit flesh on the scale. Place in the blender; pulse 6–8 s only — stop while seeds are still visibly whole. Do NOT sieve; the 4 mm sieve is not used because the per-level note states tiny seeds pass through and must be recorded, not removed. Dice the pulsed pulp with a knife to <=4 mm, keeping its own juice. Mash firmly with a fork until uniformly coarse and visibly moist. Do not add water. Do not add thickener. Log the juice volume released (ml) and confirm no separate thin liquid pools on the plate.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the specimen; it must squash and NOT spring back when pressure is released. Spoon tilt: tilt a heaped spoon to 45°; specimen must hold together with no drip, no run. Fork drip: lift fork and hold over plate 5 s; zero drops falling. Particle check: lift and inspect — visible bits must all measure <=4 mm against the ruler.
specimens.visual_qc: Coarse, glossy pink pulp with fine black seed specks evenly distributed. Clings to fork tines as a single mass. No free juice pooling under the mound on the plate.
specimens.shots: Still 1: dragon_fruit_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2: dragon_fruit_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. Still 3: dragon_fruit_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up at mid-compression. Clip 1: dragon_fruit_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. Clip 2: dragon_fruit_L5_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film with pass/fail verdict spoken on camera.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-blended → smooth puree with ruptured seeds: fails fork-pressure (squirts) and particle check; re-make and pulse shorter. Under-processed → chunks >4 mm: fails particle check; re-dice finer, do not re-blend. Standing >10 min releases thin liquid: fails spoon-tilt and fork drip; re-mash and re-shoot immediately.

specimens.prep: Start with 150 g fresh ripe dragon fruit flesh, scooped from skin, no black seeds knocked loose. Cut into cubes against a 15 mm checkerboard grid; reject any cube >15 mm. Do NOT blend — the per-level note requires dice, not puree. Do NOT sieve. Do NOT add thickener or water. Working yield: ~140 g usable dice; discard ~10 g trim and seed-loss.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press thumbnail into one cube on the fork tines. Pass = thumbnail blanches white, the cube squashes flat, and it does NOT spring back when pressure is released. Spoon-tilt test: place three cubes on a spoon and tilt to 45°. Pass = cubes sit on the spoon without sliding off or falling; small moisture is acceptable. Fork-drip test: lift loaded fork vertically. Pass = no liquid runs or drips from the cubes. (No syringe test — L3 only.)
specimens.visual_qc: Look for: (1) cubes measure ≤15 mm on every edge against the ruler; (2) flesh colour is uniform pink/magenta with visible black seed dots, no bruising or translucency; (3) cube holds its shape when lifted on the fork — if it slumps or smears, it is too wet/overripe and must be re-made with a firmer fruit.
specimens.shots: dragon_fruit_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero: ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame, 3–4 cubes fanned. dragon_fruit_L6_take1_td.jpg — top-down: checkerboard full frame, cubes spaced. dragon_fruit_L6_take1_forkpress.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail whitening visible. dragon_fruit_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one take. dragon_fruit_L6_take1_test.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence (pressure → tilt → drip).
specimens.fail_modes: (1) Cube exceeds 15 mm — re-dice smaller, do not press on. (2) Overripe fruit smears under fork-pressure instead of squashing cleanly — swap to a firmer dragon fruit and re-cut. (3) Excess free liquid pools on the plate from bruised flesh — pat cubes dry on paper; if liquid persists, re-make with drier flesh.

specimens.prep: Place 200 g fresh ripe dragon fruit on the A4 capture mat. Per the per-level note, slice as cut: produce four transverse rounds ~15 mm thick using a kitchen knife; do not blend, do not sieve, do not thicken. Weigh each round on the digital scale; record mass to 0.1 g. Set one round aside as the reference specimen, untouched. Keep two rounds for fork and spoon tests, one round for the press close-up.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the tines firmly onto a round until the thumbnail blanches white. The piece must not squish, flatten, smear, or fall apart under full pressure. Pass = shape and structure visibly retained. Spoon tilt: lift a round on a spoon and tilt to a steep angle, then invert. Pass = the round sits on the spoon, does not pour, does not slide or drip off, and remains in one piece. No fork drip test needed at L7. No syringe flow test at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: clean cut edges, vivid magenta flesh with small black seeds evenly distributed, no juice pooling on the mat, flesh holds the fork tine shape without sagging. On the spoon: round sits as a coherent disc, surface matte-to-slightly-glossy, no free liquid film under the piece.
specimens.shots: dragon_fruit_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, whole round + ruler + checkerboard in frame. dragon_fruit_L7_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard beneath the round. dragon_fruit_L7_take1_press.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. dragon_fruit_L7_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s clip of fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous audio. dragon_fruit_L7_take1_film.mp4 — 8-12 s IDDSI test film: fork pressure, spoon tilt, in sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-ripeness: flesh turns to mush or weeps pink juice on the mat — fails L7. Use a firmer fruit and re-make. Damaged skin or bruised flesh causing collapse on first press — discard, re-make with fresh rounds. Excess free liquid pooling around the piece reads as L6 — blot, re-shoot, re-grade.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g peeled soft ripe persimmon flesh; discard skin and any firm core. Blend 25-35 s in consumer blender until fully smooth, scraping once. Do not sieve — the per-level note says blend-thin, so fibre is driven by blender time, not sieve. Measure puree volume; target 100 ml. Add thickener at the calibration starting point of 3.0 g per 100 ml, sprinkle while blending 5-10 s. Stir, rest 60 s, stir again. If the IDDSI flow test leaves less than 8 ml or more than 10 ml in the syringe after 10 s, adjust by 0.25 g per 100 ml increments and record the actual grams used. Re-test after every change.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: specimen flows slowly through fork tines in a continuous thin stream, not in dollops. Spoon tilt: spoonful sits in a mound and slides off slowly when tilted to 70-90 degrees, leaving a thick coating. Fork pressure: tines leave a clear, lasting line on the surface with no recovery. Syringe flow test: fill 10 ml, release, after 10 s 8-10 ml remains. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy, homogenous orange-tan surface on the spoon. No lumps, no skin specks, no liquid separation pooling at edges. Coats a fork evenly; no translucent thin patches.
specimens.shots: soft_ripe_persimmon_L3_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. soft_ripe_persimmon_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. soft_ripe_persimmon_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. soft_ripe_persimmon_L3_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. soft_ripe_persimmon_L3_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI syringe flow test, 10 s timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Runny: passes 10 ml leaving under 8 ml — add 0.25 g thickener per 100 ml and re-test. Too thick: drips in dollops or syringe retains over 10 ml — thin with 5 ml water per 100 ml and re-test. Grainy or stringy: blender time under 25 s — re-blend 10 s. Any single failure: re-make, do not patch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g ripe persimmon flesh (skin and stem removed). Add 20-40 ml water. Blend 45-60 s until smooth, scraping the jar once. Sieve through the 4 mm sieve using a fork to push the pulp through. If the puree flows below mound height on the spoon or sits below the fork tines during the fork-drip test, thicken: start at 1.0 g thickener per 100 ml puree, blend 10 s, re-test, and record the actual grams used. Per-level note "blend-hold": hold the target shape on the spoon without adding liquid back in. If sieving through 4 mm cannot remove the persimmon fibres to give a smooth mound-holding texture, state so in the notes; do not over-thin to force passage.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: the tines leave a clear, clean imprint that holds its shape on the puree surface; the surface does not close back up. Spoon tilt: a 5-8 ml scoop sits in a mound and slides off slowly when tilted, not as a pour. Fork drip: the puree sits as a mound above the tines and does not drip or run through the gaps. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Mound on the spoon taller than it is wide, soft peak at the top. On the fork, puree clings across and between tines with no shine of free liquid around it. Uniform colour, no visible fibre strands, no standing juice pooling on the plate.
specimens.shots: Still 1 hero: 45-degree angle, specimen on the spoon, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2 top-down: plate with checkerboard underneath, fork and spoon visible. Still 3 fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into the puree. Clip 1 fork-press and spoon-tilt, 8-12 s. Clip 2 the full IDDSI test film, 8-12 s. Files: soft_ripe_persimmon_L4_take1.jpg and .mp4 for each.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: puree runs through fork tines or spreads flat on the spoon, re-add 0.2-0.5 g thickener per 100 ml and re-blend. Too thick: puree fractures or cracks on the spoon tilt, add 5 ml water per 100 ml and re-blend. Lumpy with fibres caught by the sieve: re-sieve or re-blend, and if fibres still remain note the failure; a single remake only.

specimens.prep: Use 150 g ripe persimmon flesh, skin and stem removed. Fork-mash on a plate until smooth, pressing and dragging the tines through the flesh. Work in two halves; scrape both halves together between passes so no chunks hide at the seams. Sieve the mash through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard anything that will not pass. Press retained material once more; if residue still exceeds a pea-sized clump, sieve again. No blender, no added water, no thickener. Expected yield: roughly 130–140 g of uniform pulp at room temperature.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines flat into the specimen until the blanch shows through; the pulp must squashes and not spring back. Fork-drip test: lift the loaded fork; specimen must not drip or run through the gaps. Spoon-tilt test: load a teaspoon, tilt to vertical; the pulp holds together and slides as one lump, leaving only a moist film, no separate thin liquid. If any test drips or recovers its shape, re-mash and re-sieve.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: even orange pulp with no visible flecks larger than a pinhead, soft sheen but no pooling liquid at the spoon rim. On the fork: tissue fills the gaps between tines uniformly; the back of the fork reads as a solid colour with no white specks or strings.
specimens.shots: Shoot under bright window light on the A4 kit, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame for scale. Capture soft_ripe_persimmon_L5_take1.jpg at 45-degree hero, soft_ripe_persimmon_L5_take2.jpg as top-down on the checkerboard, soft_ripe_persimmon_L5_take3.jpg as fork-press close-up mid-press. Film soft_ripe_persimmon_L5_take1.mp4 (8–12 s) of fork-press then spoon-tilt. Film soft_ripe_persimmon_L5_take2.mp4 as the full IDDSI test sequence, audio optional.
specimens.fail_modes: Visible lumps above 4 mm after sieving — re-mash and re-sieve the full batch, do not pick out specks. Free liquid pooling on the plate — drain briefly on paper; if it persists, the fruit is over-ripe and must be replaced with a firmer ripe specimen. Mash springs back under fork pressure — work it longer; if it still recovers, the fruit is under-ripe and unsuitable.

specimens.prep: Stage a firm-ripe persimmon, ripe enough to eat but firm enough to hold a cut edge; fully ripe jelly flesh will not hold an 8 mm piece, and that is the limit of this food. Peel, discard skin and stem, quarter by hand; remove seeds and any fibrous core. Weigh 150 g flesh on the scale, zeroed first. Cut by hand into 8–15 mm pieces measured against the ruler — knife-cut or hand-torn. No blender and no sieving: a 4 mm mesh caps every particle at 4 mm and forces the specimen to L5, and no mesh of any size can enforce a 15 mm limit. Do not add water, milk, or liquid — extra moisture pushes the specimen toward L5. Do not add thickener — L6 does not require thickener; adding it would push the specimen toward L4/L5 and is incompatible with the level. Calibrate scale to zero before weighing specimen for capture. Target specimen 150 g, tested within 2 min of cutting.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test, the only sanctioned test at L6: hold an 8–15 mm piece on a flat plate and press with the thumbnail until it blanches white; the piece must squash flat and not recover its original form when pressure is released — PASS. Confirm the piece measured 8–15 mm on the ruler before pressing; a specimen that is a smear before the fork touches it has not passed anything. Spoon-tilt test: NOT APPLICABLE at L6 — do not run. Fork-drip test: NOT APPLICABLE at L6 — do not run. The 10 ml/10 s syringe flow test does not apply to L6 and should not be run.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces hold a soft, rounded shape on the spoon without pooling as sauce. Every piece measures 8–15 mm on the ruler; none below 8 mm, none beyond 15 mm. Color is uniform deep orange throughout the pile, no pale fibrous lumps. Surface looks moist but not glossy-wet; nothing runs off the spoon edge when level. The spoon here is a viewing surface only: the L6 level evidence is the fork-pressure film plus the ruler measurement, so do not run, film or record a spoon-tilt result.
specimens.shots: Capture three stills: soft_ripe_persimmon_L6_take1.jpg hero at 45° with ruler and checkerboard in frame; soft_ripe_persimmon_L6_take2.jpg top-down on the checkerboard with several pieces against the 100 mm ruler; soft_ripe_persimmon_L6_take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press with thumbnail blanch visible. Capture two clips: soft_ripe_persimmon_L6_take1.mp4 the 8–12 s fork-press sequence (L6 has no spoon-tilt step); soft_ripe_persimmon_L6_take2.mp4 the full IDDSI test sequence — ruler sizing of two or three pieces, then the fork press on one of those same pieces. A retake takes the next take number; never overwrite a take.
specimens.fail_modes: Underripe fruit: pieces stay springy and recover after fork-pressure — re-make with riper fruit. Pieces slump, merge, or pool as sauce within 60 s of cutting: this food cannot be certified L6 on the bench — ripe persimmon flesh will not hold an 8–15 mm cut edge reliably, and no amount of sieving or blending fixes that (sieving guarantees L5). Record what the specimen actually is — if it spreads into a loose moist mound that does not pour it is L5, if the mass sits on the fork and holds a soft shape it is L4, if it flows off the spoon in a stream it is L3 — and shoot that level's test set instead (L5: 4 mm sieve gauge, spoon tilt, fork pressure as a supporting check; L4: fork drip, fork pressure, spoon tilt; L3: fork drip, spoon tilt, 10 ml/10 s syringe flow). Never sieve or blend an L6/L7 specimen below 15 mm. Pieces cut below 8 mm — re-cut larger. Liquid pooling on the plate after the test: moisture has separated, the fruit is too ripe for L6 — see the re-label rule above; do not sieve to rescue it.

specimens.prep: Select a ripe but firm, unbruised persimmon (Fuyu type): the flesh must be firm enough to require chewing, and a soft, melting or bruised fruit cannot reach L7 by any bench method. Chill the whole fruit at 4 °C for 30 min before cutting — chilling is the only bench lever that firms this flesh and it is the maximum firmness obtainable. Record start mass on the digital scale; target 150–200 g for the reference specimen. Wash, pat dry. Do not peel. Cut the fruit in half along the equator with a clean knife. Keep both halves intact; do not blend, do not sieve, do not add thickener, do not add liquid. The specimen is the halved fruit as normally served. Confirm the per-level note: halves as cut is the correct reference form. Blot surface juice with a paper towel immediately before the shot. Set aside one half for the test, one half for plating.
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable at L7: fork pressure only (§5.1). Spoon tilt (§5.2) and fork drip (§5.3) are L3–L5 tests and must not be run, filmed, or recorded as pass/fail at L7 — ripe persimmon flesh clinging to a spoon is expected and is not a defect. No syringe flow test above L3 (§5.4).  Fork pressure test: press the tines of a standard metal fork into the cut face of the persimmon half with normal thumb pressure until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass = the flesh does not crush, squash, or flatten, and springs back when the fork is removed with no lasting indentation; the piece requires chewing. Fail = the flesh collapses and stays flattened — that is an L6 texture, not L7.  Size check: with the 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, confirm every dimension of the half is ≥15 mm; record measured diameter and height in mm on the capture sheet.
specimens.visual_qc: Cut face shows firm, glossy, translucent orange-red flesh, no bruised or mushy areas, no weeping. Fork tines enter the flesh and it springs back with no lasting indentation. No free liquid pools on the plate — free liquid means the fruit is overripe and the specimen fails.
specimens.shots: - soft_ripe_persimmon_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, cut face up, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, smartphone leveled. - soft_ripe_persimmon_L7_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard under the half, ruler across frame. - soft_ripe_persimmon_L7_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines embedded, ruler visible. - soft_ripe_persimmon_L7_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then release, spring-back visible (L7 has no spoon-tilt step). - soft_ripe_persimmon_L7_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: fork pressure plus the 15 mm size check, voice note.
specimens.fail_modes: Under-ripe fruit: flesh is hard, dry, and astringent and does not read as a regular everyday texture — discard and remake with a ripe-but-firm specimen. Overripe, bruised, or melting fruit: free liquid runs across the plate and the flesh collapses under the fork. This is NOT acceptable texture at L7 — it fails both the no-free-liquid QC line and fork pressure, and no bench method can firm ripe fruit. Discard, remake with a chilled firm unbruised specimen, and record the rejection on the capture sheet. Flesh collapses under the fork even after 30 min chilling and firm-fruit selection: L7 is not reliably achievable in this fruit on this line. Record the specimen's actual grade — a half that squashes and does not recover is L6, soft — and report the deviation; do not report it as L7. If any test is ambiguous, retake with the second half and discard the first.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of fresh pear, peeled and cored. Steam until soft, 8–10 min. Transfer to blender, add 80 ml water, blend 30–45 s until smooth. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; press and discard any fibrous residue that will not pass — note this on the card, do not force it. Weigh the sieved purée; for L3 add thickener at the calibration starting point of 2.0 g per 100 ml purée, then stir 20–30 s and re-weigh. Add more thickener in 0.2 g increments per 100 ml only if the flow test fails; record the final grams used per 100 ml on the data sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift fork 4–5 cm; liquid drips slowly in a continuous thin stream, not in drops. Fork pressure: tines leave clear, persistent lines on the surface when pressed lightly. Spoon tilt: spoon held at 30°; specimen flows off in a steady ribbon, not a lump, not a pour. Syringe flow test: fill the 10 ml syringe, cut the tip as specified; after 10 s, 8–10 ml remains. Pass = 8–10 ml retained.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: thin even coating, drips in a slow continuous thread. On the spoon: smooth, glossy, no lumps or fibres, holds a soft mound that slumps when tilted. No free liquid pooling on the plate.
specimens.shots: pear_L3_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. pear_L3_take2.jpg — top-down with 15 mm checkerboard, full specimen visible. pear_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines depressing the surface. pear_L3_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s clip of fork press then spoon tilt at 30°. pear_L3_take2.mp4 — full 10 s syringe flow test, start and end volumes visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: drips in drops from fork, <8 ml retained in syringe. Re-make, add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, retest. Too thick: holds shape on spoon tilt, >10 ml retained. Re-make, thin with 5–10 ml water, retest. Fibrous residue not sieved: catches in fork drip or syringe tip. Re-blend finer, re-sieve fully, retest.

specimens.prep: Steam fresh pear until fork-tender. Weigh 200 g cooked flesh. Add 40 ml water. Blend 45-60 s on high until smooth. Pass through 4 mm sieve; discard fibrous residue. Re-weigh puree. If puree reads below L4 on fork drip, add thickener at 1.0 g per 100 ml as the calibration starting point; record actual grams used. Stir, rest 2 min, re-test. No second sieving, no added sugar.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a fork loaded with ~5 ml puree; puree sits as a coherent mound above the tines, does not drip or run through gaps. Pass if mound holds 5 s. Fork pressure: press fork tines into puree on a flat plate; puree yields to pressure, shows clear tine marks, but does not run back into the grooves. Pass if tine marks remain visible after the fork lifts. Spoon tilt: load a spoon, tilt to 90 degrees over a plate; puree clings, slides only as a single mass, no pour. Pass if mass stays cohesive. No separate thin liquid pools around the mound. No syringe test at L4.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is matte-glossy, uniform, with no visible fibre flecks or water separation. Colour is even cream to pale beige from end to end. Spoon retains a clean rounded heap; fork tines come up coated but the spaces between tines remain filled by puree, not empty.
specimens.shots: pear_L4_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, specimen on white plate, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, scale reading visible. pear_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard under plate, mound centred. pear_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into specimen. pear_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous move. pear_L4_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film: fork drip, fork pressure, spoon tilt, each 3-4 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Puree too wet: runs through fork tines or pools liquid on plate. Re-make: add thickener in 0.5 g per 100 ml steps, rest 2 min, retest. Puree too stiff: cracks on the spoon, falls off in chunks. Re-make: blend in 5 ml water, retest; do not exceed 60 ml total added water. Visible fibre or skin specks: re-sieve once; if still present, re-blend 15 s and re-sieve.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g fresh pear, peeled and cored. Steam 8-10 min until fork-soft. Drain. Transfer to a bowl; mash thoroughly with a fork for 60-90 s until no lumps exceed coarse crumbs. Pass the mash through the 4 mm sieve, pressing with the back of the spoon; discard retained fibres. Re-weigh; target 180-200 g yield. If the mash looks wet or releases pooling liquid, blend 5-10 s to homogenise, then re-sieve. Do not add water, milk, or juice. Thickener is not required at L5; keep thickener sealed and record 0 g.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines into a heaped teaspoonful until the tines blanch white, about 5 s. Specimen must squash and not recover its shape when the fork is removed; the tines leave a clear imprint. Spoon-tilt test: scoop a teaspoonful and tilt the spoon 30 degrees; specimen should hold together in one bolus, not slide or drip. Fork-drip test: lift a forkful 5 cm above the plate; nothing should drip through or off the tines. No separate thin liquid should pool on the plate after 60 s. No syringe flow test at L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: cohesive lumps no larger than 4 mm, surface glistens but no liquid falls when held. On the spoon: one mound that keeps its shape when tilted, no run-off. On the plate: thin film only, no free juice.
specimens.shots: Stills: pear_L5_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; pear_L5_take2.jpg — top-down with checkerboard centred; pear_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines clearly indented. Clips: pear_L5_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence; pear_L5_take2.mp4 — the IDDSI test film, one continuous take showing fork press, spoon tilt, and fork drip.
specimens.fail_modes: Lumps above 4 mm after sieving: re-mash and re-sieve; do not proceed. Visible thin liquid pooling on the plate or dripping from fork: drain 30 s on the sieve, then re-test. Specimen recovers shape after fork press or slides off the tilted spoon: too firm or too dry; add 5 g hot water per 100 g, mash again, and re-test.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g fresh pear. Steam until fork-tip enters with no resistance (~6 min). Cool 60 s. Cube to ≤15 mm on the board; trim any seed-side fibers. Confirm each piece against the 100 mm ruler. Do NOT blend and do NOT sieve — L6 requires discrete soft pieces, not a puree. Do NOT add thickener; thickener is irrelevant at L6. Reserve 50 g of steam water only if a piece looks dry, then drain.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: place one piece flat on a plate, press the fork tines down with the pad of the thumb until thumbnail blanches white. Pass: the piece squashes, cracks, and does not recover its shape. Spoon-tilt test (optional sanity): a soft piece on a spoon does not slide off when tilted to 45°. Fork-drip test is N/A at L6 (no puree flow). Syringe flow test is N/A at L6.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces are glossy, moist, and translucent at the edges. Color is uniform off-white, no browned skins. Each piece holds a clean cube shape with rounded, not ragged, corners. Surface sheen signals steam doneness, not dryness.
specimens.shots: Capture in the A4 kit, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard visible. Still 1: 45° hero, 3–4 pieces fanned beside the ruler, checkerboard in frame — pear_L6_take1.jpg. Still 2: top-down, pieces spread on checkerboard — pear_L6_take2.jpg. Still 3: fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines biting the piece — pear_L6_take3.jpg. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt — pear_L6_take1.mp4. Clip 2: full IDDSI fork-pressure test, thumbnail blanch visible — pear_L6_take2.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces >15 mm — re-trim, re-shoot. Piece springs back under thumb — under-steamed; re-steam 2 min and re-test. Piece crumbles to mush before press — over-steamed; re-cut from a fresher batch and shorten steam. Two consecutive fails on the same batch: discard and start over.

specimens.prep: Select a firm, just-ripe pear; it must resist thumbnail pressure, because a yielding pear is not L7 material. Rinse, dry, and place on a clean board. Cut lengthwise into 6 wedges; core each wedge by removing the seeds and central stem fibres with a paring knife. Cut each wedge crosswise into pieces 15-20 mm thick, and check every piece against the 100 mm ruler: each piece must measure at least 15 mm in both of its shorter dimensions, since L7 requires pieces ≥15 mm and an 8-10 mm slice is L6. Select 8-10 pieces of uniform size, 120-150 g total, as the reference specimen. Do not blend, do not sieve (an L7 specimen must never be sieved below 15 mm), do not add thickener, do not add water, and do not cut any piece below 15 mm. Serve pieces whole on a white plate as normally presented. Record the actual mass in grams and the piece size range in mm on the capture sheet. Keep the plated pieces chilled until capture; warmth softens flesh and drops it toward L6.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure is the only IDDSI test that applies at L7. Press the tines of a fork flat onto a piece with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white (protocol 5.1), then lift. The piece must not compress, squish, or change shape; it must retain its full original form. Pass: no deformation and no juice released. No spoon-tilt test at L7: spoon-tilt applies at L3, L4 and L5 only. No fork-drip test at L7: fork-drip applies at L3 and L4 only. Neither is evidence for L7, and neither may be used to accept or reject the specimen. Size confirmation, part of the L7 pass: every piece measures ≥15 mm in its two shortest dimensions against the 100 mm ruler.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces hold their shape on the fork with sharp, intact edges. Flesh surface looks matte and fibrous, never glossy or wet. No pooling liquid visible on the plate beneath the pieces. Every piece spans at least 15 mm on the ruler.
specimens.shots: Capture three stills and two clips. Still 1: 45-degree hero of the piece arrangement with the 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2: top-down plate shot with the checkerboard visible and the pieces measured against the ruler. Still 3: fork-press close-up, tines flat on the piece at full thumb pressure, the piece undeformed, ruler in frame for scale. Clip 1: 8-12 seconds of fork-pressure application and release on one piece, the piece undeformed throughout. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film for L7 — fork pressure plus size verification against the ruler. Files: pear_L7_take1.jpg and pear_L7_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Fresh pear is the L7 form for BF36 (docs/BASE_FOOD_LIST.md: fresh slices as regular), but the result is fruit-dependent: over-ripe or warm flesh yields to thumb pressure and weeps juice, so the same pear reads L6 (8-15 mm, soft) on one day and L7 on another, and nothing but the fork test tells the operator which. The closest achievable procedure is the one written above — firm, just-ripe fruit, cut 15-20 mm, chilled, captured immediately. (a) Pieces compress, squash, or release juice under fork pressure — the fruit is too ripe or too warm, so the specimen is L6 and not L7: re-shoot with a firmer, chilled pear; if firm fruit cannot be sourced, re-make the L6 specimen per docs/BASE_FOOD_LIST.md (steamed pear, cubes <= 15 mm) rather than labelling an L6 specimen L7. (b) Pieces measure less than 15 mm — too thin for L7; re-cut at 15-20 mm thickness, never thinner, and re-verify every piece against the ruler. (c) Juice pools on the plate from bruising or warming — pat pieces dry, chill, and re-shoot; weeping flesh means the fruit is past L7 firmness and the batch must be re-sourced, not re-labelled.

specimens.prep: Steam 200 g fresh apple flesh until fork-tender. Tip into blender, add 80 ml water. Blend 45 s on high. Pass through 4 mm sieve; discard coarse residue. Weigh the smooth purée; record actual grams. Stir in thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml of purée as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams added. Whisk 30 s, rest 2 min, re-whisk 10 s. Pourability must be slow drip, not pour-free. If it ribbons off the spoon, add more thickener in 0.2 g per 100 ml steps up to 3.0 g.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lifts on fork tines, then drips in a slow continuous stream within 10 s. Pass if flow is steady, not a fast pour, not a stack that holds shape.  Fork pressure: white shows through purée under thumb pressure on the back of the fork. Pass if surface blanches but mass stays cohesive.  Spoon tilt: spoon held at 45°, specimen slides off slowly as a cohesive dollop. Pass if it leaves in one slow pour, not in chunks, not in a drip trail.  Syringe flow test (L3 requirement): fill 10 ml syringe, cut nozzle to 10 mm, release for 10 s. Pass if 8–10 ml remains in barrel.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is glossy and even, no visible fibre or foam. Coats the spoon back without running clear. Drips from fork tines form a continuous thread, not discrete drops.
specimens.shots: Stills: apple_L3_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen on spoon. apple_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard fills background, specimen pooled to 15 mm depth. apple_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, thumb mid-press, surface blanching visible.  Clips: apple_L3_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt in one take. apple_L3_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI syringe flow test, 10 s timer in frame, final meniscus reading held for 2 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: drips in a fast stream, syringe reads below 8 ml. Add thickener in 0.2 g per 100 ml steps, re-test. Too thick: mounds on spoon, holds fork shape, syringe reads above 10 ml. Add water in 5 ml steps, re-test. Lumpy: sieve residue left in mass; re-blend 15 s and re-sieve. Any fail on any one test requires a full remake under the same filename with _v2.

specimens.prep: Peel and core the apple. Steam 200 g of flesh until fork-tender, ~6 min. Transfer to the blender with 60 ml of the cooking water. Blend 45 s on high, then scrape and blend 20 s more. Press through the 4 mm sieve; discard coarse residue. Return puree to blender. Decant into a measuring jug and read the volume to the nearest 10 ml (expect ~180-200 ml) and record it on the log — every thickener dose below is per 100 ml of this measured volume. Add 1.5 g thickener per 100 ml of measured puree (calibration starting point; for 200 ml that is 3.0 g). Blend 15 s to fully disperse. Total thickener is capped at 2.5 g per 100 ml (5.0 g for a 200 ml batch). If the puree still spreads when spooned at that cap, the batch is not L4 by this method — discard and re-prep; do not keep adding. Target ~250 g finished specimen (200 g flesh + 60 ml water + thickener, minus steam loss); record actual mass.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: scoop puree onto the fork; it must sit as a mound above the tines with no drip falling through in 5 s. Fork pressure: the fork tines should leave a clean imprint without the surface snapping back or splitting. Spoon tilt: a spoonful should hold its shape when the spoon is tilted 45 degrees; slow slump is acceptable, flow is not. All three tests above must pass for L4 — these are the three §5 tests that apply at L4. The thin-liquid pooling check is a visual criterion recorded under VISUAL QC, not a fourth test.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is smooth and matte with no visible fibers or lumps. Color is uniform pale cream to light beige. Holds a peaked mound on the spoon tip without slumping off the edges. No separate thin liquid pools on the plate next to the spoon.
specimens.shots: Stills: apple_L4_take1.jpg at 45 degrees with ruler and checkerboard; apple_L4_take2.jpg top-down on checkerboard; apple_L4_take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press showing clean tine imprint. Clips: apple_L4_take1.mp4 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt; apple_L4_take2.mp4 the full IDDSI test sequence in one continuous take.
specimens.fail_modes: Too wet: puree flows through the fork or pools thin liquid on the plate; add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml of measured puree volume, blend 10 s, re-test. Stop at the 2.5 g per 100 ml cap (5.0 g total for this batch); at the cap and still too wet, discard and re-prep — do not walk the batch back with water. Too stiff: mound cracks or crumbles instead of yielding; add 5 ml water per 100 ml of measured puree, re-blend 15 s, re-test. Maximum 10 ml water per 100 ml in total; still stiff after that, discard and re-prep. Lumpy or fibrous: visible specks survive the sieve; re-blend 20 s and re-sieve through the 4 mm sieve. One re-make allowed; second failure, discard and note on the log.

specimens.prep: Start with 250 g fresh apple, peeled, cored, cut into 2 cm cubes. Steam 8–10 min until fork-tender; drain. Mash thoroughly with a fork. Do not blend to a smooth purée and do not sieve — the per-level note requires mince ≤4 mm, not a smooth paste. Work the mash through a 4 mm sieve only if a first pass shows lumps >4 mm; press with the back of a spoon, discard the coarse residue. Target final specimen mass 200–220 g. No thin liquid, no added water. No thickener required at L5 — thickener is reserved for L3 calibrations. Record final mass on the capture sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the fork tines into a heaped teaspoon of specimen on a flat plate with normal thumb pressure (~5 kg feel). Pass criterion: specimen squashes, spreads, and does not spring back; tine indent stays. Fork drip test: lift a loaded fork. Pass criterion: no thin liquid drips through tines; only soft pieces may drop, and they hold shape on the plate. Spoon tilt test: tilt a heaped teaspoon 45°. Pass criterion: specimen sits cohesive, falls off in one soft clump, slides slowly, leaves residue — no runny pour. Syringe test: not required at L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: lumpy, minced texture with visible soft particles all roughly ≤4 mm, uniform pale apple colour, slight gloss from natural juice, no pooling liquid at the rim. Fork tines should leave a clean impression with edges that don't crumble dry or run wet.
specimens.shots: apple_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, specimen on white plate, 100 mm ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame, fork resting. apple_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only under the plate. apple_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines embedded. apple_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s clip: fork press then spoon tilt in one continuous take. apple_L5_take2.mp4 — 45–90 s IDDSI test film: full fork-pressure, fork-drip, spoon-tilt sequence, with verbal pass/fail call.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-steaming into a smooth purée → fails visual QC and tine test; re-mash with reserved cubes, not re-blend. Insufficient mashing leaving chunks >4 mm → fails sieve check; re-press through 4 mm sieve. Pooling juice separating as thin liquid → fails fork drip; drain on paper towel 30 s, re-test.

specimens.prep: Weigh 300 g fresh apple, peeled, cored, cut into 20 mm cubes. Steam 8-10 minutes until fork enters with no resistance. Drain, spread on tray 2 minutes. Test one cube with fork-pressure: thumbnail blanches white, cube squashes and does not recover, piece breaks apart easily — if not, steam 2 more minutes. Dice by hand into pieces ≤ 15 mm on the 4 mm sieve card (no cube passes through the 15 mm square). Do not blend. No thickener, no water added. Steam only; do not boil to mush.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure (L6 test): press the fork tines against one piece on a flat plate until thumbnail blanches white. PASS: piece squashes, breaks, does not return to original shape. Spoon tilt: place 5-7 pieces on a spoon, tilt to 90 degrees against the plate. PASS: all pieces slide or fall off together; none holds its shape as a sticky bolus. Fork drip: lift 3 pieces on fork tines, hold horizontal 5 seconds. PASS: no liquid drips from the pieces. (No syringe test — L6, not L3.)
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces are pale cream-yellow, matte, slightly translucent at edges, no dry core, no free liquid pooling on the plate. Edges are soft, not sharp; a light press with the back of a spoon leaves a clear dent. Pieces hold their cube shape on the fork but break cleanly with one nip — not stringy, not fibrous.
specimens.shots: Still 1: hero 45-degree, ruler + checkerboard in frame, 5-7 pieces fanned on white plate. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard only, pieces spaced to show size. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines contacting one piece. Clip 1 (8-12 s): fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence, audio of squash. Clip 2 (the IDDSI test film): full L6 fork-pressure protocol. Files: apple_L6_take1.jpg / apple_L6_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces > 15 mm or with sharp edges — re-dice, do not re-steam. Centre still firm (under-steamed) — re-steam 2 minutes, retest. Pieces turn to puree or free juice runs (over-steamed) — discard, start over; do not blend to recover.

specimens.prep: Take a fresh apple. Core and slice into 8 wedges, skin on, about 15-20 mm thick at the widest point, matching how an apple is normally eaten. Steam 4-6 minutes until just tender when pierced with a fork but still holding shape. Drain on a paper towel for 60 seconds. Do not blend, do not sieve, do not add thickener, do not add liquid. Working amount: 150-200 g steamed wedges. Serve at eating temperature. This is the reference specimen for L7 Regular.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: Press a standard dinner fork onto a wedge on a flat plate with normal thumb pressure for 10 seconds. Pass if the wedge flattens, cracks, or breaks apart but does not pass through the slots. Spoon tilt test: Pick up a wedge on a spoon and tilt until the spoon is near vertical. Pass if the wedge slides off or stays on the spoon without oozing through the tines. Fork drip test is not applicable at L7; record as N/A.
specimens.visual_qc: Wedge holds its shape with no puree or juice pooling on the plate. Skin intact, edges defined, steam-moist surface but not wet or dripping. Fork tines leave a clean dent without the wedge collapsing into mush.
specimens.shots: - apple_L7_take1.jpg: 45-degree hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame, two wedges fanned. - apple_L7_take1.jpg: top-down, checkerboard visible, full wedge with stem-side up. - apple_L7_take1.jpg: fork-press close-up mid-press, thumb pressure visible, fork slots clear. - apple_L7_take1.mp4: 8-12 s fork-press, full 10-second hold ending in cracking. - apple_L7_take1.mp4: IDDSI test film, spoon-tilt plus fork-pressure, continuous.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-steamed wedge turns to mush and passes through fork slots: re-make with 60 seconds less steam. Apple variety too soft (e.g., overripe McIntosh): re-make with firmer variety such as Granny Smith or Pink Lady. Sauce or juice pools on plate from under-draining: re-make with a full 90-second drain.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g seedless watermelon flesh. Blend on high 45-60 s until smooth liquid; scrape jar, blend 10 s more. Pass through the 4 mm sieve, pressing with the back of a spoon; discard pulp residue. Measure the sieved puree volume (ml). Add thickener at 3 g per 100 ml as the calibration starting point: weigh thickener to 1 decimal, whisk into puree 30 s, rest 2 min, whisk 10 s. Record actual grams used per 100 ml. If the flow test result is outside window, adjust in 0.5 g/100 ml steps and re-test. No extra water.
specimens.iddsi_test: - Fork drip: lift fork; puree drips slowly in a continuous thin stream, not a steady pour, not in lumps. - Fork pressure: puree flattens and spreads against the plate under fork tines, does not hold shape, leaves a clear fork-tine pattern. - Spoon tilt: spoon tilted to ~45 degrees; puree flows off in a single slow ribbon, not a dollop, not runny. - IDDSI flow test (10 ml syringe, 10 s): 8-10 ml remaining in syringe. <8 ml = too thin; >10 ml = too thick. Re-make.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy, uniform pink with no red pulp specks; coats the spoon back evenly without pooling fast; drips from fork tines leave a brief tail that snaps off within 1 second.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero on A4 kit, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen pooled to one side. Still 2: top-down centred, checkerboard only. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines partially buried, puree oozing between tines. Clip 1: 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. Clip 2: IDDSI flow test, timer visible, full 10 s. Naming: watermelon_L3_take1.jpg / .mp4; increment take number on remakes.
specimens.fail_modes: - Too runny (drips in a steady pour, <8 ml retained): add thickener in 0.5 g/100 ml steps, re-test. - Too stiff (holds mound, >10 ml retained, slow ribbon only): thin with 5 ml puree per 100 ml batch, re-test. - Grainy / seeds visible: re-blend 20 s and re-sieve; if specks persist, reject and re-make from a de-seeded batch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of fresh de-seeded watermelon flesh on the digital scale. Do not blend; blending releases thin juice and the per-level note forbids separate thin liquid. Dice the flesh by hand into pieces ≤4 mm using the knife and ruler as a guide; visually confirm no piece exceeds a 4 mm cube. Pour off and discard any pooled juice that separates. Mash with the fork until uniformly minced and visibly moist but with no standing liquid; if the mash looks wet, press gently against the 4 mm sieve to blot excess juice. Do not add water or thickener; for L5 no thickener is used. Note: true L5 watermelon is borderline because the fruit is mostly water; if liquid keeps separating, the specimen cannot meet L5 and must be re-made or downgraded.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines flat onto a heaped teaspoon of specimen; the mass must squash and leave clear tine prints with no elastic recovery. Spoon-tilt test: tilt a spoonful 45°; the specimen holds together as a cohesive mass, with only minimal juice that does not pour. Fork-drip test: lift a fork-load; no thin liquid drips through the tines. All three must pass; any drip of free juice is a fail.
specimens.visual_qc: Coarse mince on the fork, not a purée. Pieces are visible, soft, and glisten with juice but sit in a damp pile, not a puddle. Color is even pink-red; no whole seeds, no translucent lumps over 4 mm.
specimens.shots: watermelon_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero with ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, fork-load visible. watermelon_L5_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. watermelon_L5_take1_fork.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press showing squash. watermelon_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. watermelon_L5_take1_iddsi.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, operator hands visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Visible pooled juice on the plate or dripping from fork — re-make and blot, or downgrade. Pieces larger than 4 mm after dicing — re-dice and re-check against ruler. Specimen that runs through the 4 mm sieve as liquid — cannot meet L5; record as N/A and discard.

specimens.prep: Cut 250 g seedless watermelon flesh into 25 mm slabs, discard rind. Pulse in consumer blender 4 s, stop, scrape, pulse 3 s more — stop at coarse chop with visible chunks, do not purée. Press through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon; discard pulp and excess juice that drains through. Dice the sieve-retained solids to ≤15 mm cubes (≤15 mm in every dimension). Measure 200 g of diced pieces into the capture bowl. No thickener, no added liquid — L6 calibration point is the as-cut, as-diced specimen.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure: press fork tines fully into one piece against a white plate. Pass criterion — thumbnail blanches white on the fork tine, the piece squashes flat, and it does not spring back when the fork lifts. Fork-drip: lift five pieces on fork tines, hold 5 s above plate. Pass criterion — no juice drips off the fork. Spoon-tilt: load five pieces on spoon, tilt to 90°. Pass criterion — pieces sit on the spoon without sliding or falling. No L3 syringe test applies.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: discrete cubes with sharp 15 mm edges, bright red, moist but not pooling liquid. On the spoon at 90°: pieces hold position, a thin juice sheen — no puddle on the plate. On the plate after fork-press: flat red smear, no intact cube remains.
specimens.shots: watermelon_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame, five pieces fanned on fork. watermelon_L6_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only, 200 g bowl filled level. watermelon_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines fully through one piece. watermelon_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. watermelon_L6_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: fork-pressure, fork-drip, spoon-tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-blended to purée: fails fork-pressure, passes through sieve as liquid — re-dice from a new slab, pulse only twice. Pieces >15 mm: fails the dice rule — re-cut all pieces to ≤15 mm and re-check with ruler. Excess free juice pooling on plate: indicates sieve was skipped — return solids to sieve, press again, drain 30 s.

specimens.prep: Place the whole de-seeded wedge on the board. Cut a 50 mm × 50 mm × 25 mm specimen from the flesh with a clean knife; do not crush or trim beyond removing rind and any white pith. That cube is 62.5 cm³ and, at watermelon density (~0.95 g/cm³), weighs 55-68 g. Record mass on the scale, target 60 g. The size spec and the mass spec describe the same specimen: if the mass reads outside 55-68 g, the cube is not 50 × 50 × 25 mm and must be re-cut — do not reconcile the two by trimming to mass. Do not blend, do not sieve, do not add water, do not add thickener. The wedge-as-cut note is respected: the specimen is taken from a freshly cut surface, not reconstructed. L3 calibration does not apply at L7; record zero added thickener and zero added liquid.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the fork tines flat onto the specimen with normal thumb force; the flesh must crush, flake, or split cleanly and not return to its original shape when the fork is lifted. Sizing is part of the pass: measured against the 100 mm ruler, the cube reads 50 × 50 × 25 mm ± 2 mm and every dimension is ≥15 mm. No fork-drip test at L7, no spoon-tilt test at L7, and no syringe flow test at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: bright red flesh with visible juice on the cut surface, which is expected and acceptable at L7; tines leave a clean impression that does not spring back. Specimen edges are sharp-cut, not ragged or pulped. Measured on the 100 mm ruler: 50 × 50 × 25 mm ± 2 mm.
