specimens.fail_modes: (a) Free juice on the cut faces, or juice pooling on the plate: this is normal watermelon behaviour and is NOT a fail condition at L7 — fork drip is not an L7 test. Do not blot, which wets the surface and destroys the sharp-cut edges, and do not drain on paper. If pooling makes the ruler unreadable in the hero frame, work on a chilled board, shoot within 60 s of cutting, or re-cut from a colder interior face; record the pooling on the capture sheet and keep the specimen. (b) Flesh is pulped or shredded by knife work, giving a puree appearance: re-cut a fresh specimen with one clean stroke. (c) Rind or white pith left attached, altering bite behaviour: trim and re-cut. (d) Cube measures under 15 mm in any dimension: re-cut to 50 × 50 × 25 mm; do not submit a smaller piece as L7 evidence.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g fresh peeled orange segments on the digital scale. Add 80 ml water. Blend in the consumer blender for 45 s until smooth. Press through the 4 mm sieve; discard pulp and seeds retained. Weigh the strained purée back on the scale. Add thickener at 4.5 g per 100 ml of purée as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Stir with a fork for 30 s, rest 2 min, re-stir 15 s. If the drip through fork tines is faster than the L3 window, add thickener 0.5 g at a time, rest, and re-stir until the flow window is hit. Record final purée mass, thickener mass, and total volume used.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a forkful 5 cm over a plate; the purée should drip slowly through the tines, not run in a continuous stream. Fork pressure: pressing the fork tines into 1.5 cm of purée on a spoon leaves a clear pattern that does not flow back together. Spoon tilt: tilting a spoonful 45 degrees shows the purée moves as a single bolus, not liquid. Syringe flow test: fill the 10 ml IDDSI syringe, release, wait 10 s; 8-10 ml should remain in the syringe. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: a soft, glossy mound with no free liquid pooling at the edge. On the fork: a slow, thick drip once every 1-2 seconds, no splatter. Homogeneous orange colour with no visible pulp specks or seeds.
specimens.shots: Three stills: orange_segments_peeled_L3_take1.jpg at 45 degrees with ruler and checkerboard in frame; top-down with checkerboard only; fork-press close-up mid-press showing tines in the purée. Two clips (8-12 s each): .mp4 of fork-press and spoon-tilt; .mp4 of the full IDDSI syringe flow test with timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: drip is continuous or syringe reads under 8 ml — add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml and re-test. Too thick: no drip or syringe reads over 10 ml — thin with 5 ml water, rest, re-test. Visible pulp or seeds in final purée — re-sieve before adding more thickener; do not re-blend after thickener is added, as blending breaks the thickened matrix.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g fresh peeled orange segments on the digital scale. Add 60 ml water. Blend 45 s on high. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard coarser residue. Blend the sieved puree 15 s more to homogenize. Serve immediately; do not hold. Per-level note compliance: this food cannot reach L4 without thinning and re-thickening — record as a failure if the operator judges texture cannot be met.
specimens.iddsi_test: S Fork drip test: tip a fork loaded with 3-4 g of specimen; it sits as a mound above the tines, does not drip or run through. Pass = no flow through gaps. Fork pressure test: press the fork tines into the specimen until the tines blanch white. Specimen retains shape, does not spring back fully, leaves a clear indentation. Pass = clear thumbprint-style mark, no recovery. Spoon tilt test: scoop 5-7 g onto a spoon, tilt to 90 degrees. Specimen sits, does not pour off. Pass = no slide. No separate thin liquid must be visible in the bowl. If any liquid pools, FAIL.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: glossy orange mound, uniform color, no flecks of pulp or membrane, no liquid pooled at the tine bases. On the spoon: cohesive heap that holds its dome after tilting. Smooth surface with no graininess.
specimens.shots: orange_segments_peeled_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. orange_segments_peeled_L4_take2.jpg — top-down with checkerboard. orange_segments_peeled_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press. orange_segments_peeled_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press / spoon-tilt clip. orange_segments_peeled_L4_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film (drip + pressure + tilt).
specimens.fail_modes: Liquefaction: puree runs through the fork — re-blend briefly with 2 g thickener per 100 ml, retest. Graininess from membrane residue: visible pulp or fibrous flecks — re-sieve and re-blend; if persists, record FAIL. Liquid separation in bowl: thin layer pools — re-blend and serve at once; second separation = FAIL, do not re-make.

specimens.prep: Start with 200 g fresh peeled orange segments on the digital scale. Pull the segments apart by hand and discard any pith, seeds, or hard membrane. Coarsely chop on a board using a chef's knife until pieces are visually no larger than ~10 mm; the per-level note allows chop ≤4 mm with juice retained, so chop finer, working through until every piece is ≤4 mm. Do NOT blend: blending destroys the fibrous segment structure and produces a puree that fails L5. Do NOT sieve. Do NOT add thickener; L5 must hold its own juice. Keep all released juice in the bowl and fold it back through the chopped mass with a fork so the surface glistens but no thin liquid pools. Target final specimen mass 180–200 g.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test (primary for L5): press the fork tines into the specimen on a flat plate until the thumbnail blanches white. The mass must squash, change shape, and not spring back; crumbs between tines are acceptable. Spoon-tilt test: a small mound on a spoon must hold its shape when the spoon is tilted to 45°, then slide off in one piece when fully inverted. Fork-drip test: lifting the fork, no thin orange liquid should run off separately — only the moist mass should travel with the fork. Pass = all three.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: discrete moist particles ≤4 mm, none fibrous or whole-segment shaped; surface glistens, no puddle of juice on the plate. Colour uniform pale orange; no visible white pith strands. On the spoon: holds a rounded mound without slumping.
specimens.shots: - orange_segments_peeled_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen mounded beside them. - orange_segments_peeled_L5_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard fills frame, ruler along one edge. - orange_segments_peeled_L5_take1_forkpress.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines ¾ into specimen. - orange_segments_peeled_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s continuous: fork-press and spoon-tilt back-to-back. - orange_segments_peeled_L5_take1_iddsi.mp4 — IDDSI test film: full fork-pressure, full spoon-tilt, full fork-drip, no cuts.
specimens.fail_modes: (a) Any visible piece >4 mm — re-chop that piece, do not re-process the whole bowl. (b) Juice pools on the plate (thin liquid separates) — fold juice back through; if it still pools, the segment membranes were over-broken, re-make from 200 g fresh. (c) Mass springs back under fork or slumps off the spoon — specimen is too dry or too intact; re-chop finer and re-test. Two failed re-makes: stop and log as material unsuitable for L5.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g fresh peeled orange segments on the scale — ripe, sweet segments with seeds and membrane strands stripped. Do not blend; L6 requires visible soft pieces. Working over the tray, cut every segment crosswise on the board with a knife into pieces measuring 8-15 mm on the longest edge, checking each cut batch against the 100 mm ruler in frame; reject any seed, membrane strand, or piece longer than 15 mm. Never cut a piece below 8 mm: the BF39 L5 form is a chop to <=4 mm with the fruit's own juice, so a batch worked down toward 4 mm is an L5 specimen and must be filed as L5, not L6. Sieving is impossible for solid fruit, so do not sieve — a 4 mm mesh cannot enforce a 15 mm limit and would shred the batch to L5. No thickener, no water, no liquid added — the L6 specimen is served moist only as the fruit's own juice. Do not perform the L3 calibration step; it does not apply to L6. Lift off any juice that has pooled on the tray just before capture, and capture promptly, so the plate reads moist and not swimming. Wipe the tray rim dry before capture so juice does not lift the checkerboard.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure is the only IDDSI test that applies at L6 (protocol 5.1): press the flat of the fork onto one 8-15 mm piece, pressure through the thumbnail until the thumbnail blanches white, hold, then lift. Pass = the piece squashes, changes shape, and does not recover its shape when the fork is lifted. Juice that squeezes out under the press is the fruit's own juice and does NOT fail the piece: the L6 form of this food is cut segments served in their own juice, and the fork-pressure test carries no "no free liquid" clause — do not re-cut a piece smaller to chase a drier press. Size confirmation in the same take (protocol 5.1, L6 sizing check): hold two or three pieces against the 100 mm ruler; every piece measures <=15 mm on its longest edge and none is below 8 mm. Spoon tilt is not an L6 test (protocol 5.2 covers L3, L4 and L5 only): do not run it and do not record it as level evidence. Fork drip is not an L6 test (5.3 is L3 and L4). No syringe flow test; L3 only.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces read as soft cut cubes, 8-15 mm on the ruler, edges clean-cut and not ragged, no piece fragmented toward 4 mm. Moist with the fruit's own juice, never wet: no pool of separated juice standing on the plate at the moment of capture. No seed and no membrane strand visible on any piece. Colour uniform, no bruised or collapsed cut faces.
specimens.shots: orange_segments_peeled_L6_take1.jpg hero at 45° with ruler and checkerboard in frame. orange_segments_peeled_L6_take2.jpg top-down with checkerboard and ruler so piece sizes read. orange_segments_peeled_L6_take3.jpg fork-press close-up at mid-press, thumbnail whitening visible. orange_segments_peeled_L6_take1.mp4 8-12 s fork-press on one piece. orange_segments_peeled_L6_take2.mp4 IDDSI test film: fork pressure on the piece plus the 15 mm sizing check against the ruler in the same take.
specimens.fail_modes: Piece exceeds 15 mm — re-cut to 8-15 mm and re-verify every piece against the ruler. Piece springs back under fork pressure — the segment is firm or under-ripe, which is whole-segment (L7) material, not L6: use riper segments for the L6 specimen; do NOT re-cut smaller to force a squash, and if no ripe fruit can be sourced, file the specimen at the level its filmed test actually supports rather than forcing the L6 label. Juice squeezes out under the fork — expected for orange and not a failure; only a pool of separated juice standing on the plate fails QC: lift it off, capture promptly, and never shrink pieces below 8 mm to reduce juiciness. Seed or membrane strand present — strip and re-cut. Batch has fragmented to <=4 mm — that is the BF39 L5 form (chop <=4 mm with its juice): re-test it and file it as L5, never as L6.

specimens.prep: Remove any pith, seeds, or membrane; keep segments whole. Do NOT blend, sieve, or add thickener or water — L7 requires the food as normally served. Weigh 200 g of intact segments on the digital scale for the capture tray. This is a reference specimen, not a calibration sample, so no thickener grams per 100 ml apply. Set aside one whole segment aside for the fork-press close-up.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the tines of the fork fully into one segment on a flat plate with enough force to blanch the fingernail. The segment must NOT deform, mash, or break apart; it must return to its original shape when the fork is withdrawn. Spoon tilt test: place a segment on a spoon and tilt to 90 degrees. The segment must NOT slide, drip, or run off. Fork drip test: lift a segment on fork tines and hold for 5 seconds — no liquid must drip through the tines. Syringe flow test is N/A at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: Segment holds a defined curved, glossy orange shape with visible juice vesicles on the surface. No white pith, membrane, or seed attached. No liquid pooling on the plate beneath the specimen.
specimens.shots: Still 1: hero shot at 45° angle, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard visible in frame. Still 2: top-down with checkerboard only, segments spread but not overlapping. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, fork tines clearly indenting one segment. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence in one continuous take. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film including fork pressure, spoon tilt, and fork drip. Name all files: orange_segments_peeled_L7_take1.jpg / .mp4, increment take number on retake.
specimens.fail_modes: Segments break, crush, or weep juice under fork pressure — fails L7; re-make, select firmer fruit. Visible pith, membrane, or seeds remain — fails cleanliness; re-make and trim more carefully. Liquid pools on plate beneath specimen — fails fork drip; pat segments dry with paper towel before reshooting, do not re-make unless fruit itself is overripe.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g fresh seedless grapes on the digital scale. Add 60 ml water — grapes alone will not blend to a pourable fluid. Blend 45 s on high; stop, scrape down, blend 30 s more. Press through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon; discard pulp and skins retained. Measure the sieved volume. Per-level note says blend-thin, so start calibration at 1.5 g thickener per 100 ml of sieved liquid. Stir 30 s, rest 60 s, re-stir 15 s. This is the starting point; record the actual grams used.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: hold fork vertical; liquid drips slowly in individual drops through the tines, not a continuous stream. Fork pressure: press fork tines flat into the specimen on a plate; when lifted, a small soft mound holds shape, tines leave a clear imprint that does not level out. Spoon tilt: spoon tilted 45 degrees holds its shape on the spoon without sliding off. Syringe flow test: fill the 10 ml IDDSI syringe, release for 10 s; pass when 8-10 ml remains in the syringe.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: glossy, even purple-tan liquid, no visible skin fragments or seeds, slow drip from tines. On the spoon: holds a mound at tilt, surface smooth and homogenous, no separation of liquid pooling at the rim.
specimens.shots: seedless_grapes_L3_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. seedless_grapes_L3_take2.jpg — top-down with checkerboard centred. seedless_grapes_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines embedded. seedless_grapes_L3_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence, one continuous motion. seedless_grapes_L3_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI syringe flow test, timer visible, end volume shown.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: flows as a continuous stream through fork; re-add thickener in 0.2 g per 100 ml steps. Too thick: drops will not drip from fork; add water 5 ml at a time and re-stir. Grainy or seedy: sieve was skipped or pressed too hard; discard and re-sieve — never serve with retained solids.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g fresh seedless grapes. Rinse, destem, halve. Add to consumer blender with 40 ml water. Blend 45 s on high. Pass through the 4 mm sieve; discard skins. Return pulp to blender, blend 20 s. Re-weigh puree. Add thickener at 1.5 g per 100 ml of puree as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Stir 15 s, rest 60 s. If fork-drip test fails (see below), add 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml and repeat rest.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-drip: load fork, lift 10 cm above surface. Pass = puree sits in a mound above the tines for ≥10 s, does not drip or flow between tines. Fork pressure: press fork tines flat into specimen on a plate; puree yields to pressure, thumb blanch visible through tines, then holds the pressed shape without spreading. Spoon tilt: scoop, then tilt spoon 90°. Pass = specimen stays mounded, no thin liquid separates, none falls off. No 10 ml/10 s syringe test (L3 only).
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is uniform pale green-grey, glossy, no visible skin fragments, no free liquid pooling at plate edge. On fork tines: a cohesive mound, not a thin film. On spoon: rounds off the edges, holds a clean heap when tilted.
specimens.shots: seedless_grapes_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen on white plate. seedless_grapes_L4_take1_top.jpg — top-down with checkerboard only. seedless_grapes_L4_take1_fork.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines fully depressed. seedless_grapes_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s continuous: fork-press then spoon-tilt. seedless_grapes_L4_take1_test.mp4 — IDDSI test film, fork-drip then fork-pressure then spoon-tilt, audio of timer callouts.
specimens.fail_modes: 1. Mound flattens within 5 s on spoon tilt or liquid seeps from puree → too thin; add 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 60 s, re-test. Limit two thickener additions; if still failing, re-blend with 20 ml less water and re-test. 2. Visible skin specks or fibrous strings after sieve → sieve again through 4 mm before adding thickener. 3. Puree weeps thin green liquid onto plate within 30 s → over-blended or under-thickened; re-blend 10 s, add 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml, re-test.

specimens.prep: Wash and drain 150 g seedless grapes; discard any with skin breaks. Pulse in a consumer blender for 6–8 s total (two 3–4 s pulses, scrape down between) on medium until the skins split and the pulp releases, leaving no whole grapes. Stand 2 min, then decant the free juice into a measure and reserve it. Return 40 ml of the reserved juice per 100 g of drained pulp — about 50 ml for a typical batch — and fork-mash to a uniform coarse texture. Target final specimen 120–140 g of pulp plus returned juice; record actual grams.  Do not sieve to remove material — the 4 mm sieve is a gauge only: press one heaped tablespoon through it; if any fragment is retained, return the whole batch to the blender for a further 2 s pulse and re-check. Nothing is discarded at the sieve.  No water, no milk, no thickener in the base specimen; grapes supply their own moisture at this level.
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable tests at L5: spoon tilt (5.2) is the level test; fork pressure (5.1) is a supporting check only at L5. Fork drip (5.3) is an L3–L4 method and is not used at L5; syringe flow (5.4) is L3 only.  Spoon tilt — the level test: take one heaped teaspoon (5 ml) on a dry dessert spoon. Tilt to 45° — the specimen must sit as a mound and must not flow or pour. Continue to 90° (vertical) and tap the back of the bowl twice. Pass = the mash releases slowly as a single soft lump and slides off, leaving a thin film on the spoon. Fail = it pours off the spoon before 45° (too thin), or it forms a firm dry ball that does not move after two taps (too thick).  Fork pressure — supporting check only: press the tines into a 1 cm heap on a plate. The specimen must squash, change shape, and not spring back.
specimens.visual_qc: Coarse minced pulp on the fork, clearly wet and glossy from grape juice, holding a soft mound shape. Visible fragments all 4 mm or smaller; no skins still cupping a seed cavity; no whole grapes. On the spoon the specimen mounds softly and slowly settles, not runny. No free juice pooling separately on the plate.
specimens.shots: Shoot against the A4 kit, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. - seedless_grapes_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, specimen heap beside ruler and checkerboard. - seedless_grapes_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, heap offset. - seedless_grapes_L5_take3.jpg — spoon-tilt close-up at 45° and again at release, mound visible. - seedless_grapes_L5_take4.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines visible in the specimen. - seedless_grapes_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. - seedless_grapes_L5_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence in real time.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin — the mash pours off the spoon before 45°: stand a further 2 min, re-decant, and return only 30 ml juice per 100 g pulp. If it still pours, seedless grapes cannot reach L5 on their own juice — either record the specimen as L4 (spoon tilt, fork drip and syringe flow per protocol 5.2–5.4) or re-make with 0.5–1.0 g xanthan gum per 100 g pulp blended in 10 s. Do not label a pouring mash as L5. Too thick or too dry — the mass crumbles under fork pressure, or sits as a firm ball that will not move on the spoon: stir in 10 ml of the reserved juice at a time and re-mash. If the skins are still intact the batch is simply under-blended: pulse a further 2 s. Too chunky — a fragment is retained by the 4 mm gauge: re-pulse 2 s and re-check. Any single failure triggers a re-make from the same 150 g starting weight.

specimens.prep: Wash 200 g fresh seedless grapes; pat dry. Halve each grape lengthwise, then quarter any piece exceeding 15 mm until every piece measures <=15 mm with the 100 mm ruler. Do not blend. Do not sieve. Do not add water or thickener. Discard any piece whose seed or fibrous core resists the thumbnail press.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork tines onto one piece with thumb force equal to pressing the thumbnail until the nail blanches white. Pass: piece squashes, does not spring back, edges crumble or flatten. Repeat on three pieces from different parts of the batch. Spoon tilt: load a teaspoon, tilt 45 degrees over the capture mat. Pass: pieces sit cohesively without sliding off or dripping liquid. Fork drip: lift a loaded fork; no continuous liquid stream falls within 10 seconds. No L3 syringe test applies.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: pieces hold a soft, moist cube-like shape with visible skin sheen and no juice pooling on the mat. Pieces should dent visibly under light thumb pressure and show a crushed, non-elastic cross-section, not a clean sliced face. Colour should match the starting fresh grape.
specimens.shots: seedless_grapes_L6_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. seedless_grapes_L6_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred under pile. seedless_grapes_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail white. seedless_grapes_L6_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s clip of fork press then spoon tilt. seedless_grapes_L6_take5.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full fork-pressure sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces exceed 15 mm after quartering → re-trim and re-measure. Piece rebounds after fork pressure → grapes under-ripe or too firm; re-spec from softer fruit or discard. Excess juice pools on mat → pat pieces drier before retest.

specimens.prep: Use grapes as purchased. Select 8-10 whole seedless grapes, ~150 g total. Rinse, pat dry. Do NOT blend, sieve, chop, or add thickener or water. Per the per-level note ("whole as bought"), the reference specimen is the intact fruit exactly as served. Lay specimens on the capture board with 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler in frame; each grape must be whole, skin intact, stem scar dry.
specimens.iddsi_test: 1. Fork pressure: press tines into the side of a grape until thumbnail blanches white. The grape must split, fragment, or burst — it must NOT return to its original shape when pressure is released. Pass = clear rupture under fork. 2. Fork drip: lift the ruptured grape on the fork; no continuous drip or flow off the tines. Pass = grape stays on fork, nothing drips. 3. Spoon tilt: place a whole grape on a spoon and tilt to ~45°. It must remain on the spoon. Pass = grape sits firmly, does not slide or roll off. No L3 syringe test applies at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: - Skin smooth, taut, intact bloom, no splits or leaks. - Shape round to oval, uniform colour, no juice pooling under fruit on the board. - When pressed on fork, grape visibly bursts and releases a single wet bolus — not a flowing liquid trail.
specimens.shots: - seedless_grapes_L7_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard visible, 5-6 grapes fanned. - seedless_grapes_L7_take1.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, ruler along one edge. - seedless_grapes_L7_take1.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines deforming skin, juice just emerging. - seedless_grapes_L7_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt, continuous take. - seedless_grapes_L7_take1.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: fork pressure, fork drip, spoon tilt, in order.
specimens.fail_modes: - Skin splits before pressure applied (over-ripe, bruised) → re-make with a fresh batch from pack. - Grape rolls off tilted spoon (wet, oily, or undersized) → re-make; select larger, drier specimens. - Pulp flows or drips continuously after fork press (over-ripe, liquefying) → re-make; specimen must rupture, not run.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g chilled plain yogurt straight from the tub into a cup. Whisk 30 s until smooth and glossy — plain yogurt is homogeneous, so there is nothing to gauge or strain: do NOT press it through a 4 mm mesh (the sieve is an L4/L5 tool and there are no particles to retain). Served as-is this yogurt holds its shape on a spoon, which is the BF41 L4 form, so it must be thinned to reach L3. Thin with cold milk — not water, the per-level note specifies milk. Add 10 ml at a time and whisk 20 s after each addition, starting from 25 ml per 150 g; the fork-drip, spoon-tilt and syringe tests in section 2 decide when to stop, not the volume. If the mix pours too freely (syringe leaves less than 8 ml at t=10 s), bring it back with 0.5 g thickener per 100 g of specimen at a time, whisking 30 s and resting 60 s after each addition; never exceed 2.0 g per 100 g in total. No blending is needed. Rest 60 s, re-whisk 5 s, then run the syringe flow test as the deciding test. Record the actual milk ml and the actual thickener g per 100 g on the capture sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon tilt (protocol 5.2, L3): scoop a full spoon, hold it level, then tilt. Pass = the sample pours off the tilted spoon in a slow continuous stream, and no separate thin liquid (whey) pools on the spoon or tray — any pooling fails the level. A spoon that holds its shape is the L4 form of this food, not L3, and must not be accepted here. Fork drip (protocol 5.3, L3): scoop with the fork and hold it over the tray. Pass = the sample drips slowly through the fork tines in a continuous flow, leaving a coating on the fork. Counted single droplets are not the L3 look. Syringe flow test (protocol 5.4, deciding test at L3): fill a 10 ml slip-tip syringe to the 10 ml mark, release with the nozzle open, and time 10 s. Pass = 8-10 ml remaining in the syringe (0-2 ml flowed out), the flow continuous through the full 10 s. Film the whole 10 s with the fill level at t=0 and the reading at t=10 both legible. Fork pressure is not applicable at L3 (protocol 5.1 covers L4, L6 and L7, and L5 as a supporting check only): do not run it and do not record it as level evidence — a liquidised specimen must not be required to hold a pressure imprint. All three tests above must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Smooth, glossy, uniform surface, no lumps, grains or skin. On the tilted spoon the mass pours as a slow continuous stream and coats the spoon back in an even film; through the fork tines it runs as continuous ribbons, not counted droplets. No whey or other separate thin liquid pooling on the spoon or the tray, and no standing pool on the plate.
specimens.shots: Stills: plain_yogurt_L3_take1.jpg hero 45° with ruler+checkerboard; plain_yogurt_L3_take2.jpg top-down checkerboard; plain_yogurt_L3_take3.jpg fork-drip close-up, continuous ribbon through the tines. Clips: plain_yogurt_L3_take4.mp4 8-12 s spoon-tilt then fork-drip in one continuous take; plain_yogurt_L3_take5.mp4 IDDSI syringe flow test, full 10 s with both readings legible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin (pours off the spoon in a fast stream; syringe leaves less than 8 ml at t=10 s, i.e. more than 2 ml flowed out): add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g of specimen, whisk 30 s, rest 60 s, re-test; repeat in 0.5 g steps only, and never exceed 2.0 g per 100 g in total. Too thick (mound stands and will not move on the tilted spoon; syringe still reads 10 ml at t=10 s with no measurable flow): that is the L4 form of this food — thin with a further 10 ml milk per 150 g of specimen, whisk, re-test; do not add water, and do not pass the specimen as L3 while it still holds a spoon shape. Whey separates and pools on the spoon or tray: whisk 15 s and re-test at once; if it re-separates within 2 min the batch has broken — re-make from a fresh tub, do not capture. Grainy or streaked: under-hydrated thickener — whisk 30 s, rest 60 s, re-test; if grains persist, re-make.

specimens.prep: Scoop 150 g plain yogurt from the chilled tub into the blender jar. Blend 20 s on high, scraping the wall once at 10 s if needed. Do not add water, milk, or thickener — the per-level note says serve as-is; yogurt is already the calibration starting point. Do not sieve: it is already smooth and sieving will thin it. If a small amount of whey has pooled on top, pour it off first and re-weigh to 150 g before blending.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the fork tines flat into the specimen; the surface must blanch clearly white but the yogurt must not ooze up between or through the tines, and the fork must lift clean with very little residue. Spoon tilt test: scoop a heaped spoonful and tilt the spoon to a steep angle; the specimen must sit in a firm mound and not slide off or run off the edge. Fork drip test: lift the fork with a small mound on it and hold it above the plate for 5 s; the mound must sit proud of the tines, not drip, not run. No separate thin liquid should pool on the plate.
specimens.visual_qc: Specimen looks matte, glossy-soft, with no grain or lumps. It holds the imprint of the fork tines with a clean white dent and springs back slowly. No whey ring around the spoon.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, ruler on the left and 15 mm checkerboard on the right of the specimen. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard centred under the specimen. Still 3: fork-press close-up, fork half-pressed in, tines clearly deforming the surface. Clip 1: 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous take. Clip 2: the full IDDSI test film, fork drip then spoon tilt. Name files: plain_yogurt_L4_take1.jpg and plain_yogurt_L4_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Whey separation on standing → fail; re-make from a fresh tub and re-shoot within 60 s. Specimen drips through fork tines or runs off the spoon → fail; the yogurt is too thin — re-blend only; do not add thickener unless a full re-shot still fails, then add 0.5 g per 100 ml and re-record. Grainy or curdled texture → fail; blend 10 s longer, re-sieve only if blending alone does not smooth it.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g chilled unsweetened soy milk into the blender cup. Blend 20 s to homogenise the chilled pack (proteins settle). Pass through the 4 mm sieve into a clean cup; discard residue. Weigh the sieved milk and pour back into the blender cup. Add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml as the calibration starting point for L3 soy milk; record the actual grams used and the final batch weight on the data sheet. Blend 15 s, rest 60 s, blend 5 s. Do not add water or ice — dilution drops the spec out of L3. If 2.0 g/100 ml lands outside the flow window, adjust in 0.2 g/100 ml steps and re-test.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into 10 ml of specimen on a flat plate; surface blebs under the tines, no white liquid pools, fork lifts with a cohesive mound. Pass if it spreads <4 mm under the fork and holds shape. Spoon tilt: fill a 5 ml spoon, tilt to 90°; specimen pours off in a thick continuous ribbon, not a run. Fork drip: dip fork, raise 10 cm; drips fall slowly in a thick continuous dollop, not a steady stream. Syringe flow: fill the 10 ml IDDSI syringe, start timer at 10 s; pass if 8–10 ml remains in the barrel.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy off-white, smooth, no lumps, no skin, coats the spoon back without running. Holds a soft mound after the fork press with a clean dent, not a puddle.
specimens.shots: unsweetened_soy_milk_L3_take1_hero.jpg — 45° angle, specimen in white bowl, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, scale readout visible. unsweetened_soy_milk_L3_take1_topdown.jpg — top-down, checkerboard under bowl, fork and spoon flanking. unsweetened_soy_milk_L3_take1_forkpress.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. unsweetened_soy_milk_L3_take1_forkpress_spoontilt.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork press then spoon tilt. unsweetened_soy_milk_L3_take1_iddsitest.mp4 — full syringe flow test, timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen runs through the syringe leaving <8 ml (too thin) → add 0.2 g/100 ml thickener, re-blend, re-test. Fork drips in a stream or surface floods white (too thin) → same fix. Specimen holds the fork, does not drip, or leaves >10 ml in syringe (too thick) → add 5% of batch weight in soy milk, blend, re-test. Any sieve residue >5% of batch weight → re-sieve. Re-make from fresh if two consecutive fails.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of chilled baked egg custard into the blender cup. Add 30 ml water. Blend 25-30 s on high until fully smooth and pourable. Sieve through the 4 mm sieve into a bowl; press with the back of a spoon to pass; discard residue. Weigh the sieved liquid on the digital scale. Stir in thickener at 1.0 g per 100 ml of sieved liquid as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Stir 30 s, rest 2 min, stir 5 s. If the IDDSI flow test shows more than 10 ml retained, add thickener in 0.1 g per 100 ml increments, stir, rest, retest. If less than 8 ml is retained, thin with 2-3 ml water, stir, rest, retest.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a forkful 50 mm above the plate; liquid drips slowly in a continuous thin stream through the tines. Fork pressure: the fork tines leave a clear, persistent impression on the surface when pressed, and the surface does not flow back to level. Spoon tilt: on a spoon held at 45 degrees, the specimen sits in a mound and slides off slowly as a cohesive blob, not as a fast pour. IDDSI 10 ml syringe flow test: fill the syringe to the 10 ml mark, release for 10 s; 8-10 ml remains in the syringe.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a smooth glossy film that drips slowly without breaking into droplets. On the spoon: a soft, rounded mound that holds shape then slumps. In the sieve residue: minimal, only fine specks.
specimens.shots: baked_egg_custard_L3_take1.jpg - 45-degree hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. baked_egg_custard_L3_take2.jpg - top-down, checkerboard centred, specimen in a 90 mm dish. baked_egg_custard_L3_take3.jpg - fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines partly submerged. baked_egg_custard_L3_take1.mp4 - 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt sequence. baked_egg_custard_L3_take2.mp4 - full IDDSI syringe fill, 10 s release, final meniscus reading on the 1 ml graduations.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: flows like cream, leaves under 8 ml in the syringe, runs off a tilted spoon in under 1 s. Re-make: add thickener at 0.1 g per 100 ml increments. Too thick: sits as a stiff blob on the spoon, syringe retains over 10 ml, fork drip stops. Re-make: thin with 2-3 ml water per 100 ml and retest. Grainy or lumpy: visible specks after sieving, residue over roughly 10 percent of starting weight. Re-make: blend an extra 10 s and re-sieve; if it persists, the batch is rejected and a new 200 g portion is weighed out.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of chilled baked egg custard into the blender cup. Blend 25-30 s on high until completely smooth with no curds or lumps visible. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any residue retained on the mesh. Return sieved puree to the cup. If the puree flows through fork tines or loses mound shape on the spoon, add thickener 1.0 g per 100 ml of puree, stir 15 s, re-test. Record the actual grams added. Do not add water or milk; the custard's own moisture is the calibration starting point. Re-chill 5 min before testing.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: scoop puree, turn fork tines down for 10 s — puree must mound and sit above the tines, not drip or flow through. Fork pressure test: press fork tines into the surface until the thumb blanches; surface must retain a clear indentation with no surrounding liquid pooling. Spoon tilt test: place a heaped spoonful on a flat plate, tilt plate to 45 degrees — puree must hold shape and not slide, run, or drip. All three must pass to confirm L4.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform pale yellow, glossy, no visible curds or browned skin fragments. Coats the spoon thickly without dripping off the edge. Mound on fork tines holds a clean peak for 10 s without slumping.
specimens.shots: Stills: baked_egg_custard_L4_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. baked_egg_custard_L4_take2.jpg — top-down on A4 kit with checkerboard. baked_egg_custard_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. Clips: baked_egg_custard_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. baked_egg_custard_L4_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Puree flows through fork tines or drips in 10 s tilt — add thickener 0.5 g per 100 ml, stir, re-test. Surface weeps thin yellow liquid under fork pressure — blend a further 15 s, sieve again, re-chill. Lumpy or grainy texture after sieving — discard and start with a fresh 200 g cup; do not re-blend a failed batch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 120 g of chilled baked egg custard into a bowl. MASH with a fork against the side of the bowl until the largest visible curds are <=4 mm. Do NOT press the mash through the 4 mm sieve — pressing forces the curds through the mesh and yields the glossy, curd-free purée that section 5 calls a failed batch. Use the 4 mm sieve as a GAUGE only: tip 15 g of the mash onto the dry sieve and tilt it 3 times without pressing; return the material that falls through to the bowl, and re-mash by hand any curd retained on the mesh until the 15 g aliquot passes. Report the retained mass. Stir in water only if the mash is dry: 5 ml (1 level teaspoon) at a time, maximum 10 ml total; stop the moment it holds together when pressed with the back of a spoon and the surface looks slightly wet, not watery. Record actual water ml (0–10) on the card. Do NOT blend: blending destroys curd structure. Do NOT add thickener — L5 is calibrated from this fork-mash starting point.
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon tilt (pass/fail): tilt a spoonful 45°; the mass must sit in a pile, not slide, flow, or pour. Fork pressure (supporting check only — record it, do not gate on it): press the mash flat with the fork tines; it must SQUASH and NOT recover its shape when the fork is lifted. Fork drip is NOT in the L5 set — do not apply it. No syringe test at L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: soft, lumpy curds with a slight sheen, no pooled liquid in the cup of the tines. On the spoon: holds a mounded heap, surface slightly wet not watery, no milky runoff at the rim.
specimens.shots: baked_egg_custard_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame, portion on white plate. baked_egg_custard_L5_take2.jpg — top-down on checkerboard, ruler alongside. baked_egg_custard_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, fork mid-press, squashed curd visible. baked_egg_custard_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s clip: fork-press and spoon-tilt in one continuous action. baked_egg_custard_L5_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film: full spoon-tilt sequence, with fork pressure recorded as the supporting check, and audible pass/fail narration. Files: baked_egg_custard_L5_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Smooth, glossy purée with no visible curds (from blending, or from pressing the mash through the sieve): a slight sheen on lumpy curds is fine — visible curds are the L5 requirement — but a curd-free glossy purée is not L5, it is L4 material. Re-make by hand-mash and use the sieve as a gauge only; do not re-blend and do not press the mash through the sieve. L5 is reachable for this food only by hand-mashing plus gauging. Too wet: milky liquid pools and pours off the spoon → drain on a sieve or fine strainer for 60 s WITHOUT pressing, discard the run-off, re-test. Dry, or curds >4 mm retained on the gauge → add 5 ml water, mash 30 s more, re-gauge; if curds are still >4 mm after a second attempt the custard is under-set — re-bake or start over.

specimens.prep: Open chilled cups; scoop 200 g of set custard into blender jug. Pulse 3–4 s only, just to break the set gel into a coarse paste. Do not over-blend — L6 pieces must remain distinct, not puréed. Press the paste through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard what stays behind. Return sieved paste to jug. The per-level note requires cubes ≤15 mm; do not sieve finer. Using the fork-press method, cut the paste on a board into 15 mm × 15 mm × 15 mm cubes with a dinner knife. Record actual sieve-pass weight (g) on the capture sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press a cube flat with the fork tines for 5 s. Pass if thumbnail blanches white, the cube squashes, and it does not recover shape when fork is lifted. Spoon tilt: no flow off a tilted spoon (L6 holds shape). Fork drip: nothing drips through the tines when the cube is lifted. L6 = holds shape + squashes under fork; reject if it spreads, runs, or fully recovers.
specimens.visual_qc: Cube keeps clean 15 mm edges with slightly rounded corners from cutting; pale yellow, moist but not glossy with free liquid; no separate water pooling on the plate around the cube.
specimens.shots: Stills: 45° hero shot with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame on A4 mat; top-down with checkerboard grid only; fork-press close-up mid-press showing blanched thumbnail and compressed cube. Clips: 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence; full IDDSI L6 test film (press, hold, release, recovery check). Files: baked_egg_custard_L6_take1.jpg, baked_egg_custard_L6_take1.mp4 (use _take2 if retake needed).
specimens.fail_modes: Over-blended into smooth purée = L4/E1, remake and pulse only 2 s. Cube splits or crumbles under fork instead of squashing cleanly = too dry, remake with 5 ml water per 100 g blended before sieving. Free liquid weeps around cube on plate = too wet, drain 30 s on sieve before plating. Any fail = new take number, log the change.

specimens.prep: Weigh 120 g of chilled mango pudding into the blender jar. Blend 20-25 s on high until completely smooth and pourable. Do not sieve — the gel matrix will clog the 4 mm mesh and stall. Add 1.5 g thickener per 100 ml of pudding (1.8 g total); this is the calibration starting point, record the actual grams used. Stir 30 s with the fork, rest 60 s, stir 10 s. Target: pours in a slow ribbon, drips slowly through fork tines. Add water only if flow test reads above 10 ml; record any added ml.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: pudding drops slowly in thick drips through tines, not a steady stream. Spoon tilt: spoon at 45°, pudding slides off in 2-4 s as one mass, not a quick pour. Syringe flow test: fill to 10 ml, release 10 s, remaining volume 8-10 ml. All three must pass. Fork pressure is not an L3 test (protocol 5.1 covers L4, L6, L7); no fork-pressure criterion appears on this card and none may be added as a gate.
specimens.visual_qc: On fork tines: glossy, uniform, opaque orange-yellow, no gel lumps or fruit fibre strands. 4 mm gauge: press a teaspoonful through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon — no discrete lump larger than 4 mm may remain on the mesh (a smooth film that passes slowly is expected and is not a lump). On spoon: holds a soft mound that begins to slump within 1-2 s and levels off; it must not hold a defined peak. In flow test syringe: no separation, no air pockets.
specimens.shots: mango_pudding_L3_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame. mango_pudding_L3_take2.jpg — top-down on checkerboard only. mango_pudding_L3_take3.jpg — fork-drip close-up, drip mid-fall, ruler for scale. mango_pudding_L3_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-drip then spoon-tilt, continuous. mango_pudding_L3_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI syringe flow test, timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: reads under 8 ml in syringe, drips through fork in a stream — add 0.3 g thickener, stir 10 s, rest 60 s, retest. Too thick: reads above 10 ml, holds a stiff peak on the spoon or does not slide off within 4 s — blend in 5 ml water, rest 60 s, retest; water is the only permitted correction here, and no fork-pressure criterion may be invoked to rescue it. Lumpy or weeping: blending time too short or pudding over-thinned with water — discard and remake; do not re-blend a failed batch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of set mango pudding into the blender cup; keep it chilled, do not warm it. Blend on high for 10-15 s only — just long enough to come smooth with no visible fruit fibre or chunks. Do not blend 25-35 s: high-speed blending shears the set gel and thins the specimen below L4. Sieve is NOT used — the per-level note is "blend-hold", so the texture is set by the set pudding plus a short blend and a 60 s hold, not by sieving and not by thickener in the base run. Do NOT add water, milk, or thickener to the base run. Pour into a clean cup and rest 60 s before testing so the gel can re-form. Calibration: the no-add blend is tested first. If it does not hold on a fork, correct by thickening — weigh 1 g thickener per 100 ml of pudding, pulse-blend 5 s, rest 60 s, and re-test. Record the actual grams of thickener added per 100 ml. Never thin with water or milk: a sheared gel cannot be re-set on the bench, so a too-thin batch cannot be brought back to L4 by resting or re-blending — discard it and start a fresh 200 g batch.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: scoop a heaped teaspoon, turn the fork over the cup — the sample must SIT in a mound above the tines, not drip, flow, or drop through. Pass: cohesive mound that holds for the full 10 s observation. Fork pressure test: press the fork tines flat into the surface. The surface must keep the fork-prong marks clean and not flow back into the grooves when the fork lifts. Pass: clear tine imprints, no runnability. Spoon tilt test: tilt a heaped spoon to 90°. Sample must stay on the spoon; a thin tail is acceptable only if it does not drip off. Pass: holds shape on the spoon at full tilt.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy uniform orange-yellow surface, no liquid halo at the cup wall, no specks of skin or pulp. On the fork: a soft peak that rounds at the top, no sharp slump. On the spoon: the mound stays on the spoon as one piece at full tilt, with no run-off and no drip.
specimens.shots: mango_pudding_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler on the left, checkerboard under the cup. mango_pudding_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, full checkerboard visible, rim centred. mango_pudding_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines half-submerged mid-press, in focus. mango_pudding_L4_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press into spoon-tilt, continuous. mango_pudding_L4_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: scoop, fork flip, 10 s hold, pressure, spoon tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen flows through the fork tines or drips off the spoon → too thin (gel sheared too long, or a soft formulation): correct by THICKENING — 1 g thickener per 100 ml, pulse-blend 5 s, rest 60 s, re-test. Do not add water or milk. Grainy mouthfeel with visible pulp → blend incomplete; extend the blend to 20 s total, never longer. Re-sieving is NOT permitted at L4. Thin yellow liquid pools around the mound → serum separation; re-blend 5 s and rest 30 s, not 60 s, then re-test. Achievability limit: if a fresh 200 g batch still will not hold a mound after one measured thickener addition, this pudding's gel is below L4 and cannot be brought to L4 by blending alone on the bench — record the specimen as too thin, do not photograph it as L4 evidence, and flag the card for re-specification (the closest reliable alternative is the unblended set pudding straight from the cup, which already holds a soft shape). Any fail → discard the cup, start a fresh 200 g batch, log the actual thickener g/100 ml used, if any.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g set mango pudding + 30 g of its syrup into the bowl (230 g moist base). Do NOT blend to a smooth puree and do NOT sieve the lumps away — a lump-free specimen is L4, not L5. L5 must keep distinct moist lumps ≤4 mm. Fold and chop the pudding with a spatula into lumps ≤4 mm; press one spoonful through the 4 mm sieve as a GAUGE only — lumps that pass are correctly ≤4 mm; mince any lump left on the sieve down to ≤4 mm and fold it back in (do not discard it). If the pudding smears smooth and will not hold distinct ≤4 mm lumps, fold in 40 g fresh mango diced to ≤4 mm so 4 mm lumps are present. Add 2.0 g thickener (calibration start; record actual grams), stir 20 s, rest 60 s, stir again 10 s; keep the mass moist (the 30 g syrup is already in the bowl). Target final mass ≈232 g ± 5 g (≈272 g ± 5 g if the diced-mango fold-in is used). No added water.
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon tilt (5.2; the primary L5 test): load a heaped spoon, hold it level, then tilt it sideways to 45°. Pass = the soft moist particles hold a LOOSE MOUND that slumps and spreads only when the spoon is shaken, and the spoon is not swimming in separate liquid. No separate thin liquid may pool on the spoon or the tray; any pooling means the specimen fails its level (protocol 5.2 and QC rule 4). Boundary reads, so the tilt cannot be passed by the wrong level: sliding off the tilted spoon as ONE COHESIVE MASS with little residue left behind is the L4 result and FAILS L5; running off the spoon in a slow continuous stream is the L3 result and FAILS L5; a loose mound that holds is L5. 4 mm sieve gauge (the L5 particle-gauge test listed in protocol section 2): press one spoonful against the 4 mm sieve — material that passes is ≤4 mm; anything retained is over-size, so mince it finer and re-gauge. The sieve is a gauge only: never press the batch through it and never discard what it retains. Fork pressure (5.1; supporting check only at L5, never the pass gate): press the fork tines flat into the specimen; the ≤4 mm lumps should mash and the mass must not spring back. Log it as supporting evidence. Fork drip (5.3) and syringe flow (5.4) do NOT apply at L5 — 5.3 is L3/L4 only and 5.4 is every L3 only. Do not run them and do not record them as pass/fail. If the specimen runs off the spoon or separates free syrup onto the plate it is too thin/wet — add +0.5 g thickener, stir 20 s and re-test, to a ceiling of 3.0 g total thickener; still too thin at 3.0 g means the batch is re-made from a reserve aliquot, never corrected further.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: yellow-orange minced-and-moist mass with distinct moist lumps up to 4 mm; glossy with syrup but no free syrup pooling. On the fork: small moist lumps clearly ≤4 mm, no thin liquid running from the bottom edge. No lump larger than 4 mm passes the 4 mm gauge. Distinct ≤4 mm lumps must be visible — a smooth glassy surface means the batch is L4, not L5.
specimens.shots: Stills: mango_pudding_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero with 100 mm ruler edge-on and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; mango_pudding_L5_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, showing distinct 4 mm lumps; mango_pudding_L5_take1_press.jpg — fork-press mid-action showing white nail bed. Clips: mango_pudding_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s spoon-tilt (primary) then supporting fork-press; mango_pudding_L5_take1_iddsi.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence, slow enough to read thumbnail blanch.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen runs off the spoon or separates free syrup onto the plate → too thin/under-thickened; add +0.5 g thickener, stir 20 s, re-test (ceiling 3.0 g total thickener, then re-make). Lumps larger than 4 mm → too coarse; mince finer to ≤4 mm and re-gauge through the 4 mm sieve (keep the lumps, do not sieve them away). Specimen cracks or crumbles dry → too thick/over-thickened; thin it: add +10 g syrup and reduce thickener by 0.5 g, re-test. Achievability: mango pudding blended and sieved smooth is L4 (lump-free, holds a shape), not L5 — a smooth pudding has no 4 mm lumps. L5 is reached only if distinct ≤4 mm lumps are present and the mass stays moist yet holds on the spoon. If the pudding will not hold distinct 4 mm lumps even with the diced-mango fold-in, the specimen is L4, not L5 — certify it as L4 or use a food that naturally forms 4 mm lumps; do not certify a smooth specimen as L5.  ---

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g chilled mango pudding on the scale. Scoop from the cup, discard any loose liquid. On a clean plate, cut the gel into cubes using a kitchen knife and a ruler as a guide; trim any piece larger than 15 mm so every cube measures ≤ 15 mm on its longest side. Do not blend. Do not sieve. Do not add thickener. Per-level note requires cubes ≤ 15 mm; do not attempt fork-mash only. If any cube exceeds 15 mm after cutting, re-trim before testing.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork tines into one cube until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass: the cube squashes, does not spring back, and breaks apart; the thumbnail clearly whitens. Spoon tilt: lift a cube on a standard spoon and tilt until the spoon is vertical. Pass: the cube slides off easily with little or no residue, or falls off completely. Fork drip is not applicable to a solid L6 specimen; confirm the cube holds its shape when lifted clear of the plate. Record pass/fail for both tests on the sheet.
specimens.visual_qc: Cube edges are clean-cut, no ragged gelatin strands. Cube holds a defined rectangular block shape on the fork, not a slumped puddle. Surface shows uniform mango-yellow with no free liquid pooling on the plate beneath the cube.

No brand labels visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Cube larger than 15 mm: re-cut and re-measure with the ruler before re-testing. Cube springs back under fork pressure: cup was insufficiently set, set a fresh cup longer and re-cut. Free liquid pools under the cube: drain the cup briefly on paper towel, then re-cut. Re-make from a new cup after two consecutive fails.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g ready-to-eat black sesame paste into the blender jar. Add 120 ml cool water. Blend on high for 45 s, scraping down at 20 s. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard residue weighing more than 8 g. Weigh the sieved liquid; add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml as the calibration starting point (record actual grams used). Whisk by hand 30 s, rest 60 s, whisk 15 s. Hold the fork vertically: if threads form a steady stream (more than 2 drops per second) or the first drop falls before 1 s, add thickener 0.2 g per 100 ml, rest 60 s, retest. Stop when the first drop falls within 1-2 s and strands run at 1-2 per second. Record final liquid mass and water added.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: held vertically, liquid drips in slow, continuous strands, not a steady stream; first drop within 1-2 s. Spoon tilt: spoon at 45 degrees, sample flows off in 2-4 s, leaves a thin coating. Syringe flow: fill 10 ml, release, at 10 s residual reads 8-10 ml; pass window 7-10 ml. All three must pass before capture.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: matte jet-black, glossy but not pooling, one slow drip forming and falling. On the fork: 4-5 thin continuous strands at 1-2 per second, no run-off between prongs. No grainy specks, no separated oil sheen, no lumps catching on sieve residue.
