(1) black_sesame_paste_L3_take1.jpg, 45-degree hero, 30 cm distance, ruler and checkerboard in frame. (2) black_sesame_paste_L3_take1.jpg, top-down, checkerboard centered, spoon pool 3 cm diameter. (3) black_sesame_paste_L3_take1.jpg, fork-drip close-up, fork held vertical, slow strands at the tines. (4) black_sesame_paste_L3_take1.mp4, 10 s, fork drip then spoon tilt. (5) black_sesame_paste_L3_take1.mp4, 12 s, IDDSI syringe test stopwatch visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: threads off fork in a continuous stream and syringe reads under 7 ml; re-thicken in 0.2 g per 100 ml steps, max three attempts, then discard batch. Too thick: drops do not fall or syringe holds over 10 ml; whisk in 5 ml water, rest 60 s, retest, max twice. Gritty after sieving: residue over 8 g or visible specks on spoon; re-blend 20 s with extra 10 ml water and re-sieve once.  ---

specimens.prep: Open the ready-to-eat pack and weigh 200 g of black sesame paste into the blender cup. Blend on high for 20 s, scrape the wall, then blend 10 s more. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard residue — the sieve is a gauge for lumps only: sub-4 mm sesame grit passes it, so grit is controlled by blend time, not by sieving. The starting point is the paste as-is: add no water, milk, or thickener until the first IDDSI test has been run, and add nothing at all if the paste already holds shape with no separate thin liquid. If the fork-drip or spoon-tilt test fails, thicken from this point only, in 0.5 g per 100 g increments (1.0 g per 200 g pack), re-blending 10 s and re-testing after each increment, to a maximum of 2.0 g per 100 g. Water or milk are added only to thin a paste that cracks under fork pressure, never to rescue a separated pack. Record whether thickener or water was used, the grams and ml used, and the final specimen mass (g).
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a fork loaded with paste; the mound must sit clearly above the tines with no drip falling in 5 s. Fork pressure: press the fork tines into the paste on a flat plate; the paste must hold a clear dent without separating liquid, and the tines must not cut through cleanly — the lump stays as one piece. Spoon tilt: scoop, then tilt the spoon 45°; the paste must not slide off, only a slow tongue of paste may move. No separate thin liquid should pool on the plate under the mound.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform matte black, glossy only where smeared, with no visible lumps after sieving and no grain or husk specks — the 4 mm sieve removes lumps, not sub-4 mm grit, so grit is judged by eye on the plate. Spoon holds a sharp peak that slumps only slightly. Fork tines stay coated, never exposed by running paste.
specimens.shots: black_sesame_paste_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler left, checkerboard right. black_sesame_paste_L4_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard under plate. black_sesame_paste_L4_take1_fork.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. black_sesame_paste_L4_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. black_sesame_paste_L4_take1_test.mp4 — full IDDSI test film. Lock focus, white balance off plate, no flash glare on the dark paste.
specimens.fail_modes: Paste runs through fork tines or drips in under 5 s: too thin — add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g (1.0 g per 200 g pack), re-blend 10 s, rest 2 min, retest; maximum 2.0 g per 100 g. Too stiff — cracks or breaks under fork pressure instead of taking a clean dent: too thick — thin with 5 ml water per 100 g (10 ml per 200 g), re-blend 10 s, re-test; if it still cracks after 15 ml per 200 g, the pack is not usable for L4 — record and discard. Gritty specks visible after sieving: the 4 mm sieve will not remove sub-4 mm grit — blend 10–20 s more and re-sieve; if grit persists, the pack is not usable. Thin black liquid pools under the mound: too wet — do not add more paste to compensate; discard and start with a fresh pack.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g ready-to-eat red bean paste into the blender cup. Add 80 ml water and blend 45 s until fully smooth. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard retained skins/fibres; weigh the sieved paste and record the mass M (expect about 130 g).  Calibrate to L3 on a **mass basis only** — do not convert to ml, as no density is specified: 1.5 g thickener per 100 g of sieved paste. Dose = 1.5 g × M / 100, weighed to 0.1 g (M = 130 g → 1.95 g). Stir in, rest 2 min, stir again. Record the actual thickener mass used on the bench sheet.  Target: 8–10 ml of a 10 ml syringe fill remains at t = 10 s; fluid enough to pour in a slow ribbon, thick enough that drips are slow off the fork. - Under-thick (fewer than 8 ml remains at 10 s): add 0.2 g thickener per 100 g of paste, stir, rest 2 min, and retest. - Over-thick (more than 10 ml remains, or nothing has moved): stir in 5 ml water at a time, stir, and retest. Do not sieve after adding thickener.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: hold the loaded fork clear of the cup for 10 s. PASS — 2–4 slow drips in 10 s, not a stream, not a single drop. Spoon tilt: place a heaped teaspoon on the spoon and tilt to ~45°. PASS — the paste flows off in a thick ribbon, not a continuous pour, not a lump that drops whole. IDDSI flow test: fill the 10 ml syringe to the 10 ml mark, release, and start the stopwatch. PASS — 8–10 ml remains in the syringe at t = 10 s. All three must pass. Fork pressure is not applicable at L3 and is not run.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy uniform dark brown-red, no visible bean skins or fibres, no separated liquid pooling at the rim. Coats the back of a spoon smoothly without running into a thin film. Holds a soft peak for about 2 s then flattens.
specimens.shots: smooth_red_bean_paste_L3_take1.jpg — hero 45°, ruler and checkerboard in frame. smooth_red_bean_paste_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, no ruler. smooth_red_bean_paste_L3_take3.jpg — fork-drip close-up mid-drip, ruler visible. smooth_red_bean_paste_L3_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s spoon-tilt then fork-drip, ruler in frame. smooth_red_bean_paste_L3_take1_flow.mp4 — full 10 ml / 10 s syringe test, ruler and stopwatch visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Flow test — fewer than 8 ml remaining at 10 s: specimen is too THIN. Add 0.2 g thickener per 100 g of paste, stir, rest 2 min, and retest. Flow test — more than 10 ml remaining at 10 s, or nothing has moved: specimen is too THICK. Stir in 5 ml water, and retest. Visible skins, grainy spoon coat, or material retained on the 4 mm sieve: blender time too short or sieve skipped; re-blend 30 s and re-sieve before adding thickener, then re-run all three tests. Two consecutive failures on the same root cause: re-make from 200 g paste.

specimens.prep: Pre-screen the pack before anything else: draw a dessert spoon through the paste and lift it out — a pack that levels out within 10 s is thinner than L4; set it aside and open another, and record which pack was used. Weigh 200 g ready-to-eat red bean paste into the blender jar. Blend 20 s on high, scraping the jar down once at 10 s, to remove lumps. Pass through the 4 mm sieve with a spatula, pressing gently — at L4 the sieve is the lump-free gauge and this is the level where it is deliberately used; discard everything retained (skins, seeds, grits). Weigh back and record the actual yield (expect 180–200 g). Do not add water, milk or any thin liquid to a paste that already passes, and do not add thickener to a paste that already passes: L4 for this food is calibrated from the as-packaged paste, and the operator records the actual gram yield only. If a thin serum separates on standing, decant and discard it before capture. Bring the sieved paste to 20–25 °C before testing and capture it at 20–25 °C — warm paste flows more readily than cold, so a warm-only test will pass a paste that fails at room temperature.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-drip test (5.3): scoop a heaped 5 ml teaspoon, hold the fork tines down over a white plate for 10 s. PASS — paste sits as a mound above the tines; nothing drips or streams through. Fork-pressure test (5.1): press the fork tines into the mound on the spoon until your thumbnail blanches white. PASS — the mound deforms but does not separate, no thin liquid weeps at the edges, and no residue is left in the tine gaps. Spoon-tilt test (5.2): place one heaped 5 ml teaspoon (about 10 g) on a dessert spoon and tilt to 90°. PASS — the paste holds a soft peak and does not flow, slump or drip off the spoon. Skip the syringe flow test (5.4): it applies to L3 only.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy, uniform deep-red-brown surface with zero visible bean skins or grits; no air bubbles from blending (tap the spoon twice on the bench before shooting). Paste mounds cleanly on the spoon with straight edges and no slumping. Tines of the fork remain clean after the drip test; no serum pools on the plate. All checks made at 20–25 °C.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45-degree hero: spoon heaped with paste, 15 mm checkerboard in frame left (the checkerboard is the sizing reference; a 100 mm ruler may be added as a scale prop only). Still 2 — top-down: paste mound on white background, checkerboard centred. Still 3 — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines visibly indenting the mound. Clip 1 — 8–12 s continuous: fork-press then spoon-tilt, single take. Clip 2 — 45–60 s IDDSI test film: drip, pressure, tilt in sequence. Name all files smooth_red_bean_paste_L4_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: A. Thin serum pools on the plate during the drip test → decant again and re-test; if it recurs within 2 min, reject the pack — do not blend the serum back in. B. Visible skins, grits or bean fragments in the mound → re-sieve through the same 4 mm sieve once more, or re-blend 10 s and sieve again; if a third pass is needed, reject the pack. C. Too thin — paste flows through the fork tines, slumps off the tilted spoon, or will not hold a peak: this is L3 behaviour (lump-free, flows freely), not L5, which requires ~4 mm lumps and is not reachable from a smooth paste. Correct by THICKENING, in this order: (1) gentle evaporation — warm the 200 g in a small heavy pan over low heat, stirring constantly, until the fork-drip test holds a mound for 10 s and the spoon holds a peak; re-weigh and record the mass lost (expect 10–30 g). (2) If evaporation alone will not hold a peak, blend in a measured thickener — max 5 g cornflour or 3 g xanthan gum per 200 g — then re-run all three tests. Never add water, milk or any thin liquid at this step, and never rescue a thin paste by mixing in paste from a different pack — there is no criterion for that and it produces a mislabelled specimen. If neither step works, reject the pack. D. Too thick — paste will not pass the 4 mm sieve, or the mound stays rigid with no deformation under the thumbnail press: correct by THINNING with a measured amount of water, 5 ml at a time, blending 5 s after each addition and re-testing, to a maximum of 20 ml per 200 g. Record the total ml added; a paste needing more than 20 ml is not this pack's L4 calibration — reject it. E. Specimen tested above 25 °C (just-warm paste) → the flow result is not valid; cool to 20–25 °C and repeat all three tests before capture.  ---

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g tofu fa into the blender cup. Blend 30 s until smooth. Press through the 4 mm sieve into a bowl with the back of a spoon; discard coarse residue. Measure the sieved puree (expect about 180 ml). If the puree is stiffer than a slow pour, add measured warm water in 10 ml steps and record the total added — L3 is reached by thinning first, and water is the only thing that thins. Add thickener at the calibration starting point of 2.5 g per 100 ml (4.5 g for a 180 ml batch), weighed to 0.1 g; sprinkle, whisk, rest 90 s, whisk again. Titrate to the syringe window in 0.25 g per 100 ml steps. Record the final grams of thickener per 100 ml and the total water on the capture sheet. Thickener only ever thickens: it is never added to correct a too-thick reading.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a loaded fork clear of the bowl; the specimen drips slowly through the tines in a continuous flow and leaves a coating on the fork. Pass = steady slow drip; a free stream is too thin, a mound sitting on the tines is too thick. Spoon tilt: a full spoon tilted to 45° pours off in a slow continuous stream over 2-4 s, with no separate thin liquid pooling on the spoon or tray. Pass = slow pour. Syringe flow test (L3, mandatory): fill the 10 ml syringe to the 10 ml mark, release with the nozzle open, start the 10 s timer; pass = 8.0-10.0 ml retained at 10 s with a measurable discharge. <8.0 ml retained is too thin (L2 territory); 10.0 ml retained with no discharge is too thick (behaves as L4). Fork pressure is not an L3 test and is not performed on this specimen.
specimens.visual_qc: Even glossy surface, no lumps or bean curds visible after the sieve. On the spoon the specimen coats the bowl in an even layer and pours off as one slow ribbon; no bare streaks, and no whey or syrup running ahead of the body. On the fork it clings as a smooth continuous film that releases as a slow drip when tilted.
specimens.shots: Take the full set, then verify each file exists. Still A hero at 45 degrees with 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler in frame — tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L3_take1.jpg. Still B top-down, checkerboard flat beside the specimen — tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L3_take2.jpg. Still C fork-drip close-up, tines loaded, drip mid-fall, ruler and checkerboard in frame — tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L3_take3.jpg. Clip D 8-12 s fork-drip plus spoon-tilt sequence, continuous — tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L3_take1.mp4. Clip E IDDSI syringe flow test, 10 s timer visible, full 10 s captured, fill and final reading legible — tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L3_take2.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: flows freely off the fork as a stream, or <8.0 ml retained; re-add 0.25 g thickener per 100 ml (weighed to 0.1 g), rest 60 s, re-test. Too thick: holds a mound on the spoon, or 10.0 ml is retained with no measurable discharge at 10 s; re-blend 5 s with 5 ml warm water per 100 ml (9 ml at a 180 ml batch) and re-test — thinning, never more thickener; if it still holds a mound, discard and remake at 1.5 g thickener per 100 ml. Lumpy or grainy surface: the sieve step was skipped or the blend ran under 30 s; discard, re-blend the full 30 s, re-sieve. Tofu fa does reach L3 reliably by this route — blend, sieve, thin with measured water, then thicken to the window; if the window cannot be reached after two corrections, discard the batch and mark FAIL rather than logging it at L4.  ---

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g total of tofu fa plus its syrup into the blender cup (record the syrup weight; expect 20–30 g). Pulse-blend in 1 s bursts for 5–8 s total — the per-level note is brief blend, blend-hold, so stop the moment the surface turns glossy and stop before it loosens. Do not exceed 10 s total, including any fail-mode remedy. Do not sieve — a 4 mm sieve will shear the curd into a pourable liquid and is incompatible with L4. Do not add water, milk, or extra syrup; do not add thickener. Hold the cup still for 60 s before use so the structure recovers. Spoon onto a white plate, mounding, for testing and capture.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip (applies at L3/L4): lift a loaded fork; the specimen must sit in a cohesive mound above the tines with no continuous flow; at most a single slow tail may form over the 10 s hold. Fork pressure (primary at L4): press the fork tines into the mound; the surface must dent cleanly, the tines must blanch white, and no thin liquid may pool around the prongs. Spoon tilt (applies at L3/L4/L5): tilt a heaped spoonful to 45° — the specimen must stay on the spoon with no run, at most a slow slump. Invert to 90° — it must hold a soft mound and must NOT pour off as a stream or slide off as one mass. No fork prongs should show through the specimen when lifted (L4 holds shape).
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy, smooth, jiggle-stable surface; soft sheen, no matte dryness and no wet syrup halo. Mound keeps its peaks from the spoon, softening slowly at 90° inversion rather than dropping off in one mass. No curd lumps, no separated clear syrup around the base.
specimens.shots: tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen mounded. tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines half-submerged, mid-press. tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L4_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L4_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: fork drip, fork pressure, spoon tilt in sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-blended → specimen flows through the fork tines continuously or pours off the spoon at 90°: discard, re-make with a fresh 200 g tub and only 5 s total pulse. Under-blended → visible curds or lumps after the full 8 s: add ONE 2 s burst, hard limit 10 s total; if lumps persist, discard and re-make from a fresh 200 g tub with 5–8 s in 1 s bursts — do not keep pulsing a lumpy batch, extra blending loosens the curd past L4. Syrup separated → drain off free liquid, blot, re-test; if it still drips continuously through the tines, re-make.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g tofu fa with syrup into the blender. Pulse-blend 8-10 s until curds break to roughly pea size. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve, pressing gently with the fork; discard what stays above. The per-level note allows spoon-curds ≤4 mm in their own syrup, so do not add water or thickener — none needed and none permitted at L5. Mash the sieved curd briefly with the fork so it holds together but still shows soft pieces ≤4 mm. Record actual blender seconds and final mass on the capture sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines into a heaped spoonful until the thumbnail blanches white. The specimen must squash, not spring back, and must not flow through the tines. Spoon-tilt test: tilt a loaded spoon; the specimen sits in a clump, drops slowly only on firm tilt, leaves a thin coat, no free liquid pools. Fork-drip test: lift fork from the cup; pieces may cling but no thin syrup drips freely. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: soft irregular white curd flecks ≤4 mm, glossy with bound syrup, no loose liquid drop falling. On the spoon: heap holds shape when level, slumps only when tilted, surface matte-wet, not runny. Curds distinguishable, not a puree.
specimens.shots: tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press. tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L5_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. tofu_fa_tofu_pudding_L5_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, one continuous clip.
specimens.fail_modes: Curds stay above 4 mm after sieving — re-sieve, do not re-blend to liquid. Syrup pools separate from curds — drain briefly, re-mash, retest. Curds puree to a smooth paste (over-processed, behaves like L4) — discard and remake with shorter blend.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g chilled coconut jelly straight from the pack into the blender jar. Blend 20 s on high until fully smooth with no lumps. Sieve through the 4 mm mesh into a bowl; discard residue. Measure the sieved volume, then thin to pourable consistency by whisking in thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml of sieved sample — this is the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used and the final volume. Add 20–40 ml water only if the blend is too stiff to pour after thickener. Stir 30 s, rest 60 s, stir again. Final specimen must drip slowly through fork tines, not run.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: sample drips in a slow, continuous thin stream through the tines, not a fast pour and not a solid blob. Spoon tilt: a small mound on the spoon spreads only slightly when tilted to 45°, holds shape. Fork pressure: the tines leave a clear, soft imprint that does not fill back in immediately. Flow test: fill the 10 ml syringe to the 10 ml mark with no air gap; after 10 s the syringe must retain 8–10 ml (i.e. 0–2 ml has dripped). All four pass = L3 confirmed.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: smooth, glossy, no grains or jelly chunks catching the light. On the spoon: a soft mound that flattens at its base within 2 s of settling, no clear liquid pooling around it. Colour uniform off-white throughout, no streaks.
specimens.shots: Capture kit: A4 board, 15 mm checkerboard, 100 mm ruler, smartphone on a stable surface. Three stills: (a) 45° hero, specimen in a small cup, ruler and checkerboard in frame, coconut_jelly_L3_take1.jpg; (b) top-down with checkerboard centred under the cup, same filename _take2.jpg; (c) fork-press close-up mid-press, tines halfway into the specimen, _take3.jpg. Two clips, 8–12 s each, same naming with .mp4: one fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence, one continuous IDDSI flow-test film showing fill to the 10 ml mark and the 10 s drip.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny: passes the tines in a fast pour and the syringe empties past 2 ml — add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 60 s, re-test. Too thick: sits on the fork without dripping and the syringe retains the full 10 ml — whisk in 5–10 ml water, re-test. Grainy: visible jelly strands after sieving — re-blend 10 s and re-sieve; if strands persist, the food cannot meet L3 and must be re-recorded as a failed specimen.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g chilled coconut jelly straight from the pack into the blender cup, on the 0.1 g scale. Add 30 ml of the pack syrup that ships with it (shake the pack first so the syrup is uniform). Blend 25 s on high, stop, scrape the wall, blend 20 s more. The result should read as a smooth, opaque white puree. Pour through the 4 mm sieve using a spoon back; press and discard any fibrous bits that will not pass. Target solids caught in the sieve: under 5 g. Re-weigh the sieved puree on the 0.1 g scale and record that mass — it is the single dose base for every corrective step below, in grams per 100 g of weighed puree; never dose per ml, and never per the original 150 g batch. If the section-2 tests fail on the thin side (any drip in the fork-drip test, or the puree slides off the spoon in the spoon-tilt test), add 0.5 g of the kit thickener per 100 g of weighed puree (e.g. 160 g puree → 0.8 g thickener), hand-whisk 10 s, rest 60 s, and re-run all three tests. Record the actual thickener dose in grams on the card.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: lift a fork loaded with puree 15 cm above the plate; the mound must sit on top of the tines with no drips. Pass = zero drip in 10 s. Fork pressure test: press the fork tines flat into the puree on a plate; the surface must blanch white around the tines but the puree must not squeeze through to leave separate liquid. Pass = no thin liquid weeps out. Spoon tilt test: load a heaped teaspoon, tilt to 45 degrees; the puree must hold its shape on the spoon without sliding off. Pass = holds for 5 s.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: a soft, glossy mound that drops cleanly when tipped, no pooled liquid at the base. On the fork tines: a coherent cap that sits proud, not a glossy coat. On the plate after fork press: a clean dent, no watery ring around it. L4 is lump-free: the 4 mm sieve is the gauge for that — the catch must stay under 5 g and the puree must show no visible grain on the back of the spoon.
specimens.shots: coconut_jelly_L4_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame, puree mass noted on card. coconut_jelly_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. coconut_jelly_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. coconut_jelly_L4_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press plus spoon-tilt. coconut_jelly_L4_take5.mp4 — IDDSI test film, drip, press, tilt in sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: puree drips through the fork or flows off the spoon in the tilt test → thicken — add 0.5 g kit thickener per 100 g of the re-weighed puree, hand-whisk 10 s, rest 60 s, re-run all three tests. Too thick: puree cracks on the spoon or resists the fork press → thin — add 10 g pack syrup per 100 g of the re-weighed puree, re-blend 15 s, re-run all three tests. Grainy: sieve catches over 5 g fibre → re-blend 15 s and re-sieve; if the catch is still over 5 g, discard the batch — a grainy puree is not L4.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g chilled coconut jelly directly from the pack. Chop finely by hand with a knife on a white plate, then crush lightly with the back of the fork, pressing against the plate and scraping — stop while visible 2-4 mm lumps remain; do not keep crushing to a smooth paste. If blending, pulse 3-5 s only; stop and re-check with the sieve. Sieve check (gauge, not a filter): press one spoonful of the mince against the 4 mm mesh with the back of a spoon. Pass = the mash passes under pressure while visible 2-4 mm lumps remain in the bowl and nothing coarser than 4 mm is retained. Do NOT pass the whole batch through the sieve and discard what is retained — L5 must contain ~4 mm lumps, and a clean lump-free pass is L4. If the pack liquid runs thin and pools, fold in thickener 0.5 g per 100 ml of expressed liquid and stir until homogeneous. Record actual thickener mass, any added liquid (ml), and final weight (g) on the card.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure (supporting check only at L5): press the tines into a heaped spoonful until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass: the tines mash the visible lumps and leave a clear print; the specimen does not spring back. Spoon tilt: scoop, then tilt the spoon 45 degrees. Pass: specimen sits in a mound, holds shape, and does not slide or drip as a continuous pour; a small tongue of paste may slump but no separate thin liquid flows. Particle size: confirm visually against the 4 mm sieve reference — single lumps pass the 4 mm mesh when pressed, and the bulk still shows visible ~4 mm lumps.
specimens.visual_qc: Even pale white to translucent moist mince with visible ~4 mm lumps. No reflective pools of free liquid in the plate. A pressed smear must show fine visible lumps, not a continuous film — a continuous film with no lumps means the specimen has been taken to L4, not L5.
specimens.shots: coconut_jelly_L5_take1.jpg — hero 45° with ruler and 4 mm sieve reference in frame; coconut_jelly_L5_take2.jpg — top-down on 4 mm checkerboard; coconut_jelly_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. coconut_jelly_L5_take4.mp4 — fork-press and spoon-tilt, 8-12 s. coconut_jelly_L5_take5.mp4 — IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: Clear liquid separates, or the specimen slides off the spoon as a continuous pour — too wet: re-mix; if liquid still pools, fold in thickener 0.5 g per 100 ml of expressed liquid in 0.25 g/100 ml increments until the spoon-tilt test holds. Do not add water. Pieces above 4 mm — too coarse: mince finer by hand until the largest piece is ~4 mm. Do not fix this by sieving the batch to a clean pass; that removes the lumps and produces L4. Smear reads as a continuous film with no visible lumps, or the sieve passes with nothing retained — the specimen is L4, not L5: it cannot be re-lumped; re-make by hand mincing only and re-check with the sieve gauge at ~4 mm. Springy, recovers shape on the fork test — over-blended: re-make by hand chopping only, no blender. Water will not fix this and will create free liquid.

specimens.prep: - Keep the pack chilled until the moment of prep. Weigh 200 g of coconut jelly straight from the pack onto the scale. - On a clean board with a chef's knife, cut the jelly into cubes measuring 8–15 mm on all three sides — target ~12 mm, checked against the 100 mm ruler. Every cube must be ≥8 mm and ≤15 mm; discard any cube under 8 mm (it reads L5) and re-cut any cube over 15 mm. Discard any cube with a hard skin or set-crust edge. - Do NOT blend — blending destroys the cube structure and is incompatible with L6. - Do NOT sieve — the cubes must stay intact, and a 4 mm sieve cannot enforce a 15 mm limit in any case. - Do NOT add thickener, water, or any liquid — L6 calibration starts dry. - Record the final specimen mass and the number of cubes produced.
specimens.iddsi_test: - ACTIVE — 5.1 fork pressure. Press the fork tines firmly onto one cube on a white plate until the thumbnail blanches white; hold 3 s; lift. PASS: the cube squashes, does not spring back, and does not return to its original shape with the fork removed. Test 3 cubes; all 3 must pass. If a cube bounces back, re-test on a fresh cube; if it still recovers, chill the pack 30 min longer and re-cut. - SKIP — 5.2 spoon tilt. Applies at L3/L4/L5 only; L6 cubes must sit on a tilted spoon rather than flow, so the test cannot separate L6 from L7 — the 8–15 mm cube size does that. - SKIP — 5.3 fork drip. Applies at L3/L4 only; coconut jelly cubes carry no free liquid to drip through the tines, so the test always passes and carries no information. - SKIP — 5.4 syringe flow. Every L3 only; 8–15 mm cubes cannot be drawn through a 10 ml syringe. - L6 verdict = all cubes 8–15 mm AND 5.1 fork pressure passes.
specimens.visual_qc: - Cubes hold their shape on the fork, glossy and translucent, edges clean, each 8–15 mm against the ruler. - The surface looks moist but no free liquid pools on the plate. - A pressed cube leaves a visible flattened dent that stays after the fork is removed. - Cubes sit as distinct pieces in a heap on the fork — not a smear, not a single mass.
specimens.shots: - coconut_jelly_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 100 mm ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame. - coconut_jelly_L6_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only, full specimen spread. - coconut_jelly_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. - coconut_jelly_L6_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-pressure sequence, three cubes in order (the only active IDDSI test at L6). - coconut_jelly_L6_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: squash-and-recovery check on all three cubes.
specimens.fail_modes: - A cube measures over 15 mm: re-cut to 8–15 mm and re-measure against the ruler; re-shoot. - A cube measures under 8 mm: discard it — it reads L5. Re-cut from a larger block; do not mash the fines back together. - A cube recovers its shape after fork pressure (rubbery gel): chill the pack 30 min longer, then re-cut and re-test — a firmer gel squashes and stays squashed, which moves it toward L6. - Liquid weeps onto the plate: drain the cubes on paper towel for 30 s, blot gently, re-shoot. - The pack sets too soft to cut into 8–15 mm cubes and collapses under the knife: this pack cannot reach L6 by cutting — do not try to firm it with thickener. Note it plainly and use a firmer-set pack.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g fresh double-skin milk into blender cup. Blend 15 s on high. Push through 4 mm sieve into a clean cup; discard any solids retained. Measure poured volume. Add thickener at 0.5 g per 100 ml of sieved liquid as the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used. Stir 20 s, rest 60 s, stir 10 s. Re-pour through 4 mm sieve; if it does not drip continuously through the sieve, stop and re-make. Do not attempt to sieve the unblended set pudding — it will not pass and the specimen is invalid.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: specimen drips slowly in continuous threads through fork tines, not a steady stream. Spoon tilt: a 5 ml spoonful holds its shape on a level spoon but slides off readily when tilted past 45 degrees; it does not pour. Fork pressure: with fork held vertically, the tines leave a clear, persistent indentation when pressed to the bottom of the cup and the sample does not run back to fill it. Syringe flow test: fill the 10 ml IDDSI syringe to 10 ml, release for 10 s; pass = 8-10 ml remaining. All four tests must pass before capture.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: glossy, even coat clinging between tines with no break, no clear serum pooling. On the spoon: mound holds shape briefly, surface smooth and slightly dimpled, no weeping liquid at the rim. In the cup: uniform off-white, no lumps, no separated whey around the edge.
specimens.shots: Stills: doubleskin_milk_L3_take1.jpg hero at 45 degrees, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard visible; doubleskin_milk_L3_take2.jpg top-down, checkerboard centered; doubleskin_milk_L3_take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press. Clips: doubleskin_milk_L3_take1.mp4 fork-press and spoon-tilt, 8-12 s; doubleskin_milk_L3_take2.mp4 IDDSI syringe flow test, full 10 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin: runs like milk, pours off spoon, <8 ml retained in syringe — add 0.1 g thickener per 100 ml, rest, retest. Too thick: holds spoon shape past tilt, >10 ml retained, no drip through fork — add 2 ml water per 100 ml, stir, rest, retest. Lumpy or weeping: re-blend 10 s and re-sieve; if it fails twice, discard and start a fresh cup.

specimens.prep: Decant 200 g of fresh double-skin milk from the cup into the blender cup. Blend on high for 25-30 seconds until completely smooth with no curd flecks. Sieve through the 4 mm sieve into a small bowl; press through with the back of a spoon, discard residue. L4 is a lump-free level, so the sieve is part of the method here. Reweigh the sieved base and record.  The per-level note is "blend-hold", and the finished specimen must be lump-free and thick enough to hold a soft shape. Blending alone will not get it there: double-skin milk as served is a pourable drink that flows through the fork tines, and returning it to the blender changes nothing. The reliable bench route to L4 is calibrated thickening — whisk in the thickener at the supplier's stated Level 4 dose for this product (grams per 100 g of sieved base), whisk 30 s, rest 2 min, then test against section 2. Titrate in 0.5 g per 100 g steps until the L4 tests pass, and record the actual grams used and the final specimen mass. Do NOT thin with milk or water — that moves the specimen toward L3.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a fork loaded with ~5 g of specimen to 10 cm. Pass = sits as a mound above the tines, does not drip or flow through the gaps within 10 seconds. Fork pressure: press the fork tines flat into the specimen until the tines blanch, hold 5 seconds. Pass = tines leave a clear imprint, no separate liquid pools around the press. Spoon tilt: load a spoon, tilt to 45 degrees. Pass = specimen holds as a cohesive mound, does not slide off in 5 seconds. Syringe flow: skip — the 10 ml / 10 s syringe test is an L3 test and is not run at L4.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is glossy and uniform with no visible whey separation or curd lumps. Holds a soft peak when mounded with a spoon. Matte finger-print impression holds cleanly when pressed.
specimens.shots: Still 1: doubleskin_milk_L4_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler along front edge, checkerboard top-left, full specimen mound visible. Still 2: doubleskin_milk_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred under specimen, no ruler. Still 3: doubleskin_milk_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press, impression visible. Clip 1: doubleskin_milk_L4_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. Clip 2: doubleskin_milk_L4_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, fork-drip then fork-pressure, 8-12 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Whey separates as a thin yellow pool around the mound — whisk 20 s to re-incorporate; if free liquid still separates within 2 minutes the specimen is over-thin for L4, so add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g, whisk 30 s, rest 2 min, re-test. If it still weeps, discard and remake. Specimen flows through the fork tines or slides off the tilted spoon — too thin for L4: add 0.5 g thickener per 100 g, whisk 30 s, rest 2 min, re-test. Do not add milk or water. Lumps or grain remain after sieving — blend a further 10 s and re-sieve; if still present, discard and remake. If the as-served double-skin milk cannot be brought to hold a soft shape even at the maximum dose on the supplier's specification, this product cannot reach L4 by a reliable bench method — record the attempt, do not label it L4, and remake with a thicker double-skin milk base or a standardised L4 thickened reference specimen.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g of fresh double-skin milk from the cup. Do NOT blend — the per-level note requires spoon-broken curds, not a smooth puree. Press the cup contents with the back of a fork against the bowl side, working in small scoops until the largest curd pieces are no more than 4 mm. Sieve check (a gauge, not a processing step — L5 is not a lump-free level): weigh out 25 g of the broken curd, rub it through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon, and weigh what is retained. Retained weight must be 1 g or less (4% of the sample); if more is retained, the curds are too coarse for L5 — re-break the whole batch and re-check. Do not sieve the specimen you serve. Check on the fork (supporting check only at L5): a curd pressed by the fork base must squash flat and stay flat when the fork is lifted (no spring-back). If it springs back, keep breaking. No water, no milk, no thickener is added. Record the actual starting weight, the time spent breaking, and the sieve reject weight.
specimens.iddsi_test: Spoon-tilt test (the deciding test at L5): load a level spoonful and tilt it to 45° over 5 s. Pass if it holds together and slides as a clump with no thin liquid pouring off. Fork-pressure test (supporting check only at L5, not the defining test): press the fork tines into a curd pile on the plate; the curd must squash, the thumb blanches, and when pressure is released the curd stays flat — no recovery, no elastic bounce. Fork drip is an L3–L4 test and does not apply at L5 — do not run it and do not record it as pass/fail. No 10 ml syringe flow test is required for L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: matte, off-white curds in distinct pieces up to 4 mm, no shiny liquid pool between them, no skin film. On the spoon: mound holds its shape, surface slightly wet but not glossy, no milk weeping into the spoon well.
specimens.shots: - doubleskin_milk_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. - doubleskin_milk_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. - doubleskin_milk_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, curd deforming under tines. - doubleskin_milk_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s spoon-tilt plus fork-press clip. - doubleskin_milk_L5_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full spoon-tilt and fork-pressure sequence start to release.
specimens.fail_modes: Curd rebounds when the fork is lifted → over-sized or gummy curds; re-break and re-run the 4 mm sieve gauge, do not accept. Free thin milk pools on the plate or pours off the tilted spoon → the set is too loose or the curd was over-worked; do not add thickener to mask it, remake from a fresh cup. Curd breaks down into a smooth paste rather than discrete ~4 mm lumps → the batch reads as L4, not L5; remake from a fresh cup and record the outcome. Glossy skin films the surface → skin not broken through; scrape and re-mash before shooting.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g peanut paste into blender. Add 80 ml water. Blend 30 s until smooth. Pass through 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard residue. Measure sieved volume. Add thickener at 3 g per 100 ml of sieved volume as the calibration starting point; whisk briskly for 20 s, rest 60 s, then whisk 10 s more. Record the actual thickener mass and final volume on the card. If the 10 ml/10 s syringe leaves less than 8 ml, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml and re-whisk. If it leaves more than 10 ml, add 5 ml water per 100 ml and re-whisk. Target pour: continuous ribbon that breaks within 1-2 cm of the surface.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: hold fork clear of cup; liquid should drip slowly in thick strands, not run as a steady stream. Spoon tilt: spoon at 45 degrees; specimen slides off slowly, not in one quick sheet. Fork pressure: pressed flat, the surface shows clear tine marks with no spring-back; thumb-blanket lift holds shape only briefly. Syringe flow test: fill 10 ml, release 10 s; pass = 8-10 ml remaining in the syringe barrel. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform tan, glossy, no oil pooling on the surface. No visible peanut grit on fork tines after drip. Coats the spoon back evenly with no bare metal showing.
specimens.shots: peanut_paste_L3_take1.jpg — hero, 45 degrees, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. peanut_paste_L3_take1_topdown.jpg — top-down with checkerboard. peanut_paste_L3_take1_forkpress.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines half-embedded. peanut_paste_L3_take1_forkpress.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. peanut_paste_L3_take1_syringe.mp4 — full IDDSI syringe test, start to 10 s mark.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thick, leaves more than 10 ml in syringe or sits in a mound on the fork: thin with 5 ml water per 100 ml, re-whisk, re-test. Too thin, runs through fork tines and leaves less than 8 ml: add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, re-whisk, rest 60 s, re-test. Gritty or oily with visible separation: re-blend and re-sieve before judging. Re-make from scratch after two failed corrections.

specimens.prep: Open one ready-to-eat pack of peanut paste into the blender jar. Record starting mass on the scale (target 300 g). Blend 20-30 s on high until completely smooth with no seed or skin grit. Do NOT add water or milk - thinning will push the specimen below L4. Do NOT add thickener - the pack should already hold shape. The per-level note says serve as-is; sieving is not required if the blend is smooth. Press a small spoon-load against white paper: if no oil ring spreads and no solids remain, proceed to IDDSI tests.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: load a fork, lift it, and hold level for 5 s. Pass = the paste sits as a coherent mound on top of the tines, does not drip or fall through. Fork pressure test: press the flat of the fork into a spoonful on a plate. Pass = the paste deforms but does not separate liquid, holds a clean dent when the fork lifts, and does not run to fill the dent within 5 s. Spoon tilt test: scoop, tilt spoon to 90 degrees. Pass = the paste stays on the spoon, no flow. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface should be matte-smooth with no glossy oil pooling on top. Color uniform tan, no flecks of unblended peanut skin. Mound on the fork should hold its peak when lifted - if the peak slumps flat within 2 s, it is too thin.
specimens.shots: Still 1 - peanut_paste_L4_take1.jpg - 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard card in frame, jar label visible. Still 2 - peanut_paste_L4_take1_top.jpg - top-down with checkerboard only, spoon of paste centered. Still 3 - peanut_paste_L4_take1_fork.jpg - fork-press close-up mid-press. Clip 1 - peanut_paste_L4_take1.mp4 - 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. Clip 2 - peanut_paste_L4_take1_iddsi.mp4 - full IDDSI test sequence: fork drip, fork pressure, spoon tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Fail 1 - oil separates and pools on top or leaves a ring on paper: re-blend 10 s; if it persists, reject and re-make from a fresh pack. Fail 2 - paste flows through fork tines or drips within 5 s: it is below L4; do NOT add water to rescue, reject and re-make. Fail 3 - visible seed or skin grit after blending: blend a further 15 s, then re-check; if still gritty, sieve through the 4 mm sieve and re-test.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g curry fish balls plus sauce into the blender jar. Blend 45 s on high, scraping the jar wall once at 25 s. Sieve through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard coarse residue. Measure the blended volume in ml. Add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml of blend as the calibration starting point; whisk 15 s, rest 60 s, whisk 5 s. If the blend reads under 8 ml in the syringe after 10 s, add 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml and retest. Record the final grams per 100 ml on the card. The food list note is blend-thin, so sieving and thinning with thickener are required. Do not thin with water.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: tilt a fork with a heaped teaspoon of specimen; drips slowly in 4 to 6 discrete drops over 10 s. Fork pressure: the white of the prong shows through the specimen with light pressure and the surface returns flat when pressure is released. Spoon tilt: a teaspoonful slides off when the spoon is tilted, leaving a thin coating. Syringe flow test: 10 ml specimen in the IDDSI syringe, 10 s release; 8 to 10 ml remains. All four must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Specimen is smooth, glossy, uniform orange-brown, with no visible fish ball pieces, herbs, or oil pooling. On the spoon it mounds then levels in under 1 s. A lifted fork leaves a thin continuous trail that drops, not pours.

Still 3, fork-press close-up mid-press: curry_fish_balls_L3_take3.jpg. Clip 1, 8 to 12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt: curry_fish_balls_L3_take1.mp4. Clip 2, full IDDSI syringe flow test, timer visible: curry_fish_balls_L3_take2.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen runs off the spoon like a drink; the syringe empties below 8 ml; sieve residue contains intact fish ball chunks. Re-make from step 1, adjusting thickener in 0.3 g per 100 ml increments and re-sieving. A second failure of the syringe band means the batch is out of spec; re-blend fresh material.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g curry fish balls plus the supplied sauce into the blender jar. Blend on high for 45-60 s until completely smooth with no detectable lumps or fibre. Stop, scrape the jar wall, blend a further 15 s. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve using a spatula; discard retained solids. Do not add thickener at this stage — this is the calibration starting point; record grams per 100 ml actually used (typical 0.5-1.0 g/100 ml). Do not add water unless sauce is insufficient to blend; if so, add sauce or water in 10 ml increments only. Final specimen temperature: serve warm for testing, then cool to 20 ± 5 °C before capture.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a fork heaped with specimen to 2 cm above the plate for 5 s. Pass: specimen sits in a mound and does not flow through or drip continuously between tines. Fork pressure: press fork tines into specimen until blanching visible under the nail; specimen should yield but hold shape, no thin liquid seeping. Spoon tilt: place 5 ml on spoon, tilt to 45°. Pass: specimen holds, does not pour off. L4 only — no flow test required; absence of drip already confirms L4 over L3.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface glossy and uniform, no orange sauce pools or fish shreds visible. Mound on fork retains defined edges; on spoon tilt it slides as one piece, not as a stream. No free liquid pooled around the specimen on the plate.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45° hero: specimen mound on white plate with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, name card visible. Still 2 — top-down: checkerboard only, full plate coverage, no ruler. Still 3 — fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines blanching. Clip 1 — fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence, 8-12 s, continuous audio of texture cue. Clip 2 — full IDDSI test film: drip, pressure, tilt. Files: curry_fish_balls_L4_take1.jpg / .mp4, take2 backup only.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen flows through fork tines — too thin; remake adding 0.25 g thickener per 100 ml, retest. Specimen cracks or breaks on spoon tilt — too stiff; thin with 5 ml sauce per 100 ml and retest. Visible sauce separation or weeping — emulsion broken; reblend 20 s and recheck. Re-make maximum twice; record final thickener mass.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g cooked curry fish balls with sauce. Chop with knife until largest piece is ≤ 4 mm; reject any piece that will not reduce. Mash thoroughly with a fork so sauce coats every fragment. Add sauce only if dry; do not add water. Do not blend — blending destroys the required particle texture. Do not sieve — sauce carries solids and sieving would strip them. No thickener — L5 must show visible particles and must not be a paste. Record actual chop time, final mash consistency, and sauce volume on the capture sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press fork tines into a 15 mm portion on a flat plate until thumbnail blanches; sample must squash and not recover its shape when fork is removed. Spoon tilt test: tilt a spoon holding ~5 mm of sample; sample must sit in a cohesive mound and must not slide off or drip. Fork drip test: lift sample on fork; no thin liquid should run off the bulk. No syringe flow test — that is an L3 calibration tool only.
specimens.visual_qc: Coarse minced texture with clearly visible flecks of fish and sauce specks, no whole balls, no pooling liquid at the plate edge, soft sheen indicating moist but not runny.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero shot, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2: top-down with checkerboard centred. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines loaded. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film. Files: curry_fish_balls_L5_take1.jpg, curry_fish_balls_L5_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Visible thin liquid pooling — remake by draining excess sauce, no water added. Particles > 4 mm — recook batch, chop finer, recheck. Dry, crumbly mash that will not hold on spoon — add 5 ml sauce at a time, remash.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g cooked curry fish balls with sauce. Quarter each ball with a knife to pieces ≤15 mm; discard any piece >15 mm. Keep all sauce. Pulse in consumer blender 4 s, two pulses, just to coat pieces in sauce — do not purée. No sieve, no thickener, no added water. Note: the L3 thickener calibration is not applicable at L6; if any piece exceeds 15 mm after quartering, the batch fails — re-cut or do not submit.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines against a piece on a plate until thumbnail blanches white. Pass if the piece squashes, does not spring back, and breaks apart easily. Fork drip test does not apply at L6. Spoon tilt: scoop a piece with sauce onto a spoon and tilt; the piece must sit on the spoon without sliding off or dripping liquid freely. Also confirm piece dimensions with the 100 mm ruler — every piece must measure ≤15 mm in any direction.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: irregular chunks no bigger than the 15 mm checkerboard square, glossy from sauce, no whole or half balls present. On the fork: pieces hold shape but yield visibly under thumb pressure. Sauce should coat, not pool, around the pieces.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45° hero, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame, piece cluster visible. Still 2: top-down with checkerboard, spoon at centre. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail white. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. Clip 2: IDDSI test film, full fork-pressure sequence. Files: curry_fish_balls_L6_take1.jpg, curry_fish_balls_L6_take1.mp4, plus take 2 of each if needed.
specimens.fail_modes: Whole or half balls present (>15 mm) → re-quarter and re-shoot. Pieces spring back under fork pressure → piece too firm, re-cut or discard. Sauce so thin it pools and pours off spoon → drain excess sauce on a plate for 10 s, then re-shoot; do not add thickener.

specimens.prep: Place the curry fish balls and sauce onto the digital scale. Record the starting mass in grams as served; do not drain or blend. The per-level note states balls with sauce as served — the whole dish is the specimen, so no blender, sieve, thickener, or added water/liquid is used. Transfer the intact balls with their sauce onto the capture tray on the A4 kit, keeping balls whole and spaced so the 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler stay visible at frame edge. Confirm mass again before the first shot.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the tines firmly into a ball until the thumbnail blanches white. The ball must not fully compress, squash, or change shape so the fork slides out clean — it should dent then recover. Spoon tilt: lift a ball on a standard spoon and tilt 45 degrees; it must sit on the spoon without flowing off, dripping, or sliding. Fork drip: hold a fork with a ball clear of the plate for 10 seconds; no continuous drip, stream, or drop from the ball or clinging sauce. All three confirm L7 Regular. No syringe flow test applies at this level.
specimens.visual_qc: Ball keeps its rounded, intact shape on the fork. Sauce clings as a thin coating, not pooling or running off. Surface shows a clean fork-dent that springs back, no smear, no mashed interior visible.
specimens.shots: curry_fish_balls_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame, balls spaced. curry_fish_balls_L7_take1_topdown.jpg — top-down over checkerboard, sauce spread visible. curry_fish_balls_L7_take1_forkpress.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press showing dent. curry_fish_balls_L7_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s clip of fork-press and spoon-tilt. curry_fish_balls_L7_take1_iddsi.mp4 — IDDSI test film covering all three tests above.
specimens.fail_modes: Sauce is thin enough that the fork drip test produces a continuous drip — L7 fails, remake is not possible since the dish is served as bought; record the failure and reshoot. Ball splits or mashes fully under fork pressure, losing its shape — specimen invalid, re-record with a firmer ball from the batch. Salt crust or sauce pooling obscures the checkerboard pattern in the hero shot — blot gently with the fork tip and re-shoot.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g sweet and sour pork onto the digital scale. Add 60 ml warm water (40–50 °C) directly into the takeaway container. Blend in the consumer blender on high for 45 s, stop, scrape down with a fork, blend 30 s more. Pass the entire blend through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a fork; discard any coarse residue that will not pass — L3 is lump-free, so the 4 mm sieve is the production gauge here and a fully smooth puree is the target. Measure the sieved volume. Add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml of sieved liquid as the calibration starting point; whisk in with a fork for 20 s, rest 60 s, stir 10 s. Record the actual grams used on the data sheet. If the pour is too fast or too slow, adjust in 0.2 g/100 ml steps and re-record.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: scoop a forkful and hold the fork level, 10 cm above the plate, for 10 s; the specimen must drip through the tines as a slow continuous strand — not pour in a stream, and not sit on the fork without moving — pass. Spoon tilt test: tilt a spoonful to 30° and hold 5 s; the specimen must flow off slowly in a ribbon, not run, and must not fall off in a single blob — pass. Flow test: fill the 10 ml syringe to the 10 ml mark, hold it vertical, release and time 10 s; between 8 and 10 ml must remain in the syringe — pass. No fork pressure test at L3: that method covers L4, L6 and L7, and its "a clear pattern remains pressed in" criterion describes an L4 — do not run it here, and do not thicken the specimen to satisfy it.
specimens.visual_qc: Coating on the fork tines is even, glossy, and fully opaque with no visible pork fibre or batter specks. The specimen pours off a spoon in a slow, continuous ribbon that holds together for 1-2 cm before merging. Colour is uniform pale orange-red, no separated oil pooling on the surface.
