Sweet_and_sour_pork_L3_take3.jpg — fork-drip close-up, specimen dripping through the tines onto the plate. Sweet_and_sour_pork_L3_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s spoon-tilt and fork-drip sequence. Sweet_and_sour_pork_L3_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI flow test, syringe start to 10 s mark.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen pours too fast from the spoon, runs through the fork, or leaves under 8 ml in the syringe at 10 s — too thin; add 0.2 g/100 ml thickener, remix 20 s, rest 60 s, retest. More than 10 ml remains in the syringe at 10 s, or the specimen holds shape on the fork instead of dripping — too thick, drifting toward L4; thin with 20 ml warm water, reblend 30 s, re-sieve, then retest and only re-thicken if it now flows too fast. Specimen is lumpy — reblend 20 s and re-sieve through the 4 mm sieve, then re-calibrate against the flow test. Oil separates and pools on top — reblend with an extra 20 ml water, re-sieve, re-thicken to the flow window.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g sweet and sour pork (meat + sauce) straight from the takeaway container into the blender cup. Add 60 ml water. Blend on high for 45-60 s until fully smooth, scraping the wall once at 30 s. Sieve through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any residue. Weigh the sieved puree. Add thickener at the calibration starting point of 3 g per 100 ml of puree; whisk in, then rest 60 s and stir. If it slumps off the spoon, add 0.5 g/100 ml increments, rest 30 s between each, until it holds a clean mound. Record the final grams/100 ml used. Per-level note respected: blend with sauce, blend-hold.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: scoop a heaped teaspoonful, press the flat of the fork down once. Pass = puree holds its shape, leaves a clear fork-tine print, does not ooze back through the tines. Fork drip test: lift a fork-load 20 cm above the plate. Pass = sits as a mound above the tines, zero drip for 10 s. Spoon tilt test: load a dessert spoon and tilt to 45 degrees. Pass = puree stays on the spoon, no slide, no run-off. Repeat all three after 2 min rest; pass = identical result.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy uniform orange-red surface, no visible meat fibre, no pool of clear sauce around the mound on the plate. Fork tines leave a sharp imprint that does not fill in within 5 s.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, ruler along the front edge, checkerboard behind the mound. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard centred, no ruler. Still 3: fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into the puree. Clip 1: 8-12 s fork-press plus spoon-tilt sequence. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film (fork drip + spoon tilt). Files: sweet_and_sour_pork_L4_take1.jpg and sweet_and_sour_pork_L4_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: A) Sauce separates from meat during blending, leaving thin orange liquid at the rim — fix by blending an extra 20 s and adding 1 g/100 ml thickener; re-test. B) Puree flows through fork tines (too thin) — step thickener up by 0.5 g/100 ml, rest, re-shoot all frames. C) Puree cracks or tears when fork-pressed (too stiff) — thin with 5 ml water, re-blend 10 s, re-test. Re-make rule: any FAIL means discard the batch and start fresh; do not re-shoot a failed specimen.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g takeaway sweet and sour pork (meat + sauce) on the digital scale. Pick out only the pork pieces; discard loose sauce pooling in the container. Place pork in the consumer blender. Pulse 10 s, scrape down, pulse 10 s until coarsely minced. Press the mince through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard what stays behind. Return sieved mince to the bowl. Mash with a fork for 30 s, pressing firmly. Slowly fold in 30 ml of the original sauce to moisten (do not add water). L3 thickener is not required for L5; this is the calibration starting point and the operator records the actual sauce added.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines into the specimen until the thumbnail blanches white; the mince must squash, not recover, and the tines must leave a clear imprint. Spoon-tilt test: a small mound on a spoon must hold shape when tilted 45°; it may slide slowly but must not pour. Fork-drip test: lift forkful; no thin liquid must drip through the tines. If any of these fail, the specimen is not L5.
specimens.visual_qc: Mince sits as soft, distinct particles all visibly ≤4 mm. Surface looks glossy-moist, never dry or crumbly, and never sits in pooled sauce on the plate.
specimens.shots: Shoot: sweet_and_sour_pork_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame; sweet_and_sour_pork_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only; sweet_and_sour_pork_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press. Film: sweet_and_sour_pork_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press plus spoon-tilt; sweet_and_sour_pork_L5_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, both tests in one continuous clip.
specimens.fail_modes: Particles >4 mm after sieving — re-blend 5 s and re-sieve; do not skip sieving. Too dry, crumbs fall off fork — fold in another 5–10 ml sauce and re-test. Loose thin sauce pools on the plate — drain before plating; L5 must hold sauce within the mince, not separate.

specimens.prep: Start with 300 g takeaway sweet and sour pork, sauce removed. Separate the pieces from the sauce. Rinse the pieces briefly (10 s) under running water to strip the glossy starch-thickened coating, then pat dry with paper towel. Strip off and discard the batter crust — it does not soften to a fork-crushable texture at any steaming time. Dice the recovered meat on the 15 mm checkerboard grid to 8-15 mm cubes: each cube must be larger than half a 15 mm cell (≥8 mm) and must not exceed one full cell (≤15 mm). Pick out any fines below 8 mm by hand. Do NOT blend. Do NOT sieve: a 4 mm mesh would destroy an L6 specimen and must never be used to size one. Do NOT add thickener, sauce, water, or any liquid. Record the actual meat yield (expect 180-200 g from a 300 g battered portion). Steam the cubes in a single layer in a steamer basket over 500 ml briskly boiling water for 8 min, then check every 60 s: a cube must crush under thumbnail pressure and not spring back — target window 8-10 min. Plate 100 g of steamed cubes spread in a single layer, not mounded.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure (5.1; the only test that applies at L6), filmed as ONE unbroken take that carries both readings. (a) Softness: place one cube on the fork tines and press with the thumbnail until the nail blanches white; pass = the cube compresses or crushes under that pressure and does not spring back when the fork is lifted. (b) The L6 sizing check that 5.1 requires in the SAME take: hold two or three cubes against the 100 mm ruler; every piece must measure <= 15 mm on its longest edge and no piece may fall below 8 mm. Pass = (a) AND (b). A fork-press take with no ruler read in it is not a passed L6 test — re-film with the ruler in frame. Spoon tilt, fork drip and syringe flow do NOT apply at L6 — do not run them and do not record them as pass/fail. The 10 ml/10 s syringe-flow criterion is an L3 test only and is withdrawn from this card. There is no bench adjustment (thickener, extra liquid) that moves a solid specimen into or out of L6: the level is set by piece size (8-15 mm) and cooked softness.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface dull and matte, not glossy; no sauce film. Cubes separate, each between half a cell and one full 15 mm checkerboard cell (8-15 mm), no fines below 8 mm and nothing above 15 mm. Fork tines sink into a cube under pressure; the cube deforms and stays deformed (it may split or crush, but it must not mash to a paste). Colour matte mid-brown; no red sauce pooling on the plate; no free liquid on the plate.
specimens.shots: sweet_and_sour_pork_L6_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. sweet_and_sour_pork_L6_take2.jpg — top-down with checkerboard only. sweet_and_sour_pork_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. sweet_and_sour_pork_L6_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-pressure sequence (fork pressure only at L6). sweet_and_sour_pork_L6_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test film, full-frame: fork pressure then the 100 mm ruler sizing read in the same unbroken take (5.1 requires the L6 sizing check in the same take). Reseat ruler, wipe fork, swap checkerboard between each shot.
specimens.fail_modes: Achievability, stated plainly: takeaway sweet-and-sour pork is battered, deep-fried and sauce-coated. Stripping the batter recovers only part of the portion and the recovered meat is often already over-tender from the sauce braise, so the 8-15 mm soft-but-intact L6 window is narrow and batch-dependent. The procedure above is the closest reliable bench method; if it does not land in the window, reject the specimen and substitute slow-cooked or braised pork shoulder diced to 8-15 mm (reliably L6). Record the substitution on the data sheet. Hard batter crust left on the cubes — re-strip and re-dice; never blend. Cubes above 15 mm — re-dice against the checkerboard; never pass an L6 specimen through a sieve. Cubes below 8 mm after dicing — pick the fines out by hand; a 4 mm sieve cannot be used on an L6 specimen. Cubes do not crush under thumbnail pressure after 10 min steaming (still firm or crunchy from residual batter) — the specimen cannot be brought to L6; reject and substitute braised pork shoulder. Cubes mash to a paste under light pressure — below L6 (L5 or finer). Start from a firmer cut and steam for the 8 min minimum. Do not thicken, blend, or add liquid to recover the level. Sauce residue makes the pieces glossy and sticky so they cohere into a mass — remove all sauce, rinse 10 s, pat dry, re-plate in a single layer; if they still cohere, reject. Do not wash the meat to waterlogging.

specimens.prep: Bought form (BASE_FOOD_LIST BF52): takeaway sweet and sour pork — battered pork pieces in sweet-and-sour sauce, bought as a takeaway order. Allergens: gluten (wheat batter), egg (batter wash); confirm against the menu/pack label at portioning and record any extra in prep.notes.  Weigh 200 g of the takeaway onto the capture tray — pieces exactly as served, sauce included. Record the actual mass to 0.1 g. Do NOT blend, sieve, chop, dice, or add water or thickener: L7 is the food as bought and normally served. Pieces must keep their battered coating and glossy sauce. Wipe tray and fork before the take.
specimens.iddsi_test: 5.1 Fork pressure — ACTIVE, the only deciding test at L7. Place the largest piece on the tray and press the bowl of the fork down onto it with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass: the piece keeps its shape — it may dent or split along the batter, but it must NOT squash flat to a paste, smear, or extrude through the tine gaps, and it must still require real chewing. In the same take, hold the piece against the 100 mm ruler: every piece must measure >= 15 mm on its longest edge. Record both outcomes on camera.  5.2 Spoon tilt — skip: 5.2 applies at L3, L4 and L5 only. An L7 piece is a solid that must not pour, so a tilt take has no pass window at this level.  5.3 Fork drip — skip: 5.3 applies at L3 and L4 only. Nothing in an L7 specimen should drip through the tines, so there is nothing to measure.  5.4 Syringe flow — skip: required for every L3 specimen only; a solid battered piece cannot be drawn into a 10 ml syringe.
specimens.visual_qc: (1) Distinct battered pieces, individually visible — never a blended or stuck-together mass. (2) Glossy red-orange sauce clings to the pieces and does not pool as a separate free-liquid layer in the tray. (3) Every piece measures >= 15 mm on its longest edge against the 100 mm ruler. (4) Coating stays attached when a piece is nudged with the fork tines.
specimens.shots: 3 stills + 2 clips. sweet_and_sour_pork_L7_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 100 mm ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame, 3–4 pieces visible. sweet_and_sour_pork_L7_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only, full 200 g portion. sweet_and_sour_pork_L7_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into the largest piece, ruler in frame for the >= 15 mm read. sweet_and_sour_pork_L7_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s unbroken fork-pressure take. sweet_and_sour_pork_L7_take2.mp4 — 8–12 s full IDDSI test film, one unbroken take carrying both the fork pressure and the >= 15 mm ruler read, so the size evidence sits in the test film and not only in a still.
specimens.fail_modes: (1) Piece squashes flat, smears, or extrudes through the tines under the blanching press → softer than L7. Re-source a firmer piece from the same order or a fresh takeaway batch and re-shoot the full set. Do NOT chop, mash, blend or sieve it — that produces L6/L5/L4 material and moves the specimen away from L7. (2) Any piece under 15 mm on its longest edge → too small for L7 (that is L6 material): re-source a portion with whole pieces >= 15 mm and never capture the undersize pieces as L7. (3) Breading fallen off, pieces fused into one mass, or sauce pooled as free liquid → the portion is not the takeaway as served: re-source from a fresh order; no re-frying, re-coating, or added water or thickener. (4) A piece that resists the fork and demands real chewing is PASSING, not failing — never soften or process it to make the test easier.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g mapo tofu (sauce + curds) into blender. Blend 45 s on high, scraping halfway. Pass through 4 mm sieve; discard coarse solids (perian, scallion skins, charred bits). Stir in thickener at 0.8 g per 100 ml of puree as the calibration starting point; record actual grams on the bench sheet. If still too runny after 1 min rest, add 0.2 g increments up to 1.2 g/100 ml. Target flow leaves 8–10 ml in syringe at 10 s. Record thickener mass used.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: hold fork horizontally above bowl; liquid drips slowly through tines in a continuous but sluggish stream. Pass = steady slow drip, no pour, no drop sitting on the tine. Fork pressure: press fork tines flat into specimen until blanch shows; sample holds shape, does not return to liquid, fills tine spaces. Pass = clean impression, no separation. Spoon tilt: tilt a heaped spoon 30°; specimen slides slowly but does not run off. Pass = slow slump, stays on spoon. IDDSI flow test: fill 10 ml syringe, release 10 s; pass = 8–10 ml remaining.
specimens.visual_qc: Matte, uniform rust-red surface; no oil pooling, no visible tofu cubes, no chili flake specks. Coats spoon back without dripping when lifted. Fork tines leave a clean, defined track when dragged.
specimens.shots: mapo_tofu_L3_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, ruler end at specimen edge. mapo_tofu_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard filling frame, specimen centred. mapo_tofu_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines embedded, blanch visible. mapo_tofu_L3_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, single take, no cuts. mapo_tofu_L3_take5.mp4 — IDDSI flow test, timer visible, 10 s mark captured.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin (<8 ml remaining): drip runs off spoon; sieve did not remove solids — re-sieve, add 0.2 g thickener per 100 ml, retest. Too thick (>10 ml remaining): mass sits on fork, breaks instead of flowing — thin with 10 ml hot water per 100 g, re-blend 15 s, retest. Grainy / specks visible: blender underworked or sieve skipped — re-blend full 45 s and re-sieve before re-thickening.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g of mapo tofu (sauce and curds together) into the blender jar. Add 40 ml of water. Blend on high for 45-60 seconds until completely smooth. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any residue retained. Return the sieved puree to the blender. Add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml of puree (this is the calibration starting point; record the actual grams used). Blend 15 seconds to incorporate. Let stand 2 minutes. Re-weigh and record final specimen mass.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: lift a forkful; the puree must sit in a clear mound above the tines with no drip falling in 5 seconds. Fork pressure test: press the fork prongs into the specimen on a flat plate; the puree should yield and leave a clear indentation without running back to fill it. Spoon tilt test: a spoonful must hold its shape when the spoon is tilted to 45 degrees; no flow over the edge. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is glossy and uniform with no visible oil pools or tofu flecks. Color is even brick-red throughout with no white streaks. A forkful holds a soft peak that slumps only slightly; no liquid separates at the edge of the mound.
specimens.shots: Still 1: mapo_tofu_L4_take1.jpg, 45-degree hero shot, ruler and checkerboard in frame beside the specimen plate. Still 2: mapo_tofu_L4_take1.jpg, top-down with checkerboard centered under a forkful. Still 3: mapo_tofu_L4_take1.jpg, fork-press close-up at mid-compression. Clip 1: mapo_tofu_L4_take1.mp4, 8-12 seconds, fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. Clip 2: mapo_tofu_L4_take1.mp4, IDDSI test film showing all three tests.
specimens.fail_modes: Puree is too thin and flows through fork tines: add thickener in 0.5 g per 100 ml increments and retest. Visible oil or thin liquid pools on the surface: re-blend with an extra 15 seconds and sieve again. Grainy texture from unblended tofu curds: re-blend 30 seconds and re-sieve. Any failure means re-make from the 250 g starting weight; do not patch.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g chilled mapo tofu into the blender. Pulse 6 s, scrape, pulse 4 s — stop while soft tofu chunks remain visible. Do not fully purée; the per-level note requires visible particles. Press the mash through a 4 mm sieve using the back of a fork, discarding residue retained on the mesh. The passing mass should weigh 150–170 g; record the actual. The natural oil-chilli sauce released by the tofu provides moisture — do NOT add water or thin liquid. No thickener required at L5. Confirm particle size by visual check against the 100 mm ruler: every lump must sit inside a 4 mm window.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press the fork tines into the specimen until the thumbnail blanches white. The specimen must squash, change shape, and not spring back. Spoon-tilt test: lift 4 ml on a spoon; tilt 45°; the mass must hold together and slide as one piece, not flow or drip. Fork-drip test: lift forkful 50 mm above plate; the specimen must sit cohesive on the tines with no drip. If any of the three fails, re-mash and re-sieve.
specimens.visual_qc: Mash holds a fork-pressed ridge without collapsing. Surface shows 2–3 mm tofu flecks evenly coated in red oil sauce, glossy not pooling. No free red oil pooling around the mound on the plate.
specimens.shots: mapo_tofu_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. mapo_tofu_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. mapo_tofu_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines loaded. mapo_tofu_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press + spoon-tilt sequence. mapo_tofu_L5_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, no cuts.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-blended purée with zero particles — re-add 20 g chopped firm tofu, stir. Free red oil pooling on the plate — drain 30 s on the sieve, re-test. Specimen springs back under fork pressure — pulse 2 s more, re-sieve.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g takeaway mapo tofu (sauce + curds). Drain in a fine colander for 10 min; retain the sauce and record its mass. Do not blend at any point and do not press the curds through a fine mesh — a 4 mm mesh cannot enforce a 15 mm limit, and passing everything through it leaves a loose ≤4 mm saucy mass that is L5 at best. Cut the drained curds to 10–15 mm cubes, target 12 mm ± 2 mm, against the 100 mm ruler; discard firm tofu skin, whole chili solids and Sichuan peppercorn. Gauge for oversize only: pass the cubes over a 15 mm sieve and re-cut anything retained until nothing is held back. Simmer the retained sauce for 60 s until no free oil separates and it coats the back of a spoon; discard the separated oil. Toss the curds with no more than 15 ml of the reduced sauce per 100 g of curds — the plate must show no separate runny liquid pooling. Do not add thickener — this is L6, not L3. Do not add water. Record the final plate mass (target 150–170 g) on the scale for the log.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test — the only IDDSI test that applies at L6: press the fork tines onto a single piece until your thumbnail blanches white. The piece must squash, change shape, and not spring back when the fork is removed. Size confirmation in the same take on the 100 mm ruler: every piece must measure 10–15 mm on its longest edge. Spoon-tilt and fork-drip tests are not used at L6 and must not be run or recorded as level evidence.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a soft, irregular cube roughly 10–15 mm, surface glossy with chili oil, edges rounded not ragged. On the plate: separate pieces sitting in a light sauce film, no runny liquid pooling separately and no free oil. No crumbling to mash when the pieces are lifted.
specimens.shots: mapo_tofu_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame. mapo_tofu_L6_take2.jpg — top-down with checkerboard. mapo_tofu_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines depressing the piece. mapo_tofu_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then size check against the 100 mm ruler. mapo_tofu_L6_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film showing the fork-pressure test and size check.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces exceed 15 mm after cutting → re-cut smaller and re-gauge on the 15 mm sieve. Pieces below 10 mm, or the batch crumbles to mash when lifted → the curd is too fragile for L6; this batch cannot be produced at L6 by bench method, and the closest achievable is L5 (fork-mashable, ~4 mm) — cut to 4 mm, re-test, and file as L5 rather than filing an L6 card. Free liquid pools on the plate → drain longer, reduce the sauce a further 30 s, and re-toss with less sauce; do NOT re-blend and do NOT add water. Too stiff to squash under fork pressure → the curd is overcooked or fridge-firm; rest 5 min at room temperature, and if it still will not squash, add 10 ml of the reduced sauce and toss — do not blend, and do not add water.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of mapo tofu straight from the takeaway or chilled pack onto the digital scale. Record the actual mass. Do NOT blend. Do NOT sieve. Do NOT add thickener or water. Transfer the whole contents, sauce and all, into the capture dish. The specimen is whole food as normally served; reference specimen.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the four tines flat onto the specimen with normal thumb pressure. The food must NOT fully flow through the tine gaps and must NOT change from its original shape into a thinner liquid; the mass should compress but hold. Spoon tilt: rest a spoonful on the spoon, then tilt until the spoon is nearly vertical; the specimen must sit on the spoon without sliding off or dripping continuously. Fork drip: lift the fork from the dish; the specimen must not drip in a continuous stream through the tines. All three must pass for L7 Regular.
specimens.visual_qc: Coarse visible tofu cubes roughly 10-20 mm, distinct mince particles, glossy red-brown oil-slick sauce clinging to solids rather than pooling free, no watery layer separating from the solids on the dish.
specimens.shots: mapo_tofu_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. mapo_tofu_L7_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. mapo_tofu_L7_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. mapo_tofu_L7_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. mapo_tofu_L7_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, fork drip then spoon tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Free oil pooling across the dish bottom, indicating the solids have released grease and the mass behaves as a thin layer — fail; remix gently, do not add thickener, retest. Visible clear watery liquid separating from the sauce — fail; re-plate from fresh pack. Specimen flows fully through fork tines under light pressure — fail; the pack is genuinely L6 or below, re-record the level rather than attempting to repair the specimen.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g fresh minced pork + 30 g salted-egg yolk together. Add 100 ml room-temperature water. Blend 45–60 s until smooth paste with no fibres. Press through the 4 mm sieve; discard residue. Stir in thickener at 1.5 g per 100 ml of sieved puree as the calibration starting point. Whisk 30 s, rest 60 s, re-whisk. Record actual thickener grams on the card. If sieve clogs with fibrous pork, stop: the per-level note "blend-thin" cannot be achieved, re-blend with an extra 20 ml water.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: 4–6 slow drips per 10 s from fork tines, no continuous stream. Spoon tilt: flows as a single ribbon that levels in 1–2 s when spoon is tilted to 45°. Fork pressure: mound holds shape when fork pressed, then collapses and spreads under thumb. Syringe flow: draw 10 ml into the IDDSI syringe, release; 8–10 ml remains after 10 s (must fall within 8–10 ml band for L3).
specimens.visual_qc: Smooth, glossy, pale-orange paste with no visible pork fibre or yolk lumps. Coats the spoon back in a thin even film. Mound from the fork press slowly relaxes to a flat puddle within 2 s.
specimens.shots: Capture: (a) saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L3_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame; (b) saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L3_take2.jpg — top-down with checkerboard; (c) saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. Clip (d) saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L3_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt. Clip (e) saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L3_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI 10 ml syringe test, timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: (1) Syringe retains <8 ml → too thin; add 0.2 g thickener, rest, retest. (2) Syringe retains >10 ml or fork drip stops → too thick; whisk in 10 ml water, retest. (3) Visible fibres or yolk chunks breaking the 4 mm sieve → re-blend 20 s with 15 ml extra water, re-sieve. More than one failed retest → discard batch, re-weigh ingredients.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g fresh minced pork and 1 salted-egg yolk (≈20 g) on the digital scale — 170 g solids. Steam 12 min until just cooked; cool to ≤40 °C. Load cooked patty into the consumer blender, add 80 ml water; blend 45 s, scrape down, blend 15 s until smooth. L4 is lump-free, so the 4 mm sieve is the sizing step here: pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard residue. Water is the only thickness control and 80 ml is the L4 set point — do not add extra water on the first pass. Specimen target 230–250 g (170 g solids + 80 ml water, less sieve loss); a yield under 220 g means the batch lost too much in the sieve, re-make.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: mound on the upturned fork must sit above the tines for ≥10 s with no drip. Fork pressure: pressing the fork tines into the specimen must leave the tine prints clearly visible and the surface must not bounce back liquid. Spoon tilt: a heaped teaspoon must hold its shape when the spoon is tilted 45°, no flow off the edge. All three pass = L4 confirmed. No syringe flow test at L4.
specimens.visual_qc: On the spoon: matte, uniform pale-yellow with no pink pork flecks and no oily pooling. On the fork: sits as a single cohesive lump between/above tines, not as separate streaks. Surface after fork press: clean tine imprints, no glossy liquid return.
specimens.shots: saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + checkerboard in frame. saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press. saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L4_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press + spoon-tilt, continuous. saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L4_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, all three sub-tests labelled.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen flows through the fork tines (too thin) → THICKEN. Re-blending and re-sieving do not thicken anything; re-make with 60 ml water instead of 80 ml, or fold in 30 g more cooked pork mince, then blend 45 s, sieve, re-test. Do not add thickener to rescue a thin batch. Specimen will not leave the spoon, cracks at the edge, or takes no tine prints (too thick) → THIN: add 10 ml water at a time, up to 100 ml total, re-blend 20 s, re-sieve, re-test — never thin past the spoon-tilt pass, or the specimen becomes L3. Oily yolk separates as a thin layer (fat break) → discard batch; reboil egg, blend hotter mass, re-test. Lumpy with visible pork fibre → sieve was skipped or under-blended; re-sieve, re-shoot. Two consecutive fails = re-make from 150 g pork.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g fresh steamed minced pork with its juices onto the plate. Using a fork, mash and chop the patty against the plate until the meat breaks down and any chunks are ≤4 mm; pull and fold repeatedly for 60-90 seconds. Do not blend — blending will emulsify the fats and the fork-pressure signature will read as L6, not L5. Do not sieve the meat itself; press the released juices back in. No thickener is added — L5 does not require it, and adding thickener will push the specimen toward L4. No extra water or liquid is added. If the patty has a visible intact salted-egg yolk portion, chop that separately to ≤4 mm and fold back in; if the yolk resists mashing (rubbery), record "yolk resists ≤4 mm" and stop — the per-level note demands ≤4 mm with juices, and an unbreakable chunk disqualifies the specimen.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork tines fully into the specimen on the plate; the specimen must squash, change shape, and not spring back when the fork is removed. Spoon tilt: tilt a teaspoon of specimen 30 degrees; the mass must hold together and not slide, pour, or drip. Fork drip: lift a forkful 5 cm above the plate; no thin liquid must run through or drip off the tines. All three must pass. The 10 ml/10 s syringe flow test does not apply to L5.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a cohesive lump that holds its shape between tines, glossy surface from the juices, no free liquid pooling below. On the spoon: a mound that does not level itself when tilted. On the plate: meat granules clearly visible at ≤4 mm, no intact yolk dome, no thin broth ring around the patty.
specimens.shots: saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L5_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen centered on white plate. saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L5_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard filling frame, specimen inside the 100 mm scale. saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L5_take1_fork.jpg — fork-press close-up, fork mid-press into specimen, tines visible. saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L5_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s clip, fork-press followed immediately by spoon-tilt, continuous take. saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L5_take1_test.mp4 — 20-30 s IDDSI test film: fork pressure, spoon tilt, fork drip, in that order, one cut per test, on-screen text label "L5" only.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen reads L6 when fork-pressure leaves the patty holding its shape or springs back; re-mash with fork for another 30 seconds and re-test, max one re-make. Specimen reads L4 or L3 when juices separate and form a pourable thin liquid on the plate; drain excess juice, fold meat back, and re-test — do not add thickener. Specimen disqualified when yolk chunk remains >4 mm after two minutes of chopping; re-make from fresh pork and a softer yolk portion, otherwise abandon this food at L5 and flag.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g fresh minced pork and one salted egg (≈55 g) on the digital scale; separate yolk from white, mash the yolk with a fork, finely chop the white. Combine pork, yolk mash, chopped white, and 30 ml water; mix by hand until sticky. Shape into a flat patty ≈20 mm thick and steam 12 min until just cooked through (core 75 °C on a probe). Cool 5 min. Portion a 100 g specimen and crumble it by hand into pieces. Size by hand, not by sieve: every piece must measure 8–15 mm in its longest dimension. Check each piece against the 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler in the capture kit — re-cut any piece over 15 mm with the knife, and discard fines under 8 mm. Do NOT press the crumbles through a 4 mm sieve: a 4 mm screen caps every piece at 4 mm, which is Level 5 (minced & moist), and it can never enforce a 15 mm limit — after sieving, no 8–15 mm piece would exist to test. Do NOT blend. Do NOT add thickener; L6 needs no flow control. Record the mass of the sized specimen and the final yield in grams (target 90–100 g from the 100 g portion).
specimens.iddsi_test: Applicable at L6: fork pressure only (§5.1). Spoon tilt (§5.2) and fork drip (§5.3) are L3–L5 tests and must not be run, filmed, or recorded as pass/fail at L6. No syringe flow test above L3 (§5.4).  Fork-pressure test: place a representative 10–15 mm piece on the plate and press it with the back of the fork, normal thumb pressure, until the thumbnail blanches white; hold 5 s. Pass = the piece squashes flat and does not recover its shape when the pressure is released. Fail = the piece stays intact and springs back (too firm — undercooked), or the piece turns to paste with no 8 mm fragment left (too wet / over-worked).
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces on the fork should look moist and pale gold from the salted egg, with no pink pork showing, and should hold their crumbles without slumping when the fork is held level. Pieces should rest as separate crumbles, not a slurry, and a quick tap should not produce liquid pooling under them. Every piece in frame reads 8–15 mm against the ruler.
specimens.shots: - saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler left, checkerboard right. - saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L6_take2.jpg — top-down on checkerboard, pieces spread. - saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. - saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L6_take4.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork-press on a single piece, squash and recovery visible (L6 has no spoon-tilt step). - saltedegg_steamed_pork_p_L6_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film: fork-pressure test plus the 8–15 mm size check against the checkerboard, ≤45 s.
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces exceed 15 mm after crumbing — re-cut by hand with the knife and re-check against the 15 mm checkerboard; do NOT re-sieve (a 4 mm screen would take the specimen to Level 5). Pieces under 8 mm, or a slurry of fines — too small for L6: discard the fines and re-crumble from a fresh 100 g portion; sieving to recover them guarantees L5. Patty is too wet and pools liquid on the fork — drain on paper towel 30 s, re-weigh, re-film. Meat is undercooked and springs back under fork pressure — re-steam the intact patty 3 min, cool 5 min, re-crumble, re-test; do not steam the crumbled pieces, they collapse to a mash. If the crumb will not hold an 8–15 mm piece at all (too wet or too fine to size by hand), the batch cannot reach L6 as a hand-crumbled specimen — re-make from a fresh 100 g portion with 30 ml water and size by hand; do not sieve to force it. Two consecutive failures: re-make from a fresh 100 g portion.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g Yangzhou fried rice into blender bowl. Add 100 ml cool water. Blend 45 s on high, stopping to scrape once. Sieve through 4 mm mesh; discard retained solids. Return filtrate to blender, add 120 ml water, blend 10 s to homogenise. Weigh the slurry. Add thickener at 4 g per 100 ml of slurry as the calibration starting point; record actual mass used. Stir 30 s, rest 2 min, stir again 15 s. Re-weigh final specimen and record.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: tilt fork; slurry drips in slow, continuous dollops, not a stream. Spoon tilt: spoonful sits in a mound, slides off slowly when spoon tilted to 30 degrees. Fork pressure (no thumb): tines leave a clear, soft imprint but do not cut clean through. Syringe flow: fill 10 ml, release; 8-10 ml remains in the barrel after 10 s.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is glossy with no separated oil sheen. No visible rice grains, peas, or egg flecks. Coats the spoon back in an even, opaque layer that holds its shape for 2-3 s before sliding.
specimens.shots: yangzhou_fried_rice_L3_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen in white bowl. yangzhou_fried_rice_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred, 100 mm ruler along edge. yangzhou_fried_rice_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines half-submerged. yangzhou_fried_rice_L3_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous clip. yangzhou_fried_rice_L3_take2.mp4 — IDDSI syringe test, timer visible, full 10 s hold.
specimens.fail_modes: Syringe empties past 10 ml mark in under 10 s: too thin, add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml slurry, rest 2 min, retest. Syringe holds more than 10 ml: too thick, add 5 ml water per 100 ml slurry, reblend 5 s, retest. Visible grains or oil pooling after sieving: blend another 20 s and re-sieve; if grains persist, note and remake with longer initial blend.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g Yangzhou fried rice (confirm mixed-grain and ingredient distribution at purchase; record any large visible piece counts as outliers). Add 60–80 ml warm stock (start at 60 ml; add 10 ml increments if the blend stalls). Blend in the consumer blender on high for 45–60 s until a uniform coarse puree forms; scrape the wall, then blend a further 20 s. Pass through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard residue that will not pass and note the discard mass. Return the sieved puree to the blender and thicken to the L4 calibration starting point: add thickener at 1.5 g per 100 ml of puree, blend 15 s, rest 60 s, then re-test. Record the actual thickener mass used. Target final mass 200–220 g.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: lift a forkful 15 cm above the plate; the puree must sit in a mound above the tines and not drip continuously through. Fork pressure: press the fork tines into the mound; the surface must blanch clearly but the puree must not flow through the slots. Spoon tilt: a 5 ml spoonful on a tilted plate must hold its shape and not slide off in under 10 s. No separate thin liquid should pool around the mound.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform pale-tan colour with no visible whole rice grains, peas, egg flecks, or carrot shards. Smooth, slightly glossy surface with no weeping liquid at the edges of the mound. Coats the back of a spoon without running.

Still 3 — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines partly buried: yangzhou_fried_rice_L4_take3.jpg. Clip 1 — 8–12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt: yangzhou_fried_rice_L4_take1.mp4. Clip 2 — full IDDSI test film (drip, pressure, tilt) in one continuous take: yangzhou_fried_rice_L4_take2.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Grainy texture with visible rice or vegetable fragments: re-blend 20 s and re-sieve; if residue exceeds 15% of input, re-make from 150 g fresh. Weeping liquid pooling around the mound: too thin — add thickener in 0.5 g per 100 ml increments, rest 60 s, retest. Slides off the tilted spoon or flows through fork tines: over-thickened or under-thickened — discard and re-make; partial dilution will not rescue L4 texture.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g of takeaway Yangzhou fried rice; discard large garnishes. Pulse in consumer blender 8–10 s — short bursts to chop, not purée. Tip onto the 4 mm sieve; press and discard what does not pass, noting retained mass. Return the passing portion to a bowl, drizzle 25–30 ml warm stock, and mash with a fork until evenly moist and sticky. Fork-mash 30–40 s, scraping the bowl, until no piece exceeds 4 mm. If the mix feels loose, sprinkle 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml of added stock, stir, rest 60 s, re-test. Record the final grams of thickener used per 100 ml. Target: cohesive mince that holds a fork-load but releases a thin sheen when pressed — no pooling liquid in the bowl.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork tines flat onto a heaped spoonful until the thumbnail blanches; the mass must squash and stay squashed, no recovery. Spoon tilt: a level spoonful must slide off a tilted spoon only with a deliberate shake; it must not run. Fork drip: hold a loaded fork over an empty bowl — no drips fall within 10 s. A separate liquid pool must not form around the mound.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a cohesive lump, glints of moisture, no whole grains, peas, or shrimp fragments visible above ~4 mm. On the spoon: mound holds its peak 1–2 s before slumping, glossy not runny. Bowl shows a moist film, never a puddle.
specimens.shots: yangzhou_fried_rice_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. yangzhou_fried_rice_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. yangzhou_fried_rice_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, tines mid-press. yangzhou_fried_rice_L5_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. yangzhou_fried_rice_L5_take2.mp4 — IDDSI test sequence: fork pressure, spoon tilt, fork drip.
specimens.fail_modes: Too wet — stock pools; remedy: fold in 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, rest, retest. Too dry / crumbly — particles won't cohere and fall through fork drip test; remedy: add 5 ml stock, re-mash. Visible pieces above 4 mm after mashing — sieve was skipped or blender under-pulsed; re-pulse 3 s and re-sieve. Any failure: discard, remake from 200 g, note the deviation.

specimens.prep: L6 requires pieces 8-15 mm that are soft and squashable, and takeaway fried-rice grains are commonly 5-8 mm, which is L5 territory — so the as-bought container cannot be captured as L6 and the pieces must be built to size on the bench. Weigh 250 g Yangzhou fried rice on the scale. Do NOT blend and do NOT sieve: sieving would force the specimen below the 15 mm limit and destroy the piece structure L6 depends on. Spread the rice on a clean board and, with a knife, cut any piece larger than 15 mm down to size. Working in 30 g portions, press the rice into a 10 mm thick slab with the back of an oiled spoon, keeping rice, egg and diced vegetable in the bought proportions, then cut the slab into 10 mm squares so that every piece measures 8-15 mm in its longest dimension. Verify each piece against the 100 mm ruler and the 15 mm checkerboard: a piece clearly under 8 mm is an L5 particle and must be re-cut or discarded before plating. Scoop a 30 g portion (8-10 pieces) onto the plate. Do not add water or thickener. Record the actual piece size range in mm and the portion mass in grams on the capture sheet.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test (the required test at L6): press the fork tines firmly onto a piece until the thumbnail blanches white; the piece must squash, change shape, and not recover. Pass: the tines sink and the imprint stays. Size check, part of the L6 pass: every piece measures 8-15 mm in its longest dimension against the 100 mm ruler. No spoon-tilt test at L6: spoon-tilt applies at L3, L4 and L5 only. No fork-drip test at L6: fork-drip applies at L3 and L4 only. Neither may be used to accept or reject an L6 specimen, and the specimen must not be passed or failed on how it flows off a spoon.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: a mixed mound of cut 8-15 mm pieces in which the rice grains are clumped into the pieces, egg is soft yellow, and vegetables appear as small colour specks inside the pieces; every piece measures 8-15 mm on the ruler. On the spoon: the pieces sit in a pile with a small amount of oil sheen only, no loose liquid pool. Pieces should not appear glossy-wet, nor separated, dry and crumbly.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame at plate edge, pieces measured against the ruler. Still 2: top-down with checkerboard centred and the ruler laid alongside the pieces. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail blanching visible, piece squashing between the tines. Clip 1: 8-12 s of fork-press on two separate pieces in one continuous take. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film for L6 — fork pressure plus size verification against the ruler, with narration. Name files yangzhou_fried_rice_L6_take1.jpg and yangzhou_fried_rice_L6_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: (a) Pieces measure under 8 mm after cutting, i.e. L5 territory — do not capture; re-cut the portion to 8-15 mm and re-verify against the ruler. If the rice is too crumbly to hold an 8 mm piece together, the batch cannot reach L6 by this bench method: record it as L5 and re-shoot against a card re-levelled to L5 rather than labelling it L6. (b) Pieces over 15 mm, or hard grains and chewy meat that will not squash under thumbnail pressure — cut the oversized pieces down to 8-15 mm and discard any piece still hard or chewy; if more than about 10% of the batch resists thumbnail pressure, re-make with a fresh 250 g portion cooked softer (freshly cooked rice, longer steam, no dried-out reheated rice). (c) Excess oil pooling or watery sauce — too wet; drain on absorbent paper for 60 s and re-test. (d) Dry, crumbly pieces that crumble instead of squashing — too dry; discard the plated portion and re-make with freshly cooked rice, folding 5 ml water per 100 g into the rice before the slab is pressed. Do not re-wet the portion already on the plate.

specimens.prep: Take a 150 g portion of the takeaway Yangzhou fried rice as bought. Do not blend. Do not sieve. Do not add water or thickener — L7 is the food as normally served. Weigh the portion on the digital scale and record the actual mass. Transfer the specimen to a white plate in the A4 capture kit. Confirm the mix contains visible rice grains, egg, and vegetable/protein pieces typical of Yangzhou fried rice.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork onto the specimen until the tines blanch; the specimen must hold its shape with no separation of liquid and no flow through the gaps. Fork drip: lift the fork; no drip or runny residue falls from the tines — the fork lifts cleanly. Spoon tilt: scoop a portion and tilt the spoon; the specimen must stay on the spoon without sliding off. All three must pass. No syringe flow test applies at L7.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: distinct individual rice grains and ingredient pieces remain visible and separate, not mashed together. On the spoon: the portion holds a defined mound when tilted, with a moist but not glossy or pooling surface. Grains retain their shape and colour.
specimens.shots: 1. yangzhou_fried_rice_L7_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. 2. yangzhou_fried_rice_L7_take1_top.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. 3. yangzhou_fried_rice_L7_take1_fork.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press. Clip 1: yangzhou_fried_rice_L7_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. Clip 2: IDDSI test film, same filename.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen is wet enough that oil or sauce pools on the plate or drips from the fork — fails fork drip. Grains are overcooked and collapse to a paste under fork pressure — fails fork pressure. Pieces slide off the tilted spoon — fails spoon tilt. If any test fails, remake with a drier portion from the container and retest.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g cooked wontons plus 200 ml of their cooking liquid into the blender jar. Blend on high for 30 s, scraping down once, then blend a further 15 s. Press the puree through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard the firmer residue (skins, filling fibre). Measure the sieved volume. Add thickener at 3.0 g per 100 ml of puree as the calibration starting point; whisk in with a fork, rest 60 s, stir, re-measure volume. Top up with hot water 10 ml at a time only if the puree is thicker than the flow-test target. Record the actual grams of thickener used and the final volume on the card.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: puree should drip in slow, continuous, thread-like strands through the tines, not run as a thin stream and not sit in a mound. Spoon tilt: a 5 ml scoop on the spoon should hold its shape and only flow off when the spoon is tilted nearly vertical. Fork pressure: pressing the fork tines into 5 ml on a flat plate leaves a clear imprint with the puree slowly filling the depression; it does not level instantly. IDDSI flow test: fill the syringe to the 10 ml mark, release, after 10 s read the remaining volume — pass = 8–10 ml remaining in the syringe.
specimens.visual_qc: Smooth, glossy, even beige surface and no visible wonton skin or filling flecks after sieving. Coats the spoon back without running. Drips from the fork in slow ribbons, not drops, not a stream.
specimens.shots: wonton_soup_small_wonton_L3_take1.jpg hero 45° with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; wonton_soup_small_wonton_L3_take1.jpg top-down checkerboard only; wonton_soup_small_wonton_L3_take1.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press. wonton_soup_small_wonton_L3_take1.mp4 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt; wonton_soup_small_wonton_L3_take1.mp4 full IDDSI syringe flow test, timer visible.
specimens.fail_modes: Too runny (syringe < 8 ml, drips as stream): whisk in extra thickener 0.5 g per 100 ml and re-test. Too stiff (syringe > 10 ml, sits in mound, fork leaves no drip): thin with 5–10 ml hot water and re-test. Lumpy with skin or filling flecks visible: re-blend 15 s and pass through the 4 mm sieve again before re-thickening.

specimens.prep: - Cook: bring **500 ml** water to a brisk boil, add **200 g** frozen small wontons, simmer **4–5 min** until they float and the wrapper is fully tender. Lift out, drain **30 s**, and keep **100 ml** of the cooking broth. (With takeaway, weigh **200 g** cooked wontons and keep **100 ml** of their broth.) - Blend: the **200 g** cooked wontons and **100 ml** reserved broth into the blender. Blend on high **45 s**, scrape the walls down once, blend **20 s** more (**65 s** total). Start on low and vent the lid if the broth is still hot. - Sieve: press the blend through the **4 mm sieve** with the back of a spoon and discard what stays on the mesh (wonton-skin fragments and filling fibre). At L4 the sieve is the fibre/skin remover (equipment list item 3) and L4 is a lump-free level, so **no un-sieved specimen is tested**. Record the retained mass. - Weigh the sieved purée: target **260–300 g** (record actual). Let it stand until it is **20–40 °C** before testing. - Thicken — required, not optional: broth-thinned wonton purée will not hold a shape on its own. Whisk in thickener at the calibration starting point of **1.5 g gum-based per 100 ml** of purée (if only a starch-based thickener is stocked, start at **6.0 g per 100 ml**). Whisk **20 s**, rest **60 s**, stir **10 s**. Record the actual grams used in `prep.thickener_g`. - Titrate against section 2 in **0.5 g (gum) or 1.0 g (starch) per 100 ml** steps, up to a ceiling of **4.0 g gum / 12.0 g starch per 100 ml**.
specimens.iddsi_test: - Fork pressure (5.1): press the fork tines flat into the purée on the tray until the thumbnail blanches white, hold **5 s**, lift. **Pass** = a clear impression remains, the surface does not rebound, and the purée does not squeeze through the tine gaps. - Spoon tilt (5.2, L4 criterion): scoop a full spoon, hold it level, then tilt to **90°**. **Pass** = the purée holds its shape on the spoon and slides off as one cohesive mass with little residue left behind, and no separate thin liquid separates out. - Fork drip (5.3, L4 criterion): scoop with the fork and hold it over the tray. **Pass** = the sample sits in a mound above the tines and does **not** flow through them. - Separation check (QC rule 4): no thin broth may pool on the spoon or the tray at any point before the clip ends; any pooling fails the specimen at L4. - Syringe flow: **skip** — 5.4 is required on every L3 only. Running the 10 ml / 10 s flow test here would invite thickening toward the L3 window and drop the specimen below L4, so it is not run and is not recorded.
specimens.visual_qc: - Smooth, glossy, pale-beige purée with no visible wonton-skin fragments, no filling flecks and no lumps. - Sits in a defined peak above the fork tines and above the spoon rim; does not spread across the tray. - No free broth at the tray edge or in the spoon well.

specimens.fail_modes: - Purée flows off the tilted spoon, runs through the fork tines, or thin broth separates and pools (**too thin**): whisk in **0.5 g gum (or 1.0 g starch) per 100 ml** of purée, rest 60 s, re-stir 10 s, re-test. This moves the specimen toward L4. - Purée cracks or tears under the fork and will not spread (**too stiff** for a level that must hold a soft shape): thin with **10 ml** reserved broth per 100 ml of purée, re-blend **20 s**, re-test. - Visible skin fragments or filling flecks after sieving: re-blend **20 s** and re-sieve through the 4 mm sieve; record the retained mass. If lumps persist, this batch cannot be made lump-free — log the attempt, mark the row FAIL, and re-cook a fresh 200 g portion. - Free broth pooling under the mound: re-blend **20 s** to re-incorporate, then thicken in the steps above. Do not add water to a separated specimen — that moves it further from L4. - Achievability, stated plainly: the reliable route to L4 is to blend the **whole** wonton (wrapper and filling) with its broth and then sieve out the skins. Blending the filling alone leaves a crumbly mass that will not hold a shape, and the broth on its own will never reach L4 — the thickener is required, not optional.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g cooked wonton + broth as the starting portion. Separate wontons from broth. Chop wontons with a fork until pieces measure ≤4 mm on the ruler. If pieces cling or ball, pulse in the consumer blender 2–3 s and re-check particle size against the 4 mm sieve. Sieve chopped mass through the 4 mm sieve; reject any retained lumps. Return the sieved mince to the broth. Mash the combined mass thoroughly with the fork until no separate thin liquid pools on the plate; broth coats the mince uniformly. Do not add thickener unless spoon tilt or fork drip shows free liquid; if free liquid appears, add thickener at 1 g/100 ml of free liquid as the calibration starting point and record the actual mass used. Per-level note: chop ≤4 mm with broth is achievable with fork + brief blender pulse; no sieving failures expected.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the specimen until thumbnail blanches; the specimen must squash and not recover when fork is lifted. Spoon tilt: a heaped teaspoon tilted to 90° must hold its shape with no flow off the spoon. Fork drip: lifting fork at 20 cm above the plate, no more than a slow drip falls in 10 s; continuous pour = fail.
specimens.visual_qc: Mince visible as distinct ≤4 mm flecks across the spoon surface. Broth coats particles with a glossy sheen, no pooled clear liquid. Specimen mounds on the fork and holds its shape as a single cohesive mass, not a slurry.
specimens.shots: Capture three stills and two clips. Stills: 45-degree hero of the specimen on the plate with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; top-down on the checkerboard showing particle distribution; fork-press close-up mid-press with tines clearly indenting the mass. Clips: 8–12 s continuous showing fork-press then spoon-tilt in one take; 8–12 s IDDSI test film covering fork drip, fork pressure, and spoon tilt. Files: wonton_soup_small_wonton_L5_take1.jpg for stills; wonton_soup_small_wonton_L5_take1.mp4 for clips.
specimens.fail_modes: Particles exceed 4 mm after chopping; re-pulse blender and re-sieve. Thin broth separates and pools on the plate; add thickener 1 g/100 ml increments, remix, retest. Specimen flows off spoon at tilt or drips continuously from fork; re-mash longer and re-add thickener before re-shooting. Two consecutive fails on any single criterion = re-cook a fresh 250 g portion.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g cooked small wontons. Cut each wonton in half with kitchen shears so every piece is ≤15 mm; verify by holding a piece against the 15 mm checkerboard squares. Drain cut pieces in a sieve, reserving 60 ml of the cooking liquid for serving. Place cut pieces on a plate; do not blend — blending destroys the bite-sized pieces required at L6. If a specimen feels gummy or sticky on the fork, dust lightly with 0.5 g thickener per 100 g of pieces and re-test. Per the per-level note: serve the cut pieces drained with a small spoonful (≈15 ml) of reserved broth in a separate cup on the side — never pool the broth over the pieces.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press a piece with the underside of a fork until thumbnail blanches white; the piece must squash, change shape, and not spring back. Fork-drip test (on the broth only): a fork lifted from the broth should drip steadily through the prongs, not run in a continuous pour. Spoon-tilt test on a drained piece: a spoonful must hold its shape on a tilted spoon without sliding off. All three must pass; one fail means re-make.
specimens.visual_qc: Pieces on the fork show a clean cut edge with visible filling, mat (not glossy) surface from the dusting if used, and distinct 10–15 mm outlines against the checkerboard. Broth in the cup appears thin, pale, and free-running. No pooled liquid sits under the pieces on the plate.
specimens.shots: wonton_soup_small_wonton_L6_take1.jpg hero 45° with ruler + checkerboard; wonton_soup_small_wonton_L6_take2.jpg top-down on checkerboard; wonton_soup_small_wonton_L6_take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press. Clips: wonton_soup_small_wonton_L6_take4.mp4 (8–12 s fork-press + spoon-tilt) and wonton_soup_small_wonton_L6_take5.mp4 (IDDSI test film, full sequence).
specimens.fail_modes: Pieces >15 mm after cutting: recut and re-measure against checkerboard. Piece springs back under fork (skin too elastic): steam 1 min then retest; if still elastic, re-make with longer simmer. Pieces collapse to paste under fork (overcooked, no structure): re-make with shorter cook and retest. Broth too thick (coats spoon like L4): thin with reserved hot water and retest drip.

specimens.prep: Cook the wonton soup per pack instructions — boil 500 ml water, add 200 g frozen wontons, simmer 4-5 min until floating, add seasoning/soup sachet. Serve one portion: ladle 250-300 g total (broth + wontons) into the capture bowl. Do NOT blend, sieve, or thicken. The per-level note says "wontons in soup as served" — this IS the whole-food reference specimen. Place 4-5 wontons in broth, keeping skin intact. Record actual served mass on the scale log.
specimens.iddsi_test: - Fork pressure test: press fork tines into one wonton with normal thumb pressure. Wonton skin should resist, compress slightly, then spring back. Pass = no full squish-through, shape recovers when fork lifts. Soup itself is liquid — that is expected at L7; the L7 claim applies to the wonton solids. - Spoon tilt test: scoop one wonton plus 5 ml broth, tilt spoon at 90 degrees. Wonton stays on spoon; broth pours. Pass = solid component does not slide off. - Fork drip test: lift fork with broth only. Broth drips continuously in a thin stream. Pass = continuous drip confirms liquid soup component, consistent with L7 food-in-liquid.
specimens.visual_qc: - Wonton skin smooth and intact, no tears or starch bloom. - Broth clear to lightly cloudy, golden, no lumps. - Wontons hold a rounded dumpling shape, not collapsed or split.

specimens.fail_modes: - Wontons split during cooking → solids no longer hold shape; re-make with shorter simmer. - Skin ruptures under fork thumb pressure → overcooked; re-make and reduce cook time by 1 min. - Broth over-reduced and syrupy instead of fluid → re-make with full water volume; L7 requires the liquid component to actually drip.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g braised beef brisket noodles into blender cup. Add 80 ml warm water and 6.0 g thickener (calibration starting point — record the actual mass used). Blend on high for 45 s, stopping to scrape down once. Add another 40 ml warm water and 2.0 g thickener; blend 30 s. Push through a 4 mm sieve with the back of a spoon; discard any fibres or noodle clumps that will not pass (per-level note: blend-thin — sieving is required because brisket sinew and noodle skins will not break down fully). Stir, rest 2 min. If the slurry pours in a slow ribbon and drips in 1-2 drops per second off the fork tines, proceed; if it runs or sits in a lump, adjust in 1.0 g thickener steps up to a maximum of 12.0 g total before re-blending 15 s.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: hold fork vertically over plate — slurry drips in slow, individual drops through the tines, not a stream. Fork pressure: press fork tines into 15 mm of slurry on a spoon — tines leave a clear outline that does not fill back in; slurry does not hold the fork up. Spoon tilt: tilt a heaped spoon 30° — slurry flows off slowly as one mass, not a fast pour and not a solid lump. Syringe flow (10 ml / 10 s): draw 10 ml, release, 8-10 ml remaining at 10 s — that is the pass band; under 6 ml = too thin, over 11 ml = too thick.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform brown, no visible noodle strands, no meat shreds, no skin pieces. Coats the back of the spoon in an even, glossy film. Flows off the spoon as a slow continuous ribbon that breaks after 1-2 cm.
specimens.shots: braised_beef_brisket_noo_L3_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen on white plate. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L3_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard under, spoon of slurry centred. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L3_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, slurry visible between tines. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L3_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, single take. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L3_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI syringe test: load, t=0 release, hold, t=10 s reading.
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin (<6 ml remaining) — runoff, no coating on spoon: whisk in 1.0 g thickener, rest 1 min, re-test. Too thick (>11 ml remaining), lumpy, catches on sieve: whisk in 10 ml warm water, blend 15 s, re-test. Visible solids after sieving — do not pick them out; re-blend 20 s with extra 20 ml water, re-sieve; max one re-make, then re-weigh and start fresh.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g braised beef brisket noodles including broth and meat into the blender cup. Blend on high for 90 seconds. Stop, scrape down the sides with a fork, blend 30 seconds more. Press a small amount through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; if strands of noodle or fibre remain, blend 20 seconds further and re-sieve. The broth alone must not pass through as separate thin liquid — if it does, re-absorb by blending a further 10 seconds. Do NOT add gum thickener at L4 unless the specimen flows through the fork tines during the drip test; if it does, add thickener at 1 g per 100 ml of specimen, re-blend 15 seconds, re-test, and record the actual grams used. No extra water or liquid.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip test: lift a forkful 5 cm above the specimen surface — it must sit in a soft mound on the tines, not drip, not flow. Fork pressure test: press the fork tines into the specimen until the tines blanch white; the surface should yield with a clear indentation that holds shape, then recovers when the fork is removed. Spoon tilt test: load a dessert spoon, tilt to 45 degrees; the specimen must hold its shape and not slide off in a steady stream. All three must pass.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is smooth and uniform, no visible noodle strands or meat fibre. Colour is even brown with no separated glossy liquid pooling at the edges. Mound on the fork sits above the tine gaps with a soft, glossy peak that does not slump.
specimens.shots: braised_beef_brisket_noo_L4_take1.jpg — 45-degree hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines visible. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L4_take4.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L4_take5.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, drip, pressure, tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Specimen runs through fork tines as a steady pour — too thin; re-make and add 1 g thickener per 100 ml, re-blend, re-test. Visible noodle strands or fibrous lumps on the sieve — blend 30 seconds more and re-sieve. Separate thin broth pools on top or around the mound — too much free liquid; re-blend 15 seconds to re-absorb before adding thickener.

specimens.prep: Weigh 350 g braised beef brisket noodles, separating 220 g solids (beef + noodles) from 130 g broth. Place solids in consumer blender; pulse 6-8 s until coarsely minced. Tip onto 4 mm sieve; press through with the back of a spoon, discard retained chunks. Return mince to broth, stir to combine. If the mixture pools thin liquid on standing after 30 s, stir in thickener at 0.5 g per 100 ml of mixture incrementally until the per-level note is satisfied. Final target: ~350 g specimen, particles ≤4 mm, moist, no separate thin liquid, mashable with a fork. Per-level note from the food list is achievable.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into 15 mm of specimen on a flat plate; specimen must squash and NOT recover its shape when fork is lifted — pass if it stays deformed. Spoon tilt: place 5 ml on a spoon and tilt to 45 degrees; specimen must hold shape and slide off slowly as a cohesive mass, not pour — pass if it does not run. Fork drip: lift forkful and hold 5 s above plate; must not drip continuous flow — pass if ≤2 drops fall.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: coarse mince with visible noodle and beef flecks, all pieces ≤4 mm, glossy with absorbed broth, no standing liquid in the well. On the spoon: one cohesive mound holding its shape, dull-moist sheen, no separate thin broth pooling underneath.
specimens.shots: braised_beef_brisket_noo_L5_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L5_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard centred. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L5_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L5_take1.mp4 — 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, one continuous take. braised_beef_brisket_noo_L5_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test sequence: fork drip, fork pressure, spoon tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: Visible chunks >4 mm after sieve — re-pulse 3 s and re-sieve. Thin broth separates and pools on the plate within 30 s — add 0.5 g thickener per 100 ml, rest 60 s, re-test. Specimen recovers shape under fork — too dry or over-thickened; stir in 10 ml warm broth and re-test.

specimens.prep: Weigh out 200 g of braised beef brisket noodles onto the capture tray. Using the fork, separate the noodles and brisket; cut noodles with the fork edge and dice brisket pieces so every dimension is ≤15 mm — discard any piece that exceeds 15 mm, do not blend and do not sieve (sieving would destroy the noodle form required for L6). No thickener, no added water. Specimen is taken as served from the takeaway container.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: place one diced brisket piece on a flat plate, press the fork tines flat until the thumbnail blanches white. Pass = piece squashes, does not recover its shape, and the fork edge does not fully cut through it. Spoon-tilt test (noodle strand): load a noodle strand on the spoon and tilt; the strand must sit cohesively and slide off in one motion, not flow, drip, or run. Fork-drip test: lift a forkful; little to no liquid drips through the tines before the fork-pressure test is performed. All three must pass to confirm L6.
specimens.visual_qc: — Noodle strands visibly cut to short lengths ≤15 mm; no long strands hanging off the fork. — Brisket dice uniform, roughly cube-shaped, no piece visibly larger than the 15 mm squares on the checkerboard beside the specimen. — Surface glistening but no pooled liquid on the tray.

Still 2 — top-down, specimen spread on tray with checkerboard: braised_beef_brisket_noo_L6_take2.jpg. Still 3 — fork-press close-up, fork mid-press with thumbnail white: braised_beef_brisket_noo_L6_take3.jpg. Clip 1 — 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence: braised_beef_brisket_noo_L6_take1.mp4. Clip 2 — full IDDSI test film including size check: braised_beef_brisket_noo_L6_take2.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Noodle strands left longer than 15 mm after cutting — re-cut, do not re-plate. Brisket piece resists the fork-press and springs back, indicating under-cook or wrong cut size — re-cut smaller and retest. Pooled broth on the tray causing fork-drip fail — drain briefly on absorbent paper and re-shoot.

specimens.prep: Weigh 220 g braised beef brisket noodles as served; do not blend, sieve, or add water/liquid. Pick out and reserve 1 whole noodle strand and 1 chunk of brisket (≈2 cm) on a separate plate for stills. Spread remaining portion flat on the capture mat so a checkerboard square and 100 mm ruler are visible at the same time. If strands clump, separate gently with the fork tines only — no cutting.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into a noodle strand until the tines blanch white; food must not fully compress, ooze, or pass between tines. Hold the loaded fork vertically for 5 s — the piece must not flow or drip off (fork drip test). Spoon tilt: lift a heaped teaspoon of brisket+broth and tilt the spoon to almost vertical; the chunk must sit on the spoon, not slide off as liquid. Pass = piece holds shape and stays on utensil under its own weight; if broth runs and the piece drops, re-make.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: noodle strand ≈3 mm thick, smooth cylindrical surface, no sauce pooling between tines. On the spoon: a single intact brisket block sitting in a thin broth film, not a pool. Broth should coat, not submerge.

specimens.fail_modes: Broth thinned so brisket slides off the spoon — re-make, request thicker broth. Noodles overcooked, mash with fork tines — re-make, shorten cook or pick firmer pieces. Portion stirred into a soup — re-make, plate solids + thin broth separately. Re-make allowed once; second fail, re-source.

specimens.prep: - Weigh 250 g of the stir-fry into the blender jug; reject any burnt or bitter portion. - Add 80 ml warm water (40–50 °C) and blend 45–60 s until smooth — no egg grains or skin flecks visible when a spoonful is held to the light. - Press through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a ladle; discard the retained skin and curd. At L3 the 4 mm sieve is the lump-free gauge (the restriction on sieving applies at L5, not L3). - Measure the sieved volume V in ml and record it. Using one thickener type throughout the study (e.g. a xanthan-based dysphagia thickener), add 2.5 g per 100 ml of V while stirring briskly; let stand 60 s; stir again 15 s. - Calibrate by test, not by feel: - If it runs off the fork in a continuous stream (too THIN): add thickener in 0.5 g per 100 ml steps, up to a ceiling of 4.0 g per 100 ml. - If it will not leave the fork at all and just mounds there (too THICK): whisk in 10 ml warm water per 100 ml, then retest. - Record the actual grams of thickener per 100 ml used.
specimens.iddsi_test: - ACTIVE — 5.2 spoon tilt. Take a level spoonful; tilt the spoon smoothly to 30–45° over the bowl. PASS: the specimen slides off as one mass within 3 s and leaves a thin, complete film on the back of the spoon. - ACTIVE — 5.3 fork drip. Lift a loaded fork and hold it level over the bowl. PASS: the specimen drips through the tines slowly in separate dollops over 5 s — not a continuous stream, and not sitting there refusing to move. - ACTIVE — 5.4 syringe flow. Fill the 10 ml syringe to the 10 ml mark, release the plunger, time 10 s. PASS: 8–10 ml remain in the syringe at t = 10 s. Below 8 ml remaining = too thin (reads L2); above 10 ml remaining = too thick (reads L4). All three active tests must pass on the same specimen. - SKIP — 5.1 fork pressure. Applies at L4/L6/L7 (supporting check only at L5); an L3 specimen is a flowing, lump-free liquid with no shape to hold, so a fork press cannot separate L3 from L4 — the syringe and fork tests do that. - L3 verdict = all three active tests pass together.
specimens.visual_qc: - A spoonful coats the back of the spoon completely, no gaps, no lumps catching the edge. - A ribbon laid on a flat plate settles to a smooth mound within 2–3 s and does not run out. - Uniform pale orange-yellow; no tomato skin flecks, no egg curds, no oil film on the surface. - No blending bubbles on the surface — rest 60 s before shooting.
