specimens.fail_modes: - Syringe leaves <8 ml at 10 s (too thin, reads L2): re-blend 15 s with the thickener, then add 0.5 g per 100 ml thickener and retest — thickening moves it toward L3. Do not add water. - Syringe leaves >10 ml at 10 s (too thick, reads L4): whisk in 10 ml warm water per 100 ml and retest — thinning moves it toward L3. - Fork drip runs as a continuous stream (too thin): add thickener 0.5 g per 100 ml, retest. - Fork drip will not move off the fork (too thick): whisk in 10 ml warm water per 100 ml, retest. - Lumpy — tomato skin flecks or egg curds block the sieve: add 20 ml warm water, re-blend 60 s, re-sieve through the same 4 mm sieve. If a second pass still blocks, discard the batch and remake — a lumpy specimen is neither L3 nor L4, so do not relabel it at a coarser level.

specimens.prep: Port 350 g tomato egg stir-fry into blender; add 60 ml warm water. Blend on high for 45 s. Press 200 g of the blend through the 4 mm sieve using the back of a spoon; discard any seeds or skin that do not pass through. Return sieved blend to blender. Add thickener at 2.0 g per 100 ml of blend (calibration starting point — record actual grams used). Blend 15 s to incorporate. Let rest 2 min, then stir once. Do not add extra water after sieving.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: scoop a heaped forkful and hold level over a white plate for 10 s. Pass criterion: the entire mound sits on top of and between the tines with zero drip falling from the fork. Fork pressure: press the flat of the fork tines into the specimen until the thumbnail blanches white (approx. 17 N). Pass criterion: the indent holds clean, no liquid pools, no extrusion of thin liquid around the tines. Spoon tilt: place 5 ml on a spoon and tilt to a steep angle. Pass criterion: the specimen stays in a cohesive mound without sliding off. Do not perform the syringe flow test for L4.
specimens.visual_qc: Uniform glossy orange-pink color with no visible egg white chunks, no tomato skin flecks, no free red liquid pooling at the rim of the spoon. Surface should look smooth and slightly matte, holding a soft peak when scooped.
specimens.shots: Capture three stills and two clips. Stills: tomato_egg_stirfry_L4_take1.jpg at 45-degree hero with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; tomato_egg_stirfry_L4_take2.jpg top-down with checkerboard centered; tomato_egg_stirfry_L4_take3.jpg fork-press close-up mid-press showing the tines half-submerged. Clips: tomato_egg_stirfry_L4_take1.mp4, 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt; tomato_egg_stirfry_L4_take2.mp4, the full IDDSI test sequence. Confirm focus and lighting before each capture.
specimens.fail_modes: (a) Blend still separates a watery red layer on standing: under-blended or under-thickened; re-blend 10 s and add 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml, retest. (b) Specimen flows through fork tines or drips within 10 s: too thin; add thickener incrementally and retest. (c) Lumpy texture with visible white egg threads after sieving: blend an additional 20 s, re-sieve. Two failed attempts at the same fault → log as reject and re-cook a fresh portion.

specimens.prep: Cook or buy 300 g of tomato egg stir-fry. Remove any whole dried chilies or large aromatics. Pulse in consumer blender 4-6 s only — no longer, to keep visible bits, not a purée. Press through a 4 mm sieve, pushing soft solids through with the back of a spoon and reserving any seeds or skins that stay behind. The per-level note permits the juices; do not drain them. Weigh the sieved portion on the digital scale. Target yield ≈ 250-270 g. If the result is too wet and pools thin liquid on the plate, mix in thickener 1.0 g per 100 ml of free liquid, stir, rest 60 s, re-check. Record starting grams, blender seconds, thickener grams used, final grams.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the mound until the thumbnail blanches; the food must squash and stay squashed — no recovery. Fork drip: lift fork; nothing drips through the tines. Spoon tilt: tilt a teaspoon of the food; the mound holds its shape and slides as a cohesive lump, does not run. Thin-liquid absence: tilt the plate; no separate liquid pools at the edge.
specimens.visual_qc: Mound on spoon holds a soft peak without slumping. Flecks of yellow egg and red tomato skin visible, every piece smaller than a grain of rice. Surface glistens but no liquid collects on the plate rim.
specimens.shots: Still A: 45-degree hero, mound on white plate, 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still B: top-down, checkerboard beneath plate only. Still C: fork-press close-up, tines mid-press into mound. Clip 1: 8-12 s, fork-press followed by spoon-tilt on the same specimen. Clip 2: 8-12 s, full IDDSI test sequence — fork press, fork drip, spoon tilt. Files: tomato_egg_stirfry_L5_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Egg pieces larger than 4 mm after sieving → return to blender for 1-2 s pulse and re-sieve. Free tomato juice pools on the plate → add thickener 0.5 g per 100 ml, rest, retest. Mound cracks instead of squashing (too dry) → fold in 5-10 ml warm water and retest.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g tomato egg stir-fry straight from the container. Cut any piece over 15 mm with the side of a fork; reject any piece that will not reduce to ≤15 mm — the per-level note makes coarser pieces impossible at L6. Hold back 50 g for fork-pressure tests. To the remaining 200 g add 40 ml hot water and blend 10 s; press through the 4 mm sieve, pressing with the back of a spoon and discarding seeds and skin that will not pass. Returned specimen should read ≈220 g wet mash with discrete soft curds. No thickener — L6, not L3.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the fork flat onto a 15 mm piece until the thumbnail blanches white; the piece must squash and not recover its shape. Spoon tilt: a heaped spoon tilted 45° holds the piece without it sliding or rolling off. Fork drip: lifting the fork at normal speed, no liquid runs or drips off the tines — mash is cohesive, not soupy.
specimens.visual_qc: Glossy pale-orange mash on the spoon, not red and watery. Discrete yellow curds 8–12 mm visible against the tomato. Fork holds its shape when lifted; no sauce pools on the plate beneath.
specimens.shots: tomato_egg_stirfry_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and checkerboard in frame. tomato_egg_stirfry_L6_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. tomato_egg_stirfry_L6_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, blanched thumbnail visible. tomato_egg_stirfry_L6_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, continuous. tomato_egg_stirfry_L6_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, each step narrated.
specimens.fail_modes: Mash too wet: tomato separates and drips off the fork — re-blend 5 s, re-sieve. Pieces still above 15 mm after cutting: re-cut, do not proceed. Curds rubbery and spring back under fork pressure: over-blended — discard and start with a shorter pulse.

specimens.prep: - Weigh **200 g** of tomato egg stir-fry as served, straight from the container onto the tray, and record the mass. - **No blending, no sieving, no chopping, no thickener, no added liquid, no pressing and no folding.** L7 is the food as bought and normally served; each of those steps moves the specimen toward L6/L5/L4. - Plate as bought, at serving temperature, and capture within **10 min** of plating. Do not chill the portion — cold egg sets firmer and reads harder than the dish as it is normally eaten. - Piece-size check: hold two or three pieces (one tomato wedge and one egg curd) against the 100 mm ruler. Every piece must measure **at least 15 mm** on its longest dimension and must still need chewing. If the batch is served finely scrambled, L7 is not reachable for it — see FAIL MODES.
specimens.iddsi_test: - Fork pressure (5.1 — the only test that applies at L7): place one piece on the tray, press the flat of the fork bowl down onto it with the thumb until the thumbnail blanches white, then lift. **Pass** = the piece compresses under that pressure and does not recover its shape when the fork is lifted; it stays a distinct piece the fork lifts whole; no free red liquid runs from it. - Sizing check, in the same unbroken take: hold two or three pieces against the 100 mm ruler. Every piece must be **≥15 mm** on its longest dimension. - Spoon tilt: **skip** — 5.2 covers L3/L4/L5. L7 is not a spoonable mass, so this test is not run and is not recorded as pass/fail. - Fork drip: **skip** — 5.3 covers L3/L4. There is no flow through the tines to observe on a solid piece, so this test is not run and is not recorded as pass/fail. - Syringe flow: **skip** — 5.4 is required on every L3 only; a solid piece is not a 10 ml flow sample.
specimens.visual_qc: - Distinct tomato wedges and egg curds, each ≥15 mm, individually separable in the tray. - Red tomato juice and egg coat the pieces and the tray but do not pool into a continuous separate liquid layer. - Pieces hold their shape when nudged with the fork tines; the fork leaves a compression mark that does not spring back. - No oil layer spreading across the tray.

specimens.fail_modes: - Pieces measure **under 15 mm** on their longest dimension (a finely scrambled or over-stirred batch): no bench step increases piece size. Record the measured size, mark the row FAIL, and re-source a chunkier batch — tomato wedges of about 20–30 mm with curds of the same order. - Pieces smear to paste under blanching pressure (**too soft — below L7, drifting toward L5/L6**): the batch is over-cooked or over-stirred. Re-source a batch with intact wedges; no bench step firms a stir-fry, and chilling only stiffens the oil. - Egg curds collapse to fragments during handling: re-plate from an untouched part of the container without pressing. - Free red juice or oil pooling into a continuous layer so the pieces sit in liquid: re-plate from a freshly served portion, wipe the tray edge, re-shoot within 60 s. If the batch is inherently watery, record FAIL and re-source. - Achievability, stated plainly: this dish is normally served in ≥15 mm wedges, so L7 is reachable only from a bought form cut that way. A takeaway that serves it finely chopped cannot be labelled L7 however it is handled — this is the failure the previous empty card invited, because a soft, moist stir-fry handled carelessly lands at L5–L6 and still gets labelled L7. - **Never blend, sieve, chop or thicken an L7 specimen** — those are the L4/L3 steps and would produce a mislabelled L7 row.

specimens.prep: Weigh 150 g steamed chicken with mushrooms, place in blender. Blend 45 s, stop, scrape sides, blend 30 s more. Sieve once through the 4 mm sieve; discard residue. Add 60 ml water, blend 15 s. Measure volume of puree. Add thickener at 1.5 g per 100 ml of puree as the calibration starting point; sprinkle, blend 10 s, rest 60 s, re-blend 5 s. Record actual grams used. Target: coats spoon, pours in a slow ribbon.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork drip: spoon puree, let it fall from fork tines; passes if it drips slowly in continuous blobs, does not run in a thin stream. Spoon tilt: tilt a spoon holding 5 ml; passes if puree slides off slowly, does not pour. Fork pressure: press fork tines into puree and lift; passes if tines leave clear indent, puree mounds without running. Syringe flow test: fill 10 ml syringe, release, read at 10 s; passes if 8-10 ml remains in barrel.
specimens.visual_qc: Smooth, glossy surface with no visible mushroom or chicken flecks after sieving. Holds a soft peak when mounded on spoon, then settles slowly. Color uniform pale beige, no separation of liquid around edges.
specimens.shots: Still 1: 45-degree hero shot, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame, specimen mounded on spoon. Still 2: top-down, checkerboard under petri, full specimen spread. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, tines half-submerged. Clip 1: 8-12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt sequence. Clip 2: IDDSI syringe flow test, full 10 s. Naming: steamed_chicken_with_mus_L3_take1.jpg and .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Puree too thin, drips through fork in a steady stream, or syringe reads below 8 ml — add 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml, re-blend, re-test. Visible solids or fibers post-sieve — re-blend 20 s, re-sieve. Puree too stiff, mounds hold sharp peak, syringe reads above 10 ml — add 5 ml water per 100 ml, re-blend, re-test. Two failed re-makes: discard, restart prep, record new starting weight.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g cooked chicken+mushroom mixture. Add 60 ml hot water. Blend 90 s on high, scrape bowl, blend 60 s more. Sieve once through 4 mm; discard residue. Target yield about 300 ml puree. Thickener: start at 2.0 g per 100 ml puree (calibration point — record actual on the scorecard). Whisk thickener into warm puree, rest 2 min, stir, re-weigh. If the fork-drip test (below) is not yet passed, add 0.5 g/100 ml increments, rest, re-test. Do not add more water after sieving — re-blend is the only recovery step.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the specimen on a plate until the tines blanch. The puree must hold the indentation without liquid pooling around the print. Pass. Spoon tilt: scoop, tilt spoon 45°. Specimen must sit in a mound, not slide or drip. Pass. Fork drip: lift fork with a heaped sample; specimen must sit in a mound above the tines, not drip through in 5 s. Pass. No separate thin liquid film may be visible in the bowl.
specimens.visual_qc: Surface is matte, no shine or watery ring at the bowl edge. No visible mushroom fibres, skin flecks, or seed specks. Holds a clean spoon-shaped mound when scooped; tip does not slump.
specimens.shots: stills: steamed_chicken_with_mus_L4_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame; steamed_chicken_with_mus_L4_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard flat beside bowl; steamed_chicken_with_mus_L4_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up mid-press, ruler edge visible. clips: steamed_chicken_with_mus_L4_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s, fork-press then spoon-tilt; steamed_chicken_with_mus_L4_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film, fork-drip + spoon-tilt + fork-pressure in sequence.
specimens.fail_modes: Puree flows through fork tines or levels on the plate → under-thick; add 0.5 g/100 ml thickener, rest 2 min, re-test, re-shoot take1. Loose liquid pools around the mound → over-blended with excess water; re-blend thicker batch, do not dilute. Visible fibres or mushroom skin after sieving → sieve discard too coarse; re-sieve one pass, re-shoot take2 only.

specimens.prep: Start with 200 g of steamed chicken with mushrooms, keeping the cooking juices that accompany the dish. Strip any visible bone, skin, or gristle. Mince finely with a clean knife, then work the mince through the juices with a fork until the pieces are uniform. Pulse briefly in the consumer blender for 5-8 seconds only; the goal is to bring the particles to the 4 mm ceiling, not to puree. Press the mash through a 4 mm sieve, discarding anything retained above. Stir in 2-5 ml of the reserved juices per 100 g of mash to keep it moist; no thin liquid should pool on the surface. No thickener is required at L5; if the mash releases free liquid on standing, blot, do not add thickener.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure test: press the fork tines flat against the mash; the specimen must squash and the slots must be clearly visible through it. Release pressure; the mash must not spring back. Spoon tilt test: a teaspoon of the mash must hold its shape on the spoon when tilted, not flow or drip off. Fork drip test: lift the fork; no thin liquid should drip through or run off the tines within 10 seconds.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: cohesive clump with no loose drips, individual mince grains still visible but all smaller than a rice grain. On the spoon: a soft mound that holds its shape when tilted, surface glistening but no pooling liquid at the rim.
specimens.shots: Take 1 hero 45-degree still with the 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler in frame, file as steamed_chicken_with_mus_L5_take1.jpg. Take 1 top-down still on the checkerboard, same filename stem. Take 1 fork-press close-up mid-press, same filename stem. Capture one 8-12 second clip of the fork-press and spoon-tilt, and one IDDSI test film clip, both as steamed_chicken_with_mus_L5_take1.mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Particles above 4 mm after sieving: re-mince and re-sieve. Free thin liquid pools on the plate: blot and re-test, do not add thickener. Mash recovers shape after fork pressure: more fork work, then re-test.

specimens.prep: Dice steamed chicken into cubes ≤15 mm. Cut mushrooms into pieces ≤15 mm. Combine 200 g diced chicken with 60 g mushroom pieces. Do NOT blend. Do NOT sieve. Do NOT add thickener. Do NOT add water. Target specimen mass per capture tray: 150 g. If the chicken shreds rather than dices cleanly, the texture is wrong for L6 and must be re-cooked with a firmer piece.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into a piece until thumbnail blanches white. The piece must squash completely and not spring back. Recovery after lift = fail. Spoon tilt: no specimen should fall, drip, or slide off a tilted spoon held at 90°. Fork drip: lift a piece on fork tines — it must sit solidly, no drip, no slump within 10 seconds.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: discrete cubes under 15 mm, edges still defined, surface moist but no pooled liquid. On the spoon: holds a stable mound at a tilt; sheen is gravy, not free liquid. Pieces show visible white meat fibers and mushroom slice rings, not a paste.
specimens.shots: 3 stills: steamed_chicken_with_mus_L6_take1.jpg hero at 45° with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard visible in frame; steamed_chicken_with_mus_L6_take1.jpg top-down on checkerboard; steamed_chicken_with_mus_L6_take1.jpg fork-press mid-press close-up. 2 clips: steamed_chicken_with_mus_L6_take1.mp4 fork-press and spoon-tilt (8–12 s); steamed_chicken_with_mus_L6_take1.mp4 full IDDSI test film showing pressure and tilt.
specimens.fail_modes: (a) Pieces exceed 15 mm or are uneven — re-dice, do not blend. (b) Chicken shreds into fibers that spring back under fork — protein overcooked or wrong cut; re-cook with a firmer breast portion and re-dice. (c) Pooled liquid on the tray — drain on a sieve for 30 s, then re-weigh to 150 g. Any fail: discard batch and start a new 200 g prep.

specimens.prep: Take 250 g of steamed chicken with mushrooms as served from the home-cooked batch. Do not blend, sieve, or add thickener — L7 is the unmodified reference specimen. Place the chicken piece with mushrooms on a plate, keep sauce that clings naturally to the food; do not drain or pat dry. Record actual mass on the digital scale before plating. Set the A4 capture kit, ruler, and 15 mm checkerboard beside the plate within one arm's reach. If a blender step is attempted, stop: L7 forbids processing — re-make from fresh.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press the four tines flat onto the chicken surface with steady thumb force. The food must not fully compress, ooze liquid, or pass between tines when lifted. Fork drip: lift the fork vertically above the plate; no continuous drip should fall — only clinging sauce is acceptable. Spoon tilt: rest a spoonful on the spoon and tilt 45 degrees; the chicken must sit stably without sliding off. All three pass criteria are required; if any fails, re-classify and re-make.
specimens.visual_qc: Chicken holds its shape on the fork without slumping. Mushrooms remain intact and distinguishable. Surface looks moist, not pooling.
specimens.shots: Three stills named steamed_chicken_with_mus_L7_take1.jpg, _take2.jpg, _take3.jpg: hero at 45 degrees with ruler and checkerboard in frame, top-down on checkerboard showing full portion, fork-press close-up mid-press. Two clips .mp4, 8-12 s each: fork-press and spoon-tilt, plus the full IDDSI test film.
specimens.fail_modes: Over-steamed chicken collapses under fork — re-make with shorter steam. Loose sauce runs off fork — spoon off excess before test. Mushrooms turn to puree — pick firmer specimens.

specimens.prep: Weigh 300 g cooked lor mai gai (debone, strip chicken). Add to the blender with 120 ml warm stock at 40–50 °C (chicken or rice cooking water). Blend 45–60 s on high until homogeneous. Sieve through the 4 mm sieve, working the puree through with the back of a ladle until nothing further passes; discard retained solids — L4 is lump-free, so the sieve enforces the level here. Weigh back to confirm at least 250 g of puree.  Return the puree to the blender. Thicken with a xanthan-gum thickener at 1.0 g per 100 ml puree, blend 15 s, and rest 60 s. Record actual grams used. Target final mass 250–300 g, no standing liquid.  Pass window — the single target every branch in section 5 is judged against: the puree must sit as a mound on a fork capping the tines, flatten under thumbnail pressure and stay compressed, and release from a tilted spoon as one soft lump leaving a thin film on the bowl. It must not pour, and it must not sit as a stiff unmoving mound.
specimens.iddsi_test: All three L4 tests apply: fork pressure (5.1), spoon tilt (5.2), fork drip (5.3). No syringe flow test — 5.4 is L3 only.  Fork pressure: mound one heaped tablespoon (15 ml) of puree on a dessert fork; press with the thumbnail until it blanches white. Pass = the surface flattens and stays compressed, no crumbs, no run-through. Fail = the puree squeezes between the tines and runs through (too thin), or the mound stays domed and hard with no compression mark (too thick).  Fork drip: lift the fork 15 cm above the plate and hold 10 s. Pass = the puree sits as a mound above the tines and sheds at most a slow single strand or 2 drops. A continuous stream is a fail (too thin). Zero drip is not the L4 target — that is the L5 criterion, and chasing it over-thickens the specimen out of level.  Spoon tilt: scoop one heaped dessert spoon (15 ml), tilt to 90° and tap the back of the bowl twice with a fingertip. Pass = the puree releases as one soft lump within the two taps and slides off slowly, leaving a thin film about 1 mm on the bowl — the spoon is coated, neither empty nor still holding a mound. Fail = it pours off before 90° (too thin), or it remains a full sitting mound after two taps (too thick).  No separate thin liquid may pool on the plate after 60 s.
specimens.visual_qc: Fork: glossy mound capping all tines, clean spaces between prongs blocked by puree. Spoon: drops cleanly as a soft lump within two taps, leaving a thin film, spoon near-empty. Surface: matte-sheen, even colour, no rice grains or chicken fibres visible, no watery halo at the plate edge.
specimens.shots: Still 1 — 45° hero, ruler + 15 mm checkerboard in frame: lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L4_take1.jpg Still 2 — top-down with checkerboard centred: lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L4_take2.jpg Still 3 — fork-press close-up mid-press, tines embedded: lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L4_take3.jpg Still 4 — spoon-tilt at 90° mid-release, film left on the bowl: lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L4_take4.jpg Clip 1 — 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt, single take: lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L4_take1.mp4 Clip 2 — full IDDSI test sequence (fork pressure, fork drip, spoon tilt), 15–25 s: lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L4_take2.mp4
specimens.fail_modes: Too thin — puree pours on the spoon tilt, runs through the tines, or sheds a continuous strand on fork drip: add 0.3 g thickener per 100 ml, blend 15 s, rest 60 s, retest. Do not exceed 1.6 g per 100 ml total. Too thick — puree sits as a stiff mound that does not release after two taps, or the fork-pressure mound stays domed with no compression mark: thin with warm stock at 40–50 °C, 20 ml at a time (up to 40 ml beyond the 120 ml base), blend 15 s, rest 60 s, retest. Never add thickener to correct a specimen that has already been over-thickened. Over-thickened batch — the operator chased zero fork drip and the puree no longer releases from the spoon: this is a too-thick failure, not a pass. Thin with warm stock as above; if more than 40 ml of extra stock is needed, re-make from 300 g with 100 ml base stock. Too coarse — visible rice grains, chicken fibre, or grainy paste after sieving: re-blend 20 s, re-sieve through 4 mm, retest. Watery halo pools around the mound on the plate: phase separation — blend 10 s longer and rest 90 s before re-test. If still failing, re-make from 300 g with stock reduced to 100 ml. If the puree still cannot be brought inside the pass window — pouring at 160 ml total stock, or a stiff mound at the thickener maximum — the batch is not usable at L4; re-make from 300 g with 100 ml base stock rather than forcing it with more thickener.

specimens.prep: Weigh 250 g of steamed Lor mai gai (rice + chicken, takeaway or frozen). Discard any wrapper leaves; pull meat off bone. Pulse in the consumer blender for 6–8 s, 1 s bursts, until coarsely chopped — do not purée. Press the chop through the 4 mm sieve with the back of a fork; discard what stays on. Loosen with warm stock, ≈30–40 ml per 100 g of chop, until visibly moist and cohesive but not pooling. Fork-mash any remaining lumps. No thickener at L5.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork pressure: press fork tines into the specimen on a plate. It must squash, the tines leave a clear imprint, and the material does not spring back. Spoon tilt: a small mound on a spoon must hold shape when tilted to 45°, then slide off cleanly in 1–2 pieces when the spoon is turned — not pour. Fork drip: lift the fork; nothing drips through the tines. Pass = holds, squashes, does not recover.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork: speckled mince with visible rice and chicken flecks, all grains broken to ≤4 mm, surface glistening with stock, no free liquid pooling on the plate. On the spoon: a mound that sits 8–10 mm tall without slumping.
specimens.shots: Stills: (a) hero 45° with 100 mm ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame; (b) top-down on checkerboard showing full spread; (c) fork-press close-up mid-press, tines 5 mm into specimen. Clips: (d) 8–12 s fork-press then spoon-tilt in one continuous take; (e) IDDSI test film, full fork-pressure and spoon-tilt sequence. Name: lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L5_take1.jpg / .mp4.
specimens.fail_modes: Coarse chop: any grain or meat piece >4 mm after sieving — re-blend 2 s, re-sieve. Too dry: cracks on the spoon tilt instead of sliding — add stock 10 ml per 100 g, remix. Too wet: free liquid on the plate or drips from the fork — drain on sieve 30 s, no more stock.

specimens.prep: Weigh 200 g takeaway or steamed-then-defrosted lor mai gai. Separate filling from rice. Hand-chop filling to pieces ≤15 mm; chop the sticky rice mass to pieces ≤15 mm — do not blend, do not sieve; the per-level note requires chopped pieces, not a puree. Combine chopped filling and rice in a bowl. Record actual masses of filling and rice on the run sheet. If the mix looks dry and sheds loose rice grains, stir in 5–10 ml hot water per 100 g mix to re-bind; record ml added. No thickener required for L6; if a test shows runnier behaviour, note it and treat as a fail, not a re-thicken.
specimens.iddsi_test: Fork-pressure test: press fork tines onto a representative piece until thumbnail blanches white. Pass = piece squashes, does not recover its shape when fork is removed. Spoon tilt: place a spoonful on a spoon and tilt to near-vertical; pieces should sit in cohesion without sliding off as liquid. Fork drip: lift fork with a speared piece; pass = no continuous drip from the piece for 10 s. Repeat each test on three pieces from different zones of the batch.
specimens.visual_qc: On the fork, pieces should be irregular chunks no larger than the 15 mm square on the checkerboard, with visible chicken, mushroom, and rice grains. Rice should look clumped-into-pieces, not glossy-wet or soupy. On the spoon, the mass should hold a soft heap, not slump flat.
specimens.shots: Still 1: lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L6_take1.jpg — 45° hero, ruler and 15 mm checkerboard in frame. Still 2: top-down on checkerboard, spoon of specimen centred. Still 3: fork-press close-up mid-press, thumbnail blanch visible. Clip 1: 8–12 s fork-press and spoon-tilt sequence. Clip 2: full IDDSI test film, narrated take numbers.
specimens.fail_modes: Piece exceeds 15 mm after chopping — re-chop, do not proceed. Piece recovers shape after fork pressure — recheck batch, likely under-steamed; re-steam 3 min and retest. Rice sheds whole grains or mix weeps liquid — re-bind with 5 ml hot water per 100 g, retest; if still wet, treat as failed batch.

specimens.prep: - Reheat one whole parcel per pack — typically 20–25 min steamed from frozen, or 8–10 min from chilled — until the centre probes ≥75 °C. - Remove and discard the outer lotus leaf and any foil. Keep the rice mass with its fillings (chicken, shiitake, sausage, dried scallop) as served — do not pick them out. If any single filling piece is over 25 mm across, halve it with a knife so nothing exceeds 25 mm. - With a knife or spoon, portion the rice mass into regular pieces 15–25 mm across, measured against the 100 mm ruler (the 25 mm figure is an operational cap for the capture frame, not a texture limit — L7 requires only ≥15 mm). Discard any fragment under 15 mm: it reads L6. - Do not blend. Do not sieve — a 4 mm sieve cannot enforce a 15 mm limit. Do not add thickener or liquid — L7 is the whole-food reference. - Weigh 200 g of portioned pieces onto the plate; keep covered and warm (≤10 min) until testing.
specimens.iddsi_test: - ACTIVE — 5.1 fork pressure. Press the tines of a standard metal fork flat onto one 15–25 mm piece with steady thumb pressure until the nail blanches white; hold 5 s; lift. PASS: the piece holds its shape, the tines leave a clear, persistent indentation, the fork does not cut through in one press, and the piece does not crumble into loose grains. Test 3 pieces; all 3 must pass. This is what rules out L5 (fork-mashable) and L6 (squashes flat). - SKIP — 5.2 spoon tilt. Applies at L3/L4/L5 only; an L7 specimen is a solid that must stay put on a tilted spoon, so the test carries no discriminating information. - SKIP — 5.3 fork drip. Applies at L3/L4 only; L7 carries no free liquid to drip through the tines. - SKIP — 5.4 syringe flow. Every L3 only; 15–25 mm pieces cannot be drawn into a 10 ml syringe. - L7 verdict = all pieces 15–25 mm AND 5.1 fork pressure passes.
specimens.visual_qc: - Grains are distinct and bound only by their own stickiness; no sauce pooling and no free liquid at the parcel base. - Surface matte, not glossy with free liquid. - Every piece 15–25 mm on the ruler; no fragment below 15 mm. - Fork tines leave visible imprints; the rice does not smear or ooze between the tines.
specimens.shots: - lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L7_take1.jpg — 45° hero on the capture board with 15 mm checkerboard and 100 mm ruler in frame. - lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L7_take2.jpg — top-down, checkerboard only. - lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L7_take3.jpg — fork-press close-up, mid-press, tines embedded. - lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L7_take1.mp4 — 8–12 s fork-pressure sequence, three pieces in order. - lor_mai_gai_glutinous_ri_L7_take2.mp4 — full IDDSI test film (fork pressure only — the sole active test at L7).
specimens.fail_modes: - Free liquid pools at the parcel base (reads L6 or wetter): dab the surface and base with paper towel for 30 s before testing; if liquid returns, remake with a fresh parcel and add no sauce. - The rice mass crushes through the fork in one press (too soft — reads L5/L6): re-steam a fresh parcel 5 min longer so it sets firmer; if it still crushes, that parcel is too wet — use a drier pack. - Any piece under 15 mm, or the mass crumbling into single grains: re-cut from a fresh parcel into 15–25 mm regular pieces and discard the fines — do not press them back together. - The mass falls apart into loose grains when lifted (binding lost, under-steamed): re-steam 5 min longer, rest 2 min, re-portion. - Grains slide off the spoon when tilted: not a fail criterion at L7 — 5.2 spoon tilt is skipped. Judge the specimen on piece size and fork pressure only; if the piece also crumbles, apply the binding fail mode above.
